    18	
    19	## Milestone 1 — validated boot state and machine diagnostics
    20	
    21	- Parse and validate all loader ranges into a stable boot-info value.
    22	- Preserve reserved, reclaimable, firmware, and MMIO regions distinctly.
    23	- Add serial formatting tests, CPU feature reporting, and a framebuffer or documented serial-only console.
    24	- Establish explicit ownership and reclaim timing for loader memory.
    25	
    26	**Exit criteria:** malformed maps fail closed; an emulator test validates reported regions and boot metadata.
    27	
    28	## Milestone 2 — memory ownership and CPU exceptions
    29	
    30	- Physical frame allocator with overflow-safe range handling and exhaustion tests.
    31	- Kernel-owned page-table management and documented direct-map policy.
    32	- Global heap with deterministic out-of-memory behavior.
    33	- GDT/TSS and IDT setup; exception handlers with register/error-code diagnostics; fault-injection tests.
    34	
    35	**Exit criteria:** allocator and mapping invariants are tested, page faults are diagnosable, and the kernel remains bootable under emulator tests.
    36	
    37	## Milestone 3 — interrupts, time, and scheduling
    38	
    39	- Timer and interrupt-controller setup with explicit interrupt-safe locking rules.
    40	- Kernel threads and context switching; per-CPU data before SMP work.
    41	- Preemptive scheduling only after interrupt, stack, and lock invariants are validated.
    42	- Application processor startup as a separate milestone, not an implicit extension of single-core code.
    43	
    44	**Exit criteria:** deterministic thread lifecycle tests and bounded timer/preemption integration tests.
    45

    47	
    48	- User-mode entry/exit and isolated address spaces.
    49	- Versioned syscall ABI, validated copy-in/copy-out, and documented error semantics.
    50	- Initial process lifecycle, descriptor table, and executable-loading path.
    51	- Adversarial tests for invalid pointers, bad lengths, overflow, and process teardown.
    52	
    53	**Exit criteria:** a controlled userspace init process can execute and use a small documented syscall subset without corrupting the kernel on invalid input.
    54

    56

    58	- Process creation/exec/wait semantics, pipes or IPC, and signal-like delivery as designed.
    59	- Device discovery/driver model and networking only after ownership and isolation policies exist.
    60	- Compatibility tests for any claimed Unix/POSIX behavior; keep unsupported operations explicit.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a pinned Limine hybrid ISO and smoke-test it in QEMU.

Only Python's standard library is required. The Limine binary archive is kept
under target/ and checked against the SHA-256 published for the pinned release.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.request
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TARGET_DIR = ROOT / "target"
LIMINE_VERSION = "12.9.3"
LIMINE_ARCHIVE_NAME = "limine-binary.zip"
LIMINE_ARCHIVE_SHA256 = "1bdbbcda650c5dba9b1eca5833d598137bf11bd6289bc89b6bcc4f8f112fa676"
LIMINE_ARCHIVE_URL = (
    "https://github.com/Limine-Bootloader/Limine/releases/download/"
    f"v{LIMINE_VERSION}/{LIMINE_ARCHIVE_NAME}"
)
KERNEL = TARGET_DIR / "x86_64-unknown-none" / "release" / "rustix"
ISO_ROOT = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-iso-root"
ISO_PATH = TARGET_DIR / "rustix.iso"

REQUIRED_LIMINE_FILES = (
    "limine-bios.sys",
    "limine-bios-cd.bin",
    "limine-uefi-cd.bin",
    "BOOTX64.EFI",
)


class BuildError(RuntimeError):
    """An actionable error while preparing or testing the boot image."""


def require_tool(name: str) -> str:
    path = shutil.which(name)
    if path is None:
        raise BuildError(f"required tool '{name}' was not found on PATH")
    return path


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as source:
        for block in iter(lambda: source.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def safe_extract(archive: zipfile.ZipFile, destination: Path) -> None:
    root = destination.resolve()
    for member in archive.infolist():
        name = PurePosixPath(member.filename)
        mode = member.external_attr >> 16
        if not name.parts or name.is_absolute() or ".." in name.parts or ":" in name.parts[0]:
            raise BuildError(f"unsafe path in Limine archive: {member.filename}")
        if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
            raise BuildError(f"symlink in Limine archive is not allowed: {member.filename}")
        output = (destination / Path(*name.parts)).resolve()
        if output != root and root not in output.parents:
            raise BuildError(f"archive member escapes extraction directory: {member.filename}")
    archive.extractall(destination)


def ensure_limine() -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    cache = TARGET_DIR / "tools" / f"limine-{LIMINE_VERSION}"
    archive_path = TARGET_DIR / "tools" / LIMINE_ARCHIVE_NAME
    extracted = cache / "archive"
    cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    extracted.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if not archive_path.exists():
        print(f"Downloading Limine {LIMINE_VERSION} binary release...")
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            LIMINE_ARCHIVE_URL,
            headers={"User-Agent": "Rustix-OS-build/0.1"},
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
                with archive_path.open("wb") as output:
                    shutil.copyfileobj(response, output)
        except Exception as error:
            archive_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            raise BuildError(f"could not download pinned Limine release: {error}") from error

    actual_hash = sha256(archive_path)
    if actual_hash != LIMINE_ARCHIVE_SHA256:
        archive_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise BuildError(
            "Limine archive SHA-256 mismatch: "
            f"expected {LIMINE_ARCHIVE_SHA256}, got {actual_hash}"
        )

    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path) as archive:
            safe_extract(archive, extracted)
    except (OSError, zipfile.BadZipFile) as error:
        raise BuildError(f"could not extract the pinned Limine archive: {error}") from error

    def find_asset(name: str) -> Path:
        matches = sorted(extracted.rglob(name))
        if not matches:
            raise BuildError(f"Limine {LIMINE_VERSION} archive is missing {name}")
        return matches[0]

    limine_tool_name = "limine.exe" if sys.platform == "win32" else "limine"
    limine_tool = find_asset(limine_tool_name)
    if sys.platform != "win32":
        limine_tool.chmod(
            limine_tool.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IXUSR | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IXOTH
        )
    return limine_tool, extracted


def build_image() -> None:
    if not KERNEL.is_file():
        raise BuildError("kernel ELF not found; run 'just build' first")
    xorriso = require_tool("xorriso")
    limine_tool, limine_root = ensure_limine()

    shutil.rmtree(ISO_ROOT, ignore_errors=True)
    boot_dir = ISO_ROOT / "boot" / "limine"
    efi_dir = ISO_ROOT / "EFI" / "BOOT"
    boot_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    efi_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    shutil.copy2(KERNEL, ISO_ROOT / "boot" / "rustix")
    shutil.copy2(ROOT / "limine.conf", ISO_ROOT / "limine.conf")

    for name in REQUIRED_LIMINE_FILES:
        source = next(iter(sorted(limine_root.rglob(name))), None)
        if source is None:
            raise BuildError(f"Limine archive is missing required file {name}")
        if name == "BOOTX64.EFI":
            shutil.copy2(source, efi_dir / name)
        else:
            shutil.copy2(source, boot_dir / name)

    ISO_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    xorriso_command = [
        xorriso,
        "-as",
        "mkisofs",
        "-R",
        "-r",
        "-J",
        "-b",
        "boot/limine/limine-bios-cd.bin",
        "-no-emul-boot",
        "-boot-load-size",
        "4",
        "-boot-info-table",
        "-hfsplus",
        "-apm-block-size",
        "2048",
        "--efi-boot",
        "boot/limine/limine-uefi-cd.bin",
        "-efi-boot-part",
        "-efi-boot-image",
        "--protective-msdos-label",
        str(ISO_ROOT),
        "-o",
        str(ISO_PATH),
    ]
    subprocess.run(xorriso_command, cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    subprocess.run([str(limine_tool), "bios-install", str(ISO_PATH)], cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    print(f"Created hybrid BIOS/UEFI image: {ISO_PATH.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def smoke_test(timeout: int) -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; run 'just image' first")

    serial_log = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-qemu-serial.log"
    serial_log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    serial_log.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    serial_device = "file:" + serial_log.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
    command = [
        qemu,
        "-machine",
        "q35",
        "-m",
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        serial_device,
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]

    timed_out = False
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, timeout=timeout, check=False)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        timed_out = True
        result = None

    if not timed_out and result is not None and result.returncode != 0:
        details = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
        raise BuildError(
            f"QEMU exited with status {result.returncode} before the smoke-test timeout.\n"
            f"Serial output:\n{details}"
        )

    output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
    expected = (
        "Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap",
        "bootstrap complete; scheduler and userspace are not implemented yet",
    )
    missing = [marker for marker in expected if marker not in output]
    if missing:
        raise BuildError(
            "QEMU did not reach the expected kernel state; missing serial markers: "
            + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
            + f"\nSerial output:\n{output or '<empty>'}"
        )

    print(f"QEMU boot smoke test passed (bounded to {timeout}s).")
    print(f"Captured serial log: {serial_log.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    subparsers.add_parser("image", help="create a pinned Limine BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO")
    smoke = subparsers.add_parser("smoke", help="boot the ISO and check its serial output")
    smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:
        if args.command == "image":
            build_image()
        else:
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            smoke_test(args.timeout)
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
        print(f"Rustix boot workflow failed: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

    ]
    subprocess.run(xorriso_command, cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    subprocess.run([str(limine_tool), "bios-install", str(ISO_PATH)], cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    print(f"Created hybrid BIOS/UEFI image: {ISO_PATH.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def smoke_test(timeout: int) -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; run 'just image' first")

    serial_log = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-qemu-serial.log"
    serial_log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    serial_log.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    serial_device = "file:" + serial_log.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
    command = [
        qemu,
        "-machine",
        "q35",
        "-m",
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        serial_device,
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]

    timed_out = False
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, timeout=timeout, check=False)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        timed_out = True
        result = None

    if not timed_out and result is not None and result.returncode != 0:
        details = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
        raise BuildError(
            f"QEMU exited with status {result.returncode} before the smoke-test timeout.\n"
            f"Serial output:\n{details}"
        )

    output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
    expected = (
        "Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap",
        "bootstrap complete; scheduler and userspace are not implemented yet",
    )
    missing = [marker for marker in expected if marker not in output]
    if missing:
        raise BuildError(
            "QEMU did not reach the expected kernel state; missing serial markers: "
            + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
            + f"\nSerial output:\n{output or '<empty>'}"
        )

    print(f"QEMU boot smoke test passed (bounded to {timeout}s).")
    print(f"Captured serial log: {serial_log.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    subparsers.add_parser("image", help="create a pinned Limine BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO")
    smoke = subparsers.add_parser("smoke", help="boot the ISO and check its serial output")
    smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:
        if args.command == "image":
            build_image()
        else:
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            smoke_test(args.timeout)
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
        print(f"Rustix boot workflow failed: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

# Building Rustix

## Prerequisites

- Rust stable with `rustfmt`; the repository pins these in `rust-toolchain.toml`.
- The `x86_64-unknown-none` target. The toolchain file requests it automatically; if needed, install it with `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`.
- [`just`](https://just.systems/) to run the repository's named tasks.
- Python 3.8 or newer (standard library only), with `python` on `PATH`; `xorriso`; and QEMU with `qemu-system-x86_64` for image creation and boot smoke tests.

An ELF inspection tool such as `llvm-readelf` or `readelf` is useful when diagnosing linker output. The first image build downloads the pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary archive into `target/tools/` and verifies its published SHA-256 before extraction.

## Common commands

Run from the repository root:

```sh
just help
just fmt       # check Rust formatting
just test      # host-side unit tests for the library
just check     # type-check the freestanding kernel target
just build     # optimized kernel ELF
just image     # hybrid BIOS/UEFI ISO at target/rustix.iso
just smoke     # bounded QEMU boot and serial-banner assertion
just verify    # fmt, tests, target check, image, and QEMU smoke test
```

Equivalent Rust checks are `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --lib`, `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-none`, and `cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-none`. Image creation and QEMU validation are provided by `scripts/boot.py` and are intentionally part of `just verify`.

The optimized ELF is written to `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `cargo check` checks the target without producing a boot image. The library tests run on the host and exercise code that does not require privileged instructions.

## Target-specific linker setup

`.cargo/config.toml` applies the Rustix linker script and x86_64 kernel constraints only to `x86_64-unknown-none`. `linker.ld` emits an ELF64 x86_64 image at the higher-half base, retains Limine request sections, and defines `_start` as the entry symbol. The build uses no third-party Rust crates; the boot protocol is represented by small in-tree Rust structures and constants.

Changing the target, virtual base, relocation model, or request ABI requires updating the linker script, protocol documentation, and validation plan together. Do not use host builds of the kernel binary as evidence that the freestanding target links correctly.

## Building and smoke-testing a boot image

`limine.conf` boots the kernel immediately and enables 38,400-baud serial output. `just image` builds the ELF, fetches Limine v12.9.3's binary ZIP from its immutable GitHub release, checks the pinned SHA-256, prepares a BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO, and installs the BIOS boot code. The Limine archive and extracted tools remain under ignored `target/`; no third-party binaries are checked into the source tree.

`just smoke` launches `target/rustix.iso` in `qemu-system-x86_64` with a 256 MiB q35 machine, headless display, captured COM1 output, and a 20-second deadline. QEMU is expected to remain running because the bootstrap kernel halts; the runner terminates it at the deadline and requires both the startup and bootstrap-complete serial markers. On a failure it prints the serial log. The log remains at `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` for inspection.

`just verify` includes the emulator smoke test and therefore needs Python 3, xorriso, QEMU, network access for the first Limine download, and the Rust target. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs the system tools on Ubuntu 24.04 and runs the same command. This verifies the boot path in CI; it is still not a substitute for testing physical hardware.

## Troubleshooting

- **Target not installed:** install `x86_64-unknown-none` as shown above.
- **`just` not found:** install `just`; Rust-only checks can still be run with the Cargo commands above.
- **`xorriso` or QEMU not found:** install the host image/emulator tools listed in prerequisites, then retry `just image` or `just smoke`.
- **Limine SHA-256 mismatch:** the pinned archive may have changed or been corrupted; the script removes the mismatched download and refuses to use it. Check the official v12.9.3 release digest before changing the pin.
- **Linker-script error:** build only for `x86_64-unknown-none`; confirm the invocation runs from the repository root so `linker.ld` resolves.
- **No serial output:** inspect `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` and QEMU's stderr. The image config and Rustix COM1 driver both use 38,400 baud.

```

# Rustix roadmap

This roadmap is staged to keep each milestone reviewable and bootable. The project is currently at **Milestone 0: kernel bootstrap; image and smoke-test workflow implemented, first end-to-end pass pending**. Items below are planned unless checked off; checked implementation work is not the same as a passing end-to-end validation.

## Milestone 0 — Rust kernel bootstrap (current)

- [x] `no_std` Rust kernel binary for `x86_64-unknown-none`.
- [x] Own ELF linker layout and Limine boot-protocol requests.
- [x] COM1 serial diagnostics, memory-map/HHDM summary, and panic halt path.
- [x] Narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers and a non-blocking PS/2 raw-scancode polling driver.
- [x] `just` commands and architecture/development/security/driver documentation.
- [x] Hash-pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary distribution and checked extraction.
- [x] Reproducible BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO recipe and documented boot configuration.
- [x] Bounded QEMU serial smoke-test runner and CI workflow.
- [ ] Execute the end-to-end image build and QEMU smoke test successfully in CI or a local environment.

**Exit criteria:** a clean checkout builds the pinned image, boots it in the documented emulator, and captures the expected serial banner in automated validation. The workflow is implemented; the criterion remains pending until an end-to-end run passes.

## Milestone 1 — validated boot state and machine diagnostics

- Parse and validate all loader ranges into a stable boot-info value.
- Preserve reserved, reclaimable, firmware, and MMIO regions distinctly.
- Add serial formatting tests, CPU feature reporting, and a framebuffer or documented serial-only console.
- Establish explicit ownership and reclaim timing for loader memory.

**Exit criteria:** malformed maps fail closed; an emulator test validates reported regions and boot metadata.

## Milestone 2 — memory ownership and CPU exceptions

- Physical frame allocator with overflow-safe range handling and exhaustion tests.
- Kernel-owned page-table management and documented direct-map policy.
- Global heap with deterministic out-of-memory behavior.
- GDT/TSS and IDT setup; exception handlers with register/error-code diagnostics; fault-injection tests.

**Exit criteria:** allocator and mapping invariants are tested, page faults are diagnosable, and the kernel remains bootable under emulator tests.

## Milestone 3 — interrupts, time, and scheduling

- Timer and interrupt-controller setup with explicit interrupt-safe locking rules.
- Kernel threads and context switching; per-CPU data before SMP work.
- Preemptive scheduling only after interrupt, stack, and lock invariants are validated.
- Application processor startup as a separate milestone, not an implicit extension of single-core code.

**Exit criteria:** deterministic thread lifecycle tests and bounded timer/preemption integration tests.

## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI

- User-mode entry/exit and isolated address spaces.
- Versioned syscall ABI, validated copy-in/copy-out, and documented error semantics.
- Initial process lifecycle, descriptor table, and executable-loading path.
- Adversarial tests for invalid pointers, bad lengths, overflow, and process teardown.

**Exit criteria:** a controlled userspace init process can execute and use a small documented syscall subset without corrupting the kernel on invalid input.

## Milestone 5 — Unix-like services and storage

- VFS and mount model, file descriptors, and a first on-disk filesystem.
- Process creation/exec/wait semantics, pipes or IPC, and signal-like delivery as designed.
- Device discovery/driver model and networking only after ownership and isolation policies exist.
- Compatibility tests for any claimed Unix/POSIX behavior; keep unsupported operations explicit.

**Exit criteria:** documented userland tools can run from a reproducible image and integration tests cover process and file semantics.

## Working rule

Each milestone should add code, tests, and updated documentation together. Do not advance the stated project status merely because an interface or design note exists. Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable subsystem stubs.

````rustix/README.md
     1	# Rustix
     2	
     3	Rustix (Rust-unix) is an experimental, 64-bit, Unix-like operating system whose kernel is written in Rust. This repository builds the kernel itself; Limine is used only as the external boot protocol/loader, not as a substitute for a Rustix kernel.
     4	
     5	The project is at its **bootstrap milestone**. The current kernel is a freestanding `no_std` x86_64 ELF that accepts Limine protocol requests, initializes COM1 serial output, reports the bootloader's HHDM and memory-map summary, and then halts. It also includes a non-blocking polling driver for a legacy PS/2-compatible keyboard controller; keyboard input is not yet connected to a kernel input subsystem. Rustix does not yet provide a scheduler, processes, a syscall ABI, filesystems, networking, or a userland. See [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) for the staged plan.
     6	
     7	## Quick start
     8	
     9	Prerequisites: a Rust stable toolchain, `just`, Python 3, `xorriso`, QEMU (`qemu-system-x86_64`), and the target installed by `rust-toolchain.toml` (or `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`). The first image build downloads a pinned Limine binary release and verifies its SHA-256.
    10	
    11	```sh
    12	just help
    13	just fmt
    14	just test
    15	just check
    16	just build
    17	just image
    18	just smoke
    19	just verify
    20	```
    21	
    22	`just build` produces `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `just image` creates `target/rustix.iso`, a hybrid BIOS/UEFI image, and `just smoke` boots it under QEMU and checks for the kernel's serial banner. The full `just verify` task includes that bounded smoke test.
    23	
    24	See [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) for prerequisites, commands, linker assumptions, and emulator details; [`docs/architecture/overview.md`](docs/architecture/overview.md) for the design boundary; and [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) for the documentation map.
    25	
    26	## Project principles
    27	
    28	- The kernel and operating-system implementation are Rust-first and `no_std`; architecture-specific privileged operations are isolated under `src/arch/`.
    29	- The kernel is the product. A bootloader may initialize the machine and transfer control, but policy, memory management, scheduling, and Unix-like services belong to Rustix.
    30	- Keep unsafe code small, documented, and adjacent to its hardware/protocol boundary.
    31	- Build incrementally: every roadmap milestone should have build checks, tests where practical, and updated design documentation.
    32	- Unix-like behavior is an explicit compatibility goal, not a claim of POSIX compliance today.
    33	
    34	## Repository map
    35	
    36	- `src/main.rs` — freestanding kernel entry point and panic/idle path.
    37	- `src/boot.rs` — Limine requests and boot-memory-map reporting.
    38	- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — early COM1 polling driver.
    39	- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling.
    40	- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers.
    41	- `src/memory.rs` — architecture-independent boot-time memory accounting and host tests.
    42	- `.cargo/config.toml`, `linker.ld` — x86_64-none code generation and ELF layout.
    43	- `justfile` — formatting, tests, target checks, image creation, emulator smoke test, and aggregate verification.
    44	- `limine.conf` — pinned boot configuration for the Rustix kernel.
    45	- `scripts/boot.py` — checksum-verified Limine download, hybrid ISO assembly, and bounded QEMU validation.
    46	- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — runs `just verify` on pushes and pull requests.
    47	- `docs/` — architecture, drivers, development, security, and roadmap documentation.

     4

     6	
     7	- [x] `no_std` Rust kernel binary for `x86_64-unknown-none`.
     8	- [x] Own ELF linker layout and Limine boot-protocol requests.

    10	- [x] Narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers and a non-blocking PS/2 raw-scancode polling driver.

    16	
    17	**Exit criteria:** a clean checkout builds the pinned image, boots it in the documented emulator, and captures the expected serial banner in automated validation. The workflow is implemented; the criterion remains pending until an end-to-end run passes.
    18	
    19	## Milestone 1 — validated boot state and machine diagnostics
    20	
    21	- Parse and validate all loader ranges into a stable boot-info value.
    22	- Preserve reserved, reclaimable, firmware, and MMIO regions distinctly.
    23	- Add serial formatting tests, CPU feature reporting, and a framebuffer or documented serial-only console.
    24	- Establish explicit ownership and reclaim timing for loader memory.
    25	
    26	**Exit criteria:** malformed maps fail closed; an emulator test validates reported regions and boot metadata.
    27	
    28	## Milestone 2 — memory ownership and CPU exceptions
    29	
    30	- Physical frame allocator with overflow-safe range handling and exhaustion tests.
    31	- Kernel-owned page-table management and documented direct-map policy.
    32	- Global heap with deterministic out-of-memory behavior.
    33	- GDT/TSS and IDT setup; exception handlers with register/error-code diagnostics; fault-injection tests.
    34	
    35	**Exit criteria:** allocator and mapping invariants are tested, page faults are diagnosable, and the kernel remains bootable under emulator tests.
    36	
    37	## Milestone 3 — interrupts, time, and scheduling
    38	
    39	- Timer and interrupt-controller setup with explicit interrupt-safe locking rules.
    40	- Kernel threads and context switching; per-CPU data before SMP work.
    41	- Preemptive scheduling only after interrupt, stack, and lock invariants are validated.
    42	- Application processor startup as a separate milestone, not an implicit extension of single-core code.
    43	
    44	**Exit criteria:** deterministic thread lifecycle tests and bounded timer/preemption integration tests.
    45	
    46	## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI
    47	
    48	- User-mode entry/exit and isolated address spaces.
    49	- Versioned syscall ABI, validated copy-in/copy-out, and documented error semantics.
    50	- Initial process lifecycle, descriptor table, and executable-loading path.
    51	- Adversarial tests for invalid pointers, bad lengths, overflow, and process teardown.
    52	
    53	**Exit criteria:** a controlled userspace init process can execute and use a small documented syscall subset without corrupting the kernel on invalid input.
    54	
    55	## Milestone 5 — Unix-like services and storage
    56	
    57	- VFS and mount model, file descriptors, and a first on-disk filesystem.
    58	- Process creation/exec/wait semantics, pipes or IPC, and signal-like delivery as designed.
    59	- Device discovery/driver model and networking only after ownership and isolation policies exist.
    60	- Compatibility tests for any claimed Unix/POSIX behavior; keep unsupported operations explicit.
    61	
    62	**Exit criteria:** documented userland tools can run from a reproducible image and integration tests cover process and file semantics.
    63	
    64	## Working rule
    65	
    66	Each milestone should add code, tests, and updated documentation together. Do not advance the stated project status merely because an interface or design note exists. Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable subsystem stubs.

#![no_std]

//! Small, allocation-free command parsing for Rustix's Crabshell.
//!
//! This crate deliberately contains no terminal, filesystem, or kernel code.
//! The same command model can later be driven by a graphical terminal frontend
//! or a userspace process without coupling it to the current serial console.

/// The longest command line accepted by the bootstrap shell, excluding its NUL.
pub const MAX_LINE_LENGTH: usize = 256;

/// Parsed shell operations. The command borrows its path and text from the input
/// line, so parsing needs no allocator and the caller controls all I/O.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Command<'a> {
    Help,
    Clear,
    Pwd,
    Ls(Option<&'a str>),
    Cd(&'a str),
    Mkdir(&'a str),
    Touch(&'a str),
    Write { path: &'a str, contents: &'a str },
    Append { path: &'a str, contents: &'a str },
    Cat(&'a str),
    Rm(&'a str),
    Rmdir(&'a str),
}

/// Errors in command syntax. Unknown command names are reported separately so
/// the caller can echo the original name in its diagnostic.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ParseError {
    UnknownCommand,
    MissingArgument,
    MissingText,
    TooManyArguments,
    UnterminatedQuote,
}

/// Parse one command line. An empty or whitespace-only line returns `Ok(None)`.
///
/// `write` and `append` accept the remaining text verbatim; wrapping the whole
/// text in matching single or double quotes removes those outer quotes. Escape
/// sequences and quoted paths are intentionally not part of this first grammar.
pub fn parse(line: &str) -> Result<Option<Command<'_>>, ParseError> {
    let line = line.trim();
    if line.is_empty() {
        return Ok(None);
    }

    let (name, rest) = take_word(line).expect("non-empty command line has a first word");
    let command = match name {
        "help" => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Command::Help
        }
        "clear" => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Command::Clear
        }
        "pwd" => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Command::Pwd
        }
        "ls" => Command::Ls(optional_path(rest)?),
        "cd" => Command::Cd(one_path(rest)?),
        "mkdir" => Command::Mkdir(one_path(rest)?),
        "touch" => Command::Touch(one_path(rest)?),
        "write" => {
            let (path, contents) = path_and_text(rest)?;
            Command::Write { path, contents }
        }
        "append" => {
            let (path, contents) = path_and_text(rest)?;
            Command::Append { path, contents }
        }
        "cat" => Command::Cat(one_path(rest)?),
        "rm" => Command::Rm(one_path(rest)?),
        "rmdir" => Command::Rmdir(one_path(rest)?),
        _ => return Err(ParseError::UnknownCommand),
    };

    Ok(Some(command))
}

fn take_word(input: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str)> {
    let input = input.trim_start();
    if input.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let end = input.find(char::is_whitespace).unwrap_or(input.len());
    Some((&input[..end], input[end..].trim_start()))
}

fn no_arguments(rest: &str) -> Result<(), ParseError> {
    if rest.is_empty() {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(ParseError::TooManyArguments)
    }
}

fn optional_path(rest: &str) -> Result<Option<&str>, ParseError> {
    match take_word(rest) {
        None => Ok(None),
        Some((path, rest)) => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Ok(Some(path))
        }
    }
}

fn one_path(rest: &str) -> Result<&str, ParseError> {
    let (path, rest) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    no_arguments(rest)?;
    Ok(path)
}

fn path_and_text(rest: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), ParseError> {
    let (path, text) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    if text.is_empty() {
        return Err(ParseError::MissingText);
    }

    let first = text.as_bytes()[0];
    if first == b'\'' || first == b'"' {
        if text.len() < 2 || text.as_bytes()[text.len() - 1] != first {
            return Err(ParseError::UnterminatedQuote);
        }
        return Ok((path, &text[1..text.len() - 1]));
    }

    Ok((path, text))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{parse, Command, ParseError};

    #[test]
    fn blank_lines_are_ignored() {
        assert_eq!(parse(" \t "), Ok(None));
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_basic_navigation_and_file_commands() {
        assert_eq!(parse("pwd"), Ok(Some(Command::Pwd)));
        assert_eq!(parse("ls /home"), Ok(Some(Command::Ls(Some("/home")))));
        assert_eq!(parse("cd .."), Ok(Some(Command::Cd(".."))));
        assert_eq!(parse("mkdir /tmp/work"), Ok(Some(Command::Mkdir("/tmp/work"))));
        assert_eq!(parse("touch note.txt"), Ok(Some(Command::Touch("note.txt"))));
        assert_eq!(parse("cat note.txt"), Ok(Some(Command::Cat("note.txt"))));
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_preserves_spaces_and_strips_outer_quotes() {
        assert_eq!(
            parse("write greeting.txt hello from crabshell"),
            Ok(Some(Command::Write {
                path: "greeting.txt",
                contents: "hello from crabshell",
            }))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse("append greeting.txt \" again\""),
            Ok(Some(Command::Append {
                path: "greeting.txt",
                contents: " again",
            }))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse("write empty.txt \"\""),
            Ok(Some(Command::Write {
                path: "empty.txt",
                contents: "",
            }))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_command_arity_and_text() {
        assert_eq!(parse("cd"), Err(ParseError::MissingArgument));
        assert_eq!(parse("pwd now"), Err(ParseError::TooManyArguments));
        assert_eq!(parse("write file"), Err(ParseError::MissingText));
        assert_eq!(parse("write file \"unfinished"), Err(ParseError::UnterminatedQuote));
        assert_eq!(parse("not-a-command"), Err(ParseError::UnknownCommand));
    }
}

//! Fixed-capacity volatile filesystem for the early kernel shell.
//!
//! This is an in-memory namespace only: it has no disk driver, persistence,
//! permissions, timestamps, links, or concurrent access support.

#![allow(clippy::large_stack_arrays)]

/// Root directory node identifier.
pub const ROOT_NODE: usize = 0;
/// Maximum number of nodes, including the root directory.
pub const MAX_NODES: usize = 32;
/// Maximum UTF-8 bytes in one path component.
pub const NAME_CAPACITY: usize = 31;
/// Maximum bytes in one file.
pub const FILE_CAPACITY: usize = 1024;
/// Maximum byte length of an absolute path in this filesystem.
pub const MAX_PATH_CAPACITY: usize = MAX_NODES * (NAME_CAPACITY + 1) + 1;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EntryKind {
    Directory,
    File,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FsError {
    InvalidPath,
    InvalidName,
    NameTooLong,
    AlreadyExists,
    NotFound,
    NotDirectory,
    IsDirectory,
    DirectoryNotEmpty,
    NoSpace,
    FileTooLarge,
    RootOperation,
    BufferTooSmall,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Entry<'a> {
    pub name: &'a str,
    pub kind: EntryKind,
    pub size: usize,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Node {
    used: bool,
    kind: EntryKind,
    parent: usize,
    name: [u8; NAME_CAPACITY],
    name_len: u8,
    data: [u8; FILE_CAPACITY],
    data_len: usize,
}

impl Node {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        used: false,
        kind: EntryKind::File,
        parent: ROOT_NODE,
        name: [0; NAME_CAPACITY],
        name_len: 0,
        data: [0; FILE_CAPACITY],
        data_len: 0,
    };

    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        core::str::from_utf8(&self.name[..usize::from(self.name_len)]).unwrap_or("")
    }
}

/// A small fixed-capacity filesystem suitable for the pre-allocator shell.
pub struct RamFs {
    nodes: [Node; MAX_NODES],
}

impl RamFs {
    /// Construct a filesystem containing only its root directory.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        let mut nodes = [Node::EMPTY; MAX_NODES];
        nodes[ROOT_NODE] = Node {
            used: true,
            kind: EntryKind::Directory,
            parent: ROOT_NODE,
            name: [0; NAME_CAPACITY],
            name_len: 0,
            data: [0; FILE_CAPACITY],
            data_len: 0,
        };
        Self { nodes }
    }

    /// Create a starter Unix-like directory tree and return `/home/rustix`.
    pub fn seed_defaults(&mut self) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "bin")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "dev")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "etc")?;
        let home = self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "home")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "tmp")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "var")?;
        let user_home = self.create_dir(home, "rustix")?;
        let motd = self.create_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/etc/motd")?;
        self.write_file(motd, b"Welcome to Rustix. Files in this early shell are volatile RAM files.\n")?;
        Ok(user_home)
    }

    /// Resolve a path from a working directory. `/`, repeated separators, `.`
    /// and `..` are handled; every intermediate component must be a directory.
    pub fn resolve(&self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        if path.is_empty() {
            return Err(FsError::InvalidPath);
        }
        let mut current = if path.starts_with('/') { ROOT_NODE } else { cwd };
        let start = self.node(current)?;
        if start.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }

        for component in path.split('/') {
            match component {
                "" | "." => continue,
                ".." => current = self.node(current)?.parent,
                name => {
                    if self.node(current)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
                        return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
                    }
                    current = self
                        .find_child(current, name)
                        .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)?;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(current)
    }

    pub fn create_dir(&mut self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_node(parent, name, EntryKind::Directory)
    }

    pub fn create_file(&mut self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_node(parent, name, EntryKind::File)
    }

    pub fn create_dir_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(path)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        self.create_dir(parent, name)
    }

    pub fn create_file_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(path)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        self.create_file(parent, name)
    }

    /// Return an existing file node or create it if its path does not exist.
    pub fn open_or_create_file(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        match self.resolve(cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => {
                if self.node(node)?.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
                    Err(FsError::IsDirectory)
                } else {
                    Ok(node)
                }
            }
            Err(FsError::NotFound) => self.create_file_path(cwd, path),
            Err(error) => Err(error),
        }
    }

    pub fn kind(&self, node: usize) -> Result<EntryKind, FsError> {
        Ok(self.node(node)?.kind)
    }

    pub fn read_file(&self, node: usize) -> Result<&[u8], FsError> {
        let node = self.node(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        Ok(&node.data[..node.data_len])
    }

    pub fn write_file(&mut self, node: usize, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if contents.len() > FILE_CAPACITY {
            return Err(FsError::FileTooLarge);
        }
        let node = self.node_mut(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        node.data[..contents.len()].copy_from_slice(contents);
        node.data[contents.len()..].fill(0);
        node.data_len = contents.len();
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn append_file(&mut self, node: usize, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.node_mut(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        let new_len = node
            .data_len
            .checked_add(contents.len())
            .filter(|length| *length <= FILE_CAPACITY)
            .ok_or(FsError::FileTooLarge)?;
        node.data[node.data_len..new_len].copy_from_slice(contents);
        node.data_len = new_len;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_file(&mut self, node: usize) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if node == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        let entry = self.node(node)?;
        if entry.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        self.nodes[node] = Node::EMPTY;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_dir(&mut self, node: usize) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if node == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        let entry = self.node(node)?;
        if entry.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        if self.nodes.iter().any(|child| child.used && child.parent == node) {
            return Err(FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty);
        }
        self.nodes[node] = Node::EMPTY;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_file_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.resolve(cwd, path)?;
        self.remove_file(node)
    }

    pub fn remove_dir_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.resolve(cwd, path)?;
        self.remove_dir(node)
    }

    pub fn entry(&self, node: usize) -> Result<Entry<'_>, FsError> {
        let node = self.node(node)?;
        Ok(Entry {
            name: node.name(),
            kind: node.kind,
            size: node.data_len,
        })
    }

    pub fn child_count(&self, directory: usize) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        if self.node(directory)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        Ok(self
            .nodes
            .iter()
            .filter(|node| node.used && node.parent == directory && directory != ROOT_NODE || node.used && node.parent == directory && node.name_len != 0)
            .count())
    }

    pub fn child_at(&self, directory: usize, ordinal: usize) -> Option<Entry<'_>> {
        if self.node(directory).ok()?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return None;
        }
        self.nodes
            .iter()
            .filter(|node| node.used && node.parent == directory && !(directory == ROOT_NODE && node.name_len == 0))
            .nth(ordinal)
            .map(|node| Entry {
                name: node.name(),
                kind: node.kind,
                size: node.data_len,
            })
    }

    /// Write an absolute path into caller-provided storage and return its length.
    pub fn write_path(&self, node: usize, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.node(node)?;
        let mut ancestors = [ROOT_NODE; MAX_NODES];
        let mut depth = 0;
        let mut current = node;
        while current != ROOT_NODE {
            if depth == MAX_NODES {
                return Err(FsError::InvalidPath);
            }
            ancestors[depth] = current;
            depth += 1;
            current = self.node(current)?.parent;
        }

        let required = 1 + (0..depth).map(|index| self.nodes[ancestors[index]].name_len as usize).sum::<usize>() + depth.saturating_sub(1);
        if output.len() < required {
            return Err(FsError::BufferTooSmall);
        }

        output[0] = b'/';
        let mut length = 1;
        for index in (0..depth).rev() {
            if length > 1 {
                output[length] = b'/';
                length += 1;
            }
            let name = self.nodes[ancestors[index]].name();
            output[length..length + name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
            length += name.len();
        }
        Ok(length)
    }

    fn create_node(
        &mut self,
        parent: usize,
        name: &str,
        kind: EntryKind,
    ) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let parent_node = self.node(parent)?;
        if parent_node.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        validate_name(name)?;
        if self.find_child(parent, name).is_some() {
            return Err(FsError::AlreadyExists);
        }
        let index = self
            .nodes
            .iter()
            .position(|node| !node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NoSpace)?;
        let mut node = Node::EMPTY;
        node.used = true;
        node.kind = kind;
        node.parent = parent;
        node.name[..name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        node.name_len = name.len() as u8;
        self.nodes[index] = node;
        Ok(index)
    }

    fn find_child(&self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        self.nodes.iter().position(|node| {
            node.used && node.parent == parent && node.name_len != 0 && node.name() == name
        })
    }

    fn node(&self, index: usize) -> Result<&Node, FsError> {
        self.nodes
            .get(index)
            .filter(|node| node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)
    }

    fn node_mut(&mut self, index: usize) -> Result<&mut Node, FsError> {
        self.nodes
            .get_mut(index)
            .filter(|node| node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)
    }
}

impl Default for RamFs {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

fn validate_name(name: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
    if name.is_empty() || name == "." || name == ".." || name.contains('/') || name.contains('\0') {
        return Err(FsError::InvalidName);
    }
    if name.len() > NAME_CAPACITY {
        return Err(FsError::NameTooLong);
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn split_parent(path: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), FsError> {
    let path = path.trim_end_matches('/');
    if path.is_empty() {
        return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
    }
    match path.rsplit_once('/') {
        Some(("", name)) => Ok(("/", name)),
        Some((parent, name)) if !name.is_empty() => Ok((parent, name)),
        Some(_) => Err(FsError::InvalidPath),
        None => Ok((".", path)),
    }
}

//! Fixed-capacity volatile filesystem for the early kernel shell.
//!
//! This is an in-memory namespace only: it has no disk driver, persistence,
//! permissions, timestamps, links, or concurrent access support.

#![allow(clippy::large_stack_arrays)]

/// Root directory node identifier.
pub const ROOT_NODE: usize = 0;
/// Maximum number of nodes, including the root directory.
pub const MAX_NODES: usize = 32;
/// Maximum UTF-8 bytes in one path component.
pub const NAME_CAPACITY: usize = 31;
/// Maximum bytes in one file.
pub const FILE_CAPACITY: usize = 1024;
/// Maximum byte length of an absolute path in this filesystem.
pub const MAX_PATH_CAPACITY: usize = MAX_NODES * (NAME_CAPACITY + 1) + 1;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EntryKind {
    Directory,
    File,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FsError {
    InvalidPath,
    InvalidName,
    NameTooLong,
    AlreadyExists,
    NotFound,
    NotDirectory,
    IsDirectory,
    DirectoryNotEmpty,
    NoSpace,
    FileTooLarge,
    RootOperation,
    BufferTooSmall,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Entry<'a> {
    pub name: &'a str,
    pub kind: EntryKind,
    pub size: usize,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Node {
    used: bool,
    kind: EntryKind,
    parent: usize,
    name: [u8; NAME_CAPACITY],
    name_len: u8,
    data: [u8; FILE_CAPACITY],
    data_len: usize,
}

impl Node {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        used: false,
        kind: EntryKind::File,
        parent: ROOT_NODE,
        name: [0; NAME_CAPACITY],
        name_len: 0,
        data: [0; FILE_CAPACITY],
        data_len: 0,
    };

    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        core::str::from_utf8(&self.name[..usize::from(self.name_len)]).unwrap_or("")
    }
}

/// A small fixed-capacity filesystem suitable for the pre-allocator shell.
pub struct RamFs {
    nodes: [Node; MAX_NODES],
}

impl RamFs {
    /// Construct a filesystem containing only its root directory.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        let mut nodes = [Node::EMPTY; MAX_NODES];
        nodes[ROOT_NODE] = Node {
            used: true,
            kind: EntryKind::Directory,
            parent: ROOT_NODE,
            name: [0; NAME_CAPACITY],
            name_len: 0,
            data: [0; FILE_CAPACITY],
            data_len: 0,
        };
        Self { nodes }
    }

    /// Create a starter Unix-like directory tree and return `/home/rustix`.
    pub fn seed_defaults(&mut self) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "bin")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "dev")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "etc")?;
        let home = self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "home")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "tmp")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "var")?;
        let user_home = self.create_dir(home, "rustix")?;
        let motd = self.create_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/etc/motd")?;
        self.write_file(motd, b"Welcome to Rustix. Files in this early shell are volatile RAM files.\n")?;
        Ok(user_home)

    /// Resolve a path from a working directory. `/`, repeated separators, `.`
    /// and `..` are handled; every intermediate component must be a directory.
    pub fn resolve(&self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        if path.is_empty() {
            return Err(FsError::InvalidPath);
        }
        let mut current = if path.starts_with('/') { ROOT_NODE } else { cwd };
        let start = self.node(current)?;
        if start.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }

        for component in path.split('/') {
            match component {
                "" | "." => continue,
                ".." => current = self.node(current)?.parent,
                name => {
                    if self.node(current)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
                        return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
                    }
                    current = self
                        .find_child(current, name)
                        .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)?;
                }
            }
        }

    }

        self.create_node(parent, name, EntryKind::Directory)

        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(path)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        self.create_dir(parent, name)
    }

        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        self.create_file(parent, name)
    }

    pub fn open_or_create_file(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        match self.resolve(cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => {
                if self.node(node)?.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
                    Err(FsError::IsDirectory)

        let node = self.node(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {

        }

    pub fn write_file(&mut self, node: usize, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), FsError> {

            return Err(FsError::FileTooLarge);

            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);

    pub fn append_file(&mut self, node: usize, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), FsError> {

            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);

#![no_std]

//! Small, allocation-free command parsing for Rustix's Crabshell.
//!
//! This crate deliberately contains no terminal, filesystem, or kernel code.
//! The same command model can later be driven by a graphical terminal frontend
//! or a userspace process without coupling it to the current serial console.

/// The longest command line accepted by the bootstrap shell, excluding its NUL.
pub const MAX_LINE_LENGTH: usize = 256;

/// Parsed shell operations. The command borrows its path and text from the input
/// line, so parsing needs no allocator and the caller controls all I/O.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Command<'a> {
    Help,
    Clear,
    Pwd,
    Ls(Option<&'a str>),
    Cd(&'a str),
    Mkdir(&'a str),
    Touch(&'a str),
    Write { path: &'a str, contents: &'a str },
    Append { path: &'a str, contents: &'a str },
    Cat(&'a str),
    Rm(&'a str),
    Rmdir(&'a str),
}

/// Errors in command syntax. Unknown command names are reported separately so
/// the caller can echo the original name in its diagnostic.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ParseError {
    UnknownCommand,
    MissingArgument,
    MissingText,
    TooManyArguments,
    UnterminatedQuote,
}

/// Parse one command line. An empty or whitespace-only line returns `Ok(None)`.
///
/// `write` and `append` accept the remaining text verbatim; wrapping the whole
/// text in matching single or double quotes removes those outer quotes. Escape
/// sequences and quoted paths are intentionally not part of this first grammar.
pub fn parse(line: &str) -> Result<Option<Command<'_>>, ParseError> {
    let line = line.trim();
    if line.is_empty() {
        return Ok(None);
    }

    let (name, rest) = take_word(line).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    let command = match name {
        "help" => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Command::Help
        }
        "clear" => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Command::Clear
        }
        "pwd" => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Command::Pwd
        }
        "ls" => Command::Ls(optional_path(rest)?),
        "cd" => Command::Cd(one_path(rest)?),
        "mkdir" => Command::Mkdir(one_path(rest)?),
        "touch" => Command::Touch(one_path(rest)?),
        "write" => {
            let (path, contents) = path_and_text(rest)?;
            Command::Write { path, contents }
        }
        "append" => {
            let (path, contents) = path_and_text(rest)?;
            Command::Append { path, contents }
        }
        "cat" => Command::Cat(one_path(rest)?),
        "rm" => Command::Rm(one_path(rest)?),
        "rmdir" => Command::Rmdir(one_path(rest)?),
        _ => return Err(ParseError::UnknownCommand),
    };

    Ok(Some(command))
}

fn take_word(input: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str)> {
    let input = input.trim_start();
    if input.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let end = input.find(char::is_whitespace).unwrap_or(input.len());
    Some((&input[..end], input[end..].trim_start()))
}

fn no_arguments(rest: &str) -> Result<(), ParseError> {
    if rest.is_empty() {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(ParseError::TooManyArguments)
    }
}

fn optional_path(rest: &str) -> Result<Option<&str>, ParseError> {
    match take_word(rest) {
        None => Ok(None),
        Some((path, rest)) => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Ok(Some(path))
        }
    }
}

fn one_path(rest: &str) -> Result<&str, ParseError> {
    let (path, rest) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    no_arguments(rest)?;
    Ok(path)
}

fn path_and_text(rest: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), ParseError> {
    let (path, text) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    if text.is_empty() {
        return Err(ParseError::MissingText);
    }

    let first = text.as_bytes()[0];
    if first == b'\'' || first == b'"' {
        if text.len() < 2 || text.as_bytes()[text.len() - 1] != first {
            return Err(ParseError::UnterminatedQuote);
        }
        return Ok((path, &text[1..text.len() - 1]));
    }

    Ok((path, text))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{parse, Command, ParseError};

    #[test]
    fn blank_lines_are_ignored() {
        assert_eq!(parse(" \t "), Ok(None));
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_basic_navigation_and_file_commands() {
        assert_eq!(parse("pwd"), Ok(Some(Command::Pwd)));
        assert_eq!(parse("ls /home"), Ok(Some(Command::Ls(Some("/home")))));
        assert_eq!(parse("cd .."), Ok(Some(Command::Cd(".."))));
        assert_eq!(parse("mkdir /tmp/work"), Ok(Some(Command::Mkdir("/tmp/work"))));
        assert_eq!(parse("touch note.txt"), Ok(Some(Command::Touch("note.txt"))));
        assert_eq!(parse("cat note.txt"), Ok(Some(Command::Cat("note.txt"))));
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_preserves_spaces_and_strips_outer_quotes() {
        assert_eq!(
            parse("write greeting.txt hello from crabshell"),
            Ok(Some(Command::Write {
                path: "greeting.txt",
                contents: "hello from crabshell",
            }))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse("append greeting.txt \" again\""),
            Ok(Some(Command::Append {
                path: "greeting.txt",
                contents: " again",
            }))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse("write empty.txt \"\""),
            Ok(Some(Command::Write {
                path: "empty.txt",
                contents: "",
            }))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_command_arity_and_text() {
        assert_eq!(parse("cd"), Err(ParseError::MissingArgument));
        assert_eq!(parse("pwd now"), Err(ParseError::TooManyArguments));
        assert_eq!(parse("write file"), Err(ParseError::MissingText));
        assert_eq!(parse("write file \"unfinished"), Err(ParseError::UnterminatedQuote));
        assert_eq!(parse("not-a-command"), Err(ParseError::UnknownCommand));
    }
}

//! Minimal polling 16550-compatible serial output for early x86_64 diagnostics.

use core::fmt;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

const COM1: u16 = 0x3f8;
static INITIALIZED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

/// Configure COM1 for 38,400 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, one stop bit.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: These are the conventional legacy COM1 I/O ports on x86 PCs.
    unsafe {
        super::io::write_u8(COM1 + 1, 0x00);
        super::io::write_u8(COM1 + 3, 0x80);
        super::io::write_u8(COM1, 0x03);
        super::io::write_u8(COM1 + 1, 0x00);
        super::io::write_u8(COM1 + 3, 0x03);
        super::io::write_u8(COM1 + 2, 0xc7);
        super::io::write_u8(COM1 + 4, 0x0b);
    }
    INITIALIZED.store(true, Ordering::Release);
}

/// Write formatted text to COM1. Output is silently skipped until initialized.
pub fn print(arguments: fmt::Arguments<'_>) {
    if INITIALIZED.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
        let _ = SerialPort.write_fmt(arguments);
    }
}

/// Return a received COM1 byte if one is ready, without waiting for input.
pub fn try_read_byte() -> Option<u8> {
    if !INITIALIZED.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
        return None;
    }

    // SAFETY: COM1 is configured by `initialize`; the line-status register and
    // receive register are accessed only by the single-core polling shell.
    unsafe {
        if super::io::read_u8(COM1 + 5) & 0x01 != 0 {
            Some(super::io::read_u8(COM1))
        } else {
            None
        }
    }
}

struct SerialPort;

impl fmt::Write for SerialPort {
    fn write_str(&mut self, text: &str) -> fmt::Result {
        for byte in text.bytes() {
            // SAFETY: COM1 is initialized by `initialize`; accesses are serialized
            // by the single-core bootstrap path before the kernel starts scheduling.
            unsafe { write_byte(byte) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

unsafe fn write_byte(byte: u8) {
    // Bound the wait so a missing or misconfigured UART cannot deadlock boot.
    for _ in 0..100_000 {
        // SAFETY: The caller ensures this is a legacy x86 port-I/O operation.
        if unsafe { super::io::read_u8(COM1 + 5) } & 0x20 != 0 {
            // SAFETY: The UART transmit register is COM1's base port.
            unsafe { super::io::write_u8(COM1, byte) };
            return;
        }
        core::hint::spin_loop();
    }
}

//! Kernel-side Crabshell frontend: serial input, prompts, and RAM-filesystem commands.

use crabshell::{parse, Command, ParseError, MAX_LINE_LENGTH};
use rustix_kernel::vfs::{EntryKind, FsError, RamFs, MAX_PATH_CAPACITY};

use crate::arch::x86_64::serial;

/// Run Crabshell forever on the bootstrap CPU.
pub fn run(filesystem: &mut RamFs, mut cwd: usize) -> ! {
    crate::kprintln!("crabshell: ready (volatile RAM filesystem)");
    print_motd(filesystem, cwd);

    let mut input = [0u8; MAX_LINE_LENGTH];
    loop {
        print_prompt(filesystem, cwd);
        let length = read_line(&mut input);
        if length == 0 {
            continue;
        }

        let line = match core::str::from_utf8(&input[..length]) {
            Ok(line) => line,
            Err(_) => {
                crate::kprintln!("crabshell: input must be valid UTF-8");
                continue;
            }
        };

        match parse(line) {
            Ok(Some(command)) => execute(command, filesystem, &mut cwd),
            Ok(None) => {}
            Err(error) => print_parse_error(error),
        }
    }
}

fn print_prompt(filesystem: &RamFs, cwd: usize) {
    let mut path = [0u8; MAX_PATH_CAPACITY];
    match filesystem.write_path(cwd, &mut path) {
        Ok(length) => match core::str::from_utf8(&path[..length]) {
            Ok(path) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:{}# ", path)),
            Err(_) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:/?# ")),
        },
        Err(_) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:/?# ")),
    }
}

fn read_line(input: &mut [u8; MAX_LINE_LENGTH]) -> usize {
    let mut length = 0;
    loop {
        let Some(byte) = serial::try_read_byte() else {
            core::hint::spin_loop();
            continue;
        };

        match byte {
            b'\r' | b'\n' => {
                crate::kprintln!();
                return length;
            }
            0x03 => {
                crate::kprintln!("^C");
                return 0;
            }
            0x08 | 0x7f if length > 0 => {
                length -= 1;
                serial::print(format_args!("\x08 \x08"));
            }
            0x20..=0x7e if length < input.len() => {
                input[length] = byte;
                length += 1;
                serial::print(format_args!("{}", byte as char));
            }
            0x20..=0x7e => serial::print(format_args!("\x07")),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

fn execute(command: Command<'_>, filesystem: &mut RamFs, cwd: &mut usize) {
    match command {
        Command::Help => print_help(),
        Command::Clear => serial::print(format_args!("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")),
        Command::Pwd => {
            let mut path = [0u8; MAX_PATH_CAPACITY];
            match filesystem.write_path(*cwd, &mut path) {
                Ok(length) => match core::str::from_utf8(&path[..length]) {
                    Ok(path) => crate::kprintln!("{}", path),
                    Err(_) => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: could not display current path"),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            }
        }
        Command::Ls(path) => {
            let directory = match path {
                Some(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
                    Ok(node) => node,
                    Err(error) => {
                        report_fs_error(error);
                        return;
                    }
                },
                None => *cwd,
            };
            list_directory(filesystem, directory);
        }
        Command::Cd(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.kind(node) {
                Ok(EntryKind::Directory) => *cwd = node,
                Ok(EntryKind::File) => report_fs_error(FsError::NotDirectory),
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Mkdir(path) => match filesystem.create_dir_path(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Touch(path) => match filesystem.open_or_create_file(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Write { path, contents } => {
            match filesystem.open_or_create_file(*cwd, path) {
                Ok(node) => match filesystem.write_file(node, contents.as_bytes()) {
                    Ok(()) => {}
                    Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            }
        }
        Command::Append { path, contents } => {
            match filesystem.open_or_create_file(*cwd, path) {
                Ok(node) => match filesystem.append_file(node, contents.as_bytes()) {
                    Ok(()) => {}
                    Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            }
        }
        Command::Cat(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.read_file(node) {
                Ok(bytes) => match core::str::from_utf8(bytes) {
                    Ok(text) => print_file_contents(text),
                    Err(_) => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: binary file display is not supported"),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Rm(path) => match filesystem.remove_file_path(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Rmdir(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) if node == *cwd => {
                crate::kprintln!("crabshell: cannot remove the current directory");
            }
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.remove_dir(node) {
                Ok(()) => {}
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
    }
}

fn list_directory(filesystem: &RamFs, directory: usize) {
    match filesystem.kind(directory) {
        Ok(EntryKind::File) => match filesystem.entry(directory) {
            Ok(entry) => crate::kprintln!("{} ({} bytes)", entry.name, entry.size),
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        Ok(EntryKind::Directory) => match filesystem.child_count(directory) {
            Ok(0) => crate::kprintln!("(empty)"),
            Ok(count) => {
                for index in 0..count {
                    let Some(entry) = filesystem.child_at(directory, index) else {
                        crate::kprintln!("crabshell: directory changed while listing");
                        return;
                    };
                    match entry.kind {
                        EntryKind::Directory => crate::kprintln!("{}/", entry.name),
                        EntryKind::File => {
                            crate::kprintln!("{}  {} bytes", entry.name, entry.size)
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
    }
}

fn print_file_contents(text: &str) {
    for (index, line) in text.split('\n').enumerate() {
        if index != 0 {
            serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
        }
        serial::print(format_args!("{}", line.strip_suffix('\r').unwrap_or(line)));
    }
    if !text.ends_with('\n') {
        crate::kprintln!();
    }
}

fn print_motd(filesystem: &RamFs, cwd: usize) {
    if let Ok(node) = filesystem.resolve(cwd, "/etc/motd") {
        if let Ok(bytes) = filesystem.read_file(node) {
            if let Ok(text) = core::str::from_utf8(bytes) {
                print_file_contents(text);
            }
        }
    }
}

fn print_help() {
    crate::kprintln!("Crabshell commands:");
    crate::kprintln!("  help                 show this help");
    crate::kprintln!("  clear                clear an ANSI-compatible terminal");
    crate::kprintln!("  pwd                  print the current directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  ls [PATH]            list a directory or file");
    crate::kprintln!("  cd PATH              change the current directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  mkdir PATH            create a directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  touch PATH            create an empty file");
    crate::kprintln!("  write PATH TEXT       replace a file's contents");
    crate::kprintln!("  append PATH TEXT      append text to a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  cat PATH              print a text file");
    crate::kprintln!("  rm PATH               remove a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  rmdir PATH            remove an empty directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  write/append accept a quoted or unquoted text remainder.");
    crate::kprintln!("  This filesystem is volatile and limited to 32 entries.");
}

fn print_parse_error(error: ParseError) {
    match error {
        ParseError::UnknownCommand => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: unknown command (try 'help')"),
        ParseError::MissingArgument => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: missing path argument"),
        ParseError::MissingText => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: missing text (usage: write PATH TEXT)"),
        ParseError::TooManyArguments => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: too many arguments"),
        ParseError::UnterminatedQuote => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: unterminated text quote"),
    }
}

fn report_fs_error(error: FsError) {
    let message = match error {
        FsError::InvalidPath => "invalid path",
        FsError::InvalidName => "invalid file name",
        FsError::NameTooLong => "file name is too long (maximum 31 UTF-8 bytes)",
        FsError::AlreadyExists => "an entry with that name already exists",
        FsError::NotFound => "path not found",
        FsError::NotDirectory => "a path component is not a directory",
        FsError::IsDirectory => "operation requires a file, not a directory",
        FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty => "directory is not empty",
        FsError::NoSpace => "RAM filesystem is full",
        FsError::FileTooLarge => "file exceeds the 1024-byte limit",
        FsError::RootOperation => "operation is not permitted on the root directory",
        FsError::BufferTooSmall => "path exceeds the display buffer",
    };
    crate::kprintln!("crabshell: {}", message);
}

#![no_std]
#![no_main]

mod arch;
mod boot;
mod shell;

use core::panic::PanicInfo;
use rustix_kernel::vfs::RamFs;

static mut RAM_FILESYSTEM: RamFs = RamFs::new();

macro_rules! kprintln {
    () => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
    ($($argument:tt)*) => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!($($argument)*));
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
}

pub(crate) use kprintln;

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn _start() -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    boot::report_boot_information();

    // SAFETY: Crabshell is the only owner of this filesystem. The bootstrap is
    // single-core and has no scheduler or filesystem-touching interrupt handlers.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
        Ok(home) => shell::run(filesystem, home),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever()
        }
    }
}

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}
