```
//! Fixed-capacity volatile filesystem for the early kernel shell.
//!
//! This is an in-memory namespace only: it has no disk driver, persistence,
//! permissions, timestamps, links, or concurrent access support.

#![allow(clippy::large_stack_arrays)]

/// Root directory node identifier.
pub const ROOT_NODE: usize = 0;
/// Maximum number of nodes, including the root directory.
pub const MAX_NODES: usize = 32;
/// Maximum UTF-8 bytes in one path component.
pub const NAME_CAPACITY: usize = 31;
/// Maximum bytes in one file.
pub const FILE_CAPACITY: usize = 1024;
/// Maximum byte length of an absolute path in this filesystem.
pub const MAX_PATH_CAPACITY: usize = MAX_NODES * (NAME_CAPACITY + 1) + 1;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EntryKind {
    Directory,
    File,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FsError {
    InvalidPath,
    InvalidName,
    NameTooLong,
    AlreadyExists,
    NotFound,
    NotDirectory,
    IsDirectory,
    DirectoryNotEmpty,
    NoSpace,
    FileTooLarge,
    RootOperation,
    BufferTooSmall,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Entry<'a> {
    pub name: &'a str,
    pub kind: EntryKind,
    pub size: usize,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Node {
    used: bool,
    kind: EntryKind,
    parent: usize,
    name: [u8; NAME_CAPACITY],
    name_len: u8,
    data: [u8; FILE_CAPACITY],
    data_len: usize,
}

impl Node {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        used: false,
        kind: EntryKind::File,
        parent: ROOT_NODE,
        name: [0; NAME_CAPACITY],
        name_len: 0,
        data: [0; FILE_CAPACITY],
        data_len: 0,
    };

    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        core::str::from_utf8(&self.name[..usize::from(self.name_len)]).unwrap_or("")
    }
}

/// A small fixed-capacity filesystem suitable for the pre-allocator shell.
pub struct RamFs {
    nodes: [Node; MAX_NODES],
}

impl RamFs {
    /// Construct a filesystem containing only its root directory.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        let mut nodes = [Node::EMPTY; MAX_NODES];
        nodes[ROOT_NODE] = Node {
            used: true,
            kind: EntryKind::Directory,
            parent: ROOT_NODE,
            name: [0; NAME_CAPACITY],
            name_len: 0,
            data: [0; FILE_CAPACITY],
            data_len: 0,
        };
        Self { nodes }
    }

    /// Create a starter Unix-like directory tree and return `/home/rustix`.
    pub fn seed_defaults(&mut self) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "bin")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "dev")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "etc")?;
        let home = self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "home")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "tmp")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "var")?;
        let user_home = self.create_dir(home, "rustix")?;
        let motd = self.create_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/etc/motd")?;
        self.write_file(motd, b"Welcome to Rustix. Files in this early shell are volatile RAM files.\n")?;
        Ok(user_home)
    }

    /// Resolve a path from a working directory. `/`, repeated separators, `.`
    /// and `..` are handled; every intermediate component must be a directory.
    pub fn resolve(&self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        if path.is_empty() {
            return Err(FsError::InvalidPath);
        }
        let mut current = if path.starts_with('/') { ROOT_NODE } else { cwd };
        let start = self.node(current)?;
        if start.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }

        for component in path.split('/') {
            if component.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            if self.node(current)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
                return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
            }
            match component {
                "." => {}
                ".." => current = self.node(current)?.parent,
                name => {
                    current = self
                        .find_child(current, name)
                        .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)?;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(current)
    }

    pub fn create_dir(&mut self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_node(parent, name, EntryKind::Directory)
    }

    pub fn create_file(&mut self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_node(parent, name, EntryKind::File)
    }

    pub fn create_dir_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(path)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        self.create_dir(parent, name)
    }

    pub fn create_file_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(path)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        self.create_file(parent, name)
    }

    /// Return an existing file node or create it if its path does not exist.
    pub fn open_or_create_file(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        match self.resolve(cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => {
                if self.node(node)?.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
                    Err(FsError::IsDirectory)
                } else {
                    Ok(node)
                }
            }
            Err(FsError::NotFound) => self.create_file_path(cwd, path),
            Err(error) => Err(error),
        }
    }

    pub fn kind(&self, node: usize) -> Result<EntryKind, FsError> {
        Ok(self.node(node)?.kind)
    }

    pub fn read_file(&self, node: usize) -> Result<&[u8], FsError> {
        let node = self.node(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        Ok(&node.data[..node.data_len])
    }

    pub fn write_file(&mut self, node: usize, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if contents.len() > FILE_CAPACITY {
            return Err(FsError::FileTooLarge);
        }
        let node = self.node_mut(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        node.data[..contents.len()].copy_from_slice(contents);
        node.data[contents.len()..].fill(0);
        node.data_len = contents.len();
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn append_file(&mut self, node: usize, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.node_mut(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        let new_len = node
            .data_len
            .checked_add(contents.len())
            .filter(|length| *length <= FILE_CAPACITY)
            .ok_or(FsError::FileTooLarge)?;
        node.data[node.data_len..new_len].copy_from_slice(contents);
        node.data_len = new_len;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_file(&mut self, node: usize) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if node == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        let entry = self.node(node)?;
        if entry.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        self.nodes[node] = Node::EMPTY;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_dir(&mut self, node: usize) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if node == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        let entry = self.node(node)?;
        if entry.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        if self.nodes.iter().any(|child| child.used && child.parent == node) {
            return Err(FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty);
        }
        self.nodes[node] = Node::EMPTY;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_file_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.resolve(cwd, path)?;
        self.remove_file(node)
    }

    pub fn remove_dir_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.resolve(cwd, path)?;
        self.remove_dir(node)
    }

    pub fn entry(&self, node: usize) -> Result<Entry<'_>, FsError> {
        let node = self.node(node)?;
        Ok(Entry {
            name: node.name(),
            kind: node.kind,
            size: node.data_len,
        })
    }

    pub fn child_count(&self, directory: usize) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        if self.node(directory)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        Ok(self
            .nodes
            .iter()
            .filter(|node| {
                            node.used
                                && node.parent == directory
                                && !(directory == ROOT_NODE && node.name_len == 0)
                        })
            .count())
    }

    pub fn child_at(&self, directory: usize, ordinal: usize) -> Option<Entry<'_>> {
        if self.node(directory).ok()?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return None;
        }
        self.nodes
            .iter()
            .filter(|node| node.used && node.parent == directory && !(directory == ROOT_NODE && node.name_len == 0))
            .nth(ordinal)
            .map(|node| Entry {
                name: node.name(),
                kind: node.kind,
                size: node.data_len,
            })
    }

    /// Write an absolute path into caller-provided storage and return its length.
    pub fn write_path(&self, node: usize, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.node(node)?;
        let mut ancestors = [ROOT_NODE; MAX_NODES];
        let mut depth = 0;
        let mut current = node;
        while current != ROOT_NODE {
            if depth == MAX_NODES {
                return Err(FsError::InvalidPath);
            }
            ancestors[depth] = current;
            depth += 1;
            current = self.node(current)?.parent;
        }

        let required = 1 + (0..depth).map(|index| self.nodes[ancestors[index]].name_len as usize).sum::<usize>() + depth.saturating_sub(1);
        if output.len() < required {
            return Err(FsError::BufferTooSmall);
        }

        output[0] = b'/';
        let mut length = 1;
        for index in (0..depth).rev() {
            if length > 1 {
                output[length] = b'/';
                length += 1;
            }
            let name = self.nodes[ancestors[index]].name();
            output[length..length + name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
            length += name.len();
        }
        Ok(length)
    }

    fn create_node(
        &mut self,
        parent: usize,
        name: &str,
        kind: EntryKind,
    ) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let parent_node = self.node(parent)?;
        if parent_node.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        validate_name(name)?;
        if self.find_child(parent, name).is_some() {
            return Err(FsError::AlreadyExists);
        }
        let index = self
            .nodes
            .iter()
            .position(|node| !node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NoSpace)?;
        let mut node = Node::EMPTY;
        node.used = true;
        node.kind = kind;
        node.parent = parent;
        node.name[..name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        node.name_len = name.len() as u8;
        self.nodes[index] = node;
        Ok(index)
    }

    fn find_child(&self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        self.nodes.iter().position(|node| {
            node.used && node.parent == parent && node.name_len != 0 && node.name() == name
        })
    }

    fn node(&self, index: usize) -> Result<&Node, FsError> {
        self.nodes
            .get(index)
            .filter(|node| node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)
    }

    fn node_mut(&mut self, index: usize) -> Result<&mut Node, FsError> {
        self.nodes
            .get_mut(index)
            .filter(|node| node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)
    }
}

impl Default for RamFs {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

fn validate_name(name: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
    if name.is_empty() || name == "." || name == ".." || name.contains('/') || name.contains('\0') {
        return Err(FsError::InvalidName);
    }
    if name.len() > NAME_CAPACITY {
        return Err(FsError::NameTooLong);
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn split_parent(path: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), FsError> {
    let path = path.trim_end_matches('/');
    if path.is_empty() {
        return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
    }
    match path.rsplit_once('/') {
        Some(("", name)) => Ok(("/", name)),
        Some((parent, name)) if !name.is_empty() => Ok((parent, name)),
        Some(_) => Err(FsError::InvalidPath),
        None => Ok((".", path)),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{EntryKind, FsError, RamFs, ROOT_NODE};

    #[test]
    fn resolves_absolute_relative_and_parent_components() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let home = fs.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "home").unwrap();
        let user = fs.create_dir(home, "rustix").unwrap();
        let notes = fs.create_dir(user, "notes").unwrap();

        assert_eq!(fs.resolve(user, ".").unwrap(), user);
        assert_eq!(fs.resolve(notes, "../..").unwrap(), home);
        assert_eq!(fs.resolve(ROOT_NODE, "/home/rustix/notes/").unwrap(), notes);
    }

    #[test]
    fn creates_reads_appends_and_removes_files() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let file = fs.create_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/note.txt").unwrap();
        fs.write_file(file, b"hello").unwrap();
        fs.append_file(file, b" rustix").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs.read_file(file).unwrap(), b"hello rustix");
        fs.remove_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/note.txt").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs.resolve(ROOT_NODE, "/note.txt"), Err(FsError::NotFound));
    }

    #[test]
    fn refuses_to_remove_nonempty_directories() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let directory = fs.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "work").unwrap();
        fs.create_file(directory, "note").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs.remove_dir(directory), Err(FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty));
    }

    #[test]
    fn path_output_and_kinds_are_consistent() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let docs = fs.create_dir_path(ROOT_NODE, "/home").unwrap();
        let file = fs.create_file(docs, "readme").unwrap();
        let mut path = [0; 64];
        let length = fs.write_path(file, &mut path).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(&path[..length], b"/home/readme");
        assert_eq!(fs.kind(docs), Ok(EntryKind::Directory));
        assert_eq!(fs.kind(file), Ok(EntryKind::File));
    }
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a pinned Limine hybrid ISO and smoke-test it in QEMU.

Only Python's standard library is required. The Limine binary archive is kept
under target/ and checked against the SHA-256 published for the pinned release.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.request
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TARGET_DIR = ROOT / "target"
LIMINE_VERSION = "12.9.3"
LIMINE_ARCHIVE_NAME = "limine-binary.zip"
LIMINE_ARCHIVE_SHA256 = "1bdbbcda650c5dba9b1eca5833d598137bf11bd6289bc89b6bcc4f8f112fa676"
LIMINE_ARCHIVE_URL = (
    "https://github.com/Limine-Bootloader/Limine/releases/download/"
    f"v{LIMINE_VERSION}/{LIMINE_ARCHIVE_NAME}"
)
KERNEL = TARGET_DIR / "x86_64-unknown-none" / "release" / "rustix"
ISO_ROOT = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-iso-root"
ISO_PATH = TARGET_DIR / "rustix.iso"

REQUIRED_LIMINE_FILES = (
    "limine-bios.sys",
    "limine-bios-cd.bin",
    "limine-uefi-cd.bin",
    "BOOTX64.EFI",
)


class BuildError(RuntimeError):
    """An actionable error while preparing or testing the boot image."""


def require_tool(name: str) -> str:
    path = shutil.which(name)
    if path is None:
        raise BuildError(f"required tool '{name}' was not found on PATH")
    return path


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as source:
        for block in iter(lambda: source.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def safe_extract(archive: zipfile.ZipFile, destination: Path) -> None:
    root = destination.resolve()
    for member in archive.infolist():
        name = PurePosixPath(member.filename)
        mode = member.external_attr >> 16
        if not name.parts or name.is_absolute() or ".." in name.parts or ":" in name.parts[0]:
            raise BuildError(f"unsafe path in Limine archive: {member.filename}")
        if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
            raise BuildError(f"symlink in Limine archive is not allowed: {member.filename}")
        output = (destination / Path(*name.parts)).resolve()
        if output != root and root not in output.parents:
            raise BuildError(f"archive member escapes extraction directory: {member.filename}")
    archive.extractall(destination)


def ensure_limine() -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    cache = TARGET_DIR / "tools" / f"limine-{LIMINE_VERSION}"
    archive_path = TARGET_DIR / "tools" / LIMINE_ARCHIVE_NAME
    extracted = cache / "archive"
    cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    extracted.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if not archive_path.exists():
        print(f"Downloading Limine {LIMINE_VERSION} binary release...")
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            LIMINE_ARCHIVE_URL,
            headers={"User-Agent": "Rustix-OS-build/0.1"},
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response, archive_path.open(
                "wb"
            ) as output:
                shutil.copyfileobj(response, output)
        except Exception as error:
            archive_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            raise BuildError(f"could not download pinned Limine release: {error}") from error

    actual_hash = sha256(archive_path)
    if actual_hash != LIMINE_ARCHIVE_SHA256:
        archive_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise BuildError(
            "Limine archive SHA-256 mismatch: "
            f"expected {LIMINE_ARCHIVE_SHA256}, got {actual_hash}"
        )

    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path) as archive:
            safe_extract(archive, extracted)
    except (OSError, zipfile.BadZipFile) as error:
        raise BuildError(f"could not extract the pinned Limine archive: {error}") from error

    def find_asset(name: str) -> Path:
        matches = sorted(extracted.rglob(name))
        if not matches:
            raise BuildError(f"Limine {LIMINE_VERSION} archive is missing {name}")
        return matches[0]

    limine_tool_name = "limine.exe" if sys.platform == "win32" else "limine"
    limine_tool = find_asset(limine_tool_name)
    if sys.platform != "win32":
        limine_tool.chmod(
            limine_tool.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IXUSR | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IXOTH
        )
    return limine_tool, extracted


def build_image() -> None:
    if not KERNEL.is_file():
        raise BuildError("kernel ELF not found; run 'just build' first")
    xorriso = require_tool("xorriso")
    limine_tool, limine_root = ensure_limine()

    shutil.rmtree(ISO_ROOT, ignore_errors=True)
    boot_dir = ISO_ROOT / "boot" / "limine"
    efi_dir = ISO_ROOT / "EFI" / "BOOT"
    boot_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    efi_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    shutil.copy2(KERNEL, ISO_ROOT / "boot" / "rustix")
    shutil.copy2(ROOT / "limine.conf", ISO_ROOT / "limine.conf")

    for name in REQUIRED_LIMINE_FILES:
        source = next(iter(sorted(limine_root.rglob(name))), None)
        if source is None:
            raise BuildError(f"Limine archive is missing required file {name}")
        if name == "BOOTX64.EFI":
            shutil.copy2(source, efi_dir / name)
        else:
            shutil.copy2(source, boot_dir / name)

    ISO_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    xorriso_command = [
        xorriso,
        "-as",
        "mkisofs",
        "-R",
        "-r",
        "-J",
        "-b",
        "boot/limine/limine-bios-cd.bin",
        "-no-emul-boot",
        "-boot-load-size",
        "4",
        "-boot-info-table",
        "-hfsplus",
        "-apm-block-size",
        "2048",
        "--efi-boot",
        "boot/limine/limine-uefi-cd.bin",
        "-efi-boot-part",
        "-efi-boot-image",
        "--protective-msdos-label",
        str(ISO_ROOT),
        "-o",
        str(ISO_PATH),
    ]
    subprocess.run(xorriso_command, cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    subprocess.run([str(limine_tool), "bios-install", str(ISO_PATH)], cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    print(f"Created hybrid BIOS/UEFI image: {ISO_PATH.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def smoke_test(timeout: int) -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; run 'just image' first")

    serial_log = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-qemu-serial.log"
    serial_log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    serial_log.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    serial_device = "file:" + serial_log.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
    command = [
        qemu,
        "-machine",
        "q35",
        "-m",
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        serial_device,
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]

    timed_out = False
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, timeout=timeout, check=False)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        timed_out = True
        result = None

    if not timed_out and result is not None and result.returncode != 0:
        details = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
        raise BuildError(
            f"QEMU exited with status {result.returncode} before the smoke-test timeout.\n"
            f"Serial output:\n{details}"
        )

    output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
    expected = (
        "Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap",
        "crabshell: ready (volatile RAM filesystem)",
        "root@rustix:/home/rustix# ",
    )
    missing = [marker for marker in expected if marker not in output]
    if missing:
        raise BuildError(
            "QEMU did not reach the expected kernel state; missing serial markers: "
            + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
            + f"\nSerial output:\n{output or '<empty>'}"
        )

    print(f"QEMU boot smoke test passed (bounded to {timeout}s).")
    print(f"Captured serial log: {serial_log.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def run_interactive() -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; run 'just image' first")
    command = [
        qemu,
        "-machine",
        "q35",
        "-m",
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        "stdio",
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=False)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise BuildError(f"QEMU exited with status {result.returncode}")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    subparsers.add_parser("image", help="create a pinned Limine BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO")
    smoke = subparsers.add_parser("smoke", help="boot the ISO and check its serial output")
    smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    subparsers.add_parser("run", help="run the ISO with an interactive serial terminal")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:
        if args.command == "image":
            build_image()
        elif args.command == "run":
            run_interactive()
        else:
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            smoke_test(args.timeout)
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
        print(f"Rustix boot workflow failed: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

````rustix/README.md
     1	# Rustix
     2	
     3	Rustix (Rust-unix) is an experimental, 64-bit, Unix-like operating system whose kernel is written in Rust. This repository builds the kernel itself; Limine is used only as the external boot protocol/loader, not as a substitute for a Rustix kernel.
     4	
     5	The project is at its **bootstrap milestone**. The current kernel is a freestanding `no_std` x86_64 ELF that accepts Limine protocol requests, initializes COM1 serial output, reports the bootloader's HHDM and memory-map summary, and then halts. It also includes a non-blocking polling driver for a legacy PS/2-compatible keyboard controller; keyboard input is not yet connected to a kernel input subsystem. Rustix does not yet provide a scheduler, processes, a syscall ABI, filesystems, networking, or a userland. See [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) for the staged plan.
     6	
     7	## Quick start
     8	
     9	Prerequisites: a Rust stable toolchain, `just`, Python 3, `xorriso`, QEMU (`qemu-system-x86_64`), and the target installed by `rust-toolchain.toml` (or `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`). The first image build downloads a pinned Limine binary release and verifies its SHA-256.
    10	
    11	```sh
    12	just help
    13	just fmt
    14	just test
    15	just check
    16	just build
    17	just image
    18	just smoke
    19	just verify
    20	```
    21	
    22	`just build` produces `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `just image` creates `target/rustix.iso`, a hybrid BIOS/UEFI image, and `just smoke` boots it under QEMU and checks for the kernel's serial banner. The full `just verify` task includes that bounded smoke test.
    23	
    24	See [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) for prerequisites, commands, linker assumptions, and emulator details; [`docs/architecture/overview.md`](docs/architecture/overview.md) for the design boundary; and [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) for the documentation map.
    25	
    26	## Project principles
    27	
    28	- The kernel and operating-system implementation are Rust-first and `no_std`; architecture-specific privileged operations are isolated under `src/arch/`.
    29	- The kernel is the product. A bootloader may initialize the machine and transfer control, but policy, memory management, scheduling, and Unix-like services belong to Rustix.
    30	- Keep unsafe code small, documented, and adjacent to its hardware/protocol boundary.
    31	- Build incrementally: every roadmap milestone should have build checks, tests where practical, and updated design documentation.
    32	- Unix-like behavior is an explicit compatibility goal, not a claim of POSIX compliance today.
    33	
    34	## Repository map
    35	
    36	- `src/main.rs` — freestanding kernel entry point and panic/idle path.
    37	- `src/boot.rs` — Limine requests and boot-memory-map reporting.
    38	- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — early COM1 polling driver.
    39	- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling.
    40	- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers.
    41	- `src/memory.rs` — architecture-independent boot-time memory accounting and host tests.
    42	- `.cargo/config.toml`, `linker.ld` — x86_64-none code generation and ELF layout.
    43	- `justfile` — formatting, tests, target checks, image creation, emulator smoke test, and aggregate verification.
    44	- `limine.conf` — pinned boot configuration for the Rustix kernel.
    45	- `scripts/boot.py` — checksum-verified Limine download, hybrid ISO assembly, and bounded QEMU validation.
    46	- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — runs `just verify` on pushes and pull requests.
    47	- `docs/` — architecture, drivers, development, security, and roadmap documentation.

````rustix/docs/architecture/overview.md
     1	# Architecture overview
     2	
     3	## Goals
     4	
     5	Rustix is a from-scratch operating system project with its own kernel, written in Rust. The intended initial platform is 64-bit x86 (`x86_64`), with a Unix-like process and file-descriptor model. The kernel should eventually own machine initialization, physical and virtual memory management, interrupt handling, scheduling, system calls, and device policy. A bootloader is a transport into the kernel, not a replacement for those facilities.
     6	
     7	Unix-like is a compatibility direction. It does **not** mean the current kernel is POSIX-compliant, nor does it commit the project to a particular existing kernel's internals. Compatibility profiles and a userland should be defined only after the underlying process, descriptor, and syscall semantics are implemented and tested.
     8	
     9	## Current implementation (bootstrap)
    10	
    11	1. Cargo builds a `no_std`, `no_main` ELF for `x86_64-unknown-none`.
    12	2. `linker.ld` places the image in the x86_64 higher-half kernel region and preserves Limine request sections.
    13	3. The Limine protocol provides a handoff, a higher-half direct-map (HHDM) response, and a physical memory-map response.
    14	4. `_start` initializes the COM1 serial driver, prints a startup banner and a compact boot-information summary, then halts the bootstrap processor.
    15	5. A separate polling PS/2-compatible keyboard driver exposes raw controller bytes but is not yet connected to an input subsystem.
    16	6. The architecture-independent library contains a checked usable-RAM byte accumulator with host-side unit tests.
    17	
    18	No heap, page tables managed by Rustix, interrupt descriptor table, context switching, scheduler, process model, syscall entry, filesystem, network stack, device discovery, or userspace exists yet.
    19	
    20	## Intended layers (planned)
    21	
    22	```text
    23	User programs and system utilities
    24	        | versioned syscall ABI
    25	Kernel services: processes, descriptors, VFS, IPC, signals
    26	        | explicit ownership and authorization checks
    27	Core kernel: scheduler, virtual memory, physical frames, interrupts
    28	        | narrow architecture abstractions
    29	x86_64 platform: paging, exceptions, timers, AP startup, drivers
    30	        | Limine boot handoff only
    31	Firmware and hardware
    32	```
    33	
    34	The diagram is a target decomposition, not a claim that those layers are implemented. Architecture-independent policy should live in safe Rust where possible; privileged instructions and raw device access should stay in small, reviewed architecture modules.
    35	
    36	## Design constraints
    37	
    38	- **Freestanding:** kernel code does not link `std`; allocation must be introduced deliberately after a physical-frame and heap strategy exists.
    39	- **Explicit unsafe boundaries:** raw pointers from boot protocol responses and x86 port I/O are unsafe. Each use must document its preconditions and remain short-lived.
    40	- **Fail visibly:** early boot failures should produce serial diagnostics where possible and then halt, rather than continue with invalid machine state.
    41	- **Checked arithmetic:** physical ranges, sizes, and address translations must reject overflow.
    42	- **No premature ABI:** userspace interfaces stay unstable until process lifetime, error conventions, copy-in/copy-out, and versioning are designed together.
    43	- **Hardware-independent tests:** parsing, range arithmetic, and policy should be testable as ordinary host-side Rust wherever possible.
    44	
    45	## Boot and CPU assumptions
    46	
    47	The current target is x86_64, with a 4 KiB page-oriented linker layout and no red zone. Limine performs the initial platform setup required by its protocol. Rustix must not assume that receiving a memory-map response means it owns the loader's page tables or can overwrite reserved regions. The current bootstrap does not enable interrupts or start application processors.
    48	
    49	See [Boot protocol](boot.md), [Memory management](memory.md), [x86_64 drivers](drivers.md), and [the roadmap](../roadmap/README.md) for subsystem boundaries and planned acceptance criteria.

````

````rustix/docs/development/building.md
     1	# Building Rustix
     2	
     3	## Prerequisites
     4	
     5	- Rust stable with `rustfmt`; the repository pins these in `rust-toolchain.toml`.
     6	- The `x86_64-unknown-none` target. The toolchain file requests it automatically; if needed, install it with `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`.
     7	- [`just`](https://just.systems/) to run the repository's named tasks.
     8	- Python 3.8 or newer (standard library only), with `python` on `PATH`; `xorriso`; and QEMU with `qemu-system-x86_64` for image creation and boot smoke tests.
     9	
    10	An ELF inspection tool such as `llvm-readelf` or `readelf` is useful when diagnosing linker output. The first image build downloads the pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary archive into `target/tools/` and verifies its published SHA-256 before extraction.
    11	
    12	## Common commands
    13	
    14	Run from the repository root:
    15	
    16	```sh
    17	just help
    18	just fmt       # check Rust formatting
    19	just test      # host-side unit tests for the library
    20	just check     # type-check the freestanding kernel target
    21	just build     # optimized kernel ELF
    22	just image     # hybrid BIOS/UEFI ISO at target/rustix.iso
    23	just smoke     # bounded QEMU boot and serial-banner assertion
    24	just verify    # fmt, tests, target check, image, and QEMU smoke test
    25	```
    26	
    27	Equivalent Rust checks are `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --lib`, `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-none`, and `cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-none`. Image creation and QEMU validation are provided by `scripts/boot.py` and are intentionally part of `just verify`.
    28	
    29	The optimized ELF is written to `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `cargo check` checks the target without producing a boot image. The library tests run on the host and exercise code that does not require privileged instructions.
    30	
    31	## Target-specific linker setup
    32	
    33	`.cargo/config.toml` applies the Rustix linker script and x86_64 kernel constraints only to `x86_64-unknown-none`. `linker.ld` emits an ELF64 x86_64 image at the higher-half base, retains Limine request sections, and defines `_start` as the entry symbol. The build uses no third-party Rust crates; the boot protocol is represented by small in-tree Rust structures and constants.
    34	
    35	Changing the target, virtual base, relocation model, or request ABI requires updating the linker script, protocol documentation, and validation plan together. Do not use host builds of the kernel binary as evidence that the freestanding target links correctly.
    36	
    37	## Building and smoke-testing a boot image
    38	
    39	`limine.conf` boots the kernel immediately and enables 38,400-baud serial output. `just image` builds the ELF, fetches Limine v12.9.3's binary ZIP from its immutable GitHub release, checks the pinned SHA-256, prepares a BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO, and installs the BIOS boot code. The Limine archive and extracted tools remain under ignored `target/`; no third-party binaries are checked into the source tree.
    40	
    41	`just smoke` launches `target/rustix.iso` in `qemu-system-x86_64` with a 256 MiB q35 machine, headless display, captured COM1 output, and a 20-second deadline. QEMU is expected to remain running because the bootstrap kernel halts; the runner terminates it at the deadline and requires both the startup and bootstrap-complete serial markers. On a failure it prints the serial log. The log remains at `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` for inspection.
    42	
    43	`just verify` includes the emulator smoke test and therefore needs Python 3, xorriso, QEMU, network access for the first Limine download, and the Rust target. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs the system tools on Ubuntu 24.04 and runs the same command. This verifies the boot path in CI; it is still not a substitute for testing physical hardware.
    44	
    45	## Troubleshooting
    46	
    47	- **Target not installed:** install `x86_64-unknown-none` as shown above.
    48	- **`just` not found:** install `just`; Rust-only checks can still be run with the Cargo commands above.
    49	- **`xorriso` or QEMU not found:** install the host image/emulator tools listed in prerequisites, then retry `just image` or `just smoke`.
    50	- **Limine SHA-256 mismatch:** the pinned archive may have changed or been corrupted; the script removes the mismatched download and refuses to use it. Check the official v12.9.3 release digest before changing the pin.
    51	- **Linker-script error:** build only for `x86_64-unknown-none`; confirm the invocation runs from the repository root so `linker.ld` resolves.
    52	- **No serial output:** inspect `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` and QEMU's stderr. The image config and Rustix COM1 driver both use 38,400 baud.

````

     1	# Security and unsafe-code policy
     2	
     3	Rustix is an early kernel prototype, not a security-reviewed operating system. It has no user/kernel separation implementation, process isolation, security boundary, or supported deployment profile today.
     4	
     5	## Current unsafe boundaries
     6	
     7	- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` issues privileged x86 port-I/O instructions behind narrow driver wrappers.
     8	- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` configures and writes to the legacy COM1 UART. It is intended for early kernel context only.
     9	- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` reads raw bytes from a legacy PS/2-compatible controller; callers must poll without blocking.
    10	- `src/boot.rs` reads Limine response pointers and memory-map entries. These pointers are trusted under the current loader handoff contract and are not yet protected by a validated boot-info abstraction.
    11	- `src/main.rs` uses `cli` and `hlt` to stop the bootstrap CPU after reporting status.
    12	
    13	Unsafe blocks should remain as small as practical and state the assumptions that make each operation valid. Avoid widening `unsafe impl` or introducing raw-pointer-based public APIs without a documented safety argument. The PS/2 routine consumes bytes from the controller, including discarding auxiliary/error bytes, so it must only be used by a single owner of that controller until input serialization is designed. External boot inputs, user pointers, MMIO, and DMA must not be treated as trusted merely because current boot data is trusted.
    14	
    15	## Security requirements for future subsystems
    16	
    17	- Validate every physical range and checked address calculation before mapping or allocating it.
    18	- Enforce least privilege in page mappings; avoid writable-executable pages by default.
    19	- Keep user memory untrusted and use explicit copy-in/copy-out routines at syscall boundaries.
    20	- Define ownership and lifetime rules for descriptors, processes, shared memory, and device buffers.
    21	- Test malformed input and error paths as well as successful operation.
    22	- Do not claim isolation or security guarantees until those properties have end-to-end tests and review.

# Rustix

Rustix (Rust-unix) is an experimental, 64-bit, Unix-like operating system whose kernel is written in Rust. This repository builds the kernel itself; Limine is used only as the external boot protocol/loader, not as a substitute for a Rustix kernel.

Rustix now boots into **Crabshell**, a small kernel-mode shell on the COM1 serial terminal. It includes basic navigation and file commands backed by a fixed-capacity RAM filesystem. The filesystem is volatile and reset at every boot; this is an early kernel shell, not a userspace process or POSIX shell. The command parser lives in a separate, allocation-free `crabshell` crate so a future GUI terminal can reuse it. Scheduling, process isolation, persistent storage, a syscall ABI, networking, and userspace are still future work. See [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) for the staged plan.

## Quick start

Prerequisites: a Rust stable toolchain, `just`, Python 3, `xorriso`, QEMU (`qemu-system-x86_64`), and the target installed by `rust-toolchain.toml` (or `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`). The first image build downloads a pinned Limine binary release and verifies its SHA-256.

```sh
just help
just fmt
just test
just check
just build
just image
just smoke
just run       # interactive serial shell in QEMU; exit with Ctrl+C
just verify
```

`just build` produces `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `just image` creates `target/rustix.iso`, a hybrid BIOS/UEFI image; `just smoke` checks that Crabshell reaches its prompt; and `just run` starts an interactive QEMU session attached to the current terminal.

Try `pwd`, `ls /`, `mkdir notes`, `write notes/hello.txt "hello from Rustix"`, `cat notes/hello.txt`, and `cd ..` in Crabshell. Commands include `help`, `clear`, `pwd`, `ls`, `cd`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `write`, `append`, `cat`, `rm`, and `rmdir`. The RAM filesystem holds at most 32 entries, with files capped at 1024 bytes. See [`docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](docs/architecture/crabshell.md) for the shell and filesystem contract, [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) for build/emulator details, and [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) for the documentation map.

## Project principles

- The kernel and operating-system implementation are Rust-first and `no_std`; architecture-specific privileged operations are isolated under `src/arch/`.
- The kernel is the product. A bootloader may initialize the machine and transfer control, but policy, memory management, scheduling, and Unix-like services belong to Rustix.
- Keep unsafe code small, documented, and adjacent to its hardware/protocol boundary.
- Build incrementally: every roadmap milestone should have build checks, tests where practical, and updated design documentation.
- Unix-like behavior is an explicit compatibility goal, not a claim of POSIX compliance today.

## Repository map

- `src/main.rs` — freestanding kernel entry point and Crabshell handoff.
- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel command executor.
- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem, with host-side tests.
- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` command parser crate; no I/O or filesystem coupling.
- `src/boot.rs` — Limine requests and boot-memory-map reporting.
- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — early COM1 polling driver.
- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling.
- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers.
- `src/memory.rs` — architecture-independent boot-time memory accounting and host tests.
- `.cargo/config.toml`, `linker.ld` — x86_64-none code generation and ELF layout.
- `justfile` — formatting, tests, target checks, image creation, emulator smoke test, and aggregate verification.
- `limine.conf` — pinned boot configuration for the Rustix kernel.
- `scripts/boot.py` — checksum-verified Limine download, hybrid ISO assembly, and bounded QEMU validation.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — runs `just verify` on pushes and pull requests.
- `docs/` — architecture, drivers, development, security, and roadmap documentation.

```

# Rustix documentation

Rustix is a 64-bit, Rust-first, Unix-like operating-system project. This index separates current implementation facts from planned interfaces: roadmap items are proposals until the corresponding code and tests exist.

## Start here

- [Project and implementation overview](architecture/overview.md)

- [Build and toolchain guide](development/building.md)
- [Testing and verification](development/testing.md)
- [Security and unsafe-code policy](security.md)
- [Milestones and acceptance criteria](roadmap/README.md)

## Current status

The repository contains a bare-metal `no_std` Rust kernel for `x86_64-unknown-none`. It uses Limine's boot protocol to receive control and inspect a memory map/HHDM, initializes the COM1 serial driver for diagnostics, and includes a non-blocking raw-byte polling driver for a legacy PS/2-compatible keyboard controller. Keyboard input is not yet integrated into a kernel input subsystem. A hash-pinned hybrid image builder, bounded QEMU smoke-test runner, and CI job are now present; their end-to-end run is still pending. The bootloader is not the kernel. There is not yet an allocator, interrupt subsystem, scheduler, userspace, or Unix compatibility layer.

## Documentation conventions

- **Implemented** means present in the repository and checked by current code or tests.
- **Planned** means an architectural direction, not a stable ABI or delivered capability.
- Any future ABI proposal must state versioning, error behavior, memory ownership, and compatibility expectations before it is treated as stable.

# Architecture overview

## Goals

Rustix is a from-scratch operating system project with its own kernel, written in Rust. The intended initial platform is 64-bit x86 (`x86_64`), with a Unix-like process and file-descriptor model. The kernel should eventually own machine initialization, physical and virtual memory management, interrupt handling, scheduling, system calls, and device policy. A bootloader is a transport into the kernel, not a replacement for those facilities.

Unix-like is a compatibility direction. It does **not** mean the current kernel is POSIX-compliant, nor does it commit the project to a particular existing kernel's internals. Compatibility profiles and a userland should be defined only after the underlying process, descriptor, and syscall semantics are implemented and tested.

## Current implementation

1. Cargo builds a `no_std`, `no_main` ELF for `x86_64-unknown-none` and uses Limine for the boot handoff.
2. `_start` initializes COM1, reports the boot memory map/HHDM, initializes a fixed-capacity RAM filesystem, and enters Crabshell.
3. Crabshell reads an ASCII command line from the serial UART and supports basic navigation, directory creation/listing, and text-file operations.
4. The separately packaged `crabshell` `no_std` crate parses commands without allocation or dependence on kernel I/O, making that layer reusable by a future graphical frontend.
5. The kernel library contains checked memory accounting and the bounded VFS implementation, both covered by host-side unit tests.

The current shell and filesystem run in kernel mode. Files exist only in RAM and disappear at reboot. There is no heap, Rustix-owned page-table manager, interrupt descriptor table, scheduler, user/kernel isolation, syscall ABI, on-disk filesystem, network stack, or userspace process.

## Intended layers (planned)

```text
User programs and system utilities
        | versioned syscall ABI
Kernel services: processes, descriptors, VFS, IPC, signals
        | explicit ownership and authorization checks
Core kernel: scheduler, virtual memory, physical frames, interrupts
        | narrow architecture abstractions
x86_64 platform: paging, exceptions, timers, AP startup, drivers
        | Limine boot handoff only
Firmware and hardware
```

The diagram is a target decomposition, not a claim that those layers are implemented. Architecture-independent policy should live in safe Rust where possible; privileged instructions and raw device access should stay in small, reviewed architecture modules.

## Design constraints

- **Freestanding:** kernel code does not link `std`; allocation must be introduced deliberately after a physical-frame and heap strategy exists.
- **Explicit unsafe boundaries:** raw pointers from boot protocol responses and x86 port I/O are unsafe. Each use must document its preconditions and remain short-lived.
- **Fail visibly:** early boot failures should produce serial diagnostics where possible and then halt, rather than continue with invalid machine state.
- **Checked arithmetic:** physical ranges, sizes, and address translations must reject overflow.
- **No premature ABI:** userspace interfaces stay unstable until process lifetime, error conventions, copy-in/copy-out, and versioning are designed together.
- **Hardware-independent tests:** parsing, range arithmetic, and policy should be testable as ordinary host-side Rust wherever possible.

## Boot and CPU assumptions

The current target is x86_64, with a 4 KiB page-oriented linker layout and no red zone. Limine performs the initial platform setup required by its protocol. Rustix must not assume that receiving a memory-map response means it owns the loader's page tables or can overwrite reserved regions. The current bootstrap does not enable interrupts or start application processors.

See [Boot protocol](boot.md), [Memory management](memory.md), [x86_64 drivers](drivers.md), [Crabshell](crabshell.md), and [the roadmap](../roadmap/README.md) for subsystem boundaries and planned acceptance criteria.

```

# Security and unsafe-code policy

Rustix is an early kernel prototype, not a security-reviewed operating system. It has no user/kernel separation implementation, process isolation, security boundary, or supported deployment profile today.

## Current unsafe boundaries

- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` issues privileged x86 port-I/O instructions behind narrow driver wrappers.
- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` configures and writes to the legacy COM1 UART. It is intended for early kernel context only.
- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` reads raw bytes from a legacy PS/2-compatible controller; callers must poll without blocking.
- `src/boot.rs` reads Limine response pointers and memory-map entries. These pointers are trusted under the current loader handoff contract and are not yet protected by a validated boot-info abstraction.
- `src/main.rs` uses `cli` and `hlt` to stop the bootstrap CPU after a fatal startup error.
- `src/vfs.rs` and `src/shell.rs` provide a kernel-mode RAM filesystem and shell. They have no user/kernel isolation, permissions, persistence, or protection from kernel bugs; shell commands are trusted kernel code, not sandboxed applications.

Unsafe blocks should remain as small as practical and state the assumptions that make each operation valid. Avoid widening `unsafe impl` or introducing raw-pointer-based public APIs without a documented safety argument. The PS/2 routine consumes bytes from the controller, including discarding auxiliary/error bytes, so it must only be used by a single owner of that controller until input serialization is designed. External boot inputs, user pointers, MMIO, and DMA must not be treated as trusted merely because current boot data is trusted.

## Security requirements for future subsystems

- Validate every physical range and checked address calculation before mapping or allocating it.
- Enforce least privilege in page mappings; avoid writable-executable pages by default.
- Keep user memory untrusted and use explicit copy-in/copy-out routines at syscall boundaries.
- Define ownership and lifetime rules for descriptors, processes, shared memory, and device buffers.
- Test malformed input and error paths as well as successful operation.
- Do not claim isolation or security guarantees until those properties have end-to-end tests and review.

```

```rustix/docs/architecture/boot.md
     1	# Boot protocol and kernel entry
     2	
     3	## Current boot contract
     4	
     5	Rustix currently expects a Limine-compatible x86_64 handoff. Limine is an external loader; it does not implement Rustix's kernel services. The kernel requests protocol base revision 3, the higher-half direct-map (HHDM) offset, and the memory map.
     6	
     7	Requests are kept in `.limine_requests_start`, `.limine_requests`, and `.limine_requests_end` by `linker.ld`. The ELF entry symbol is `_start`.
     8	
     9	### Entry sequence
    10	
    11	1. Limine loads the ELF and transfers control to `_start` under the x86_64 Limine protocol.
    12	2. `_start` configures the legacy COM1 UART driver for polling output.
    13	3. The kernel prints the HHDM offset and totals ordinary usable regions from the supplied memory-map entries.
    14	4. A PS/2-compatible keyboard driver is available for non-blocking raw-byte polling, but is not called during boot and is not attached to an input queue.
    15	5. The bootstrap prints an explicit status message and halts. It does not enable interrupts or return to the loader.
    16	
    17	The memory-map response describes physical regions. Its existence does not authorize Rustix to access every region, reclaim bootloader memory, or mutate the current page tables. The HHDM offset is reported for diagnostics only; the bootstrap does not yet translate or dereference physical addresses through it.
    18	
    19	## Link and target configuration
    20	
    21	- Rust target: `x86_64-unknown-none`
    22	- Linker script: `linker.ld`
    23	- Kernel virtual base: `0xffffffff80000000`
    24	- Required code-generation constraints: kernel code model, static relocation, and disabled red zone
    25	- Rust panic strategy: abort; the panic handler logs and halts
    26	
    27	See [`../development/building.md`](../development/building.md) for commands and toolchain setup.
    28	
    29	## Failure behavior and limitations
    30	
    31	Missing boot responses and invalid pointer/count combinations are reported and cause the affected information to be skipped. The implementation trusts the bootloader to provide valid readable response structures for the duration of boot; this trust assumption must be revisited before adding untrusted boot sources. COM1 writes use a bounded polling loop so a non-responsive UART does not block forever.
    32	
    33	The repository now includes a Limine v12.9.3 binary archive pin with SHA-256 verification, a hybrid ISO recipe, and a bounded QEMU serial smoke test. These workflows are automated in CI, but the milestone is not considered complete until that end-to-end job passes. There is still no framebuffer console, reboot/shutdown interface, or broader boot-protocol compatibility test. The available serial and keyboard drivers do not imply a general device model. A future boot-image milestone must pin loader provenance/version and exercise the actual ELF in an emulator before claiming a bootable release.
    34	
    35	## Future boot work
    36	
    37	Before adding more kernel subsystems, establish a reproducible boot artifact and emulator test. Then define ownership of loader-reclaimable regions, preserve firmware reservations, parse the full map into validated ranges, initialize a Rustix-owned frame allocator, and document which page tables and CPU state are inherited versus replaced.

```

# Crabshell and the early RAM filesystem

Crabshell is Rustix's first command-line interface. The current implementation is a **kernel-mode bootstrap shell** attached to COM1, not a separate user process. Its command parser is isolated in a separate crate so the same grammar can later be reused by a graphical terminal frontend or by a userspace terminal application.

## Crate boundary

- `crates/crabshell` is an allocation-free `no_std` Rust library. It parses a borrowed command line into a `Command` value and performs no I/O, filesystem access, scheduling, or privilege changes.
- `src/shell.rs` adapts the parser to the kernel serial driver, provides a small line editor, implements commands, and owns the current working-directory node.
- `src/vfs.rs` is a fixed-capacity in-memory filesystem used by the early shell. It is not a disk filesystem and is not persistent.

This is a useful separation now: future terminal frontends can reuse parsing without importing kernel hardware or filesystem code. A future user-mode Crabshell should keep its frontend/parser layer but execute operations through a documented syscall/VFS interface; it must not link the kernel's internal filesystem as a privilege shortcut.

## Build and run

```sh
just test
just image
just smoke
just run
```

`just run` starts a headless QEMU machine and connects the guest serial port to the current terminal. Use `Ctrl+C` in the host terminal to stop QEMU. The BIOS/UEFI boot image is `target/rustix.iso`.

The kernel welcomes the user in `/home/rustix`. The initial namespace contains `/bin`, `/dev`, `/etc`, `/home/rustix`, `/tmp`, and `/var`; `/etc/motd` explains that storage is volatile.

## Commands

| Command | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `help` | List available commands and limits. |
| `clear` | Send the ANSI clear-screen/home sequence. |
| `pwd` | Print the absolute working directory. |
| `ls [PATH]` | List a directory; a file path prints that file's name and size. Defaults to the current directory. |
| `cd PATH` | Change to an existing directory. Supports absolute and relative paths, `.`, and `..`. |
| `mkdir PATH` | Create one directory; its parent must already exist. |
| `touch PATH` | Create an empty file, or leave an existing file unchanged. |
| `write PATH TEXT` | Create a file if needed and replace its contents with the remaining line. Matching outer single or double quotes around the text are removed. |
| `append PATH TEXT` | Create a file if needed and append the remaining line. |
| `cat PATH` | Print a UTF-8 text file. Binary data is not displayed. |
| `rm PATH` | Remove a file. Directories are rejected. |
| `rmdir PATH` | Remove an empty directory other than the current directory. |

Example:

```text
root@rustix:/home/rustix# mkdir notes
root@rustix:/home/rustix# write notes/hello.txt "hello from Rustix"
root@rustix:/home/rustix# cat notes/hello.txt
hello from Rustix
root@rustix:/home/rustix# cd ..
root@rustix:/home# pwd
/home
```

The grammar intentionally does not yet support quoted paths, escaped quotes, variables, pipes, redirection, globbing, command substitution, history, or a process launcher. Input is a single ASCII line (up to 256 bytes) from the serial port.

## RAM filesystem contract

- The root plus at most 31 live entries fit in the fixed 32-node table.
- Path components are limited to 31 UTF-8 bytes; file contents are limited to 1024 bytes each.
- Paths may be absolute or relative and support repeated `/`, `.`, and `..`.
- `write` replaces a file; `append` adds bytes; `touch` never truncates.
- `rm` handles files only. `rmdir` refuses non-empty directories and the current directory.
- Filesystem allocation is fixed-capacity; errors are reported rather than allocating a heap.
- Every file and directory disappears when the machine resets. There is no block device, journaling, metadata persistence, permission model, links, or concurrent access yet.

## Tests and limitations

Host-side tests cover path traversal, file create/write/append/remove, entry kinds, path rendering, directory emptiness, and the parser's syntax/arity. The QEMU smoke test checks that the serial shell reaches its prompt; it does not emulate reboot persistence or prove isolation. Since the shell runs in ring 0, a parser or filesystem bug can panic the entire kernel. This implementation must not be presented as a secure or POSIX-compliant shell.

# Crabshell command parser

`crabshell` is a small `no_std`, allocation-free Rust library containing the command enum and parser used by the Rustix shell. It intentionally knows nothing about serial terminals, kernel privileges, filesystems, or process management.

The initial grammar supports `help`, `clear`, `pwd`, `ls`, `cd`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `write`, `append`, `cat`, `rm`, and `rmdir`. `write` and `append` borrow the remaining text from the input line and optionally remove matching outer quotes. See [`../../docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](../../docs/architecture/crabshell.md) for command semantics, limits, and current kernel integration.

Run its parser tests from the repository root with `cargo test -p crabshell --lib` or `just test`.

# Boot protocol and kernel entry

## Current boot contract

Rustix currently expects a Limine-compatible x86_64 handoff. Limine is an external loader; it does not implement Rustix's kernel services. The kernel requests protocol base revision 3, the higher-half direct-map (HHDM) offset, and the memory map.

Requests are kept in `.limine_requests_start`, `.limine_requests`, and `.limine_requests_end` by `linker.ld`. The ELF entry symbol is `_start`.

### Entry sequence

1. Limine loads the ELF and transfers control to `_start` under the x86_64 Limine protocol.
2. `_start` configures the legacy COM1 UART for polling output and input.
3. The kernel prints the HHDM offset and totals ordinary usable regions from the supplied memory-map entries.
4. It seeds a small volatile RAM filesystem and enters Crabshell on the serial console.
5. The shell busy-polls COM1 because no scheduler or UART interrupt handler exists yet. The kernel does not return to the loader.

The memory-map response describes physical regions. Its existence does not authorize Rustix to access every region, reclaim bootloader memory, or mutate the current page tables. The HHDM offset is reported for diagnostics only; the bootstrap does not yet translate or dereference physical addresses through it.

## Link and target configuration

- Rust target: `x86_64-unknown-none`
- Linker script: `linker.ld`
- Kernel virtual base: `0xffffffff80000000`
- Required code-generation constraints: kernel code model, static relocation, and disabled red zone
- Rust panic strategy: abort; the panic handler logs and halts

See [`../development/building.md`](../development/building.md) for commands and toolchain setup.

## Failure behavior and limitations

Missing boot responses and invalid pointer/count combinations are reported and cause the affected information to be skipped. The implementation trusts the bootloader to provide valid readable response structures for the duration of boot; this trust assumption must be revisited before adding untrusted boot sources. COM1 writes use a bounded polling loop so a non-responsive UART does not block forever.

The repository now includes a Limine v12.9.3 binary archive pin with SHA-256 verification, a hybrid ISO recipe, and a bounded QEMU serial smoke test that checks Crabshell's prompt. These workflows are automated in CI, but the boot milestone is not considered complete until that end-to-end job passes. There is still no framebuffer console, reboot/shutdown interface, or broader boot-protocol compatibility test. The available serial and keyboard drivers do not imply a general device model.

## Future boot work

The boot artifact and emulator test path now exist. Next, define ownership of loader-reclaimable regions, preserve firmware reservations, parse the full map into validated ranges, initialize a Rustix-owned frame allocator, and document which page tables and CPU state are inherited versus replaced.

# Testing and verification

## Current checks

`just verify` runs the intended pre-change sequence:

1. `just fmt` — fail on formatting differences across the workspace.
2. `just test` — run host-side memory, RAM-filesystem, and Crabshell parser tests.
3. `just check` — check the `x86_64-unknown-none` kernel target.
4. `just smoke` — build the pinned hybrid ISO, boot it in QEMU, and check that Crabshell reaches its prompt within a deadline.

Keep the Crabshell parser and VFS independent of hardware so syntax, path handling, and storage semantics can be tested without booting. Add tests for boundaries and failure behavior when introducing new pure kernel helpers. The kernel binary is not a host test target.

## What current checks do not prove

- `cargo check` does not perform a final target link.
- A successful ELF link does not prove the boot protocol is recognized or `_start` is reached.
- Host unit tests do not validate privileged instructions, UART behavior, memory-map pointer validity, page tables, interrupts, or actual hardware.
- The QEMU smoke test proves the kernel reaches the shell prompt; it does not yet send interactive file commands or prove persistence across reboot.
- There is no on-disk filesystem integration test, syscall/userspace test, fuzz target, or physical-hardware test.

## Validation policy

For changes to the kernel entry, linker script, boot requests, architecture code, shell, or VFS, run `just verify`. For memory-management and ABI code, add negative tests for overflow, malformed ranges, permission failures, and invalid user pointers before exposing those paths to userspace.

Record commands actually run and any environment limitation in change summaries; never call an unexecuted build “passing.”

# Rustix documentation

Rustix is a 64-bit, Rust-first, Unix-like operating-system project. This index separates current implementation facts from planned interfaces: roadmap items are proposals until the corresponding code and tests exist.

## Start here

- [Project and implementation overview](architecture/overview.md)
- [Boot protocol and current entry path](architecture/boot.md)
- [Memory-management direction](architecture/memory.md)
- [x86_64 drivers and hardware boundary](architecture/drivers.md)
- [Crabshell and the volatile RAM filesystem](architecture/crabshell.md)
- [Unix-like process and syscall direction](architecture/syscall-abi.md)
- [Build and toolchain guide](development/building.md)
- [Testing and verification](development/testing.md)
- [Security and unsafe-code policy](security.md)
- [Milestones and acceptance criteria](roadmap/README.md)

## Current status

The repository contains a bare-metal `no_std` Rust kernel for `x86_64-unknown-none`. After Limine handoff it reports boot memory information, seeds a volatile RAM filesystem, and runs Crabshell over the COM1 serial console. Crabshell's allocation-free parser is a separate crate; the kernel handles command execution. The image builder and bounded QEMU prompt smoke test are wired into CI, but the end-to-end run remains pending. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process: there is not yet an allocator, interrupt subsystem, scheduler, process isolation, persistent filesystem, or Unix compatibility layer.

## Documentation conventions

- **Implemented** means present in the repository and checked by current code or tests.
- **Planned** means an architectural direction, not a stable ABI or delivered capability.
- Any future ABI proposal must state versioning, error behavior, memory ownership, and compatibility expectations before it is treated as stable.

# Rustix roadmap

This roadmap is staged to keep each milestone reviewable and bootable. The project is currently at **Milestone 0: kernel bootstrap; image and smoke-test workflow implemented, first end-to-end pass pending**. Items below are planned unless checked off; checked implementation work is not the same as a passing end-to-end validation.

## Milestone 0 — Rust kernel bootstrap (current)

- [x] `no_std` Rust kernel binary for `x86_64-unknown-none`.
- [x] Own ELF linker layout and Limine boot-protocol requests.
- [x] COM1 serial diagnostics, memory-map/HHDM summary, and panic halt path.
- [x] Narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers and a non-blocking PS/2 raw-scancode polling driver.
- [x] `just` commands and architecture/development/security/driver documentation.
- [x] Hash-pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary distribution and checked extraction.
- [x] Reproducible BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO recipe and documented boot configuration.
- [x] Bounded QEMU serial smoke-test runner and CI workflow.
- [x] Separate no-std Crabshell command-parser crate and kernel serial shell frontend.
- [x] Fixed-capacity RAM filesystem with basic directory and text-file operations.
- [ ] Execute the end-to-end image build and QEMU Crabshell prompt smoke test successfully in CI or a local environment.

**Exit criteria:** a clean checkout builds the pinned image, boots it in the documented emulator, and captures the expected serial banner in automated validation. The workflow is implemented; the criterion remains pending until an end-to-end run passes.

## Milestone 1 — validated boot state and machine diagnostics

- Parse and validate all loader ranges into a stable boot-info value.
- Preserve reserved, reclaimable, firmware, and MMIO regions distinctly.
- Add serial formatting tests, CPU feature reporting, and a framebuffer or documented serial-only console.
- Establish explicit ownership and reclaim timing for loader memory.

**Exit criteria:** malformed maps fail closed; an emulator test validates reported regions and boot metadata.

## Milestone 2 — memory ownership and CPU exceptions

- Physical frame allocator with overflow-safe range handling and exhaustion tests.
- Kernel-owned page-table management and documented direct-map policy.
- Global heap with deterministic out-of-memory behavior.
- GDT/TSS and IDT setup; exception handlers with register/error-code diagnostics; fault-injection tests.

**Exit criteria:** allocator and mapping invariants are tested, page faults are diagnosable, and the kernel remains bootable under emulator tests.

## Milestone 3 — interrupts, time, and scheduling

- Timer and interrupt-controller setup with explicit interrupt-safe locking rules.
- Kernel threads and context switching; per-CPU data before SMP work.
- Preemptive scheduling only after interrupt, stack, and lock invariants are validated.
- Application processor startup as a separate milestone, not an implicit extension of single-core code.

**Exit criteria:** deterministic thread lifecycle tests and bounded timer/preemption integration tests.

## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI

- User-mode entry/exit and isolated address spaces.
- Versioned syscall ABI, validated copy-in/copy-out, and documented error semantics.
- Initial process lifecycle, descriptor table, and executable-loading path.
- Adversarial tests for invalid pointers, bad lengths, overflow, and process teardown.

**Exit criteria:** a controlled userspace init process can execute and use a small documented syscall subset without corrupting the kernel on invalid input.

## Milestone 5 — Unix-like services and storage

- VFS and mount model, file descriptors, and a first on-disk filesystem.
- Process creation/exec/wait semantics, pipes or IPC, and signal-like delivery as designed.
- Device discovery/driver model and networking only after ownership and isolation policies exist.
- Compatibility tests for any claimed Unix/POSIX behavior; keep unsupported operations explicit.

**Exit criteria:** documented userland tools can run from a reproducible image and integration tests cover process and file semantics.

## Working rule

Each milestone should add code, tests, and updated documentation together. Do not advance the stated project status merely because an interface or design note exists. Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable subsystem stubs.

    27	Equivalent Rust checks are `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --lib`, `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-none`, and `cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-none`. Image creation and QEMU validation are provided by `scripts/boot.py` and are intentionally part of `just verify`.
    28	
    29	The optimized ELF is written to `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `cargo check` checks the target without producing a boot image. The library tests run on the host and exercise code that does not require privileged instructions.
    30	
    31	## Target-specific linker setup
    32	
    33	`.cargo/config.toml` applies the Rustix linker script and x86_64 kernel constraints only to `x86_64-unknown-none`. `linker.ld` emits an ELF64 x86_64 image at the higher-half base, retains Limine request sections, and defines `_start` as the entry symbol. The build uses no third-party Rust crates; the boot protocol is represented by small in-tree Rust structures and constants.
    34	
    35	Changing the target, virtual base, relocation model, or request ABI requires updating the linker script, protocol documentation, and validation plan together. Do not use host builds of the kernel binary as evidence that the freestanding target links correctly.
    36	
    37	## Building and smoke-testing a boot image
    38	
    39	`limine.conf` boots the kernel immediately and enables 38,400-baud serial output. `just image` builds the ELF, fetches Limine v12.9.3's binary ZIP from its immutable GitHub release, checks the pinned SHA-256, prepares a BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO, and installs the BIOS boot code. The Limine archive and extracted tools remain under ignored `target/`; no third-party binaries are checked into the source tree.
    40	
    41	`just smoke` launches `target/rustix.iso` in `qemu-system-x86_64` with a 256 MiB q35 machine, headless display, captured COM1 output, and a 20-second deadline. QEMU is expected to remain running because the bootstrap kernel halts; the runner terminates it at the deadline and requires both the startup and bootstrap-complete serial markers. On a failure it prints the serial log. The log remains at `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` for inspection.
    42	
    43	`just verify` includes the emulator smoke test and therefore needs Python 3, xorriso, QEMU, network access for the first Limine download, and the Rust target. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs the system tools on Ubuntu 24.04 and runs the same command. This verifies the boot path in CI; it is still not a substitute for testing physical hardware.
    44	
    45	## Troubleshooting
    46	
    47	- **Target not installed:** install `x86_64-unknown-none` as shown above.
    48	- **`just` not found:** install `just`; Rust-only checks can still be run with the Cargo commands above.
    49	- **`xorriso` or QEMU not found:** install the host image/emulator tools listed in prerequisites, then retry `just image` or `just smoke`.
    50	- **Limine SHA-256 mismatch:** the pinned archive may have changed or been corrupted; the script removes the mismatched download and refuses to use it. Check the official v12.9.3 release digest before changing the pin.
    51	- **Linker-script error:** build only for `x86_64-unknown-none`; confirm the invocation runs from the repository root so `linker.ld` resolves.
    52	- **No serial output:** inspect `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` and QEMU's stderr. The image config and Rustix COM1 driver both use 38,400 baud.

     5	## Crate boundary
     6	
     7	- `crates/crabshell` is an allocation-free `no_std` Rust library. It parses a borrowed command line into a `Command` value and performs no I/O, filesystem access, scheduling, or privilege changes.
     8	- `src/shell.rs` adapts the parser to the kernel serial driver, provides a small line editor, implements commands, and owns the current working-directory node.
     9	- `src/vfs.rs` is a fixed-capacity in-memory filesystem used by the early shell. It is not a disk filesystem and is not persistent.
    10	
    11	This is a useful separation now: future terminal frontends can reuse parsing without importing kernel hardware or filesystem code. A future user-mode Crabshell should keep its frontend/parser layer but execute operations through a documented syscall/VFS interface; it must not link the kernel's internal filesystem as a privilege shortcut.
    12	
    13	## Build and run
    14	
    15	```sh
    16	just test
    17	just image
    18	just smoke
    19	just run
    20	```
    21	
    22	`just run` starts a headless QEMU machine and connects the guest serial port to the current terminal. Use `Ctrl+C` in the host terminal to stop QEMU. The BIOS/UEFI boot image is `target/rustix.iso`.
    23	
    24	The kernel welcomes the user in `/home/rustix`. The initial namespace contains `/bin`, `/dev`, `/etc`, `/home/rustix`, `/tmp`, and `/var`; `/etc/motd` explains that storage is volatile.
    25	
    26	## Commands
    27	
    28	| Command | Behavior |
    29	|---|---|
    30	| `help` | List available commands and limits. |
    31	| `clear` | Send the ANSI clear-screen/home sequence. |
    32	| `pwd` | Print the absolute working directory. |
    33	| `ls [PATH]` | List a directory; a file path prints that file's name and size. Defaults to the current directory. |
    34	| `cd PATH` | Change to an existing directory. Supports absolute and relative paths, `.`, and `..`. |
    35	| `mkdir PATH` | Create one directory; its parent must already exist. |
    36	| `touch PATH` | Create an empty file, or leave an existing file unchanged. |
    37	| `write PATH TEXT` | Create a file if needed and replace its contents with the remaining line. Matching outer single or double quotes around the text are removed. |
    38	| `append PATH TEXT` | Create a file if needed and append the remaining line. |
    39	| `cat PATH` | Print a UTF-8 text file. Binary data is not displayed. |
    40	| `rm PATH` | Remove a file. Directories are rejected. |
    41	| `rmdir PATH` | Remove an empty directory other than the current directory. |
    42	
    43	Example:
    44	
    45	```text
    46	root@rustix:/home/rustix# mkdir notes
    47	root@rustix:/home/rustix# write notes/hello.txt "hello from Rustix"
    48	root@rustix:/home/rustix# cat notes/hello.txt
    49	hello from Rustix
    50	root@rustix:/home/rustix# cd ..
    51	root@rustix:/home# pwd
    52	/home
    53	```
    54	
    55	The grammar intentionally does not yet support quoted paths, escaped quotes, variables, pipes, redirection, globbing, command substitution, history, or a process launcher. Input is a single ASCII line (up to 256 bytes) from the serial port.
    56	
    57	## RAM filesystem contract
    58	
    59	- The root plus at most 31 live entries fit in the fixed 32-node table.
    60	- Path components are limited to 31 UTF-8 bytes; file contents are limited to 1024 bytes each.
    61	- Paths may be absolute or relative and support repeated `/`, `.`, and `..`.
    62	- `write` replaces a file; `append` adds bytes; `touch` never truncates.
    63	- `rm` handles files only. `rmdir` refuses non-empty directories and the current directory.
    64	- Filesystem allocation is fixed-capacity; errors are reported rather than allocating a heap.
    65	- Every file and directory disappears when the machine resets. There is no block device, journaling, metadata persistence, permission model, links, or concurrent access yet.
    66	
    67	## Tests and limitations
    68	
    69	Host-side tests cover path traversal, file create/write/append/remove, entry kinds, path rendering, directory emptiness, and the parser's syntax/arity. The QEMU smoke test checks that the serial shell reaches its prompt; it does not emulate reboot persistence or prove isolation. Since the shell runs in ring 0, a parser or filesystem bug can panic the entire kernel. This implementation must not be presented as a secure or POSIX-compliant shell.
