```rustix/docs/architecture/boot.md
     1	# Boot protocol and kernel entry
     2	
     3	## Current boot contract
     4	
     5	Rustix currently expects a Limine-compatible x86_64 handoff. Limine is an external loader; it does not implement Rustix's kernel services. The kernel requests protocol base revision 3, the higher-half direct-map (HHDM) offset, and the memory map.
     6	
     7	Requests are kept in `.limine_requests_start`, `.limine_requests`, and `.limine_requests_end` by `linker.ld`. The ELF entry symbol is `_start`.
     8	
     9	### Entry sequence
    10	
    11	1. Limine loads the ELF and transfers control to `_start` under the x86_64 Limine protocol.
    12	2. `_start` configures the legacy COM1 UART for polling output and input.
    13	3. The kernel prints the HHDM offset and totals ordinary usable regions from the supplied memory-map entries.
    14	4. It seeds a small volatile RAM filesystem and enters Crabshell on the serial console.
    15	5. The shell busy-polls COM1 because no scheduler or UART interrupt handler exists yet. The kernel does not return to the loader.
    16	
    17	The memory-map response describes physical regions. Its existence does not authorize Rustix to access every region, reclaim bootloader memory, or mutate the current page tables. The HHDM offset is reported for diagnostics only; the bootstrap does not yet translate or dereference physical addresses through it.
    18	
    19	## Link and target configuration
    20	
    21	- Rust target: `x86_64-unknown-none`
    22	- Linker script: `linker.ld`
    23	- Kernel virtual base: `0xffffffff80000000`
    24	- Required code-generation constraints: kernel code model, static relocation, and disabled red zone
    25	- Rust panic strategy: abort; the panic handler logs and halts
    26	
    27	See [`../development/building.md`](../development/building.md) for commands and toolchain setup.
    28	
    29	## Failure behavior and limitations
    30	
    31	Missing boot responses and invalid pointer/count combinations are reported and cause the affected information to be skipped. The implementation trusts the bootloader to provide valid readable response structures for the duration of boot; this trust assumption must be revisited before adding untrusted boot sources. COM1 writes use a bounded polling loop so a non-responsive UART does not block forever.
    32	
    33	The repository now includes a Limine v12.9.3 binary archive pin with SHA-256 verification, a hybrid ISO recipe, and a bounded QEMU serial smoke test that checks Crabshell's prompt. These workflows are automated in CI, but the boot milestone is not considered complete until that end-to-end job passes. There is still no framebuffer console, reboot/shutdown interface, or broader boot-protocol compatibility test. The available serial and keyboard drivers do not imply a general device model.
    34	
    35	## Future boot work
    36	
    37	The boot artifact and emulator test path now exist. Next, define ownership of loader-reclaimable regions, preserve firmware reservations, parse the full map into validated ranges, initialize a Rustix-owned frame allocator, and document which page tables and CPU state are inherited versus replaced.

    28	    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    29	    boot::report_boot_information();
    30	
    31	    // SAFETY: Crabshell is the only owner of this filesystem. The bootstrap is
    32	    // single-core and has no scheduler or filesystem-touching interrupt handlers.
    33	    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    34	    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
    35	        Ok(home) => shell::run(filesystem, home),
    36	        Err(error) => {
    37	            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
    38	            halt_forever()
    39	        }
    40	    }
    41	}

    46	    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    47	    halt_forever()
    48	}
    49	
    50	fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    51	    loop {
    52	        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
    53	        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    54	    }

# Building Rustix

## Prerequisites

- Rust stable with `rustfmt`; the repository pins these in `rust-toolchain.toml`.
- The `x86_64-unknown-none` target. The toolchain file requests it automatically; if needed, install it with `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`.
- [`just`](https://just.systems/) to run the repository's named tasks.
- Python 3.8 or newer (standard library only), with `python` on `PATH`; `xorriso`; and QEMU with `qemu-system-x86_64` for image creation and boot smoke tests.

An ELF inspection tool such as `llvm-readelf` or `readelf` is useful when diagnosing linker output. The first image build downloads the pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary archive into `target/tools/` and verifies its published SHA-256 before extraction.

## Common commands

Run from the repository root:

```sh
just help
just fmt       # check Rust formatting
just test      # parser, RAM-filesystem, and memory tests
just check     # type-check the freestanding kernel target
just build     # optimized kernel ELF
just image     # hybrid BIOS/UEFI ISO at target/rustix.iso
just smoke     # bounded QEMU boot to the Crabshell prompt
just run       # interactive serial shell in QEMU (Ctrl+C to stop)
just verify    # fmt, workspace tests, target check, image, and QEMU smoke test
```

Equivalent Rust checks are `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --lib`, `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-none`, and `cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-none`. Image creation and QEMU validation are provided by `scripts/boot.py` and are intentionally part of `just verify`.

The optimized ELF is written to `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `cargo check` checks the target without producing a boot image. The library tests run on the host and exercise code that does not require privileged instructions.

## Target-specific linker setup

`.cargo/config.toml` applies the Rustix linker script and x86_64 kernel constraints only to `x86_64-unknown-none`. `linker.ld` emits an ELF64 x86_64 image at the higher-half base, retains Limine request sections, and defines `_start` as the entry symbol. The build uses no third-party Rust crates; the boot protocol is represented by small in-tree Rust structures and constants.

Changing the target, virtual base, relocation model, or request ABI requires updating the linker script, protocol documentation, and validation plan together. Do not use host builds of the kernel binary as evidence that the freestanding target links correctly.

## Building and smoke-testing a boot image

`limine.conf` boots the kernel immediately and enables 38,400-baud serial output. `just image` builds the ELF, fetches Limine v12.9.3's binary ZIP from its immutable GitHub release, checks the pinned SHA-256, prepares a BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO, and installs the BIOS boot code. The Limine archive and extracted tools remain under ignored `target/`; no third-party binaries are checked into the source tree.

`just smoke` launches `target/rustix.iso` in `qemu-system-x86_64` with a 256 MiB q35 machine, headless display, captured COM1 output, and a 20-second deadline. QEMU is expected to remain running at the interactive shell; the runner terminates it at the deadline and requires the startup banner, Crabshell-ready message, and initial prompt. On a failure it prints the serial log. The log remains at `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` for inspection.

`just run` launches the same image with the serial port attached to the host terminal, allowing interactive shell use. Stop the emulator with `Ctrl+C`.

`just verify` includes the emulator smoke test and therefore needs Python 3, xorriso, QEMU, network access for the first Limine download, and the Rust target. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs the system tools on Ubuntu 24.04 and runs the same command. This verifies the boot path in CI; it is still not a substitute for testing physical hardware.

## Troubleshooting

- **Target not installed:** install `x86_64-unknown-none` as shown above.
- **`just` not found:** install `just`; Rust-only checks can still be run with the Cargo commands above.
- **`xorriso` or QEMU not found:** install the host image/emulator tools listed in prerequisites, then retry `just image` or `just smoke`.
- **Limine SHA-256 mismatch:** the pinned archive may have changed or been corrupted; the script removes the mismatched download and refuses to use it. Check the official v12.9.3 release digest before changing the pin.
- **Linker-script error:** build only for `x86_64-unknown-none`; confirm the invocation runs from the repository root so `linker.ld` resolves.
- **No serial output:** inspect `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` and QEMU's stderr. The image config and Rustix COM1 driver both use 38,400 baud.

     6

    23	
    24	For changes to the kernel entry, linker script, boot requests, architecture code, shell, or VFS, run `just verify`. For memory-management and ABI code, add negative tests for overflow, malformed ranges, permission failures, and invalid user pointers before exposing those paths to userspace.

#![no_std]

//! Small, allocation-free command parsing for Rustix's Crabshell.
//!
//! This crate deliberately contains no terminal, filesystem, or kernel code.
//! The same command model can later be driven by a graphical terminal frontend
//! or a userspace process without coupling it to the current serial console.

/// The longest command line accepted by the bootstrap shell, excluding its NUL.
pub const MAX_LINE_LENGTH: usize = 256;

/// Parsed shell operations. The command borrows its path and text from the input
/// line, so parsing needs no allocator and the caller controls all I/O.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Command<'a> {
    Help,
    Clear,
    Pwd,
    Ls(Option<&'a str>),
    Cd(&'a str),
    Mkdir(&'a str),
    Touch(&'a str),
    Write { path: &'a str, contents: &'a str },
    Append { path: &'a str, contents: &'a str },
    Cp { source: &'a str, destination: &'a str },
    Mv { source: &'a str, destination: &'a str },
    Cat(&'a str),
    Rm(&'a str),
    Rmdir(&'a str),
}

/// Errors in command syntax. Unknown command names are reported separately so
/// the caller can echo the original name in its diagnostic.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ParseError {
    UnknownCommand,
    MissingArgument,
    MissingText,
    TooManyArguments,
    UnterminatedQuote,
}

/// Parse one command line. An empty or whitespace-only line returns `Ok(None)`.
///
/// `write` and `append` accept the remaining text verbatim; wrapping the whole
/// text in matching single or double quotes removes those outer quotes. Escape
/// sequences and quoted paths are intentionally not part of this first grammar.
pub fn parse(line: &str) -> Result<Option<Command<'_>>, ParseError> {
    let line = line.trim();
    if line.is_empty() {
        return Ok(None);
    }

    let (name, rest) = take_word(line).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    let command = match name {
        "help" => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Command::Help
        }
        "clear" => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Command::Clear
        }
        "pwd" => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Command::Pwd
        }
        "ls" => Command::Ls(optional_path(rest)?),
        "cd" => Command::Cd(one_path(rest)?),
        "mkdir" => Command::Mkdir(one_path(rest)?),
        "touch" => Command::Touch(one_path(rest)?),
        "write" => {
            let (path, contents) = path_and_text(rest)?;
            Command::Write { path, contents }
        }
        "append" => {
            let (path, contents) = path_and_text(rest)?;
            Command::Append { path, contents }
        }
        "cp" => {
            let (source, destination) = two_paths(rest)?;
            Command::Cp { source, destination }
        }
        "mv" => {
            let (source, destination) = two_paths(rest)?;
            Command::Mv { source, destination }
        }
        "cat" => Command::Cat(one_path(rest)?),
        "rm" => Command::Rm(one_path(rest)?),
        "rmdir" => Command::Rmdir(one_path(rest)?),
        _ => return Err(ParseError::UnknownCommand),
    };

    Ok(Some(command))
}

fn take_word(input: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str)> {
    let input = input.trim_start();
    if input.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let end = input.find(char::is_whitespace).unwrap_or(input.len());
    Some((&input[..end], input[end..].trim_start()))
}

fn no_arguments(rest: &str) -> Result<(), ParseError> {
    if rest.is_empty() {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(ParseError::TooManyArguments)
    }
}

fn optional_path(rest: &str) -> Result<Option<&str>, ParseError> {
    match take_word(rest) {
        None => Ok(None),
        Some((path, rest)) => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Ok(Some(path))
        }
    }
}

fn one_path(rest: &str) -> Result<&str, ParseError> {
    let (path, rest) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    no_arguments(rest)?;
    Ok(path)
}

fn two_paths(rest: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), ParseError> {
    let (source, rest) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    let (destination, rest) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    no_arguments(rest)?;
    Ok((source, destination))
}

fn path_and_text(rest: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), ParseError> {
    let (path, text) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    if text.is_empty() {
        return Err(ParseError::MissingText);
    }

    let first = text.as_bytes()[0];
    if first == b'\'' || first == b'"' {
        if text.len() < 2 || text.as_bytes()[text.len() - 1] != first {
            return Err(ParseError::UnterminatedQuote);
        }
        return Ok((path, &text[1..text.len() - 1]));
    }

    Ok((path, text))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{parse, Command, ParseError};

    #[test]
    fn blank_lines_are_ignored() {
        assert_eq!(parse(" \t "), Ok(None));
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_basic_navigation_and_file_commands() {
        assert_eq!(parse("pwd"), Ok(Some(Command::Pwd)));
        assert_eq!(parse("ls /home"), Ok(Some(Command::Ls(Some("/home")))));
        assert_eq!(parse("cd .."), Ok(Some(Command::Cd(".."))));
        assert_eq!(parse("mkdir /tmp/work"), Ok(Some(Command::Mkdir("/tmp/work"))));
        assert_eq!(parse("touch note.txt"), Ok(Some(Command::Touch("note.txt"))));
        assert_eq!(parse("cat note.txt"), Ok(Some(Command::Cat("note.txt"))));
        assert_eq!(
            parse("cp note.txt copy.txt"),
            Ok(Some(Command::Cp {
                source: "note.txt",
                destination: "copy.txt",
            }))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse("mv copy.txt saved.txt"),
            Ok(Some(Command::Mv {
                source: "copy.txt",
                destination: "saved.txt",
            }))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_preserves_spaces_and_strips_outer_quotes() {
        assert_eq!(
            parse("write greeting.txt hello from crabshell"),
            Ok(Some(Command::Write {
                path: "greeting.txt",
                contents: "hello from crabshell",
            }))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse("append greeting.txt \" again\""),
            Ok(Some(Command::Append {
                path: "greeting.txt",
                contents: " again",
            }))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse("write empty.txt \"\""),
            Ok(Some(Command::Write {
                path: "empty.txt",
                contents: "",
            }))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_command_arity_and_text() {
        assert_eq!(parse("cd"), Err(ParseError::MissingArgument));
        assert_eq!(parse("pwd now"), Err(ParseError::TooManyArguments));
        assert_eq!(parse("cp only-one"), Err(ParseError::MissingArgument));
        assert_eq!(parse("mv a b c"), Err(ParseError::TooManyArguments));
        assert_eq!(parse("write file"), Err(ParseError::MissingText));
        assert_eq!(parse("write file \"unfinished"), Err(ParseError::UnterminatedQuote));
        assert_eq!(parse("not-a-command"), Err(ParseError::UnknownCommand));
    }
}

//! Fixed-capacity volatile filesystem for the early kernel shell.
//!
//! This is an in-memory namespace only: it has no disk driver, persistence,
//! permissions, timestamps, links, or concurrent access support.

#![allow(clippy::large_stack_arrays)]

/// Root directory node identifier.
pub const ROOT_NODE: usize = 0;
/// Maximum number of nodes, including the root directory.
pub const MAX_NODES: usize = 32;
/// Maximum UTF-8 bytes in one path component.
pub const NAME_CAPACITY: usize = 31;
/// Maximum bytes in one file.
pub const FILE_CAPACITY: usize = 1024;
/// Maximum byte length of an absolute path in this filesystem.
pub const MAX_PATH_CAPACITY: usize = MAX_NODES * (NAME_CAPACITY + 1) + 1;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EntryKind {
    Directory,
    File,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FsError {
    InvalidPath,
    InvalidName,
    NameTooLong,
    AlreadyExists,
    NotFound,
    NotDirectory,
    IsDirectory,
    DirectoryNotEmpty,
    NoSpace,
    FileTooLarge,
    RootOperation,
    BufferTooSmall,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Entry<'a> {
    pub name: &'a str,
    pub kind: EntryKind,
    pub size: usize,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Node {
    used: bool,
    kind: EntryKind,
    parent: usize,
    name: [u8; NAME_CAPACITY],
    name_len: u8,
    data: [u8; FILE_CAPACITY],
    data_len: usize,
}

impl Node {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        used: false,
        kind: EntryKind::File,
        parent: ROOT_NODE,
        name: [0; NAME_CAPACITY],
        name_len: 0,
        data: [0; FILE_CAPACITY],
        data_len: 0,
    };

    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        core::str::from_utf8(&self.name[..usize::from(self.name_len)]).unwrap_or("")
    }
}

/// A small fixed-capacity filesystem suitable for the pre-allocator shell.
pub struct RamFs {
    nodes: [Node; MAX_NODES],
}

impl RamFs {
    /// Construct a filesystem containing only its root directory.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        let mut nodes = [Node::EMPTY; MAX_NODES];
        nodes[ROOT_NODE] = Node {
            used: true,
            kind: EntryKind::Directory,
            parent: ROOT_NODE,
            name: [0; NAME_CAPACITY],
            name_len: 0,
            data: [0; FILE_CAPACITY],
            data_len: 0,
        };
        Self { nodes }
    }

    /// Create a starter Unix-like directory tree and return `/home/rustix`.
    pub fn seed_defaults(&mut self) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "bin")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "dev")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "etc")?;
        let home = self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "home")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "tmp")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "var")?;
        let user_home = self.create_dir(home, "rustix")?;
        let motd = self.create_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/etc/motd")?;
        self.write_file(motd, b"Welcome to Rustix. Files in this early shell are volatile RAM files.\n")?;
        Ok(user_home)
    }

    /// Resolve a path from a working directory. `/`, repeated separators, `.`
    /// and `..` are handled; every intermediate component must be a directory.
    pub fn resolve(&self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        if path.is_empty() {
            return Err(FsError::InvalidPath);
        }
        let mut current = if path.starts_with('/') { ROOT_NODE } else { cwd };
        let start = self.node(current)?;
        if start.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }

        for component in path.split('/') {
            if component.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            if self.node(current)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
                return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
            }
            match component {
                "." => {}
                ".." => current = self.node(current)?.parent,
                name => {
                    current = self
                        .find_child(current, name)
                        .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)?;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(current)
    }

    pub fn create_dir(&mut self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_node(parent, name, EntryKind::Directory)
    }

    pub fn create_file(&mut self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_node(parent, name, EntryKind::File)
    }

    pub fn create_dir_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(path)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        self.create_dir(parent, name)
    }

    pub fn create_file_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(path)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        self.create_file(parent, name)
    }

    /// Return an existing file node or create it if its path does not exist.
    pub fn open_or_create_file(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        match self.resolve(cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => {
                if self.node(node)?.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
                    Err(FsError::IsDirectory)
                } else {
                    Ok(node)
                }
            }
            Err(FsError::NotFound) => self.create_file_path(cwd, path),
            Err(error) => Err(error),
        }
    }

    pub fn kind(&self, node: usize) -> Result<EntryKind, FsError> {
        Ok(self.node(node)?.kind)
    }

    pub fn read_file(&self, node: usize) -> Result<&[u8], FsError> {
        let node = self.node(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        Ok(&node.data[..node.data_len])
    }

    pub fn write_file(&mut self, node: usize, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if contents.len() > FILE_CAPACITY {
            return Err(FsError::FileTooLarge);
        }
        let node = self.node_mut(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        node.data[..contents.len()].copy_from_slice(contents);
        node.data[contents.len()..].fill(0);
        node.data_len = contents.len();
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn append_file(&mut self, node: usize, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.node_mut(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        let new_len = node
            .data_len
            .checked_add(contents.len())
            .filter(|length| *length <= FILE_CAPACITY)
            .ok_or(FsError::FileTooLarge)?;
        node.data[node.data_len..new_len].copy_from_slice(contents);
        node.data_len = new_len;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Copy a file to a destination path, replacing an existing destination file.
    pub fn copy_file_path(
        &mut self,
        cwd: usize,
        source_path: &str,
        destination_path: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let source = self.resolve(cwd, source_path)?;
        let mut contents = [0u8; FILE_CAPACITY];
        let length = {
            let source_contents = self.read_file(source)?;
            contents[..source_contents.len()].copy_from_slice(source_contents);
            source_contents.len()
        };
        let destination = self.open_or_create_file(cwd, destination_path)?;
        self.write_file(destination, &contents[..length])
    }

    /// Move or rename a file. Existing destinations are never overwritten.
    pub fn move_file_path(
        &mut self,
        cwd: usize,
        source_path: &str,
        destination_path: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let source = self.resolve(cwd, source_path)?;
        if source == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        if self.kind(source)? == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }

        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(destination_path)?;
        validate_name(name)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        if self.node(parent)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        if let Some(existing) = self.find_child(parent, name) {
            return if existing == source {
                Ok(())
            } else {
                Err(FsError::AlreadyExists)
            };
        }

        let node = self.node_mut(source)?;
        node.parent = parent;
        node.name.fill(0);
        node.name[..name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        node.name_len = name.len() as u8;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_file(&mut self, node: usize) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if node == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        let entry = self.node(node)?;
        if entry.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        self.nodes[node] = Node::EMPTY;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_dir(&mut self, node: usize) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if node == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        let entry = self.node(node)?;
        if entry.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        if self.nodes.iter().any(|child| child.used && child.parent == node) {
            return Err(FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty);
        }
        self.nodes[node] = Node::EMPTY;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_file_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.resolve(cwd, path)?;
        self.remove_file(node)
    }

    pub fn remove_dir_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.resolve(cwd, path)?;
        self.remove_dir(node)
    }

    pub fn entry(&self, node: usize) -> Result<Entry<'_>, FsError> {
        let node = self.node(node)?;
        Ok(Entry {
            name: node.name(),
            kind: node.kind,
            size: node.data_len,
        })
    }

    pub fn child_count(&self, directory: usize) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        if self.node(directory)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        Ok(self
            .nodes
            .iter()
            .filter(|node| {
                            node.used
                                && node.parent == directory
                                && !(directory == ROOT_NODE && node.name_len == 0)
                        })
            .count())
    }

    pub fn child_at(&self, directory: usize, ordinal: usize) -> Option<Entry<'_>> {
        if self.node(directory).ok()?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return None;
        }
        self.nodes
            .iter()
            .filter(|node| node.used && node.parent == directory && !(directory == ROOT_NODE && node.name_len == 0))
            .nth(ordinal)
            .map(|node| Entry {
                name: node.name(),
                kind: node.kind,
                size: node.data_len,
            })
    }

    /// Write an absolute path into caller-provided storage and return its length.
    pub fn write_path(&self, node: usize, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.node(node)?;
        let mut ancestors = [ROOT_NODE; MAX_NODES];
        let mut depth = 0;
        let mut current = node;
        while current != ROOT_NODE {
            if depth == MAX_NODES {
                return Err(FsError::InvalidPath);
            }
            ancestors[depth] = current;
            depth += 1;
            current = self.node(current)?.parent;
        }

        let required = 1 + (0..depth).map(|index| self.nodes[ancestors[index]].name_len as usize).sum::<usize>() + depth.saturating_sub(1);
        if output.len() < required {
            return Err(FsError::BufferTooSmall);
        }

        output[0] = b'/';
        let mut length = 1;
        for index in (0..depth).rev() {
            if length > 1 {
                output[length] = b'/';
                length += 1;
            }
            let name = self.nodes[ancestors[index]].name();
            output[length..length + name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
            length += name.len();
        }
        Ok(length)
    }

    fn create_node(
        &mut self,
        parent: usize,
        name: &str,
        kind: EntryKind,
    ) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let parent_node = self.node(parent)?;
        if parent_node.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        validate_name(name)?;
        if self.find_child(parent, name).is_some() {
            return Err(FsError::AlreadyExists);
        }
        let index = self
            .nodes
            .iter()
            .position(|node| !node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NoSpace)?;
        let mut node = Node::EMPTY;
        node.used = true;
        node.kind = kind;
        node.parent = parent;
        node.name[..name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        node.name_len = name.len() as u8;
        self.nodes[index] = node;
        Ok(index)
    }

    fn find_child(&self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        self.nodes.iter().position(|node| {
            node.used && node.parent == parent && node.name_len != 0 && node.name() == name
        })
    }

    fn node(&self, index: usize) -> Result<&Node, FsError> {
        self.nodes
            .get(index)
            .filter(|node| node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)
    }

    fn node_mut(&mut self, index: usize) -> Result<&mut Node, FsError> {
        self.nodes
            .get_mut(index)
            .filter(|node| node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)
    }
}

impl Default for RamFs {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

fn validate_name(name: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
    if name.is_empty() || name == "." || name == ".." || name.contains('/') || name.contains('\0') {
        return Err(FsError::InvalidName);
    }
    if name.len() > NAME_CAPACITY {
        return Err(FsError::NameTooLong);
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn split_parent(path: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), FsError> {
    let path = path.trim_end_matches('/');
    if path.is_empty() {
        return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
    }
    match path.rsplit_once('/') {
        Some(("", name)) => Ok(("/", name)),
        Some((parent, name)) if !name.is_empty() => Ok((parent, name)),
        Some(_) => Err(FsError::InvalidPath),
        None => Ok((".", path)),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{EntryKind, FsError, RamFs, ROOT_NODE};

    #[test]
    fn resolves_absolute_relative_and_parent_components() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let home = fs.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "home").unwrap();
        let user = fs.create_dir(home, "rustix").unwrap();
        let notes = fs.create_dir(user, "notes").unwrap();

        assert_eq!(fs.resolve(user, ".").unwrap(), user);
        assert_eq!(fs.resolve(notes, "../..").unwrap(), home);
        assert_eq!(fs.resolve(ROOT_NODE, "/home/rustix/notes/").unwrap(), notes);
    }

    #[test]
    fn creates_reads_appends_and_removes_files() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let file = fs.create_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/note.txt").unwrap();
        fs.write_file(file, b"hello").unwrap();
        fs.append_file(file, b" rustix").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs.read_file(file).unwrap(), b"hello rustix");
        fs.remove_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/note.txt").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs.resolve(ROOT_NODE, "/note.txt"), Err(FsError::NotFound));
    }

    #[test]
    fn copies_and_moves_files_without_overwriting_destinations() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let source = fs.create_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/source.txt").unwrap();
        fs.write_file(source, b"data").unwrap();

        fs.copy_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/source.txt", "/copy.txt")
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs.read_file(fs.resolve(ROOT_NODE, "/copy.txt").unwrap()), Ok(&b"data"[..]));
        fs.move_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/copy.txt", "/saved.txt")
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs.resolve(ROOT_NODE, "/copy.txt"), Err(FsError::NotFound));
        assert_eq!(fs.read_file(fs.resolve(ROOT_NODE, "/saved.txt").unwrap()), Ok(&b"data"[..]));
        assert_eq!(
            fs.move_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/source.txt", "/saved.txt"),
            Err(FsError::AlreadyExists)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn refuses_to_remove_nonempty_directories() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let directory = fs.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "work").unwrap();
        fs.create_file(directory, "note").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs.remove_dir(directory), Err(FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty));
    }

    #[test]
    fn path_output_and_kinds_are_consistent() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let docs = fs.create_dir_path(ROOT_NODE, "/home").unwrap();
        let file = fs.create_file(docs, "readme").unwrap();
        let mut path = [0; 64];
        let length = fs.write_path(file, &mut path).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(&path[..length], b"/home/readme");
        assert_eq!(fs.kind(docs), Ok(EntryKind::Directory));
        assert_eq!(fs.kind(file), Ok(EntryKind::File));
    }
}

```
//! Kernel-side Crabshell frontend: serial input, prompts, and RAM-filesystem commands.

use crabshell::{parse, Command, ParseError, MAX_LINE_LENGTH};
use rustix_kernel::vfs::{EntryKind, FsError, RamFs, MAX_PATH_CAPACITY};

use crate::arch::x86_64::serial;

/// Run Crabshell forever on the bootstrap CPU.
pub fn run(filesystem: &mut RamFs, mut cwd: usize) -> ! {
    crate::kprintln!("crabshell: ready (volatile RAM filesystem)");
    print_motd(filesystem, cwd);

    let mut input = [0u8; MAX_LINE_LENGTH];
    loop {
        print_prompt(filesystem, cwd);
        let length = read_line(&mut input);
        if length == 0 {
            continue;
        }

        let line = match core::str::from_utf8(&input[..length]) {
            Ok(line) => line,
            Err(_) => {
                crate::kprintln!("crabshell: input must be valid UTF-8");
                continue;
            }
        };

        match parse(line) {
            Ok(Some(command)) => execute(command, filesystem, &mut cwd),
            Ok(None) => {}
            Err(error) => print_parse_error(error),
        }
    }
}

fn print_prompt(filesystem: &RamFs, cwd: usize) {
    let mut path = [0u8; MAX_PATH_CAPACITY];
    match filesystem.write_path(cwd, &mut path) {
        Ok(length) => match core::str::from_utf8(&path[..length]) {
            Ok(path) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:{}# ", path)),
            Err(_) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:/?# ")),
        },
        Err(_) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:/?# ")),
    }
}

fn read_line(input: &mut [u8; MAX_LINE_LENGTH]) -> usize {
    let mut length = 0;
    loop {
        let Some(byte) = serial::try_read_byte() else {
            core::hint::spin_loop();
            continue;
        };

        match byte {
            b'\r' | b'\n' => {
                crate::kprintln!();
                return length;
            }
            0x03 => {
                crate::kprintln!("^C");
                return 0;
            }
            0x08 | 0x7f if length > 0 => {
                length -= 1;
                serial::print(format_args!("\x08 \x08"));
            }
            0x20..=0x7e if length < input.len() => {
                input[length] = byte;
                length += 1;
                serial::print(format_args!("{}", byte as char));
            }
            0x20..=0x7e => serial::print(format_args!("\x07")),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

fn execute(command: Command<'_>, filesystem: &mut RamFs, cwd: &mut usize) {
    match command {
        Command::Help => print_help(),
        Command::Clear => serial::print(format_args!("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")),
        Command::Pwd => {
            let mut path = [0u8; MAX_PATH_CAPACITY];
            match filesystem.write_path(*cwd, &mut path) {
                Ok(length) => match core::str::from_utf8(&path[..length]) {
                    Ok(path) => crate::kprintln!("{}", path),
                    Err(_) => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: could not display current path"),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            }
        }
        Command::Ls(path) => {
            let directory = match path {
                Some(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
                    Ok(node) => node,
                    Err(error) => {
                        report_fs_error(error);
                        return;
                    }
                },
                None => *cwd,
            };
            list_directory(filesystem, directory);
        }
        Command::Cd(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.kind(node) {
                Ok(EntryKind::Directory) => *cwd = node,
                Ok(EntryKind::File) => report_fs_error(FsError::NotDirectory),
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Mkdir(path) => match filesystem.create_dir_path(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Touch(path) => match filesystem.open_or_create_file(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Write { path, contents } => {
            match filesystem.open_or_create_file(*cwd, path) {
                Ok(node) => match filesystem.write_file(node, contents.as_bytes()) {
                    Ok(()) => {}
                    Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            }
        }
        Command::Append { path, contents } => {
            match filesystem.open_or_create_file(*cwd, path) {
                Ok(node) => match filesystem.append_file(node, contents.as_bytes()) {
                    Ok(()) => {}
                    Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            }
        }
        Command::Cp {
            source,
            destination,
        } => match filesystem.copy_file_path(*cwd, source, destination) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Mv {
            source,
            destination,
        } => match filesystem.move_file_path(*cwd, source, destination) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Cat(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.read_file(node) {
                Ok(bytes) => match core::str::from_utf8(bytes) {
                    Ok(text) => print_file_contents(text),
                    Err(_) => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: binary file display is not supported"),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Rm(path) => match filesystem.remove_file_path(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Rmdir(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) if node == *cwd => {
                crate::kprintln!("crabshell: cannot remove the current directory");
            }
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.remove_dir(node) {
                Ok(()) => {}
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
    }
}

fn list_directory(filesystem: &RamFs, directory: usize) {
    match filesystem.kind(directory) {
        Ok(EntryKind::File) => match filesystem.entry(directory) {
            Ok(entry) => crate::kprintln!("{} ({} bytes)", entry.name, entry.size),
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        Ok(EntryKind::Directory) => match filesystem.child_count(directory) {
            Ok(0) => crate::kprintln!("(empty)"),
            Ok(count) => {
                for index in 0..count {
                    let Some(entry) = filesystem.child_at(directory, index) else {
                        crate::kprintln!("crabshell: directory changed while listing");
                        return;
                    };
                    match entry.kind {
                        EntryKind::Directory => crate::kprintln!("{}/", entry.name),
                        EntryKind::File => {
                            crate::kprintln!("{}  {} bytes", entry.name, entry.size)
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
    }
}

fn print_file_contents(text: &str) {
    for (index, line) in text.split('\n').enumerate() {
        if index != 0 {
            serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
        }
        serial::print(format_args!("{}", line.strip_suffix('\r').unwrap_or(line)));
    }
    if !text.ends_with('\n') {
        crate::kprintln!();
    }
}

fn print_motd(filesystem: &RamFs, cwd: usize) {
    if let Ok(node) = filesystem.resolve(cwd, "/etc/motd") {
        if let Ok(bytes) = filesystem.read_file(node) {
            if let Ok(text) = core::str::from_utf8(bytes) {
                print_file_contents(text);
            }
        }
    }
}

fn print_help() {
    crate::kprintln!("Crabshell commands:");
    crate::kprintln!("  help                 show this help");
    crate::kprintln!("  clear                clear an ANSI-compatible terminal");
    crate::kprintln!("  pwd                  print the current directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  ls [PATH]            list a directory or file");
    crate::kprintln!("  cd PATH              change the current directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  mkdir PATH            create a directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  touch PATH            create an empty file");
    crate::kprintln!("  write PATH TEXT       replace a file's contents");
    crate::kprintln!("  append PATH TEXT      append text to a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  cp SOURCE DEST        copy a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  mv SOURCE DEST        move/rename a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  cat PATH              print a text file");
    crate::kprintln!("  rm PATH               remove a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  rmdir PATH            remove an empty directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  write/append accept a quoted or unquoted text remainder.");
    crate::kprintln!("  RAM filesystem: 31 entries plus root; files up to 1024 bytes.");
}

fn print_parse_error(error: ParseError) {
    match error {
        ParseError::UnknownCommand => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: unknown command (try 'help')"),
        ParseError::MissingArgument => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: missing path argument"),
        ParseError::MissingText => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: missing text (usage: write PATH TEXT)"),
        ParseError::TooManyArguments => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: too many arguments"),
        ParseError::UnterminatedQuote => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: unterminated text quote"),
    }
}

fn report_fs_error(error: FsError) {
    let message = match error {
        FsError::InvalidPath => "invalid path",
        FsError::InvalidName => "invalid file name",
        FsError::NameTooLong => "file name is too long (maximum 31 UTF-8 bytes)",
        FsError::AlreadyExists => "an entry with that name already exists",
        FsError::NotFound => "path not found",
        FsError::NotDirectory => "a path component is not a directory",
        FsError::IsDirectory => "operation requires a file, not a directory",
        FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty => "directory is not empty",
        FsError::NoSpace => "RAM filesystem is full",
        FsError::FileTooLarge => "file exceeds the 1024-byte limit",
        FsError::RootOperation => "operation is not permitted on the root directory",
        FsError::BufferTooSmall => "path exceeds the display buffer",
    };
    crate::kprintln!("crabshell: {}", message);
}

# Crabshell and the early RAM filesystem

Crabshell is Rustix's first command-line interface. The current implementation is a **kernel-mode bootstrap shell** attached to COM1, not a separate user process. Its command parser is isolated in a separate crate so the same grammar can later be reused by a graphical terminal frontend or by a userspace terminal application.

## Crate boundary

- `crates/crabshell` is an allocation-free `no_std` Rust library. It parses a borrowed command line into a `Command` value and performs no I/O, filesystem access, scheduling, or privilege changes.
- `src/shell.rs` adapts the parser to the kernel serial driver, provides a small line editor, implements commands, and owns the current working-directory node.
- `src/vfs.rs` is a fixed-capacity in-memory filesystem used by the early shell. It is not a disk filesystem and is not persistent.

This is a useful separation now: future terminal frontends can reuse parsing without importing kernel hardware or filesystem code. A future user-mode Crabshell should keep its frontend/parser layer but execute operations through a documented syscall/VFS interface; it must not link the kernel's internal filesystem as a privilege shortcut.

## Build and run

```sh
just test
just image
just smoke
just run
```

`just run` starts a headless QEMU machine and connects the guest serial port to the current terminal. Use `Ctrl+C` in the host terminal to stop QEMU. The BIOS/UEFI boot image is `target/rustix.iso`.

The kernel welcomes the user in `/home/rustix`. The initial namespace contains `/bin`, `/dev`, `/etc`, `/home/rustix`, `/tmp`, and `/var`; `/etc/motd` explains that storage is volatile.

## Commands

| Command | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `help` | List available commands and limits. |
| `clear` | Send the ANSI clear-screen/home sequence. |
| `pwd` | Print the absolute working directory. |
| `ls [PATH]` | List a directory; a file path prints that file's name and size. Defaults to the current directory. |
| `cd PATH` | Change to an existing directory. Supports absolute and relative paths, `.`, and `..`. |
| `mkdir PATH` | Create one directory; its parent must already exist. |
| `touch PATH` | Create an empty file, or leave an existing file unchanged. |
| `write PATH TEXT` | Create a file if needed and replace its contents with the remaining line. Matching outer single or double quotes around the text are removed. |
| `append PATH TEXT` | Create a file if needed and append the remaining line. |
| `cp SOURCE DEST` | Copy a file; an existing destination file is replaced. |
| `mv SOURCE DEST` | Move/rename a file; directories and existing destinations are rejected. |
| `cat PATH` | Print a UTF-8 text file. Binary data is not displayed. |
| `rm PATH` | Remove a file. Directories are rejected. |
| `rmdir PATH` | Remove an empty directory other than the current directory. |

Example:

```text
root@rustix:/home/rustix# mkdir notes
root@rustix:/home/rustix# write notes/hello.txt "hello from Rustix"
root@rustix:/home/rustix# cat notes/hello.txt
hello from Rustix
root@rustix:/home/rustix# cd ..
root@rustix:/home# pwd
/home
```

The grammar intentionally does not yet support quoted paths, escaped quotes, variables, pipes, redirection, globbing, command substitution, history, or a process launcher. Input is a single ASCII line (up to 256 bytes) from the serial port.

## RAM filesystem contract

- The root plus at most 31 live entries fit in the fixed 32-node table.
- Path components are limited to 31 UTF-8 bytes; file contents are limited to 1024 bytes each.
- Paths may be absolute or relative and support repeated `/`, `.`, and `..`.
- `write` replaces a file; `append` adds bytes; `touch` never truncates.
- `cp` copies files; `mv` moves files only and never overwrites an existing destination. `rm` handles files only. `rmdir` refuses non-empty directories and the current directory.
- Filesystem allocation is fixed-capacity; errors are reported rather than allocating a heap.
- Every file and directory disappears when the machine resets. There is no block device, journaling, metadata persistence, permission model, links, or concurrent access yet.

## Tests and limitations

Host-side tests cover path traversal, file create/write/append/copy/move/remove, entry kinds, path rendering, directory emptiness, and the parser's syntax/arity. The QEMU smoke test checks that the serial shell reaches its prompt; it does not emulate reboot persistence or prove isolation. Since the shell runs in ring 0, a parser or filesystem bug can panic the entire kernel. This implementation must not be presented as a secure or POSIX-compliant shell.

# Crabshell command parser

`crabshell` is a small `no_std`, allocation-free Rust library containing the command enum and parser used by the Rustix shell. It intentionally knows nothing about serial terminals, kernel privileges, filesystems, or process management.

The initial grammar supports `help`, `clear`, `pwd`, `ls`, `cd`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `write`, `append`, `cp`, `mv`, `cat`, `rm`, and `rmdir`. `write` and `append` borrow the remaining text from the input line and optionally remove matching outer quotes. See [`../../docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](../../docs/architecture/crabshell.md) for command semantics, limits, and current kernel integration.

Run its parser tests from the repository root with `cargo test -p crabshell --lib` or `just test`.

# Rustix

Rustix (Rust-unix) is an experimental, 64-bit, Unix-like operating system whose kernel is written in Rust. This repository builds the kernel itself; Limine is used only as the external boot protocol/loader, not as a substitute for a Rustix kernel.

Rustix now boots into **Crabshell**, a small kernel-mode shell on the COM1 serial terminal. It includes basic navigation and file commands backed by a fixed-capacity RAM filesystem. The filesystem is volatile and reset at every boot; this is an early kernel shell, not a userspace process or POSIX shell. The command parser lives in a separate, allocation-free `crabshell` crate so a future GUI terminal can reuse it. Scheduling, process isolation, persistent storage, a syscall ABI, networking, and userspace are still future work. See [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) for the staged plan.

## Quick start

Prerequisites: a Rust stable toolchain, `just`, Python 3, `xorriso`, QEMU (`qemu-system-x86_64`), and the target installed by `rust-toolchain.toml` (or `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`). The first image build downloads a pinned Limine binary release and verifies its SHA-256.

```sh
just help
just fmt
just test
just check
just build
just image
just smoke
just run       # interactive serial shell in QEMU; exit with Ctrl+C
just verify
```

`just build` produces `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `just image` creates `target/rustix.iso`, a hybrid BIOS/UEFI image; `just smoke` checks that Crabshell reaches its prompt; and `just run` starts an interactive QEMU session attached to the current terminal.

Try `pwd`, `ls /`, `mkdir notes`, `write notes/hello.txt "hello from Rustix"`, `cat notes/hello.txt`, and `cd ..` in Crabshell. Commands include `help`, `clear`, `pwd`, `ls`, `cd`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `write`, `append`, `cp`, `mv`, `cat`, `rm`, and `rmdir`. The RAM filesystem holds at most 32 entries, with files capped at 1024 bytes. See [`docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](docs/architecture/crabshell.md) for the shell and filesystem contract, [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) for build/emulator details, and [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) for the documentation map.

## Project principles

- The kernel and operating-system implementation are Rust-first and `no_std`; architecture-specific privileged operations are isolated under `src/arch/`.
- The kernel is the product. A bootloader may initialize the machine and transfer control, but policy, memory management, scheduling, and Unix-like services belong to Rustix.
- Keep unsafe code small, documented, and adjacent to its hardware/protocol boundary.
- Build incrementally: every roadmap milestone should have build checks, tests where practical, and updated design documentation.
- Unix-like behavior is an explicit compatibility goal, not a claim of POSIX compliance today.

## Repository map

- `src/main.rs` — freestanding kernel entry point and Crabshell handoff.
- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel command executor.
- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem, with host-side tests.
- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` command parser crate; no I/O or filesystem coupling.
- `src/boot.rs` — Limine requests and boot-memory-map reporting.
- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — early COM1 polling driver.
- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling.
- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers.
- `src/memory.rs` — architecture-independent boot-time memory accounting and host tests.
- `.cargo/config.toml`, `linker.ld` — x86_64-none code generation and ELF layout.
- `justfile` — formatting, tests, target checks, image creation, emulator smoke test, and aggregate verification.
- `limine.conf` — pinned boot configuration for the Rustix kernel.
- `scripts/boot.py` — checksum-verified Limine download, hybrid ISO assembly, and bounded QEMU validation.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — runs `just verify` on pushes and pull requests.
- `docs/` — architecture, drivers, development, security, and roadmap documentation.

# Testing and verification

## Current checks

`just verify` runs the intended pre-change sequence:

1. `just fmt` — fail on formatting differences across the workspace.
2. `just test` — run host-side memory, RAM-filesystem, and Crabshell parser tests.
3. `just check` — check the `x86_64-unknown-none` kernel target.
4. `just smoke` — build the pinned hybrid ISO, boot it in QEMU, and check that Crabshell reaches its prompt within a deadline.

Keep the Crabshell parser and VFS independent of hardware so syntax, path handling, and storage semantics (including copy and move) can be tested without booting. Add tests for boundaries and failure behavior when introducing new pure kernel helpers. The kernel binary is not a host test target.

## What current checks do not prove

- `cargo check` does not perform a final target link.
- A successful ELF link does not prove the boot protocol is recognized or `_start` is reached.
- Host unit tests do not validate privileged instructions, UART behavior, memory-map pointer validity, page tables, interrupts, or actual hardware.
- The QEMU smoke test proves the kernel reaches the shell prompt; it does not yet send interactive file commands or prove persistence across reboot.
- There is no on-disk filesystem integration test, syscall/userspace test, fuzz target, or physical-hardware test.

## Validation policy

For changes to the kernel entry, linker script, boot requests, architecture code, shell, or VFS, run `just verify`. For memory-management and ABI code, add negative tests for overflow, malformed ranges, permission failures, and invalid user pointers before exposing those paths to userspace.

Record commands actually run and any environment limitation in change summaries; never call an unexecuted build “passing.”

```

   366	            return Err(FsError::BufferTooSmall);
   367	        }

     1	# x86_64 drivers
     2	
     3	## Driver boundary
     4	
     5	Rustix keeps privileged platform access in `src/arch/x86_64/`. Device-facing routines should be small, explicit about polling/interrupt assumptions, and separated from policy such as terminal input or process I/O. The current drivers are intentionally early-boot building blocks, not a finished device model.
     6	
     7	## Implemented drivers
     8	
     9	| Driver | Source | Status and limits |
    10	|---|---|---|
    11	| 16550-compatible COM1 serial | [`src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs`](../../src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs) | Initialized during `_start`; polling formatted output; bounded transmit waits; intended for boot diagnostics. |
    12	| x86 port I/O primitives | [`src/arch/x86_64/io.rs`](../../src/arch/x86_64/io.rs) | Small unsafe `in`/`out` wrappers used by platform drivers. |
    13	| PS/2-compatible keyboard controller | [`src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs`](../../src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs) | Non-blocking raw-byte polling API; filters auxiliary-device and controller-error bytes. Not yet connected to a kernel input queue. |
    14	
    15	The keyboard routine assumes a legacy controller is present and enabled. It does not initialize the controller, decode scancode sets, support USB HID, or use interrupts. Callers must not spin waiting for input; use `try_read_scancode()` when the kernel has a suitable polling opportunity.
    16	
    17	## Driver development rules
    18	
    19	- Keep port I/O, MMIO, DMA, and interrupt entry points in architecture/device modules; do not expose raw I/O ports to generic kernel services.
    20	- Document required privilege level, device assumptions, concurrency/interrupt context, and whether a call can block.
    21	- Bound waits in early boot, avoid allocation in low-level paths, and propagate/report device absence rather than hanging startup.
    22	- Separate raw hardware events from key mapping, terminal semantics, and user-visible input policy.
    23	- Add emulator/hardware tests when an integration harness exists; host tests alone cannot validate port I/O.
    24	
    25	## Planned driver work
    26	
    27	Add a timer and interrupt-controller path before interrupt-driven keyboard input; establish locking and per-CPU rules before enabling concurrency. Then consider framebuffer/console output, PCI discovery, storage, and networking as independently reviewed drivers. No support for those devices is implied by this plan.

    71	        "touch" => Command::Touch(one_path(rest)?),

//! Fixed-capacity volatile filesystem for the early kernel shell.
//!
//! This is an in-memory namespace only: it has no disk driver, persistence,
//! permissions, timestamps, links, or concurrent access support.

#![allow(clippy::large_stack_arrays)]

/// Root directory node identifier.
pub const ROOT_NODE: usize = 0;
/// Maximum number of nodes, including the root directory.
pub const MAX_NODES: usize = 32;
/// Maximum UTF-8 bytes in one path component.
pub const NAME_CAPACITY: usize = 31;
/// Maximum bytes in one file.
pub const FILE_CAPACITY: usize = 1024;
/// Maximum byte length of an absolute path in this filesystem.
pub const MAX_PATH_CAPACITY: usize = MAX_NODES * (NAME_CAPACITY + 1) + 1;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EntryKind {
    Directory,
    File,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FsError {
    InvalidPath,
    InvalidName,
    NameTooLong,
    AlreadyExists,
    NotFound,
    NotDirectory,
    IsDirectory,
    DirectoryNotEmpty,
    NoSpace,
    FileTooLarge,
    RootOperation,
    BufferTooSmall,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Entry<'a> {
    pub name: &'a str,
    pub kind: EntryKind,
    pub size: usize,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Node {
    used: bool,
    kind: EntryKind,
    parent: usize,
    name: [u8; NAME_CAPACITY],
    name_len: u8,
    data: [u8; FILE_CAPACITY],
    data_len: usize,
}

impl Node {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        used: false,
        kind: EntryKind::File,
        parent: ROOT_NODE,
        name: [0; NAME_CAPACITY],
        name_len: 0,
        data: [0; FILE_CAPACITY],
        data_len: 0,
    };

    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        core::str::from_utf8(&self.name[..usize::from(self.name_len)]).unwrap_or("")
    }
}

/// A small fixed-capacity filesystem suitable for the pre-allocator shell.
pub struct RamFs {
    nodes: [Node; MAX_NODES],
}

impl RamFs {
    /// Construct a filesystem containing only its root directory.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        let mut nodes = [Node::EMPTY; MAX_NODES];
        nodes[ROOT_NODE] = Node {
            used: true,
            kind: EntryKind::Directory,
            parent: ROOT_NODE,
            name: [0; NAME_CAPACITY],
            name_len: 0,
            data: [0; FILE_CAPACITY],
            data_len: 0,
        };
        Self { nodes }
    }

    /// Create a starter Unix-like directory tree and return `/home/rustix`.
    pub fn seed_defaults(&mut self) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "bin")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "dev")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "etc")?;
        let home = self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "home")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "tmp")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "var")?;
        let user_home = self.create_dir(home, "rustix")?;
        let motd = self.create_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/etc/motd")?;
        self.write_file(
            motd,
            b"Welcome to Rustix. Files in this early shell are volatile RAM files.\n",
        )?;
        Ok(user_home)
    }

    /// Resolve a path from a working directory. `/`, repeated separators, `.`
    /// and `..` are handled; every intermediate component must be a directory.
    pub fn resolve(&self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        if path.is_empty() {
            return Err(FsError::InvalidPath);
        }
        let mut current = if path.starts_with('/') {
            ROOT_NODE
        } else {
            cwd
        };
        let start = self.node(current)?;
        if start.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }

        for component in path.split('/') {
            if component.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            if self.node(current)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
                return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
            }
            match component {
                "." => {}
                ".." => current = self.node(current)?.parent,
                name => {
                    current = self
                        .find_child(current, name)
                        .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)?;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(current)
    }

    pub fn create_dir(&mut self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_node(parent, name, EntryKind::Directory)
    }

    pub fn create_file(&mut self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_node(parent, name, EntryKind::File)
    }

    pub fn create_dir_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(path)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        self.create_dir(parent, name)
    }

    pub fn create_file_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(path)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        self.create_file(parent, name)
    }

    /// Return an existing file node or create it if its path does not exist.
    pub fn open_or_create_file(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        match self.resolve(cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => {
                if self.node(node)?.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
                    Err(FsError::IsDirectory)
                } else {
                    Ok(node)
                }
            }
            Err(FsError::NotFound) => self.create_file_path(cwd, path),
            Err(error) => Err(error),
        }
    }

    pub fn kind(&self, node: usize) -> Result<EntryKind, FsError> {
        Ok(self.node(node)?.kind)
    }

    pub fn read_file(&self, node: usize) -> Result<&[u8], FsError> {
        let node = self.node(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        Ok(&node.data[..node.data_len])
    }

    pub fn write_file(&mut self, node: usize, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if contents.len() > FILE_CAPACITY {
            return Err(FsError::FileTooLarge);
        }
        let node = self.node_mut(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        node.data[..contents.len()].copy_from_slice(contents);
        node.data[contents.len()..].fill(0);
        node.data_len = contents.len();
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn append_file(&mut self, node: usize, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.node_mut(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        let new_len = node
            .data_len
            .checked_add(contents.len())
            .filter(|length| *length <= FILE_CAPACITY)
            .ok_or(FsError::FileTooLarge)?;
        node.data[node.data_len..new_len].copy_from_slice(contents);
        node.data_len = new_len;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Copy a file to a destination path, replacing an existing destination file.
    pub fn copy_file_path(
        &mut self,
        cwd: usize,
        source_path: &str,
        destination_path: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let source = self.resolve(cwd, source_path)?;
        let mut contents = [0u8; FILE_CAPACITY];
        let length = {
            let source_contents = self.read_file(source)?;
            contents[..source_contents.len()].copy_from_slice(source_contents);
            source_contents.len()
        };
        let destination = self.open_or_create_file(cwd, destination_path)?;
        self.write_file(destination, &contents[..length])
    }

    /// Move or rename a file. Existing destinations are never overwritten.
    pub fn move_file_path(
        &mut self,
        cwd: usize,
        source_path: &str,
        destination_path: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let source = self.resolve(cwd, source_path)?;
        if source == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        if self.kind(source)? == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }

        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(destination_path)?;
        validate_name(name)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        if self.node(parent)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        if let Some(existing) = self.find_child(parent, name) {
            return if existing == source {
                Ok(())
            } else {
                Err(FsError::AlreadyExists)
            };
        }

        let node = self.node_mut(source)?;
        node.parent = parent;
        node.name.fill(0);
        node.name[..name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        node.name_len = name.len() as u8;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_file(&mut self, node: usize) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if node == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        let entry = self.node(node)?;
        if entry.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        self.nodes[node] = Node::EMPTY;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_dir(&mut self, node: usize) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if node == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        let entry = self.node(node)?;
        if entry.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        if self.nodes.iter().any(|child| child.used && child.parent == node) {
            return Err(FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty);
        }
        self.nodes[node] = Node::EMPTY;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_file_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.resolve(cwd, path)?;
        self.remove_file(node)
    }

    pub fn remove_dir_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.resolve(cwd, path)?;
        self.remove_dir(node)
    }

    pub fn entry(&self, node: usize) -> Result<Entry<'_>, FsError> {
        let node = self.node(node)?;
        Ok(Entry {
            name: node.name(),
            kind: node.kind,
            size: node.data_len,
        })
    }

    pub fn child_count(&self, directory: usize) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        if self.node(directory)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        Ok(self
            .nodes
            .iter()
            .filter(|node| {
                node.used
                    && node.parent == directory
                    && !(directory == ROOT_NODE && node.name_len == 0)
            })
            .count())
    }

    pub fn child_at(&self, directory: usize, ordinal: usize) -> Option<Entry<'_>> {
        if self.node(directory).ok()?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return None;
        }
        self.nodes
            .iter()
            .filter(|node| {
                node.used
                    && node.parent == directory
                    && !(directory == ROOT_NODE && node.name_len == 0)
            })
            .nth(ordinal)
            .map(|node| Entry {
                name: node.name(),
                kind: node.kind,
                size: node.data_len,
            })
    }

    /// Write an absolute path into caller-provided storage and return its length.
    pub fn write_path(&self, node: usize, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.node(node)?;
        let mut ancestors = [ROOT_NODE; MAX_NODES];
        let mut depth = 0;
        let mut current = node;
        while current != ROOT_NODE {
            if depth == MAX_NODES {
                return Err(FsError::InvalidPath);
            }
            ancestors[depth] = current;
            depth += 1;
            current = self.node(current)?.parent;
        }

        let component_bytes = (0..depth)
            .map(|index| usize::from(self.nodes[ancestors[index]].name_len))
            .sum::<usize>();
        let required = 1 + component_bytes + depth.saturating_sub(1);
        if output.len() < required {
            return Err(FsError::BufferTooSmall);
        }

        output[0] = b'/';
        let mut length = 1;
        for index in (0..depth).rev() {
            if length > 1 {
                output[length] = b'/';
                length += 1;
            }
            let name = self.nodes[ancestors[index]].name();
            output[length..length + name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
            length += name.len();
        }
        Ok(length)
    }

    fn create_node(
        &mut self,
        parent: usize,
        name: &str,
        kind: EntryKind,
    ) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let parent_node = self.node(parent)?;
        if parent_node.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        validate_name(name)?;
        if self.find_child(parent, name).is_some() {
            return Err(FsError::AlreadyExists);
        }
        let index = self
            .nodes
            .iter()
            .position(|node| !node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NoSpace)?;
        let mut node = Node::EMPTY;
        node.used = true;
        node.kind = kind;
        node.parent = parent;
        node.name[..name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        node.name_len = name.len() as u8;
        self.nodes[index] = node;
        Ok(index)
    }

    fn find_child(&self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        self.nodes.iter().position(|node| {
            node.used && node.parent == parent && node.name_len != 0 && node.name() == name
        })
    }

    fn node(&self, index: usize) -> Result<&Node, FsError> {
        self.nodes
            .get(index)
            .filter(|node| node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)
    }

    fn node_mut(&mut self, index: usize) -> Result<&mut Node, FsError> {
        self.nodes
            .get_mut(index)
            .filter(|node| node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)
    }
}

impl Default for RamFs {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

fn validate_name(name: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
    if name.is_empty()
        || name == "."
        || name == ".."
        || name.contains('/')
        || name.contains('\0')
    {
        return Err(FsError::InvalidName);
    }
    if name.len() > NAME_CAPACITY {
        return Err(FsError::NameTooLong);
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn split_parent(path: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), FsError> {
    let path = path.trim_end_matches('/');
    if path.is_empty() {
        return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
    }
    match path.rsplit_once('/') {
        Some(("", name)) => Ok(("/", name)),
        Some((parent, name)) if !name.is_empty() => Ok((parent, name)),
        Some(_) => Err(FsError::InvalidPath),
        None => Ok((".", path)),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{EntryKind, FsError, RamFs, ROOT_NODE};

    #[test]
    fn resolves_absolute_relative_and_parent_components() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let home = fs.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "home").unwrap();
