//! Fixed-capacity volatile filesystem for the early kernel shell.
//!
//! This is an in-memory namespace only: it has no disk driver, persistence,
//! permissions, timestamps, links, or concurrent access support.

#![allow(clippy::large_stack_arrays)]

/// Root directory node identifier.
pub const ROOT_NODE: usize = 0;
/// Maximum number of nodes, including the root directory.
pub const MAX_NODES: usize = 32;
/// Maximum UTF-8 bytes in one path component.
pub const NAME_CAPACITY: usize = 31;
/// Maximum bytes in one file.
pub const FILE_CAPACITY: usize = 1024;
/// Maximum byte length of an absolute path in this filesystem.
pub const MAX_PATH_CAPACITY: usize = MAX_NODES * (NAME_CAPACITY + 1) + 1;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EntryKind {
    Directory,
    File,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FsError {
    InvalidPath,
    InvalidName,
    NameTooLong,
    AlreadyExists,
    NotFound,
    NotDirectory,
    IsDirectory,
    DirectoryNotEmpty,
    NoSpace,
    FileTooLarge,
    RootOperation,
    BufferTooSmall,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Entry<'a> {
    pub name: &'a str,
    pub kind: EntryKind,
    pub size: usize,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Node {
    used: bool,
    kind: EntryKind,
    parent: usize,
    name: [u8; NAME_CAPACITY],
    name_len: u8,
    data: [u8; FILE_CAPACITY],
    data_len: usize,
}

impl Node {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        used: false,
        kind: EntryKind::File,
        parent: ROOT_NODE,
        name: [0; NAME_CAPACITY],
        name_len: 0,
        data: [0; FILE_CAPACITY],
        data_len: 0,
    };

    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        core::str::from_utf8(&self.name[..usize::from(self.name_len)]).unwrap_or("")
    }
}

/// A small fixed-capacity filesystem suitable for the pre-allocator shell.
pub struct RamFs {
    nodes: [Node; MAX_NODES],
}

impl RamFs {
    /// Construct a filesystem containing only its root directory.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        let mut nodes = [Node::EMPTY; MAX_NODES];
        nodes[ROOT_NODE] = Node {
            used: true,
            kind: EntryKind::Directory,
            parent: ROOT_NODE,
            name: [0; NAME_CAPACITY],
            name_len: 0,
            data: [0; FILE_CAPACITY],
            data_len: 0,
        };
        Self { nodes }
    }

    /// Create a starter Unix-like directory tree and return `/home/rustix`.
    pub fn seed_defaults(&mut self) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "bin")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "dev")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "etc")?;
        let home = self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "home")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "tmp")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "var")?;
        let user_home = self.create_dir(home, "rustix")?;
        let motd = self.create_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/etc/motd")?;
        self.write_file(
            motd,
            b"Welcome to Rustix. Files in this early shell are volatile RAM files.\n",
        )?;
        Ok(user_home)
    }

    /// Resolve a path from a working directory. `/`, repeated separators, `.`
    /// and `..` are handled; every intermediate component must be a directory.
    pub fn resolve(&self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        if path.is_empty() {
            return Err(FsError::InvalidPath);
        }
        let mut current = if path.starts_with('/') { ROOT_NODE } else { cwd };
        let start = self.node(current)?;
        if start.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }

        for component in path.split('/') {
            if component.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            if self.node(current)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
                return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
            }
            match component {
                "." => {}
                ".." => current = self.node(current)?.parent,
                name => {
                    current = self
                        .find_child(current, name)
                        .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)?;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(current)
    }

    pub fn create_dir(&mut self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_node(parent, name, EntryKind::Directory)
    }

    pub fn create_file(&mut self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_node(parent, name, EntryKind::File)
    }

    pub fn create_dir_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(path)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        self.create_dir(parent, name)
    }

    pub fn create_file_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(path)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        self.create_file(parent, name)
    }

    /// Return an existing file node or create it if its path does not exist.
    pub fn open_or_create_file(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        match self.resolve(cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => {
                if self.node(node)?.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
                    Err(FsError::IsDirectory)
                } else {
                    Ok(node)
                }
            }
            Err(FsError::NotFound) => self.create_file_path(cwd, path),
            Err(error) => Err(error),
        }
    }

    pub fn kind(&self, node: usize) -> Result<EntryKind, FsError> {
        Ok(self.node(node)?.kind)
    }

    pub fn read_file(&self, node: usize) -> Result<&[u8], FsError> {
        let node = self.node(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        Ok(&node.data[..node.data_len])
    }

    pub fn write_file(&mut self, node: usize, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if contents.len() > FILE_CAPACITY {
            return Err(FsError::FileTooLarge);
        }
        let node = self.node_mut(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        node.data[..contents.len()].copy_from_slice(contents);
        node.data[contents.len()..].fill(0);
        node.data_len = contents.len();
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn append_file(&mut self, node: usize, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.node_mut(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        let new_len = node
            .data_len
            .checked_add(contents.len())
            .filter(|length| *length <= FILE_CAPACITY)
            .ok_or(FsError::FileTooLarge)?;
        node.data[node.data_len..new_len].copy_from_slice(contents);
        node.data_len = new_len;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Copy a file to a destination path, replacing an existing destination file.
    pub fn copy_file_path(
        &mut self,
        cwd: usize,
        source_path: &str,
        destination_path: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let source = self.resolve(cwd, source_path)?;
        let mut contents = [0u8; FILE_CAPACITY];
        let length = {
            let source_contents = self.read_file(source)?;
            contents[..source_contents.len()].copy_from_slice(source_contents);
            source_contents.len()
        };
        let destination = self.open_or_create_file(cwd, destination_path)?;
        self.write_file(destination, &contents[..length])
    }

    /// Move or rename a file. Existing destinations are never overwritten.
    pub fn move_file_path(
        &mut self,
        cwd: usize,
        source_path: &str,
        destination_path: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let source = self.resolve(cwd, source_path)?;
        if source == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        if self.kind(source)? == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }

        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(destination_path)?;
        validate_name(name)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        if self.node(parent)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        if let Some(existing) = self.find_child(parent, name) {
            return if existing == source {
                Ok(())
            } else {
                Err(FsError::AlreadyExists)
            };
        }

        let node = self.node_mut(source)?;
        node.parent = parent;
        node.name.fill(0);
        node.name[..name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        node.name_len = name.len() as u8;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_file(&mut self, node: usize) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if node == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        let entry = self.node(node)?;
        if entry.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        self.nodes[node] = Node::EMPTY;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_dir(&mut self, node: usize) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if node == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        let entry = self.node(node)?;
        if entry.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        if self.nodes.iter().any(|child| child.used && child.parent == node) {
            return Err(FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty);
        }
        self.nodes[node] = Node::EMPTY;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_file_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.resolve(cwd, path)?;
        self.remove_file(node)
    }

    pub fn remove_dir_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.resolve(cwd, path)?;
        self.remove_dir(node)
    }

    pub fn entry(&self, node: usize) -> Result<Entry<'_>, FsError> {
        let node = self.node(node)?;
        Ok(Entry {
            name: node.name(),
            kind: node.kind,
            size: node.data_len,
        })
    }

    pub fn child_count(&self, directory: usize) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        if self.node(directory)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        Ok(self
            .nodes
            .iter()
            .filter(|node| {
                node.used
                    && node.parent == directory
                    && !(directory == ROOT_NODE && node.name_len == 0)
            })
            .count())
    }

    pub fn child_at(&self, directory: usize, ordinal: usize) -> Option<Entry<'_>> {
        if self.node(directory).ok()?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return None;
        }
        self.nodes
            .iter()
            .filter(|node| {
                node.used
                    && node.parent == directory
                    && !(directory == ROOT_NODE && node.name_len == 0)
            })
            .nth(ordinal)
            .map(|node| Entry {
                name: node.name(),
                kind: node.kind,
                size: node.data_len,
            })
    }

    /// Write an absolute path into caller-provided storage and return its length.
    pub fn write_path(&self, node: usize, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.node(node)?;
        let mut ancestors = [ROOT_NODE; MAX_NODES];
        let mut depth = 0;
        let mut current = node;
        while current != ROOT_NODE {
            if depth == MAX_NODES {
                return Err(FsError::InvalidPath);
            }
            ancestors[depth] = current;
            depth += 1;
            current = self.node(current)?.parent;
        }

        let component_bytes = (0..depth)
            .map(|index| usize::from(self.nodes[ancestors[index]].name_len))
            .sum::<usize>();
        let required = 1 + component_bytes + depth.saturating_sub(1);
        if output.len() < required {
            return Err(FsError::BufferTooSmall);
        }

        output[0] = b'/';
        let mut length = 1;
        for index in (0..depth).rev() {
            if length > 1 {
                output[length] = b'/';
                length += 1;
            }
            let name = self.nodes[ancestors[index]].name();
            output[length..length + name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
            length += name.len();
        }
        Ok(length)
    }

    fn create_node(
        &mut self,
        parent: usize,
        name: &str,
        kind: EntryKind,
    ) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let parent_node = self.node(parent)?;
        if parent_node.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        validate_name(name)?;
        if self.find_child(parent, name).is_some() {
            return Err(FsError::AlreadyExists);
        }
        let index = self
            .nodes
            .iter()
            .position(|node| !node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NoSpace)?;
        let mut node = Node::EMPTY;
        node.used = true;
        node.kind = kind;
        node.parent = parent;
        node.name[..name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        node.name_len = name.len() as u8;
        self.nodes[index] = node;
        Ok(index)
    }

    fn find_child(&self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        self.nodes.iter().position(|node| {
            node.used && node.parent == parent && node.name_len != 0 && node.name() == name
        })
    }

    fn node(&self, index: usize) -> Result<&Node, FsError> {
        self.nodes
            .get(index)
            .filter(|node| node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)
    }

    fn node_mut(&mut self, index: usize) -> Result<&mut Node, FsError> {
        self.nodes
            .get_mut(index)
            .filter(|node| node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)
    }
}

impl Default for RamFs {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

fn validate_name(name: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
    if name.is_empty()
        || name == "."
        || name == ".."
        || name.contains('/')
        || name.contains('\0')
    {
        return Err(FsError::InvalidName);
    }
    if name.len() > NAME_CAPACITY {
        return Err(FsError::NameTooLong);
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn split_parent(path: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), FsError> {
    let path = path.trim_end_matches('/');
    if path.is_empty() {
        return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
    }
    match path.rsplit_once('/') {
        Some(("", name)) => Ok(("/", name)),
        Some((parent, name)) if !name.is_empty() => Ok((parent, name)),
        Some(_) => Err(FsError::InvalidPath),
        None => Ok((".", path)),
    }
}

//! Small, architecture-independent helpers for boot-time memory accounting.

/// Limine's memory-map type for ordinary usable RAM.
pub const MEMORY_MAP_USABLE: u64 = 0;

/// Add a memory-map entry to a running usable-memory total.
///
/// Non-usable regions leave the total unchanged. `None` signals arithmetic
/// overflow so callers can report malformed or unrepresentable maps.
pub const fn add_usable_bytes(total: u64, region_kind: u64, region_length: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    if region_kind == MEMORY_MAP_USABLE {
        total.checked_add(region_length)
    } else {
        Some(total)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use core::assert_eq;

    use super::{add_usable_bytes, MEMORY_MAP_USABLE};

    #[test]
    fn counts_only_usable_regions() {
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(4096, MEMORY_MAP_USABLE, 2048), Some(6144));
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(4096, 1, 2048), Some(4096));
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_total_overflow() {
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(u64::MAX - 4, MEMORY_MAP_USABLE, 8), None);
    }
}

    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        core::str::from_utf8(&self.name[..usize::from(self.name_len)]).unwrap_or("")
    }
}

/// A small fixed-capacity filesystem suitable for the pre-allocator shell.
pub struct RamFs {
    nodes: [Node; MAX_NODES],
}

impl RamFs {
    /// Construct a filesystem containing only its root directory.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        let mut nodes = [Node::EMPTY; MAX_NODES];
        nodes[ROOT_NODE] = Node {
            used: true,
            kind: EntryKind::Directory,
            parent: ROOT_NODE,
            name: [0; NAME_CAPACITY],
            name_len: 0,
            data: [0; FILE_CAPACITY],
            data_len: 0,
        };
        Self { nodes }
    }

    /// Create a starter Unix-like directory tree and return `/home/rustix`.
    pub fn seed_defaults(&mut self) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "bin")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "dev")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "etc")?;
        let home = self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "home")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "tmp")?;
        self.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "var")?;
        let user_home = self.create_dir(home, "rustix")?;
        let motd = self.create_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/etc/motd")?;
        self.write_file(
            motd,
            b"Welcome to Rustix. Files in this early shell are volatile RAM files.\n",
        )?;
        Ok(user_home)
    }

    /// Resolve a path from a working directory. `/`, repeated separators, `.`
    /// and `..` are handled; every intermediate component must be a directory.
    pub fn resolve(&self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        if path.is_empty() {
            return Err(FsError::InvalidPath);
        }
        let mut current = if path.starts_with('/') { ROOT_NODE } else { cwd };
        let start = self.node(current)?;
        if start.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }

        for component in path.split('/') {
            if component.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            if self.node(current)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
                return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
            }
            match component {
                "." => {}
                ".." => current = self.node(current)?.parent,
                name => {
                    current = self
                        .find_child(current, name)
                        .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)?;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(current)
    }

    pub fn create_dir(&mut self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_node(parent, name, EntryKind::Directory)
    }

    pub fn create_file(&mut self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.create_node(parent, name, EntryKind::File)
    }

    pub fn create_dir_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(path)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        self.create_dir(parent, name)
    }

    pub fn create_file_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(path)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        self.create_file(parent, name)
    }

    /// Return an existing file node or create it if its path does not exist.
    pub fn open_or_create_file(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        match self.resolve(cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => {
                if self.node(node)?.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
                    Err(FsError::IsDirectory)
                } else {
                    Ok(node)
                }
            }
            Err(FsError::NotFound) => self.create_file_path(cwd, path),
            Err(error) => Err(error),
        }
    }

    pub fn kind(&self, node: usize) -> Result<EntryKind, FsError> {
        Ok(self.node(node)?.kind)
    }

    pub fn read_file(&self, node: usize) -> Result<&[u8], FsError> {
        let node = self.node(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        Ok(&node.data[..node.data_len])
    }

    pub fn write_file(&mut self, node: usize, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if contents.len() > FILE_CAPACITY {
            return Err(FsError::FileTooLarge);
        }
        let node = self.node_mut(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        node.data[..contents.len()].copy_from_slice(contents);
        node.data[contents.len()..].fill(0);
        node.data_len = contents.len();
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn append_file(&mut self, node: usize, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.node_mut(node)?;
        if node.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        let new_len = node
            .data_len
            .checked_add(contents.len())
            .filter(|length| *length <= FILE_CAPACITY)
            .ok_or(FsError::FileTooLarge)?;
        node.data[node.data_len..new_len].copy_from_slice(contents);
        node.data_len = new_len;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Copy a file to a destination path, replacing an existing destination file.
    pub fn copy_file_path(
        &mut self,
        cwd: usize,
        source_path: &str,
        destination_path: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let source = self.resolve(cwd, source_path)?;
        let mut contents = [0u8; FILE_CAPACITY];
        let length = {
            let source_contents = self.read_file(source)?;
            contents[..source_contents.len()].copy_from_slice(source_contents);
            source_contents.len()
        };
        let destination = self.open_or_create_file(cwd, destination_path)?;
        self.write_file(destination, &contents[..length])
    }

    /// Move or rename a file. Existing destinations are never overwritten.
    pub fn move_file_path(
        &mut self,
        cwd: usize,
        source_path: &str,
        destination_path: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let source = self.resolve(cwd, source_path)?;
        if source == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        if self.kind(source)? == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }

        let (parent_path, name) = split_parent(destination_path)?;
        validate_name(name)?;
        let parent = self.resolve(cwd, parent_path)?;
        if self.node(parent)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        if let Some(existing) = self.find_child(parent, name) {
            return if existing == source {
                Ok(())
            } else {
                Err(FsError::AlreadyExists)
            };
        }

        let node = self.node_mut(source)?;
        node.parent = parent;
        node.name.fill(0);
        node.name[..name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        node.name_len = name.len() as u8;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_file(&mut self, node: usize) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if node == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        let entry = self.node(node)?;
        if entry.kind == EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::IsDirectory);
        }
        self.nodes[node] = Node::EMPTY;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_dir(&mut self, node: usize) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        if node == ROOT_NODE {
            return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
        }
        let entry = self.node(node)?;
        if entry.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        if self.nodes.iter().any(|child| child.used && child.parent == node) {
            return Err(FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty);
        }
        self.nodes[node] = Node::EMPTY;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn remove_file_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.resolve(cwd, path)?;
        self.remove_file(node)
    }

    pub fn remove_dir_path(&mut self, cwd: usize, path: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
        let node = self.resolve(cwd, path)?;
        self.remove_dir(node)
    }

    pub fn entry(&self, node: usize) -> Result<Entry<'_>, FsError> {
        let node = self.node(node)?;
        Ok(Entry {
            name: node.name(),
            kind: node.kind,
            size: node.data_len,
        })
    }

    pub fn child_count(&self, directory: usize) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        if self.node(directory)?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        Ok(self
            .nodes
            .iter()
            .filter(|node| {
                node.used
                    && node.parent == directory
                    && !(directory == ROOT_NODE && node.name_len == 0)
            })
            .count())
    }

    pub fn child_at(&self, directory: usize, ordinal: usize) -> Option<Entry<'_>> {
        if self.node(directory).ok()?.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return None;
        }
        self.nodes
            .iter()
            .filter(|node| {
                node.used
                    && node.parent == directory
                    && !(directory == ROOT_NODE && node.name_len == 0)
            })
            .nth(ordinal)
            .map(|node| Entry {
                name: node.name(),
                kind: node.kind,
                size: node.data_len,
            })
    }

    /// Write an absolute path into caller-provided storage and return its length.
    pub fn write_path(&self, node: usize, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        self.node(node)?;
        let mut ancestors = [ROOT_NODE; MAX_NODES];
        let mut depth = 0;
        let mut current = node;
        while current != ROOT_NODE {
            if depth == MAX_NODES {
                return Err(FsError::InvalidPath);
            }
            ancestors[depth] = current;
            depth += 1;
            current = self.node(current)?.parent;
        }

        let component_bytes = (0..depth)
            .map(|index| usize::from(self.nodes[ancestors[index]].name_len))
            .sum::<usize>();
        let required = 1 + component_bytes + depth.saturating_sub(1);
        if output.len() < required {
            return Err(FsError::BufferTooSmall);
        }

        output[0] = b'/';
        let mut length = 1;
        for index in (0..depth).rev() {
            if length > 1 {
                output[length] = b'/';
                length += 1;
            }
            let name = self.nodes[ancestors[index]].name();
            output[length..length + name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
            length += name.len();
        }
        Ok(length)
    }

    fn create_node(
        &mut self,
        parent: usize,
        name: &str,
        kind: EntryKind,
    ) -> Result<usize, FsError> {
        let parent_node = self.node(parent)?;
        if parent_node.kind != EntryKind::Directory {
            return Err(FsError::NotDirectory);
        }
        validate_name(name)?;
        if self.find_child(parent, name).is_some() {
            return Err(FsError::AlreadyExists);
        }
        let index = self
            .nodes
            .iter()
            .position(|node| !node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NoSpace)?;
        let mut node = Node::EMPTY;
        node.used = true;
        node.kind = kind;
        node.parent = parent;
        node.name[..name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        node.name_len = name.len() as u8;
        self.nodes[index] = node;
        Ok(index)
    }

    fn find_child(&self, parent: usize, name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        self.nodes.iter().position(|node| {
            node.used && node.parent == parent && node.name_len != 0 && node.name() == name
        })
    }

    fn node(&self, index: usize) -> Result<&Node, FsError> {
        self.nodes
            .get(index)
            .filter(|node| node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)
    }

    fn node_mut(&mut self, index: usize) -> Result<&mut Node, FsError> {
        self.nodes
            .get_mut(index)
            .filter(|node| node.used)
            .ok_or(FsError::NotFound)
    }
}

impl Default for RamFs {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

fn validate_name(name: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
    if name.is_empty()
        || name == "."
        || name == ".."
        || name.contains('/')
        || name.contains('\0')
    {
        return Err(FsError::InvalidName);
    }
    if name.len() > NAME_CAPACITY {
        return Err(FsError::NameTooLong);
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn split_parent(path: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), FsError> {
    let path = path.trim_end_matches('/');
    if path.is_empty() {
        return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
    }
    match path.rsplit_once('/') {
        Some(("", name)) => Ok(("/", name)),
        Some((parent, name)) if !name.is_empty() => Ok((parent, name)),
        Some(_) => Err(FsError::InvalidPath),
        None => Ok((".", path)),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use core::assert_eq;

    use super::{EntryKind, FsError, RamFs, ROOT_NODE};

    #[test]
    fn resolves_absolute_relative_and_parent_components() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let home = fs.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "home").unwrap();
        let user = fs.create_dir(home, "rustix").unwrap();
        let notes = fs.create_dir(user, "notes").unwrap();

        assert_eq!(fs.resolve(user, ".").unwrap(), user);
        assert_eq!(fs.resolve(notes, "../..").unwrap(), home);
        assert_eq!(fs.resolve(ROOT_NODE, "/home/rustix/notes/").unwrap(), notes);
    }

    #[test]
    fn creates_reads_appends_and_removes_files() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let file = fs.create_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/note.txt").unwrap();
        fs.write_file(file, b"hello").unwrap();
        fs.append_file(file, b" rustix").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs.read_file(file).unwrap(), b"hello rustix");
        fs.remove_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/note.txt").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs.resolve(ROOT_NODE, "/note.txt"), Err(FsError::NotFound));
    }

    #[test]
    fn copies_and_moves_files_without_overwriting_destinations() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let source = fs.create_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/source.txt").unwrap();
        fs.write_file(source, b"data").unwrap();

        fs.copy_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/source.txt", "/copy.txt")
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            fs.read_file(fs.resolve(ROOT_NODE, "/copy.txt").unwrap()),
            Ok(&b"data"[..])
        );
        fs.move_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/copy.txt", "/saved.txt")
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs.resolve(ROOT_NODE, "/copy.txt"), Err(FsError::NotFound));
        assert_eq!(
            fs.read_file(fs.resolve(ROOT_NODE, "/saved.txt").unwrap()),
            Ok(&b"data"[..])
        );
        assert_eq!(
            fs.move_file_path(ROOT_NODE, "/source.txt", "/saved.txt"),
            Err(FsError::AlreadyExists)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn refuses_to_remove_nonempty_directories() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let directory = fs.create_dir(ROOT_NODE, "work").unwrap();
        fs.create_file(directory, "note").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs.remove_dir(directory), Err(FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty));
    }

    #[test]
    fn path_output_and_kinds_are_consistent() {
        let mut fs = RamFs::new();
        let docs = fs.create_dir_path(ROOT_NODE, "/home").unwrap();
        let file = fs.create_file(docs, "readme").unwrap();
        let mut path = [0; 64];
        let length = fs.write_path(file, &mut path).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(&path[..length], b"/home/readme");
        assert_eq!(fs.kind(docs), Ok(EntryKind::Directory));
        assert_eq!(fs.kind(file), Ok(EntryKind::File));
    }
}

#![no_std]

//! Small, allocation-free command parsing for Rustix's Crabshell.
//!
//! This crate deliberately contains no terminal, filesystem, or kernel code.
//! The same command model can later be driven by a graphical terminal frontend
//! or a userspace process without coupling it to the current serial console.

/// The longest command line accepted by the bootstrap shell, excluding its NUL.
pub const MAX_LINE_LENGTH: usize = 256;

/// Parsed shell operations. The command borrows its path and text from the input
/// line, so parsing needs no allocator and the caller controls all I/O.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Command<'a> {
    Help,
    Clear,
    Pwd,
    Ls(Option<&'a str>),
    Cd(&'a str),
    Mkdir(&'a str),
    Touch(&'a str),
    Write { path: &'a str, contents: &'a str },
    Append { path: &'a str, contents: &'a str },
    Cp { source: &'a str, destination: &'a str },
    Mv { source: &'a str, destination: &'a str },
    Cat(&'a str),
    Rm(&'a str),
    Rmdir(&'a str),
}

/// Errors in command syntax. Unknown command names are reported separately so
/// the caller can echo the original name in its diagnostic.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ParseError {
    UnknownCommand,
    MissingArgument,
    MissingText,
    TooManyArguments,
    UnterminatedQuote,
}

/// Parse one command line. An empty or whitespace-only line returns `Ok(None)`.
///
/// `write` and `append` accept the remaining text verbatim; wrapping the whole
/// text in matching single or double quotes removes those outer quotes. Escape
/// sequences and quoted paths are intentionally not part of this first grammar.
pub fn parse(line: &str) -> Result<Option<Command<'_>>, ParseError> {
    let line = line.trim();
    if line.is_empty() {
        return Ok(None);
    }

    let (name, rest) = take_word(line).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    let command = match name {
        "help" => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Command::Help
        }
        "clear" => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Command::Clear
        }
        "pwd" => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Command::Pwd
        }
        "ls" => Command::Ls(optional_path(rest)?),
        "cd" => Command::Cd(one_path(rest)?),
        "mkdir" => Command::Mkdir(one_path(rest)?),
        "touch" => Command::Touch(one_path(rest)?),
        "write" => {
            let (path, contents) = path_and_text(rest)?;
            Command::Write { path, contents }
        }
        "append" => {
            let (path, contents) = path_and_text(rest)?;
            Command::Append { path, contents }
        }
        "cp" => {
            let (source, destination) = two_paths(rest)?;
            Command::Cp { source, destination }
        }
        "mv" => {
            let (source, destination) = two_paths(rest)?;
            Command::Mv { source, destination }
        }
        "cat" => Command::Cat(one_path(rest)?),
        "rm" => Command::Rm(one_path(rest)?),
        "rmdir" => Command::Rmdir(one_path(rest)?),
        _ => return Err(ParseError::UnknownCommand),
    };

    Ok(Some(command))
}

fn take_word(input: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str)> {
    let input = input.trim_start();
    if input.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let end = input.find(char::is_whitespace).unwrap_or(input.len());
    Some((&input[..end], input[end..].trim_start()))
}

fn no_arguments(rest: &str) -> Result<(), ParseError> {
    if rest.is_empty() {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(ParseError::TooManyArguments)
    }
}

fn optional_path(rest: &str) -> Result<Option<&str>, ParseError> {
    match take_word(rest) {
        None => Ok(None),
        Some((path, rest)) => {
            no_arguments(rest)?;
            Ok(Some(path))
        }
    }
}

fn one_path(rest: &str) -> Result<&str, ParseError> {
    let (path, rest) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    no_arguments(rest)?;
    Ok(path)
}

fn two_paths(rest: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), ParseError> {
    let (source, rest) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    let (destination, rest) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    no_arguments(rest)?;
    Ok((source, destination))
}

fn path_and_text(rest: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), ParseError> {
    let (path, text) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
    if text.is_empty() {
        return Err(ParseError::MissingText);
    }

    let first = text.as_bytes()[0];
    if first == b'\'' || first == b'"' {
        if text.len() < 2 || text.as_bytes()[text.len() - 1] != first {
            return Err(ParseError::UnterminatedQuote);
        }
        return Ok((path, &text[1..text.len() - 1]));
    }

    Ok((path, text))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use core::assert_eq;

    use super::{parse, Command, ParseError};

    #[test]
    fn blank_lines_are_ignored() {
        assert_eq!(parse(" \t "), Ok(None));
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_basic_navigation_and_file_commands() {
        assert_eq!(parse("pwd"), Ok(Some(Command::Pwd)));
        assert_eq!(parse("ls /home"), Ok(Some(Command::Ls(Some("/home")))));
        assert_eq!(parse("cd .."), Ok(Some(Command::Cd(".."))));
        assert_eq!(parse("mkdir /tmp/work"), Ok(Some(Command::Mkdir("/tmp/work"))));
        assert_eq!(parse("touch note.txt"), Ok(Some(Command::Touch("note.txt"))));
        assert_eq!(parse("cat note.txt"), Ok(Some(Command::Cat("note.txt"))));
        assert_eq!(
            parse("cp note.txt copy.txt"),
            Ok(Some(Command::Cp {
                source: "note.txt",
                destination: "copy.txt",
            }))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse("mv copy.txt saved.txt"),
            Ok(Some(Command::Mv {
                source: "copy.txt",
                destination: "saved.txt",
            }))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_preserves_spaces_and_strips_outer_quotes() {
        assert_eq!(
            parse("write greeting.txt hello from crabshell"),
            Ok(Some(Command::Write {
                path: "greeting.txt",
                contents: "hello from crabshell",
            }))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse("append greeting.txt \" again\""),
            Ok(Some(Command::Append {
                path: "greeting.txt",
                contents: " again",
            }))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse("write empty.txt \"\""),
            Ok(Some(Command::Write {
                path: "empty.txt",
                contents: "",
            }))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_command_arity_and_text() {
        assert_eq!(parse("cd"), Err(ParseError::MissingArgument));
        assert_eq!(parse("pwd now"), Err(ParseError::TooManyArguments));
        assert_eq!(parse("cp only-one"), Err(ParseError::MissingArgument));
        assert_eq!(parse("mv a b c"), Err(ParseError::TooManyArguments));
        assert_eq!(parse("write file"), Err(ParseError::MissingText));
        assert_eq!(parse("write file \"unfinished"), Err(ParseError::UnterminatedQuote));
        assert_eq!(parse("not-a-command"), Err(ParseError::UnknownCommand));
    }
}

# x86_64 drivers

## Driver boundary

Rustix keeps privileged platform access in `src/arch/x86_64/`. Device-facing routines should be small, explicit about polling/interrupt assumptions, and separated from policy such as terminal input or process I/O. The current drivers are intentionally early-boot building blocks, not a finished device model.

## Implemented drivers

| Driver | Source | Status and limits |
|---|---|---|
| 16550-compatible COM1 serial | [`src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs`](../../src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs) | Initialized during `_start`; polling formatted output and non-blocking input for Crabshell; bounded transmit waits. |
| x86 port I/O primitives | [`src/arch/x86_64/io.rs`](../../src/arch/x86_64/io.rs) | Small unsafe `in`/`out` wrappers used by platform drivers. |
| PS/2-compatible keyboard controller | [`src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs`](../../src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs) | Non-blocking raw-byte polling API; filters auxiliary-device and controller-error bytes. Not yet connected to a kernel input queue. |

The keyboard routine assumes a legacy controller is present and enabled. It does not initialize the controller, decode scancode sets, support USB HID, or use interrupts. Callers must not spin waiting for input; use `try_read_scancode()` when the kernel has a suitable polling opportunity.

## Driver development rules

- Keep port I/O, MMIO, DMA, and interrupt entry points in architecture/device modules; do not expose raw I/O ports to generic kernel services.
- Document required privilege level, device assumptions, concurrency/interrupt context, and whether a call can block.
- Bound waits in early boot, avoid allocation in low-level paths, and propagate/report device absence rather than hanging startup.
- Separate raw hardware events from key mapping, terminal semantics, and user-visible input policy.
- Add emulator/hardware tests when an integration harness exists; host tests alone cannot validate port I/O.

## Planned driver work

Add a timer and interrupt-controller path before interrupt-driven keyboard input; establish locking and per-CPU rules before enabling concurrency. Then consider framebuffer/console output, PCI discovery, storage, and networking as independently reviewed drivers. No support for those devices is implied by this plan.

````rustix/docs/development/building.md
     1	# Building Rustix
     2	
     3	## Prerequisites
     4	
     5	- Rust stable with `rustfmt`; the repository pins these in `rust-toolchain.toml`.
     6	- The `x86_64-unknown-none` target. The toolchain file requests it automatically; if needed, install it with `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`.
     7	- [`just`](https://just.systems/) to run the repository's named tasks.
     8	- Python 3.8 or newer (standard library only), with `python` on `PATH`; `xorriso`; and QEMU with `qemu-system-x86_64` for image creation and boot smoke tests.
     9	
    10	An ELF inspection tool such as `llvm-readelf` or `readelf` is useful when diagnosing linker output. The first image build downloads the pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary archive into `target/tools/` and verifies its published SHA-256 before extraction.
    11	
    12	## Common commands
    13	
    14	Run from the repository root:
    15	
    16	```sh
    17	just help
    18	just fmt       # check Rust formatting
    19	just test      # parser, RAM-filesystem, and memory tests
    20	just check     # type-check the freestanding kernel target
    21	just build     # optimized kernel ELF
    22	just image     # hybrid BIOS/UEFI ISO at target/rustix.iso
    23	just smoke     # bounded QEMU boot to the Crabshell prompt
    24	just run       # interactive serial shell in QEMU (Ctrl+C to stop)
    25	just verify    # fmt, workspace tests, target check, image, and QEMU smoke test
    26	```
    27	
    28	Equivalent Rust checks are `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --lib`, `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-none`, and `cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-none`. Image creation and QEMU validation are provided by `scripts/boot.py` and are intentionally part of `just verify`.
    29	
    30	The optimized ELF is written to `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `cargo check` checks the target without producing a boot image. The library tests run on the host and exercise code that does not require privileged instructions.
    31	
    32	## Target-specific linker setup
    33	
    34	`.cargo/config.toml` applies the Rustix linker script and x86_64 kernel constraints only to `x86_64-unknown-none`. `linker.ld` emits an ELF64 x86_64 image at the higher-half base, retains Limine request sections, and defines `_start` as the entry symbol. The build uses no third-party Rust crates; the boot protocol is represented by small in-tree Rust structures and constants.
    35	
    36	Changing the target, virtual base, relocation model, or request ABI requires updating the linker script, protocol documentation, and validation plan together. Do not use host builds of the kernel binary as evidence that the freestanding target links correctly.
    37	
    38	## Building and smoke-testing a boot image
    39	
    40	`limine.conf` boots the kernel immediately and enables 38,400-baud serial output. `just image` builds the ELF, fetches Limine v12.9.3's binary ZIP from its immutable GitHub release, checks the pinned SHA-256, prepares a BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO, and installs the BIOS boot code. The Limine archive and extracted tools remain under ignored `target/`; no third-party binaries are checked into the source tree.
    41	
    42	`just smoke` launches `target/rustix.iso` in `qemu-system-x86_64` with a 256 MiB q35 machine, headless display, captured COM1 output, and a 20-second deadline. QEMU is expected to remain running at the interactive shell; the runner terminates it at the deadline and requires the startup banner, Crabshell-ready message, and initial prompt. On a failure it prints the serial log. The log remains at `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` for inspection.
    43	
    44	`just run` launches the same image with the serial port attached to the host terminal, allowing interactive shell use. Stop the emulator with `Ctrl+C`.
    45	
    46	`just verify` includes the emulator smoke test and therefore needs Python 3, xorriso, QEMU, network access for the first Limine download, and the Rust target. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs the system tools on Ubuntu 24.04 and runs the same command. This verifies the boot path in CI; it is still not a substitute for testing physical hardware.
    47	
    48	## Troubleshooting
    49	
    50	- **Target not installed:** install `x86_64-unknown-none` as shown above.
    51	- **`just` not found:** install `just`; Rust-only checks can still be run with the Cargo commands above.
    52	- **`xorriso` or QEMU not found:** install the host image/emulator tools listed in prerequisites, then retry `just image` or `just smoke`.
    53	- **Limine SHA-256 mismatch:** the pinned archive may have changed or been corrupted; the script removes the mismatched download and refuses to use it. Check the official v12.9.3 release digest before changing the pin.
    54	- **Linker-script error:** build only for `x86_64-unknown-none`; confirm the invocation runs from the repository root so `linker.ld` resolves.
    55	- **No serial output:** inspect `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` and QEMU's stderr. The image config and Rustix COM1 driver both use 38,400 baud.

     6	
     7	- [x] `no_std` Rust kernel binary for `x86_64-unknown-none`.
     8	- [x] Own ELF linker layout and Limine boot-protocol requests.
     9	- [x] COM1 serial diagnostics, memory-map/HHDM summary, and panic halt path.

    18	
    19	**Exit criteria:** a clean checkout builds the pinned image, boots it in the documented emulator, and captures the expected serial banner in automated validation. The workflow is implemented; the criterion remains pending until an end-to-end run passes.
    20	
    21	## Milestone 1 — validated boot state and machine diagnostics
    22	
    23	- Parse and validate all loader ranges into a stable boot-info value.
    24	- Preserve reserved, reclaimable, firmware, and MMIO regions distinctly.
    25	- Add serial formatting tests, CPU feature reporting, and a framebuffer or documented serial-only console.
    26	- Establish explicit ownership and reclaim timing for loader memory.
    27	
    28	**Exit criteria:** malformed maps fail closed; an emulator test validates reported regions and boot metadata.
    29	
    30	## Milestone 2 — memory ownership and CPU exceptions
    31	
    32	- Physical frame allocator with overflow-safe range handling and exhaustion tests.
    33	- Kernel-owned page-table management and documented direct-map policy.
    34	- Global heap with deterministic out-of-memory behavior.
    35	- GDT/TSS and IDT setup; exception handlers with register/error-code diagnostics; fault-injection tests.
    36	
    37	**Exit criteria:** allocator and mapping invariants are tested, page faults are diagnosable, and the kernel remains bootable under emulator tests.
    38	
    39	## Milestone 3 — interrupts, time, and scheduling
    40	
    41	- Timer and interrupt-controller setup with explicit interrupt-safe locking rules.
    42	- Kernel threads and context switching; per-CPU data before SMP work.
    43	- Preemptive scheduling only after interrupt, stack, and lock invariants are validated.
    44	- Application processor startup as a separate milestone, not an implicit extension of single-core code.
    45	
    46	**Exit criteria:** deterministic thread lifecycle tests and bounded timer/preemption integration tests.
    47	
    48	## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI
    49	
    50	- User-mode entry/exit and isolated address spaces.
    51	- Versioned syscall ABI, validated copy-in/copy-out, and documented error semantics.
    52	- Initial process lifecycle, descriptor table, and executable-loading path.
    53	- Adversarial tests for invalid pointers, bad lengths, overflow, and process teardown.
    54	
    55	**Exit criteria:** a controlled userspace init process can execute and use a small documented syscall subset without corrupting the kernel on invalid input.
    56	
    57	## Milestone 5 — Unix-like services and storage
    58	
    59	- VFS and mount model, file descriptors, and a first on-disk filesystem.
    60	- Process creation/exec/wait semantics, pipes or IPC, and signal-like delivery as designed.
    61	- Device discovery/driver model and networking only after ownership and isolation policies exist.
    62	- Compatibility tests for any claimed Unix/POSIX behavior; keep unsupported operations explicit.
    63	
    64	**Exit criteria:** documented userland tools can run from a reproducible image and integration tests cover process and file semantics.
    65	
    66	## Working rule
    67	
    68	Each milestone should add code, tests, and updated documentation together. Do not advance the stated project status merely because an interface or design note exists. Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable subsystem stubs.

````rustix/README.md
     1	# Rustix
     2	
     3	Rustix (Rust-unix) is an experimental, 64-bit, Unix-like operating system whose kernel is written in Rust. This repository builds the kernel itself; Limine is used only as the external boot protocol/loader, not as a substitute for a Rustix kernel.
     4	
     5	Rustix now boots into **Crabshell**, a small kernel-mode shell on the COM1 serial terminal. It includes basic navigation and file commands backed by a fixed-capacity RAM filesystem. The filesystem is volatile and reset at every boot; this is an early kernel shell, not a userspace process or POSIX shell. The command parser lives in a separate, allocation-free `crabshell` crate so a future GUI terminal can reuse it. Scheduling, process isolation, persistent storage, a syscall ABI, networking, and userspace are still future work. See [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) for the staged plan.
     6	
     7	## Quick start
     8	
     9	Prerequisites: a Rust stable toolchain, `just`, Python 3, `xorriso`, QEMU (`qemu-system-x86_64`), and the target installed by `rust-toolchain.toml` (or `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`). The first image build downloads a pinned Limine binary release and verifies its SHA-256.
    10	
    11	```sh
    12	just help
    13	just fmt
    14	just test
    15	just check
    16	just build
    17	just image
    18	just smoke
    19	just run       # interactive serial shell in QEMU; exit with Ctrl+C
    20	just verify
    21	```
    22	
    23	`just build` produces `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `just image` creates `target/rustix.iso`, a hybrid BIOS/UEFI image; `just smoke` checks that Crabshell reaches its prompt; and `just run` starts an interactive QEMU session attached to the current terminal.
    24	
    25	Try `pwd`, `ls /`, `mkdir notes`, `write notes/hello.txt "hello from Rustix"`, `cat notes/hello.txt`, and `cd ..` in Crabshell. Commands include `help`, `clear`, `pwd`, `ls`, `cd`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `write`, `append`, `cp`, `mv`, `cat`, `rm`, and `rmdir`. The RAM filesystem holds at most 32 entries, with files capped at 1024 bytes. See [`docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](docs/architecture/crabshell.md) for the shell and filesystem contract, [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) for build/emulator details, and [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) for the documentation map.
    26	
    27	## Project principles
    28	
    29	- The kernel and operating-system implementation are Rust-first and `no_std`; architecture-specific privileged operations are isolated under `src/arch/`.
    30	- The kernel is the product. A bootloader may initialize the machine and transfer control, but policy, memory management, scheduling, and Unix-like services belong to Rustix.
    31	- Keep unsafe code small, documented, and adjacent to its hardware/protocol boundary.
    32	- Build incrementally: every roadmap milestone should have build checks, tests where practical, and updated design documentation.
    33	- Unix-like behavior is an explicit compatibility goal, not a claim of POSIX compliance today.
    34	
    35	## Repository map
    36	
    37	- `src/main.rs` — freestanding kernel entry point and Crabshell handoff.
    38	- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel command executor.
    39	- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem, with host-side tests.
    40	- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` command parser crate; no I/O or filesystem coupling.
    41	- `src/boot.rs` — Limine requests and boot-memory-map reporting.
    42	- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — early COM1 polling driver.
    43	- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling.
    44	- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers.
    45	- `src/memory.rs` — architecture-independent boot-time memory accounting and host tests.
    46	- `.cargo/config.toml`, `linker.ld` — x86_64-none code generation and ELF layout.
    47	- `justfile` — formatting, tests, target checks, image creation, emulator smoke test, and aggregate verification.
    48	- `limine.conf` — pinned boot configuration for the Rustix kernel.
    49	- `scripts/boot.py` — checksum-verified Limine download, hybrid ISO assembly, and bounded QEMU validation.
    50	- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — runs `just verify` on pushes and pull requests.
    51	- `docs/` — architecture, drivers, development, security, and roadmap documentation.

# Rustix

Rustix (Rust-unix) is an experimental, 64-bit, Unix-like operating system whose kernel is written in Rust. This repository builds the kernel itself; Limine is used only as the external boot protocol/loader, not as a substitute for a Rustix kernel.

Rustix now boots into **Crabshell**, a small kernel-mode shell on the COM1 serial terminal. It includes basic navigation and file commands backed by a fixed-capacity RAM filesystem. The filesystem is volatile and reset at every boot; this is an early kernel shell, not a userspace process or POSIX shell. The command parser lives in a separate, allocation-free `crabshell` crate so a future GUI terminal can reuse it. Scheduling, process isolation, persistent storage, a syscall ABI, networking, and userspace are still future work. See [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) for the staged plan.

## Quick start

Prerequisites: a Rust stable toolchain, `just`, Python 3, `xorriso`, QEMU (`qemu-system-x86_64`), and the target installed by `rust-toolchain.toml` (or `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`). The first image build downloads a pinned Limine binary release and verifies its SHA-256.

```sh
just help
just fmt
just test
just check
just build
just image
just smoke
just run       # interactive serial shell in QEMU; exit with Ctrl+C
just verify
```

`just build` produces `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `just image` creates `target/rustix.iso`, a hybrid BIOS/UEFI image; `just smoke` checks that Crabshell reaches its prompt; and `just run` starts an interactive QEMU session attached to the current terminal.

Try `pwd`, `ls /`, `mkdir notes`, `write notes/hello.txt "hello from Rustix"`, `cat notes/hello.txt`, and `cd ..` in Crabshell. Commands include `help`, `clear`, `pwd`, `ls`, `cd`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `write`, `append`, `cp`, `mv`, `cat`, `rm`, and `rmdir`. The RAM filesystem holds at most 31 entries plus its root, with files capped at 1024 bytes. See [`docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](docs/architecture/crabshell.md) for the shell and filesystem contract, [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) for build/emulator details, and [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) for the documentation map.

## Project principles

- The kernel and operating-system implementation are Rust-first and `no_std`; architecture-specific privileged operations are isolated under `src/arch/`.
- The kernel is the product. A bootloader may initialize the machine and transfer control, but policy, memory management, scheduling, and Unix-like services belong to Rustix.
- Keep unsafe code small, documented, and adjacent to its hardware/protocol boundary.
- Build incrementally: every roadmap milestone should have build checks, tests where practical, and updated design documentation.
- Unix-like behavior is an explicit compatibility goal, not a claim of POSIX compliance today.

## Repository map

- `src/main.rs` — freestanding kernel entry point and Crabshell handoff.
- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel command executor.
- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem, with host-side tests.
- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` command parser crate; no I/O or filesystem coupling.
- `src/boot.rs` — Limine requests and boot-memory-map reporting.
- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — COM1 polling driver used for shell output and input.
- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling.
- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers.
- `src/memory.rs` — architecture-independent boot-time memory accounting and host tests.
- `.cargo/config.toml`, `linker.ld` — x86_64-none code generation and ELF layout.
- `justfile` — formatting, tests, target checks, image creation, emulator smoke test, and aggregate verification.
- `limine.conf` — pinned boot configuration for the Rustix kernel.
- `scripts/boot.py` — checksum-verified Limine download, hybrid ISO assembly, and bounded QEMU validation.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — runs `just verify` on pushes and pull requests.
- `docs/` — architecture, drivers, development, security, and roadmap documentation.

## Context and decisions

- User wants Rustix’s own kernel, not a bootloader pretending to be the OS. Limine is only the external boot handoff.
- Current shell is kernel-mode and COM1-based; it is not a user process, secure shell, POSIX shell, or persistent filesystem.
- Example workflow: `just run`, then `pwd`, `ls /`, `mkdir notes`, `write notes/hello.txt "hello from Rustix"`, `cat notes/hello.txt`, etc. `cp` replaces a destination file; `mv` supports files only and refuses overwrite.
- Input is ASCII, max 256 bytes; quoted filenames, escapes, pipes, redirection, history, and process launching are not implemented.

    48	pub fn parse(line: &str) -> Result<Option<Command<'_>>, ParseError> {

    97	fn take_word(input: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str)> {
    98	    let input = input.trim_start();
    99	    if input.is_empty() {
   100	        return None;
   101	    }
   102	    let end = input.find(char::is_whitespace).unwrap_or(input.len());
   103	    Some((&input[..end], input[end..].trim_start()))
   104	}
   105	
   106	fn no_arguments(rest: &str) -> Result<(), ParseError> {
   107	    if rest.is_empty() {
   108	        Ok(())
   109	    } else {
   110	        Err(ParseError::TooManyArguments)
   111	    }
   112	}
   113	
   114	fn optional_path(rest: &str) -> Result<Option<&str>, ParseError> {
   115	    match take_word(rest) {
   116	        None => Ok(None),
   117	        Some((path, rest)) => {
   118	            no_arguments(rest)?;
   119	            Ok(Some(path))
   120	        }
   121	    }
   122	}
   123	
   124	fn one_path(rest: &str) -> Result<&str, ParseError> {
   125	    let (path, rest) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
   126	    no_arguments(rest)?;
   127	    Ok(path)
   128	}
   129	
   130	fn two_paths(rest: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), ParseError> {
   131	    let (source, rest) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
   132	    let (destination, rest) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
   133	    no_arguments(rest)?;
   134	    Ok((source, destination))
   135	}
   136	
   137	fn path_and_text(rest: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), ParseError> {
   138	    let (path, text) = take_word(rest).ok_or(ParseError::MissingArgument)?;
   139	    if text.is_empty() {
   140	        return Err(ParseError::MissingText);
   141	    }
   142	
   143	    let first = text.as_bytes()[0];
   144	    if first == b'\'' || first == b'"' {
   145	        if text.len() < 2 || text.as_bytes()[text.len() - 1] != first {
   146	            return Err(ParseError::UnterminatedQuote);
   147	        }
   148	        return Ok((path, &text[1..text.len() - 1]));
   149	    }
   150	
   151	    Ok((path, text))
   152	}

     8	/// Run Crabshell forever on the bootstrap CPU.
     9	pub fn run(filesystem: &mut RamFs, mut cwd: usize) -> ! {
    10	    crate::kprintln!("crabshell: ready (volatile RAM filesystem)");
    11	    print_motd(filesystem, cwd);
    12	
    13	    let mut input = [0u8; MAX_LINE_LENGTH];
    14	    loop {
    15	        print_prompt(filesystem, cwd);
    16	        let length = read_line(&mut input);
    17	        if length == 0 {
    18	            continue;
    19	        }
    20	
    21	        let line = match core::str::from_utf8(&input[..length]) {
    22	            Ok(line) => line,
    23	            Err(_) => {
    24	                crate::kprintln!("crabshell: input must be valid UTF-8");
    25	                continue;
    26	            }
    27	        };
    28	
    29	        match parse(line) {
    30	            Ok(Some(command)) => execute(command, filesystem, &mut cwd),
    31	            Ok(None) => {}
    32	            Err(error) => print_parse_error(error),
    33	        }
    34	    }
    35	}
    36	
    37	fn print_prompt(filesystem: &RamFs, cwd: usize) {
    38	    let mut path = [0u8; MAX_PATH_CAPACITY];
    39	    match filesystem.write_path(cwd, &mut path) {
    40	        Ok(length) => match core::str::from_utf8(&path[..length]) {
    41	            Ok(path) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:{}# ", path)),
    42	            Err(_) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:/?# ")),
    43	        },
    44	        Err(_) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:/?# ")),
    45	    }
    46	}
    47	
    48	fn read_line(input: &mut [u8; MAX_LINE_LENGTH]) -> usize {
    49	    let mut length = 0;
    50	    loop {
    51	        let Some(byte) = serial::try_read_byte() else {
    52	            core::hint::spin_loop();
    53	            continue;
    54	        };
    55	
    56	        match byte {
    57	            b'\r' | b'\n' => {
    58	                crate::kprintln!();
    59	                return length;
    60	            }
    61	            0x03 => {
    62	                crate::kprintln!("^C");
    63	                return 0;
    64	            }
    65	            0x08 | 0x7f if length > 0 => {
    66	                length -= 1;
    67	                serial::print(format_args!("\x08 \x08"));
    68	            }
    69	            0x20..=0x7e if length < input.len() => {
    70	                input[length] = byte;
    71	                length += 1;
    72	                serial::print(format_args!("{}", byte as char));
    73	            }
    74	            0x20..=0x7e => serial::print(format_args!("\x07")),
    75	            _ => {}
    76	        }
    77	    }
    78	}

   182	fn list_directory(filesystem: &RamFs, directory: usize) {
   183	    match filesystem.kind(directory) {
   184	        Ok(EntryKind::File) => match filesystem.entry(directory) {
   185	            Ok(entry) => crate::kprintln!("{} ({} bytes)", entry.name, entry.size),
   186	            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
   187	        },
   188	        Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
   189	        Ok(EntryKind::Directory) => match filesystem.child_count(directory) {
   190	            Ok(0) => crate::kprintln!("(empty)"),
   191	            Ok(count) => {
   192	                for index in 0..count {
   193	                    let Some(entry) = filesystem.child_at(directory, index) else {
   194	                        crate::kprintln!("crabshell: directory changed while listing");
   195	                        return;
   196	                    };
   197	                    match entry.kind {
   198	                        EntryKind::Directory => crate::kprintln!("{}/", entry.name),
   199	                        EntryKind::File => {
   200	                            crate::kprintln!("{}  {} bytes", entry.name, entry.size)
   201	                        }
   202	                    }
   203	                }
   204	            }
   205	            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
   206	        },
   207	    }
   208	}
   209	
   210	fn print_file_contents(text: &str) {
   211	    for (index, line) in text.split('\n').enumerate() {
   212	        if index != 0 {
   213	            serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
   214	        }
   215	        serial::print(format_args!("{}", line.strip_suffix('\r').unwrap_or(line)));
   216	    }
   217	    if !text.ends_with('\n') {
   218	        crate::kprintln!();
   219	    }
   220	}
   221	
   222	fn print_motd(filesystem: &RamFs, cwd: usize) {
   223	    if let Ok(node) = filesystem.resolve(cwd, "/etc/motd") {
   224	        if let Ok(bytes) = filesystem.read_file(node) {
   225	            if let Ok(text) = core::str::from_utf8(bytes) {
   226	                print_file_contents(text);
   227	            }
   228	        }
   229	    }
   230	}

   237	    crate::kprintln!("  ls [PATH]            list a directory or file");
   238	    crate::kprintln!("  cd PATH              change the current directory");
   239	    crate::kprintln!("  mkdir PATH            create a directory");
   240	    crate::kprintln!("  touch PATH            create an empty file");
   241	    crate::kprintln!("  write PATH TEXT       replace a file's contents");
   242	    crate::kprintln!("  append PATH TEXT      append text to a file");
   243	    crate::kprintln!("  cp SOURCE DEST        copy a file");
   244	    crate::kprintln!("  mv SOURCE DEST        move/rename a file");
   245	    crate::kprintln!("  cat PATH              print a text file");
   246	    crate::kprintln!("  rm PATH               remove a file");

   255	        ParseError::MissingArgument => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: missing path argument"),
   256	        ParseError::MissingText => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: missing text (usage: write PATH TEXT)"),
   257	        ParseError::TooManyArguments => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: too many arguments"),
   258	        ParseError::UnterminatedQuote => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: unterminated text quote"),
   259	    }

   266	        FsError::NameTooLong => "file name is too long (maximum 31 UTF-8 bytes)",
   267	        FsError::AlreadyExists => "an entry with that name already exists",
   268	        FsError::NotFound => "path not found",
   269	        FsError::NotDirectory => "a path component is not a directory",
   270	        FsError::IsDirectory => "operation requires a file, not a directory",
   271	        FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty => "directory is not empty",
   272	        FsError::NoSpace => "RAM filesystem is full",
   273	        FsError::FileTooLarge => "file exceeds the 1024-byte limit",
   274	        FsError::RootOperation => "operation is not permitted on the root directory",
   275	        FsError::BufferTooSmall => "path exceeds the display buffer",

    45	def require_tool(name: str) -> str:
    46	    path = shutil.which(name)
    47	    if path is None:
    48	        raise BuildError(f"required tool '{name}' was not found on PATH")
    49	    return path

    52	def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    53	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    54	    with path.open("rb") as source:
    55	        for block in iter(lambda: source.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
    56	            digest.update(block)
    57	    return digest.hexdigest()
    58

    60	def safe_extract(archive: zipfile.ZipFile, destination: Path) -> None:
    61	    root = destination.resolve()
    62	    for member in archive.infolist():
    63	        name = PurePosixPath(member.filename)
    64	        mode = member.external_attr >> 16
    65	        if not name.parts or name.is_absolute() or ".." in name.parts or ":" in name.parts[0]:
    66	            raise BuildError(f"unsafe path in Limine archive: {member.filename}")
    67	        if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
    68	            raise BuildError(f"symlink in Limine archive is not allowed: {member.filename}")
    69	        output = (destination / Path(*name.parts)).resolve()
    70	        if output != root and root not in output.parents:
    71	            raise BuildError(f"archive member escapes extraction directory: {member.filename}")
    72	    archive.extractall(destination)
    73

   466	    if path.is_empty() {
   467	        return Err(FsError::RootOperation);
   468	    }
   469	    match path.rsplit_once('/') {
   470	        Some(("", name)) => Ok(("/", name)),
   471	        Some((parent, name)) if !name.is_empty() => Ok((parent, name)),
   472	        Some(_) => Err(FsError::InvalidPath),
   473	        None => Ok((".", path)),
   474	    }
   475	}

    13	macro_rules! kprintln {
    14	    () => {{
    15	        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    16	    }};
    17	    ($($argument:tt)*) => {{
    18	        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!($($argument)*));
    19	        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    20	    }};
    21	}
    22	
    23	pub(crate) use kprintln;
    24	
    25	#[no_mangle]
    26	pub extern "C" fn _start() -> ! {
    27	    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    28	    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    29	    boot::report_boot_information();
    30	
    31	    // SAFETY: Crabshell is the only owner of this filesystem. The bootstrap is
    32	    // single-core and has no scheduler or filesystem-touching interrupt handlers.
    33	    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    34	    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
    35	        Ok(home) => shell::run(filesystem, home),
    36	        Err(error) => {
    37	            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
    38	            halt_forever()
    39	        }
    40	    }
    41	}
    42	
    43	#[panic_handler]
    44	fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    45	    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    46	    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    47	    halt_forever()
    48	}
    49	
    50	fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    51	    loop {
    52	        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
    53	        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    54	    }
    55	}

     1	//! Minimal polling 16550-compatible serial output for early x86_64 diagnostics.
     2	
     3	use core::fmt;
     4	use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
     5	
     6	const COM1: u16 = 0x3f8;
     7	static INITIALIZED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
     8	
     9	/// Configure COM1 for 38,400 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, one stop bit.
    10	pub fn initialize() {
    11	    // SAFETY: These are the conventional legacy COM1 I/O ports on x86 PCs.
    12	    unsafe {
    13	        super::io::write_u8(COM1 + 1, 0x00);
    14	        super::io::write_u8(COM1 + 3, 0x80);
    15	        super::io::write_u8(COM1, 0x03);
    16	        super::io::write_u8(COM1 + 1, 0x00);
    17	        super::io::write_u8(COM1 + 3, 0x03);
    18	        super::io::write_u8(COM1 + 2, 0xc7);
    19	        super::io::write_u8(COM1 + 4, 0x0b);
    20	    }
    21	    INITIALIZED.store(true, Ordering::Release);
    22	}
    23	
    24	/// Write formatted text to COM1. Output is silently skipped until initialized.
    25	pub fn print(arguments: fmt::Arguments<'_>) {
    26	    if INITIALIZED.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
    27	        let _ = SerialPort.write_fmt(arguments);
    28	    }
    29	}
    30	
    31	/// Return a received COM1 byte if one is ready, without waiting for input.
    32	pub fn try_read_byte() -> Option<u8> {
    33	    if !INITIALIZED.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
    34	        return None;
    35	    }
    36	
    37	    // SAFETY: COM1 is configured by `initialize`; the line-status register and
    38	    // receive register are accessed only by the single-core polling shell.
    39	    unsafe {
    40	        if super::io::read_u8(COM1 + 5) & 0x01 != 0 {
    41	            Some(super::io::read_u8(COM1))
    42	        } else {
    43	            None
    44	        }
    45	    }
    46	}
    47	
    48	struct SerialPort;
    49	
    50	impl fmt::Write for SerialPort {
    51	    fn write_str(&mut self, text: &str) -> fmt::Result {
    52	        for byte in text.bytes() {
    53	            // SAFETY: COM1 is initialized by `initialize`; accesses are serialized
    54	            // by the single-core bootstrap path before the kernel starts scheduling.
    55	            unsafe { write_byte(byte) };
    56	        }
    57	        Ok(())
    58	    }
    59	}
    60	
    61	unsafe fn write_byte(byte: u8) {
    62	    // Bound the wait so a missing or misconfigured UART cannot deadlock boot.
    63	    for _ in 0..100_000 {
    64	        // SAFETY: The caller ensures this is a legacy x86 port-I/O operation.
    65	        if unsafe { super::io::read_u8(COM1 + 5) } & 0x20 != 0 {
    66	            // SAFETY: The UART transmit register is COM1's base port.
    67	            unsafe { super::io::write_u8(COM1, byte) };
    68	            return;
    69	        }
    70	        core::hint::spin_loop();
    71	    }
    72	}

````rustix/README.md
     1	# Rustix
     2	
     3	Rustix (Rust-unix) is an experimental, 64-bit, Unix-like operating system whose kernel is written in Rust. This repository builds the kernel itself; Limine is used only as the external boot protocol/loader, not as a substitute for a Rustix kernel.
     4	
     5	Rustix now boots into **Crabshell**, a small kernel-mode shell on the COM1 serial terminal. It includes basic navigation and file commands backed by a fixed-capacity RAM filesystem. The filesystem is volatile and reset at every boot; this is an early kernel shell, not a userspace process or POSIX shell. The command parser lives in a separate, allocation-free `crabshell` crate so a future GUI terminal can reuse it. Scheduling, process isolation, persistent storage, a syscall ABI, networking, and userspace are still future work. See [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) for the staged plan.
     6	
     7	## Quick start
     8	
     9	Prerequisites: a Rust stable toolchain, `just`, Python 3, `xorriso`, QEMU (`qemu-system-x86_64`), and the target installed by `rust-toolchain.toml` (or `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`). The first image build downloads a pinned Limine binary release and verifies its SHA-256.
    10	
    11	```sh
    12	just help
    13	just fmt
    14	just test
    15	just check
    16	just build
    17	just image
    18	just smoke
    19	just run       # interactive serial shell in QEMU; exit with Ctrl+C
    20	just verify
    21	```
    22	
    23	`just build` produces `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `just image` creates `target/rustix.iso`, a hybrid BIOS/UEFI image; `just smoke` checks that Crabshell reaches its prompt; and `just run` starts an interactive QEMU session attached to the current terminal.
    24	
    25	Try `pwd`, `ls /`, `mkdir notes`, `write notes/hello.txt "hello from Rustix"`, `cat notes/hello.txt`, and `cd ..` in Crabshell. Commands include `help`, `clear`, `pwd`, `ls`, `cd`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `write`, `append`, `cp`, `mv`, `cat`, `rm`, and `rmdir`. The RAM filesystem holds at most 31 entries plus its root, with files capped at 1024 bytes. See [`docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](docs/architecture/crabshell.md) for the shell and filesystem contract, [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) for build/emulator details, and [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) for the documentation map.
    26	
    27	## Project principles
    28	
    29	- The kernel and operating-system implementation are Rust-first and `no_std`; architecture-specific privileged operations are isolated under `src/arch/`.
    30	- The kernel is the product. A bootloader may initialize the machine and transfer control, but policy, memory management, scheduling, and Unix-like services belong to Rustix.
    31	- Keep unsafe code small, documented, and adjacent to its hardware/protocol boundary.
    32	- Build incrementally: every roadmap milestone should have build checks, tests where practical, and updated design documentation.
    33	- Unix-like behavior is an explicit compatibility goal, not a claim of POSIX compliance today.
    34	
    35	## Repository map
    36	
    37	- `src/main.rs` — freestanding kernel entry point and Crabshell handoff.
    38	- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel command executor.
    39	- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem, with host-side tests.
    40	- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` command parser crate; no I/O or filesystem coupling.
    41	- `src/boot.rs` — Limine requests and boot-memory-map reporting.
    42	- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — COM1 polling driver used for shell output and input.
    43	- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling.
    44	- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers.
    45	- `src/memory.rs` — architecture-independent boot-time memory accounting and host tests.
    46	- `.cargo/config.toml`, `linker.ld` — x86_64-none code generation and ELF layout.
    47	- `justfile` — formatting, tests, target checks, image creation, emulator smoke test, and aggregate verification.
    48	- `limine.conf` — pinned boot configuration for the Rustix kernel.
    49	- `scripts/boot.py` — checksum-verified Limine download, hybrid ISO assembly, and bounded QEMU validation.
    50	- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — runs `just verify` on pushes and pull requests.
    51	- `docs/` — architecture, drivers, development, security, and roadmap documentation.

````
