//! Architecture-independent validation and accounting for physical memory maps.

/// Limine's memory-map type for ordinary usable RAM.
pub const MEMORY_MAP_USABLE: u64 = 0;
/// Maximum number of memory regions retained in the boot snapshot.
pub const MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS: usize = 256;

/// Classification of a physical memory region from the Limine memory map.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RegionKind {
    Usable,
    Reserved,
    AcpiReclaimable,
    AcpiNvs,
    BadMemory,
    BootloaderReclaimable,
    ExecutableAndModules,
    Framebuffer,
    Unknown(u64),
}

impl RegionKind {
    const fn from_limine(kind: u64) -> Self {
        match kind {
            0 => Self::Usable,
            1 => Self::Reserved,
            2 => Self::AcpiReclaimable,
            3 => Self::AcpiNvs,
            4 => Self::BadMemory,
            5 => Self::BootloaderReclaimable,
            6 => Self::ExecutableAndModules,
            7 => Self::Framebuffer,
            unknown => Self::Unknown(unknown),
        }
    }
}

/// Unvalidated region fields copied from a boot protocol response.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RawMemoryRegion {
    pub base: u64,
    pub length: u64,
    pub kind: u64,
}

/// Validated half-open physical address range `[start, end)`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PhysicalRegion {
    start: u64,
    end: u64,
    kind: RegionKind,
}

impl PhysicalRegion {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        start: 0,
        end: 0,
        kind: RegionKind::Unknown(0),
    };

    pub const fn start(&self) -> u64 {
        self.start
    }

    pub const fn end(&self) -> u64 {
        self.end
    }

    pub const fn length(&self) -> u64 {
        self.end - self.start
    }

    pub const fn kind(&self) -> RegionKind {
        self.kind
    }
}

/// Errors produced when a memory map is malformed or exceeds kernel capacity.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MemoryMapError {
    EmptyMap,
    TooManyRegions,
    EmptyRegion { index: usize },
    AddressOverflow { index: usize },
    OverlappingRegions { first: usize, second: usize },
    UsableTotalOverflow,
}

/// Validated, allocation-free snapshot of the physical memory map.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MemoryMap {
    regions: [PhysicalRegion; MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS],
    region_count: usize,
    usable_bytes: u64,
}

impl MemoryMap {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        regions: [PhysicalRegion::EMPTY; MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS],
        region_count: 0,
        usable_bytes: 0,
    };

    pub fn from_raw(regions: &[RawMemoryRegion]) -> Result<Self, MemoryMapError> {
        let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
        for region in regions {
            builder.push(region.base, region.length, region.kind)?;
        }
        builder.finish()
    }

    pub fn regions(&self) -> &[PhysicalRegion] {
        &self.regions[..self.region_count]
    }

    pub const fn usable_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
        self.usable_bytes
    }
}

/// Incremental validator used to copy loader entries without an intermediate heap.
pub struct MemoryMapBuilder {
    map: MemoryMap,
}

impl MemoryMapBuilder {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            map: MemoryMap::EMPTY,
        }
    }

    pub fn push(&mut self, base: u64, length: u64, raw_kind: u64) -> Result<(), MemoryMapError> {
        let index = self.map.region_count;
        if index == MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
            return Err(MemoryMapError::TooManyRegions);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyRegion { index });
        }
        let end = base
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(MemoryMapError::AddressOverflow { index })?;
        let kind = RegionKind::from_limine(raw_kind);

        for (other_index, other) in self.map.regions().iter().enumerate() {
            if base < other.end && other.start < end {
                return Err(MemoryMapError::OverlappingRegions {
                    first: other_index,
                    second: index,
                });
            }
        }

        let usable_bytes = if kind == RegionKind::Usable {
            self.map
                .usable_bytes
                .checked_add(length)
                .ok_or(MemoryMapError::UsableTotalOverflow)?
        } else {
            self.map.usable_bytes
        };

        self.map.regions[index] = PhysicalRegion { start: base, end, kind };
        self.map.region_count += 1;
        self.map.usable_bytes = usable_bytes;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn finish(self) -> Result<MemoryMap, MemoryMapError> {
        if self.map.region_count == 0 {
            Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyMap)
        } else {
            Ok(self.map)
        }
    }
}

impl Default for MemoryMapBuilder {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// Add an already-validated usable region length to a running total.
///
/// Non-usable regions leave the total unchanged. `None` signals arithmetic
/// overflow so callers can report malformed or unrepresentable maps.
pub const fn add_usable_bytes(total: u64, region_kind: u64, region_length: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    if region_kind == MEMORY_MAP_USABLE {
        total.checked_add(region_length)
    } else {
        Some(total)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use core::assert_eq;

    use super::{
        add_usable_bytes, MemoryMap, MemoryMapBuilder, MemoryMapError, RawMemoryRegion,
        RegionKind, MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS, MEMORY_MAP_USABLE,
    };

    #[test]
    fn counts_only_usable_regions() {
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(4096, MEMORY_MAP_USABLE, 2048), Some(6144));
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(4096, 1, 2048), Some(4096));
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_total_overflow() {
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(u64::MAX - 4, MEMORY_MAP_USABLE, 8), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_ranges_and_preserves_all_region_kinds() {
        let raw = [
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x1000, length: 0x2000, kind: 0 },
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x4000, length: 0x1000, kind: 5 },
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x5000, length: 0x1000, kind: 99 },
        ];
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&raw).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(map.usable_bytes(), 0x2000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].start(), 0x1000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].end(), 0x3000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].length(), 0x2000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].kind(), RegionKind::Usable);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[1].kind(), RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[2].kind(), RegionKind::Unknown(99));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_empty_zero_length_overflowing_and_overlapping_maps() {
        assert_eq!(MemoryMap::from_raw(&[]), Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyMap));
        assert_eq!(
            MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion { base: 0, length: 0, kind: 0 }]),
            Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyRegion { index: 0 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion { base: u64::MAX - 3, length: 8, kind: 0 }]),
            Err(MemoryMapError::AddressOverflow { index: 0 })
        );

        let overlap = [
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x1000, length: 0x2000, kind: 0 },
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x2fff, length: 0x1000, kind: 1 },
        ];
        assert_eq!(
            MemoryMap::from_raw(&overlap),
            Err(MemoryMapError::OverlappingRegions { first: 0, second: 1 })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepts_adjacent_ranges_and_rejects_excess_entries() {
        let adjacent = [
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x1000, length: 0x1000, kind: 0 },
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x2000, length: 0x1000, kind: 1 },
        ];
        assert!(MemoryMap::from_raw(&adjacent).is_ok());

        let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
        for index in 0..MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
            builder.push((index as u64) * 0x2000, 0x1000, 1).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(builder.push(0x1_0000_0000, 0x1000, 1), Err(MemoryMapError::TooManyRegions));
    }
}

# Rustix roadmap

This roadmap is staged to keep each milestone reviewable and bootable. **Milestone 0's end-to-end image and boot validation remains pending. Milestone 1's snapshot, range-validation, and CPU-reporting implementation is underway but has not yet been compiled or boot-tested in the current environment.** Items below are planned unless checked off; checked implementation work is not the same as a passing end-to-end validation.

## Milestone 0 — Rust kernel bootstrap (current)

- [x] `no_std` Rust kernel binary for `x86_64-unknown-none`.
- [x] Own ELF linker layout and Limine boot-protocol requests.
- [x] COM1 serial diagnostics, memory-map/HHDM summary, and panic halt path.
- [x] Narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers and a non-blocking PS/2 raw-scancode polling driver.
- [x] `just` commands and architecture/development/security/driver documentation.
- [x] Hash-pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary distribution and checked extraction.
- [x] Reproducible BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO recipe and documented boot configuration.
- [x] Bounded QEMU serial smoke-test runner and CI workflow.
- [x] Separate no-std Crabshell command-parser crate and kernel serial shell frontend.
- [x] Fixed-capacity RAM filesystem with basic directory and text-file operations.
- [ ] Execute the end-to-end image build and QEMU Crabshell prompt smoke test successfully in CI or a local environment.

**Exit criteria:** a clean checkout builds the pinned image, boots it in the documented emulator, and captures the expected serial banner in automated validation. The workflow is implemented; the criterion remains pending until an end-to-end run passes.

## Milestone 1 — validated boot state and machine diagnostics (implementation underway)

- [x] Copy HHDM and memory-map responses into an owned `BootInfo` snapshot before shell startup.
- [x] Validate response presence/alignment, bounded entry count, nonzero ranges, checked range ends, and non-overlap; reject a malformed snapshot before entering Crabshell.
- [x] Preserve reserved, ACPI, bad-memory, loader-reclaimable, executable/module, framebuffer, and unknown region classifications without reclaiming any memory.
- [x] Report baseline CPUID vendor and kernel-relevant feature bits; document the current serial-only console.
- [x] Document that loader- and ACPI-reclaimable ranges remain reserved until their respective data is no longer needed.
- [ ] Add serial-formatting tests and validate the snapshot and diagnostics in a successful target build and emulator boot.

**Exit criteria:** malformed maps fail closed; an emulator test validates reported regions and boot metadata. The source implementation is not yet build- or boot-verified.

## Milestone 2 — memory ownership and CPU exceptions

- Physical frame allocator with overflow-safe range handling and exhaustion tests.
- Kernel-owned page-table management and documented direct-map policy.
- Global heap with deterministic out-of-memory behavior.
- GDT/TSS and IDT setup; exception handlers with register/error-code diagnostics; fault-injection tests.

**Exit criteria:** allocator and mapping invariants are tested, page faults are diagnosable, and the kernel remains bootable under emulator tests.

## Milestone 3 — interrupts, time, and scheduling

- Timer and interrupt-controller setup with explicit interrupt-safe locking rules.
- Kernel threads and context switching; per-CPU data before SMP work.
- Preemptive scheduling only after interrupt, stack, and lock invariants are validated.
- Application processor startup as a separate milestone, not an implicit extension of single-core code.

**Exit criteria:** deterministic thread lifecycle tests and bounded timer/preemption integration tests.

## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI

- User-mode entry/exit and isolated address spaces.
- Versioned syscall ABI, validated copy-in/copy-out, and documented error semantics.
- Initial process lifecycle, descriptor table, and executable-loading path.
- Adversarial tests for invalid pointers, bad lengths, overflow, and process teardown.

**Exit criteria:** a controlled userspace init process can execute and use a small documented syscall subset without corrupting the kernel on invalid input.

## Milestone 5 — Unix-like services and storage

- VFS and mount model, file descriptors, and a first on-disk filesystem.
- Process creation/exec/wait semantics, pipes or IPC, and signal-like delivery as designed.
- Device discovery/driver model and networking only after ownership and isolation policies exist.
- Compatibility tests for any claimed Unix/POSIX behavior; keep unsupported operations explicit.

**Exit criteria:** documented userland tools can run from a reproducible image and integration tests cover process and file semantics.

## Working rule

Each milestone should add code, tests, and updated documentation together. Do not advance the stated project status merely because an interface or design note exists. Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable subsystem stubs.

### # Boot protocol and kernel entry › ## Current boot contract › L5-6
```
Rustix currently expects a Limine-compatible x86_64 handoff. Limine is an external loader; it does not implement Rustix's kernel services. The kernel requests protocol base revision 3, the higher-half direct-map (HHDM) offset, and the memory map.

```

### # Boot protocol and kernel entry › ## Current boot contract › L7-8
```
Requests are kept in `.limine_requests_start`, `.limine_requests`, and `.limine_requests_end` by `linker.ld`. The response-bearing request records are mutable and the output `.limine_requests` section is placed in a writable load segment because Limine fills their response pointers before entering Rustix. The ELF entry symbol is `_start`.

```

### # Boot protocol and kernel entry › ## Current boot contract › ### Entry sequence › L11-12
```
1. Limine loads the ELF and transfers control to `_start` under the x86_64 Limine protocol.
2. `_start` configures the legacy COM1 UART for polling output and input.
```

### # Boot protocol and kernel entry › ## Current boot contract › ### Entry sequence › L13-15
```
3. The kernel copies the HHDM and memory-map responses into an owned `BootInfo` snapshot. It rejects missing, misaligned, oversized, overflowing, empty, or overlapping metadata before using it.
4. The kernel reports validated ranges and baseline CPUID features, then seeds a volatile RAM filesystem and enters Crabshell on the serial console.
5. The shell busy-polls COM1 because no scheduler or UART interrupt handler exists yet. The kernel does not return to the loader.
```

### # Boot protocol and kernel entry › ## Current boot contract › ### Entry sequence › L17-18
```
The memory-map snapshot stores physical regions as checked half-open ranges `[start, end)` and retains Limine's known classifications plus unknown type values. It is diagnostic metadata only: it does not authorize Rustix to access every region, reclaim loader memory, or mutate the current page tables. The HHDM offset is validated and reported but is not yet used to translate or dereference physical addresses.

```

### # Boot protocol and kernel entry › ## Failure behavior and limitations › L31-32
```
Missing responses, bad alignment, invalid HHDM values, excessive counts, null entries, address arithmetic overflow, and invalid or overlapping physical ranges reject the complete boot snapshot. `_start` halts before starting Crabshell rather than continuing with partial memory metadata. Structural checks cannot establish that a non-null loader pointer is mapped and readable; that remains an explicit trust assumption of the Limine handoff. COM1 writes use a bounded polling loop so a non-responsive UART does not block forever.

```

### # Boot protocol and kernel entry › ## Failure behavior and limitations › L33-34
```
The repository now includes a Limine v12.9.3 binary archive pin with SHA-256 verification, a hybrid ISO recipe, and a bounded QEMU serial smoke test that checks Crabshell's prompt. These workflows are automated in CI, but the boot milestone is not considered complete until that end-to-end job passes. There is still no framebuffer console, reboot/shutdown interface, or broader boot-protocol compatibility test. The available serial and keyboard drivers do not imply a general device model.

```

### # Boot protocol and kernel entry › ## Future boot work › L37-38
```
The kernel now snapshots and validates the Limine map and preserves firmware and loader-reclaimable classifications without reclaiming them. No region is considered Rustix-owned or free for allocation yet. Loader-reclaimable memory must remain unavailable until Rustix has copied any needed boot data and explicitly reaches a documented reclaim point; ACPI reclaimable memory needs the ACPI tables to be copied or parsed first. Frame allocation, page-table replacement, and ownership transfer remain future work.

```

`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation and classification. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.

This is validation and reporting only, not ownership. Rustix does not allocate from any region, reclaim bootloader memory, manage page tables, provide a heap, or expose a safe physical-memory abstraction. The HHDM offset is checked and logged, not used for memory access.

# Architecture overview

## Goals

Rustix is a from-scratch operating system project with its own kernel, written in Rust. The intended initial platform is 64-bit x86 (`x86_64`), with a Unix-like process and file-descriptor model. The kernel should eventually own machine initialization, physical and virtual memory management, interrupt handling, scheduling, system calls, and device policy. A bootloader is a transport into the kernel, not a replacement for those facilities.

Unix-like is a compatibility direction. It does **not** mean the current kernel is POSIX-compliant, nor does it commit the project to a particular existing kernel's internals. Compatibility profiles and a userland should be defined only after the underlying process, descriptor, and syscall semantics are implemented and tested.

## Current implementation

1. Cargo builds a `no_std`, `no_main` ELF for `x86_64-unknown-none` and uses Limine for the boot handoff.
2. `_start` initializes COM1, captures and validates a bounded boot-info snapshot, reports the memory map and CPUID features, initializes a fixed-capacity RAM filesystem, and enters Crabshell.
3. Crabshell reads an ASCII command line from the serial UART and supports basic navigation, directory creation/listing, and text-file operations.
4. The separately packaged `crabshell` `no_std` crate parses commands without allocation or dependence on kernel I/O, making that layer reusable by a future graphical frontend.
5. The kernel library contains checked memory accounting and the bounded VFS implementation, both covered by host-side unit tests.

The current shell and filesystem run in kernel mode. Files exist only in RAM and disappear at reboot. There is no heap, Rustix-owned page-table manager, interrupt descriptor table, scheduler, user/kernel isolation, syscall ABI, on-disk filesystem, network stack, or userspace process.

## Intended layers (planned)

```text
User programs and system utilities
        | versioned syscall ABI
Kernel services: processes, descriptors, VFS, IPC, signals
        | explicit ownership and authorization checks
Core kernel: scheduler, virtual memory, physical frames, interrupts
        | narrow architecture abstractions
x86_64 platform: paging, exceptions, timers, AP startup, drivers
        | Limine boot handoff only
Firmware and hardware
```

The diagram is a target decomposition, not a claim that those layers are implemented. Architecture-independent policy should live in safe Rust where possible; privileged instructions and raw device access should stay in small, reviewed architecture modules.

## Design constraints

- **Freestanding:** kernel code does not link `std`; allocation must be introduced deliberately after a physical-frame and heap strategy exists.
- **Explicit unsafe boundaries:** raw pointers from boot protocol responses and x86 port I/O are unsafe. Each use must document its preconditions and remain short-lived.
- **Fail visibly:** early boot failures should produce serial diagnostics where possible and then halt, rather than continue with invalid machine state.
- **Checked arithmetic:** physical ranges, sizes, and address translations must reject overflow.
- **No premature ABI:** userspace interfaces stay unstable until process lifetime, error conventions, copy-in/copy-out, and versioning are designed together.
- **Hardware-independent tests:** parsing, range arithmetic, and policy should be testable as ordinary host-side Rust wherever possible.

## Boot and CPU assumptions

The current target is x86_64, with a 4 KiB page-oriented linker layout and no red zone. Limine performs the initial platform setup required by its protocol. Rustix must not assume that receiving a memory-map response means it owns the loader's page tables or can overwrite reserved regions. The current bootstrap does not enable interrupts or start application processors.

See [Boot protocol](boot.md), [Memory management](memory.md), [x86_64 drivers](drivers.md), [Crabshell](crabshell.md), and [the roadmap](../roadmap/README.md) for subsystem boundaries and planned acceptance criteria.

```

# Rustix documentation

Rustix is a 64-bit, Rust-first, Unix-like operating-system project. This index separates current implementation facts from planned interfaces: roadmap items are proposals until the corresponding code and tests exist.

## Start here

- [Project and implementation overview](architecture/overview.md)
- [Boot protocol and current entry path](architecture/boot.md)
- [Memory-management direction](architecture/memory.md)
- [x86_64 drivers and hardware boundary](architecture/drivers.md)
- [Crabshell and the volatile RAM filesystem](architecture/crabshell.md)
- [Unix-like process and syscall direction](architecture/syscall-abi.md)
- [Build and toolchain guide](development/building.md)
- [Testing and verification](development/testing.md)
- [Security and unsafe-code policy](security.md)
- [Milestones and acceptance criteria](roadmap/README.md)

## Current status

The repository contains a bare-metal `no_std` Rust kernel for `x86_64-unknown-none`. After Limine handoff it validates and copies memory-map metadata into an owned snapshot, reports baseline CPUID features, seeds a volatile RAM filesystem, and runs Crabshell over the COM1 serial console. Crabshell's allocation-free parser is a separate crate; the kernel handles command execution. The image builder and bounded QEMU prompt smoke test are wired into CI, but the latest source changes have not yet been built or boot-tested and Milestone 0's end-to-end run remains pending. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process: there is not yet an allocator, interrupt subsystem, scheduler, process isolation, persistent filesystem, or Unix compatibility layer.

## Documentation conventions

- **Implemented** means present in the repository and checked by current code or tests.
- **Planned** means an architectural direction, not a stable ABI or delivered capability.
- Any future ABI proposal must state versioning, error behavior, memory ownership, and compatibility expectations before it is treated as stable.

# Building Rustix

## Prerequisites

- Rust stable with `rustfmt`; the repository pins these in `rust-toolchain.toml`.
- The `x86_64-unknown-none` target. The toolchain file requests it automatically; if needed, install it with `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`.
- [`just`](https://just.systems/) to run the repository's named tasks.
- Python 3.8 or newer (standard library only), with `python` on `PATH`; `xorriso`; and QEMU with `qemu-system-x86_64` for image creation and boot smoke tests.

An ELF inspection tool such as `llvm-readelf` or `readelf` is useful when diagnosing linker output. The first image build downloads the pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary archive into `target/tools/` and verifies its published SHA-256 before extraction.

## Common commands

Run from the repository root:

```sh
just help
just fmt       # check Rust formatting
just test      # parser, RAM-filesystem, and memory tests
just check     # type-check the freestanding kernel target
just build     # optimized kernel ELF
just image     # hybrid BIOS/UEFI ISO at target/rustix.iso
just smoke     # bounded QEMU boot to the Crabshell prompt
just run       # interactive serial shell in QEMU (Ctrl+C to stop)
just verify    # fmt, workspace tests, target check, image, and QEMU smoke test
```

Equivalent Rust checks are `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --lib`, `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-none`, and `cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-none`. Image creation and QEMU validation are provided by `scripts/boot.py` and are intentionally part of `just verify`.

The optimized ELF is written to `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `cargo check` checks the target without producing a boot image. The library tests run on the host and exercise code that does not require privileged instructions.

## Target-specific linker setup

`.cargo/config.toml` applies the Rustix linker script and x86_64 kernel constraints only to `x86_64-unknown-none`. `linker.ld` emits an ELF64 x86_64 image at the higher-half base, retains Limine request sections in a writable load segment for bootloader response pointers, and defines `_start` as the entry symbol. The build uses no third-party Rust crates; the boot protocol is represented by small in-tree Rust structures and constants.

Changing the target, virtual base, relocation model, or request ABI requires updating the linker script, protocol documentation, and validation plan together. Do not use host builds of the kernel binary as evidence that the freestanding target links correctly.

## Building and smoke-testing a boot image

`limine.conf` boots the kernel immediately and enables 38,400-baud serial output. `just image` builds the ELF, fetches Limine v12.9.3's binary ZIP from its immutable GitHub release, checks the pinned SHA-256, prepares a BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO, and installs the BIOS boot code. The Limine archive and extracted tools remain under ignored `target/`; no third-party binaries are checked into the source tree.

`just smoke` launches `target/rustix.iso` in `qemu-system-x86_64` with a 256 MiB q35 machine, headless display, captured COM1 output, and a 20-second deadline. QEMU is expected to remain running at the interactive shell; the runner terminates it at the deadline and requires the startup banner, Crabshell-ready message, and initial prompt. On a failure it prints the serial log. The log remains at `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` for inspection.

`just run` launches the same image with the serial port attached to the host terminal, allowing interactive shell use. Stop the emulator with `Ctrl+C`.

`just verify` includes the emulator smoke test and therefore needs Python 3, xorriso, QEMU, network access for the first Limine download, and the Rust target. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs the system tools on Ubuntu 24.04 and runs the same command. This verifies the boot path in CI; it is still not a substitute for testing physical hardware.

## Troubleshooting

- **Target not installed:** install `x86_64-unknown-none` as shown above.
- **`just` not found:** install `just`; Rust-only checks can still be run with the Cargo commands above.
- **`xorriso` or QEMU not found:** install the host image/emulator tools listed in prerequisites, then retry `just image` or `just smoke`.
- **Limine SHA-256 mismatch:** the pinned archive may have changed or been corrupted; the script removes the mismatched download and refuses to use it. Check the official v12.9.3 release digest before changing the pin.
- **Linker-script error:** build only for `x86_64-unknown-none`; confirm the invocation runs from the repository root so `linker.ld` resolves.
- **No serial output:** inspect `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` and QEMU's stderr. The image config and Rustix COM1 driver both use 38,400 baud.

```

        0xc7b1_dd30_df4c_8b88,
        0x0a82_e883_a194_f07b,
        0x67cf_3d9d_378a_806f,
        0xe304_acdf_c50c_3c62,
    ],
    revision: 0,
    response: core::ptr::null_mut(),
};

/// Owned kernel snapshot of the handoff values Rustix currently consumes.
pub struct BootInfo {
    pub hhdm_revision: u64,
    pub hhdm_offset: u64,
    pub memory_map_revision: u64,
    pub memory_map: MemoryMap,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BootInfoError {
    MissingHhdmResponse,
    InvalidHhdmResponsePointer,
    InvalidHhdmOffset,
    MissingMemoryMapResponse,
    InvalidMemoryMapResponsePointer,
    MemoryMapCountDoesNotFit,
    TooManyMemoryRegions,
    EmptyMemoryMap,
    InvalidEntriesPointer,
    EntriesAddressOverflow,
    InvalidEntryPointer { index: usize },
    InvalidMemoryMap(MemoryMapError),
}

/// Copy and validate the boot data needed by the current kernel.
///
/// Structural checks can reject malformed pointers and ranges, but cannot prove
/// that a loader-provided pointer is mapped and readable. That remains part of
/// the documented Limine handoff trust boundary until the kernel owns its maps.
pub fn capture_boot_information() -> Result<BootInfo, BootInfoError> {
    let hhdm_request = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(HHDM_REQUEST) };
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let hhdm_pointer = unsafe {
        core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*hhdm_request).response))
    };
    if hhdm_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingHhdmResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(hhdm_pointer) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let hhdm = unsafe { hhdm_pointer.read_volatile() };
    if hhdm.offset & 0xfff != 0 || !is_canonical_virtual_address(hhdm.offset) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmOffset);
    }

    let memory_map_request = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(MEMORY_MAP_REQUEST) };
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let memory_map_pointer = unsafe {
        core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*memory_map_request).response))
    };
    if memory_map_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingMemoryMapResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(memory_map_pointer) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMapResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let response = unsafe { memory_map_pointer.read_volatile() };
    let entry_count = usize::try_from(response.entry_count)
        .map_err(|_| BootInfoError::MemoryMapCountDoesNotFit)?;
    if entry_count > MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
        return Err(BootInfoError::TooManyMemoryRegions);
    }
    if entry_count == 0 {
        return Err(BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap);
    }
    if response.entries.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(response.entries) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    let entry_bytes = entry_count
        .checked_mul(size_of::<*const MemoryMapEntry>())
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    let entries_start = response.entries as usize;
    let entries_end = entries_start
        .checked_add(entry_bytes)
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(entries_start as u64)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address((entries_end - 1) as u64)
    {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }

    let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
    for index in 0..entry_count {
        // SAFETY: Limine promises an array of `entry_count` pointers. The count
        // is capped and pointer alignment/address arithmetic are checked above.
        let entry_pointer = unsafe { response.entries.add(index).read_volatile() };
        if !is_valid_pointer(entry_pointer) {
            return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntryPointer { index });
        }
        // SAFETY: Limine promises each non-null entry pointer is readable.
        let entry = unsafe { entry_pointer.read_volatile() };
        builder
            .push(entry.base, entry.length, entry.kind)
            .map_err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap)?;
    }

    let memory_map = builder.finish().map_err(|error| match error {
        MemoryMapError::EmptyMap => BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap,
        other => BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap(other),
    })?;

    Ok(BootInfo {
        hhdm_revision: hhdm.revision,
        hhdm_offset: hhdm.offset,
        memory_map_revision: response.revision,
        memory_map,
    })
}

/// Print a report from the copied snapshot; no loader pointers are used here.
pub fn report_boot_information(boot_info: &BootInfo) {
    crate::kprintln!(
        "HHDM: offset {:#018x}, response revision {}",
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.hhdm_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "memory map: {} validated regions, {} MiB usable RAM, response revision {}",
        boot_info.memory_map.regions().len(),
        boot_info.memory_map.usable_bytes() / (1024 * 1024),
        boot_info.memory_map_revision
    );
    for region in boot_info.memory_map.regions() {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "  [{:#018x}, {:#018x}) {:?}",
            region.start(),
            region.end(),
            region.kind()
        );
    }
    crate::kprintln!("console: COM1 serial (polling)");

    let cpu = crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::identify();
    let vendor = core::str::from_utf8(&cpu.vendor).unwrap_or("unknown");
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU: {} (basic leaf {}, extended leaf {:#x})",
        vendor,
        cpu.max_basic_leaf,
        cpu.max_extended_leaf
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU features: SSE2={}, NX={}, 1GiB-pages={}, long-mode={}, LA57-supported={}",
        cpu.has_sse2,
        cpu.has_nx,
        cpu.has_1g_pages,
        cpu.has_long_mode,
        cpu.has_la57
    );
}

fn is_valid_pointer<T>(pointer: *const T) -> bool {
    let start = pointer as usize;
    let Some(end) = start.checked_add(size_of::<T>()) else {
        return false;
    };
    !pointer.is_null()
        && start & (align_of::<T>() - 1) == 0
        && is_canonical_virtual_address(start as u64)
        && is_canonical_virtual_address((end - 1) as u64)
}

fn is_canonical_virtual_address(address: u64) -> bool {
    let upper_48 = address >> 48;
    let upper_57 = address >> 57;
    upper_48 == 0 || upper_48 == 0xffff || upper_57 == 0 || upper_57 == 0x7f
}

//! Architecture-independent validation and accounting for physical memory maps.

/// Limine's memory-map type for ordinary usable RAM.
pub const MEMORY_MAP_USABLE: u64 = 0;
/// Maximum number of memory regions retained in the boot snapshot.
pub const MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS: usize = 256;

/// Classification of a physical memory region from the Limine memory map.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RegionKind {
    Usable,
    Reserved,
    AcpiReclaimable,
    AcpiNvs,
    BadMemory,
    BootloaderReclaimable,
    ExecutableAndModules,
    Framebuffer,
    Unknown(u64),
}

impl RegionKind {
    const fn from_limine(kind: u64) -> Self {
        match kind {
            0 => Self::Usable,
            1 => Self::Reserved,
            2 => Self::AcpiReclaimable,
            3 => Self::AcpiNvs,
            4 => Self::BadMemory,
            5 => Self::BootloaderReclaimable,
            6 => Self::ExecutableAndModules,
            7 => Self::Framebuffer,
            unknown => Self::Unknown(unknown),
        }
    }
}

/// Unvalidated region fields copied from a boot protocol response.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RawMemoryRegion {
    pub base: u64,
    pub length: u64,
    pub kind: u64,
}

/// Validated half-open physical address range `[start, end)`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PhysicalRegion {
    start: u64,
    end: u64,
    kind: RegionKind,
}

impl PhysicalRegion {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        start: 0,
        end: 0,
        kind: RegionKind::Unknown(0),
    };

    pub const fn start(&self) -> u64 {
        self.start
    }

    pub const fn end(&self) -> u64 {
        self.end
    }

    pub const fn length(&self) -> u64 {
        self.end - self.start
    }

    pub const fn kind(&self) -> RegionKind {
        self.kind
    }
}

/// Errors produced when a memory map is malformed or exceeds kernel capacity.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MemoryMapError {
    EmptyMap,
    TooManyRegions,
    EmptyRegion { index: usize },
    AddressOverflow { index: usize },
    OverlappingRegions { first: usize, second: usize },
    UsableTotalOverflow,
}

/// Validated, allocation-free snapshot of the physical memory map.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MemoryMap {
    regions: [PhysicalRegion; MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS],
    region_count: usize,
    usable_bytes: u64,
}

impl MemoryMap {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        regions: [PhysicalRegion::EMPTY; MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS],
        region_count: 0,
        usable_bytes: 0,
    };

    pub fn from_raw(regions: &[RawMemoryRegion]) -> Result<Self, MemoryMapError> {
        let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
        for region in regions {
            builder.push(region.base, region.length, region.kind)?;
        }
        builder.finish()
    }

    pub fn regions(&self) -> &[PhysicalRegion] {
        &self.regions[..self.region_count]
    }

    pub const fn usable_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
        self.usable_bytes
    }
}

/// Incremental validator used to copy loader entries without an intermediate heap.
pub struct MemoryMapBuilder {
    map: MemoryMap,
}

impl MemoryMapBuilder {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            map: MemoryMap::EMPTY,
        }
    }

    pub fn push(&mut self, base: u64, length: u64, raw_kind: u64) -> Result<(), MemoryMapError> {
        let index = self.map.region_count;
        if index == MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
            return Err(MemoryMapError::TooManyRegions);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyRegion { index });
        }
        let end = base
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(MemoryMapError::AddressOverflow { index })?;
        let kind = RegionKind::from_limine(raw_kind);

        for (other_index, other) in self.map.regions().iter().enumerate() {
            if base < other.end && other.start < end {
                return Err(MemoryMapError::OverlappingRegions {
                    first: other_index,
                    second: index,
                });
            }
        }

        let usable_bytes = if kind == RegionKind::Usable {
            self.map
                .usable_bytes
                .checked_add(length)
                .ok_or(MemoryMapError::UsableTotalOverflow)?
        } else {
            self.map.usable_bytes
        };

        self.map.regions[index] = PhysicalRegion { start: base, end, kind };
        self.map.region_count += 1;
        self.map.usable_bytes = usable_bytes;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn finish(self) -> Result<MemoryMap, MemoryMapError> {
        if self.map.region_count == 0 {
            Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyMap)
        } else {
            Ok(self.map)
        }
    }
}

impl Default for MemoryMapBuilder {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// Add an already-validated usable region length to a running total.
///
/// Non-usable regions leave the total unchanged. `None` signals arithmetic
/// overflow so callers can report malformed or unrepresentable maps.
pub const fn add_usable_bytes(total: u64, region_kind: u64, region_length: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    if region_kind == MEMORY_MAP_USABLE {
        total.checked_add(region_length)
    } else {
        Some(total)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use core::assert_eq;

    use super::{
        add_usable_bytes, MemoryMap, MemoryMapBuilder, MemoryMapError, RawMemoryRegion,
        RegionKind, MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS, MEMORY_MAP_USABLE,
    };

    #[test]
    fn counts_only_usable_regions() {
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(4096, MEMORY_MAP_USABLE, 2048), Some(6144));
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(4096, 1, 2048), Some(4096));
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_total_overflow() {
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(u64::MAX - 4, MEMORY_MAP_USABLE, 8), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_ranges_and_preserves_all_region_kinds() {
        let raw = [
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x1000, length: 0x2000, kind: 0 },
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x4000, length: 0x1000, kind: 5 },
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x5000, length: 0x1000, kind: 99 },
        ];
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&raw).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(map.usable_bytes(), 0x2000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].start(), 0x1000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].end(), 0x3000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].length(), 0x2000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].kind(), RegionKind::Usable);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[1].kind(), RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[2].kind(), RegionKind::Unknown(99));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_empty_zero_length_overflowing_and_overlapping_maps() {
        assert_eq!(MemoryMap::from_raw(&[]), Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyMap));
        assert_eq!(
            MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion { base: 0, length: 0, kind: 0 }]),
            Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyRegion { index: 0 })
        );
        let overflowing = [RawMemoryRegion {
            base: u64::MAX - 3,
            length: 8,
            kind: 0,
        }];
        assert_eq!(
            MemoryMap::from_raw(&overflowing),
            Err(MemoryMapError::AddressOverflow { index: 0 })
        );

        let overlap = [
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x1000, length: 0x2000, kind: 0 },
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x2fff, length: 0x1000, kind: 1 },
        ];
        assert_eq!(
            MemoryMap::from_raw(&overlap),
            Err(MemoryMapError::OverlappingRegions { first: 0, second: 1 })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepts_adjacent_ranges_and_rejects_excess_entries() {
        let adjacent = [
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x1000, length: 0x1000, kind: 0 },
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x2000, length: 0x1000, kind: 1 },
        ];
        assert!(MemoryMap::from_raw(&adjacent).is_ok());

        let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
        for index in 0..MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
            builder.push((index as u64) * 0x2000, 0x1000, 1).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(
            builder.push(0x1_0000_0000, 0x1000, 1),
            Err(MemoryMapError::TooManyRegions)
        );
    }
}

//! Minimal CPUID identification for boot diagnostics on x86_64.

use core::arch::x86_64::{__cpuid, __cpuid_count};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CpuInfo {
    pub vendor: [u8; 12],
    pub max_basic_leaf: u32,
    pub max_extended_leaf: u32,
    pub has_sse2: bool,
    pub has_nx: bool,
    pub has_1g_pages: bool,
    pub has_long_mode: bool,
    pub has_la57: bool,
}

/// Read CPUID identity and a small set of baseline kernel-relevant features.
pub fn identify() -> CpuInfo {
    // CPUID is part of the x86_64 architectural baseline.
    let basic = unsafe { __cpuid(0) };
    let mut vendor = [0; 12];
    vendor[0..4].copy_from_slice(&basic.ebx.to_le_bytes());
    vendor[4..8].copy_from_slice(&basic.edx.to_le_bytes());
    vendor[8..12].copy_from_slice(&basic.ecx.to_le_bytes());

    let basic_features = if basic.eax >= 1 {
        Some(unsafe { __cpuid(1) })
    } else {
        None
    };
    let extended = unsafe { __cpuid(0x8000_0000) };
    let extended_features = if extended.eax >= 0x8000_0001 {
        Some(unsafe { __cpuid(0x8000_0001) })
    } else {
        None
    };
    let structured_features = if basic.eax >= 7 {
        Some(unsafe { __cpuid_count(7, 0) })
    } else {
        None
    };

    CpuInfo {
        vendor,
        max_basic_leaf: basic.eax,
        max_extended_leaf: extended.eax,
        has_sse2: basic_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 26) != 0),
        has_nx: extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 20) != 0),
        has_1g_pages: extended_features
            .is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 26) != 0),
        has_long_mode: extended_features
            .is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 29) != 0),
        has_la57: structured_features
            .is_some_and(|features| features.ecx & (1 << 16) != 0),
    }
}

pub fn capture_boot_information() -> Result<BootInfo, BootInfoError> {

    }

    let memory_map_request = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(MEMORY_MAP_REQUEST) };
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let memory_map_pointer = unsafe {
        core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*memory_map_request).response))
    };
    if memory_map_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingMemoryMapResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(memory_map_pointer) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMapResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let response = unsafe { memory_map_pointer.read_volatile() };
    let entry_count = usize::try_from(response.entry_count)
        .map_err(|_| BootInfoError::MemoryMapCountDoesNotFit)?;
    if entry_count > MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
        return Err(BootInfoError::TooManyMemoryRegions);
    }
    if entry_count == 0 {
        return Err(BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap);
    }
    if response.entries.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(response.entries) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    let entry_bytes = entry_count
        .checked_mul(size_of::<*const MemoryMapEntry>())
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    let entries_start = response.entries as usize;
    let entries_end = entries_start
        .checked_add(entry_bytes)
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(entries_start as u64)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address((entries_end - 1) as u64)
    {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }

    let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
    for index in 0..entry_count {
        // SAFETY: Limine promises an array of `entry_count` pointers. The count
        // is capped and pointer alignment/address arithmetic are checked above.
        let entry_pointer = unsafe { response.entries.add(index).read_volatile() };
        if !is_valid_pointer(entry_pointer) {
            return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntryPointer { index });
        }
        // SAFETY: Limine promises each non-null entry pointer is readable.
        let entry = unsafe { entry_pointer.read_volatile() };
        builder
            .push(entry.base, entry.length, entry.kind)
            .map_err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap)?;
    }

    let memory_map = builder.finish().map_err(|error| match error {
        MemoryMapError::EmptyMap => BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap,
        other => BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap(other),
    })?;

    Ok(BootInfo {
        hhdm_revision: hhdm.revision,
        hhdm_offset: hhdm.offset,
        memory_map_revision: response.revision,
        memory_map,
    })
}

/// Print a report from the copied snapshot; no loader pointers are used here.
pub fn report_boot_information(boot_info: &BootInfo) {
    crate::kprintln!(
        "HHDM: offset {:#018x}, response revision {}",
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.hhdm_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "memory map: {} validated regions, {} MiB usable RAM, response revision {}",
        boot_info.memory_map.regions().len(),
        boot_info.memory_map.usable_bytes() / (1024 * 1024),
        boot_info.memory_map_revision
    );
    for region in boot_info.memory_map.regions() {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "  [{:#018x}, {:#018x}) {:?}",
            region.start(),
            region.end(),
            region.kind()
        );
    }
    crate::kprintln!("console: COM1 serial (polling)");

    let cpu = crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::identify();
    let vendor = core::str::from_utf8(&cpu.vendor).unwrap_or("unknown");
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU: {} (basic leaf {}, extended leaf {:#x})",
        vendor,
        cpu.max_basic_leaf,
        cpu.max_extended_leaf
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU feature support: SSE2={}, NX={}, 1GiB-pages={}, long-mode={}, LA57={}",
        cpu.has_sse2,
        cpu.has_nx,
        cpu.has_1g_pages,
        cpu.has_long_mode,
        cpu.has_la57
    );
}

fn is_valid_pointer<T>(pointer: *const T) -> bool {
    let start = pointer as usize;
    let Some(end) = start.checked_add(size_of::<T>()) else {
        return false;
    };
    !pointer.is_null()
        && start & (align_of::<T>() - 1) == 0
        && is_canonical_virtual_address(start as u64)
        && is_canonical_virtual_address((end - 1) as u64)
}

fn is_canonical_virtual_address(address: u64) -> bool {
    let upper_48 = address >> 48;
    let upper_57 = address >> 57;
    upper_48 == 0 || upper_48 == 0xffff || upper_57 == 0 || upper_57 == 0x7f
}

//! Fixed-capacity physical frame allocator built from validated memory regions.
//!
//! This module assigns physical frame addresses only. It does not map or access
//! them, and it never promotes loader- or firmware-reclaimable memory to free RAM.

use crate::memory::{MemoryMap, RegionKind, MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS};

/// The current x86_64 base page size used by Rustix.
pub const FRAME_SIZE: u64 = 4096;
/// Keep the first MiB unavailable even if a loader labels it usable.
pub const LOW_MEMORY_RESERVED_END: u64 = 0x10_0000;
/// Maximum number of disjoint ranges kept in each fixed range table.
pub const MAX_FRAME_RANGES: usize = MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Frame(u64);

impl Frame {
    /// Physical address of the beginning of this frame.
    pub const fn address(self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }

    /// Construct a candidate frame address for release to the allocator.
    ///
    /// `FrameAllocator::deallocate` validates alignment, managed-range
    /// membership, and whether the frame is already free.
    pub const fn from_address(address: u64) -> Self {
        Self(address)
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FrameError {
    RangeTableFull,
    RangeOverlap,
    UnalignedFrame,
    NotManaged,
    AlreadyFree,
    AccountingOverflow,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct FrameRange {
    start: u64,
    end: u64,
}

impl FrameRange {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self { start: 0, end: 0 };
}

/// A bounded allocator over only validated `Usable` memory-map ranges.
///
/// Both range tables are sorted, disjoint, page-aligned half-open ranges. The
/// allocator returns `None` on exhaustion and reports invalid frees explicitly.
pub struct FrameAllocator {
    managed: [FrameRange; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
    managed_count: usize,
    free: [FrameRange; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
    free_count: usize,
    managed_frames: u64,
    free_frames: u64,
}

impl FrameAllocator {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        managed: [FrameRange::EMPTY; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
        managed_count: 0,
        free: [FrameRange::EMPTY; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
        free_count: 0,
        managed_frames: 0,
        free_frames: 0,
    };

    /// Build allocator metadata without allocating or touching physical memory.
    pub fn from_memory_map(map: &MemoryMap) -> Result<Self, FrameError> {
        let mut allocator = Self::EMPTY;
        let page_mask = !(FRAME_SIZE - 1);

        for region in map.regions() {
            if region.kind() != RegionKind::Usable {
                continue;
            }

            let start = region.start().max(LOW_MEMORY_RESERVED_END);
            let Some(start) = start
                .checked_add(FRAME_SIZE - 1)
                .map(|address| address & page_mask)
            else {
                continue;
            };
            let end = region.end() & page_mask;
            if start >= end {
                continue;
            }

            let range = FrameRange { start, end };
            Self::insert_range(&mut allocator.managed, &mut allocator.managed_count, range)?;
            Self::insert_range(&mut allocator.free, &mut allocator.free_count, range)?;

            let frames = (end - start) / FRAME_SIZE;
            allocator.managed_frames = allocator
                .managed_frames
                .checked_add(frames)
                .ok_or(FrameError::AccountingOverflow)?;
            allocator.free_frames = allocator
                .free_frames
                .checked_add(frames)
                .ok_or(FrameError::AccountingOverflow)?;
        }

        Ok(allocator)
    }

    /// Number of complete frames inside eligible usable regions.
    pub const fn managed_frames(&self) -> u64 {
        self.managed_frames
    }

    /// Number of currently unallocated frames.
    pub const fn free_frames(&self) -> u64 {
        self.free_frames
    }

    /// Allocate the lowest-address available frame, or return `None` on exhaustion.
    pub fn allocate(&mut self) -> Option<Frame> {
        if self.free_count == 0 {
            return None;
        }

        let address = self.free[0].start;
        self.free[0].start += FRAME_SIZE;
        self.free_frames -= 1;
        if self.free[0].start == self.free[0].end {
            Self::remove_range(&mut self.free, &mut self.free_count, 0);
        }
        Some(Frame(address))
    }

    /// Return a frame to the allocator, merging adjacent free ranges.
    pub fn deallocate(&mut self, frame: Frame) -> Result<(), FrameError> {
        let address = frame.address();
        if address & (FRAME_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(FrameError::UnalignedFrame);
        }
        let end = address
            .checked_add(FRAME_SIZE)
            .ok_or(FrameError::NotManaged)?;
        if !self
            .managed
            .iter()
            .take(self.managed_count)
            .any(|range| range.start <= address && end <= range.end)
        {
            return Err(FrameError::NotManaged);
        }
        if self
            .free
            .iter()
            .take(self.free_count)
            .any(|range| address < range.end && range.start < end)
        {
            return Err(FrameError::AlreadyFree);
        }

        let new_free_count = self
            .free_frames
            .checked_add(1)
            .ok_or(FrameError::AccountingOverflow)?;
        Self::insert_range(
            &mut self.free,
            &mut self.free_count,
            FrameRange { start: address, end },
        )?;
        self.free_frames = new_free_count;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn insert_range(
        ranges: &mut [FrameRange; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
        count: &mut usize,
        incoming: FrameRange,
    ) -> Result<(), FrameError> {
        let mut index = 0;
        while index < *count && ranges[index].start < incoming.start {
            index += 1;
        }

        if (index > 0 && ranges[index - 1].end > incoming.start)
            || (index < *count && incoming.end > ranges[index].start)
        {
            return Err(FrameError::RangeOverlap);
        }

        let joins_previous = index > 0 && ranges[index - 1].end == incoming.start;
        let joins_next = index < *count && incoming.end == ranges[index].start;
        match (joins_previous, joins_next) {
            (true, true) => {
                ranges[index - 1].end = ranges[index].end;
                Self::remove_range(ranges, count, index);
            }
            (true, false) => ranges[index - 1].end = incoming.end,
            (false, true) => ranges[index].start = incoming.start,
            (false, false) => {
                if *count == MAX_FRAME_RANGES {
                    return Err(FrameError::RangeTableFull);
                }
                for move_index in (index..*count).rev() {
                    ranges[move_index + 1] = ranges[move_index];
                }
                ranges[index] = incoming;
                *count += 1;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn remove_range(
        ranges: &mut [FrameRange; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
        count: &mut usize,
        index: usize,
    ) {
        for move_index in index..(*count - 1) {
            ranges[move_index] = ranges[move_index + 1];
        }
        *count -= 1;
        ranges[*count] = FrameRange::EMPTY;
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use core::assert_eq;

    use super::{
        Frame, FrameAllocator, FrameError, MAX_FRAME_RANGES, FRAME_SIZE,
        LOW_MEMORY_RESERVED_END,
    };
    use crate::memory::{MemoryMap, RawMemoryRegion};

    fn allocator_for(regions: &[RawMemoryRegion]) -> FrameAllocator {
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(regions).unwrap();
        FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn aligns_usable_ranges_and_ignores_reserved_regions() {
        let regions = [
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x10_0003, length: 0x5000, kind: 0 },
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x10_8000, length: 0x2000, kind: 1 },
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x11_0000, length: 0x1000, kind: 0 },
        ];
        let mut allocator = allocator_for(&regions);

        assert_eq!(allocator.managed_frames(), 5);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 5);
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocate().unwrap().address(), 0x10_1000);
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocate().unwrap().address(), 0x10_2000);
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocate().unwrap().address(), 0x10_3000);
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocate().unwrap().address(), 0x10_4000);
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocate().unwrap().address(), 0x11_0000);
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocate(), None);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn reserves_low_memory_and_discards_partial_pages() {
        let regions = [RawMemoryRegion {
            base: 0,
            length: 0x20_0064,
            kind: 0,
        }];
        let allocator = allocator_for(&regions);

        assert_eq!(allocator.managed_frames(), 256);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 256);
        assert!(LOW_MEMORY_RESERVED_END >= 0x10_0000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn deallocation_rejects_bad_frames_and_coalesces_neighbors() {
        let regions = [RawMemoryRegion {
            base: 0x10_0000,
            length: FRAME_SIZE * 4,
            kind: 0,
        }];
        let mut allocator = allocator_for(&regions);
        let first = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let second = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let third = allocator.allocate().unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            allocator.deallocate(Frame::from_address(first.address() + 1)),
            Err(FrameError::UnalignedFrame)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            allocator.deallocate(Frame::from_address(0x20_0000)),
            Err(FrameError::NotManaged)
        );

        allocator.deallocate(second).unwrap();
        allocator.deallocate(third).unwrap();
        allocator.deallocate(first).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 4);
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocate(), Some(first));
        assert_eq!(allocator.deallocate(first), Err(FrameError::AlreadyFree));
    }

    #[test]
    fn adjacent_usable_ranges_are_coalesced() {
        let regions = [
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x10_0000, length: FRAME_SIZE, kind: 0 },
            RawMemoryRegion { base: 0x10_1000, length: FRAME_SIZE, kind: 0 },
        ];
        let mut allocator = allocator_for(&regions);

        assert_eq!(allocator.managed_frames(), 2);
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocate().unwrap().address(), 0x10_0000);
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocate().unwrap().address(), 0x10_1000);
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocate(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn fragmentation_is_bounded_by_the_fixed_range_table() {
        let frame_count = MAX_FRAME_RANGES * 2 + 1;
        let regions = [RawMemoryRegion {
            base: 0x10_0000,
            length: FRAME_SIZE * frame_count as u64,
            kind: 0,
        }];
        let mut allocator = allocator_for(&regions);
        let mut allocated = [Frame::from_address(0); MAX_FRAME_RANGES * 2 + 1];

        for frame in &mut allocated {
            *frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        }
        for index in (0..allocated.len()).step_by(2) {
            let result = allocator.deallocate(allocated[index]);
            if index == MAX_FRAME_RANGES * 2 {
                assert_eq!(result, Err(FrameError::RangeTableFull));
            } else {
                assert_eq!(result, Ok(()));
            }
        }
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), MAX_FRAME_RANGES as u64);
    }
}

//! Fixed-capacity physical frame allocator built from validated memory regions.
//!
//! This module assigns physical frame addresses only. It does not map or access
//! them, and it never promotes loader- or firmware-reclaimable memory to free RAM.

use crate::memory::{MemoryMap, RegionKind, MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS};

/// The current x86_64 base page size used by Rustix.
pub const FRAME_SIZE: u64 = 4096;
/// Keep the first MiB unavailable even if a loader labels it usable.
pub const LOW_MEMORY_RESERVED_END: u64 = 0x10_0000;
/// Maximum number of disjoint ranges kept in each fixed range table.
pub const MAX_FRAME_RANGES: usize = MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Frame(u64);

impl Frame {
    /// Physical address of the beginning of this frame.
    pub const fn address(self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }

    /// Construct a candidate frame address for release to the allocator.
    ///
    /// `FrameAllocator::deallocate` validates alignment, managed-range
    /// membership, and whether the frame is already free.
    pub const fn from_address(address: u64) -> Self {
        Self(address)
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FrameError {
    RangeTableFull,
    RangeOverlap,
    UnalignedFrame,
    NotManaged,
    AlreadyFree,
    AccountingOverflow,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct FrameRange {
    start: u64,
    end: u64,
}

impl FrameRange {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self { start: 0, end: 0 };
}

/// A bounded allocator over only validated `Usable` memory-map ranges.
///
/// Both range tables are sorted, disjoint, page-aligned half-open ranges. The
/// allocator returns `None` on exhaustion and reports invalid frees explicitly.
pub struct FrameAllocator {
    managed: [FrameRange; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
    managed_count: usize,
    free: [FrameRange; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
    free_count: usize,
    managed_frames: u64,
    free_frames: u64,
}

impl FrameAllocator {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        managed: [FrameRange::EMPTY; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
        managed_count: 0,
        free: [FrameRange::EMPTY; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
        free_count: 0,
        managed_frames: 0,
        free_frames: 0,
    };

    /// Build allocator metadata without allocating or touching physical memory.
    pub fn from_memory_map(map: &MemoryMap) -> Result<Self, FrameError> {
        let mut allocator = Self::EMPTY;
        let page_mask = !(FRAME_SIZE - 1);

        for region in map.regions() {
            if region.kind() != RegionKind::Usable {
                continue;
            }

            let start = region.start().max(LOW_MEMORY_RESERVED_END);
            let Some(start) = start
                .checked_add(FRAME_SIZE - 1)
                .map(|address| address & page_mask)
            else {
                continue;
            };
            let end = region.end() & page_mask;
            if start >= end {
                continue;
            }

            let range = FrameRange { start, end };
            Self::insert_range(&mut allocator.managed, &mut allocator.managed_count, range)?;
            Self::insert_range(&mut allocator.free, &mut allocator.free_count, range)?;

            let frames = (end - start) / FRAME_SIZE;
            allocator.managed_frames = allocator
                .managed_frames
                .checked_add(frames)
                .ok_or(FrameError::AccountingOverflow)?;
            allocator.free_frames = allocator
                .free_frames
                .checked_add(frames)
                .ok_or(FrameError::AccountingOverflow)?;
        }

        Ok(allocator)
    }

    /// Number of complete frames inside eligible usable regions.
    pub const fn managed_frames(&self) -> u64 {
        self.managed_frames
    }

    /// Number of currently unallocated frames.
    pub const fn free_frames(&self) -> u64 {
        self.free_frames
    }

    /// Allocate the lowest-address available frame, or return `None` on exhaustion.
    pub fn allocate(&mut self) -> Option<Frame> {
        if self.free_count == 0 {
            return None;
        }

        let address = self.free[0].start;
        self.free[0].start += FRAME_SIZE;
        self.free_frames -= 1;
        if self.free[0].start == self.free[0].end {
            Self::remove_range(&mut self.free, &mut self.free_count, 0);
        }
        Some(Frame(address))
    }

    /// Return a frame to the allocator, merging adjacent free ranges.
    pub fn deallocate(&mut self, frame: Frame) -> Result<(), FrameError> {
        let address = frame.address();
        if address & (FRAME_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(FrameError::UnalignedFrame);
        }
        let end = address
            .checked_add(FRAME_SIZE)
            .ok_or(FrameError::NotManaged)?;
        if !self
            .managed
            .iter()
            .take(self.managed_count)
            .any(|range| range.start <= address && end <= range.end)
        {
            return Err(FrameError::NotManaged);
        }
        if self
            .free
            .iter()
            .take(self.free_count)
            .any(|range| address < range.end && range.start < end)
        {
            return Err(FrameError::AlreadyFree);
        }

        let new_free_count = self
            .free_frames
            .checked_add(1)
            .ok_or(FrameError::AccountingOverflow)?;
        Self::insert_range(
            &mut self.free,
            &mut self.free_count,
            FrameRange { start: address, end },
        )?;
        self.free_frames = new_free_count;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn insert_range(
        ranges: &mut [FrameRange; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
        count: &mut usize,
        incoming: FrameRange,
    ) -> Result<(), FrameError> {
        let mut index = 0;
        while index < *count && ranges[index].start < incoming.start {
            index += 1;
        }

        if (index > 0 && ranges[index - 1].end > incoming.start)
            || (index < *count && incoming.end > ranges[index].start)
        {
            return Err(FrameError::RangeOverlap);
        }

        let joins_previous = index > 0 && ranges[index - 1].end == incoming.start;
        let joins_next = index < *count && incoming.end == ranges[index].start;
        match (joins_previous, joins_next) {
            (true, true) => {
                ranges[index - 1].end = ranges[index].end;
                Self::remove_range(ranges, count, index);
            }
            (true, false) => ranges[index - 1].end = incoming.end,
            (false, true) => ranges[index].start = incoming.start,
            (false, false) => {
                if *count == MAX_FRAME_RANGES {
                    return Err(FrameError::RangeTableFull);
                }
                for move_index in (index..*count).rev() {
                    ranges[move_index + 1] = ranges[move_index];
                }
                ranges[index] = incoming;
                *count += 1;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn remove_range(
        ranges: &mut [FrameRange; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
        count: &mut usize,
        index: usize,
    ) {
        for move_index in index..(*count - 1) {
            ranges[move_index] = ranges[move_index + 1];
        }
        *count -= 1;
        ranges[*count] = FrameRange::EMPTY;
    }
}

# Rustix roadmap

This roadmap is staged to keep each milestone reviewable and bootable. **Milestone 0's end-to-end image and boot validation remains pending. Milestone 1's snapshot and CPU-reporting source, plus Milestone 2's frame-allocator core, have not yet been compiled or boot-tested in the current environment.** Items below are planned unless checked off; checked implementation work is not the same as a passing end-to-end validation.

## Milestone 0 — Rust kernel bootstrap (current)

- [x] `no_std` Rust kernel binary for `x86_64-unknown-none`.
- [x] Own ELF linker layout and Limine boot-protocol requests.
- [x] COM1 serial diagnostics, memory-map/HHDM summary, and panic halt path.
- [x] Narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers and a non-blocking PS/2 raw-scancode polling driver.
- [x] `just` commands and architecture/development/security/driver documentation.
- [x] Hash-pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary distribution and checked extraction.
- [x] Reproducible BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO recipe and documented boot configuration.
- [x] Bounded QEMU serial smoke-test runner and CI workflow.
- [x] Separate no-std Crabshell command-parser crate and kernel serial shell frontend.
- [x] Fixed-capacity RAM filesystem with basic directory and text-file operations.
- [ ] Execute the end-to-end image build and QEMU Crabshell prompt smoke test successfully in CI or a local environment.

**Exit criteria:** a clean checkout builds the pinned image, boots it in the documented emulator, and captures the expected serial banner in automated validation. The workflow is implemented; the criterion remains pending until an end-to-end run passes.

## Milestone 1 — validated boot state and machine diagnostics (implementation underway)

- [x] Copy HHDM and memory-map responses into an owned `BootInfo` snapshot before shell startup.
- [x] Validate response presence/alignment, bounded entry count, nonzero ranges, checked range ends, and non-overlap; reject a malformed snapshot before entering Crabshell.
- [x] Preserve reserved, ACPI, bad-memory, loader-reclaimable, executable/module, framebuffer, and unknown region classifications without reclaiming any memory.
- [x] Report baseline CPUID vendor and kernel-relevant feature bits; document the current serial-only console.
- [x] Document that loader- and ACPI-reclaimable ranges remain reserved until their respective data is no longer needed.
- [ ] Add serial-formatting tests and validate the snapshot and diagnostics in a successful target build and emulator boot.

**Exit criteria:** malformed maps fail closed; an emulator test validates reported regions and boot metadata. The source implementation is not yet build- or boot-verified.

## Milestone 2 — memory ownership and CPU exceptions (in progress)

- [x] Fixed-capacity frame-allocator core over validated usable ranges, with alignment, low-memory reservation, deallocation/coalescing, fragmentation limits, and host-side tests (`src/frame.rs`). It is not yet initialized by or wired into the live kernel.
- [ ] Kernel-owned page-table management and a direct-map policy; allocated frames must not be dereferenced until mappings are explicitly established.
- [ ] Global heap with deterministic out-of-memory behavior, built only after frame allocation and page mapping work.
- [ ] GDT/TSS and IDT setup; exception handlers with register/error-code diagnostics and fault-injection tests.
- [ ] Target build, host tests, and emulator validation for the milestone.

**Exit criteria:** allocator and mapping invariants are tested, page faults are diagnosable, and the kernel remains bootable under emulator tests.

## Milestone 3 — interrupts, time, and scheduling

- Timer and interrupt-controller setup with explicit interrupt-safe locking rules.
- Kernel threads and context switching; per-CPU data before SMP work.
- Preemptive scheduling only after interrupt, stack, and lock invariants are validated.
- Application processor startup as a separate milestone, not an implicit extension of single-core code.

**Exit criteria:** deterministic thread lifecycle tests and bounded timer/preemption integration tests.

## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI

- User-mode entry/exit and isolated address spaces.
- Versioned syscall ABI, validated copy-in/copy-out, and documented error semantics.
- Initial process lifecycle, descriptor table, and executable-loading path.
- Adversarial tests for invalid pointers, bad lengths, overflow, and process teardown.

**Exit criteria:** a controlled userspace init process can execute and use a small documented syscall subset without corrupting the kernel on invalid input.

## Milestone 5 — Unix-like services and storage

- VFS and mount model, file descriptors, and a first on-disk filesystem.
- Process creation/exec/wait semantics, pipes or IPC, and signal-like delivery as designed.
- Device discovery/driver model and networking only after ownership and isolation policies exist.
- Compatibility tests for any claimed Unix/POSIX behavior; keep unsupported operations explicit.

**Exit criteria:** documented userland tools can run from a reproducible image and integration tests cover process and file semantics.

## Working rule

Each milestone should add code, tests, and updated documentation together. Do not advance the stated project status merely because an interface or design note exists. Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable subsystem stubs.

# Testing and verification

## Current checks

`just verify` runs the standard development verification sequence:

1. `just fmt` — fail on formatting differences across the workspace.
2. `just test` — run host-side memory-map, frame-allocator, RAM-filesystem, and Crabshell parser tests.
3. `just check` — check the `x86_64-unknown-none` kernel target.
4. `just smoke` — build the pinned hybrid ISO, boot it in QEMU, and check that Crabshell reaches its prompt within a deadline.

Keep the Crabshell parser, VFS, memory-map validator, and frame allocator independent of hardware so syntax, path handling, storage semantics, and frame ownership can be tested without booting. Add tests for boundaries and failure behavior when introducing new pure kernel helpers. The kernel binary is not a host test target.

## What current checks do not prove

- `cargo check` does not perform a final target link.
- A successful ELF link does not prove the boot protocol is recognized or `_start` is reached.
- Host unit tests do not validate privileged instructions, UART behavior, memory-map pointer validity, page tables, interrupts, or actual hardware.
- The QEMU smoke test proves the kernel reaches the shell prompt; it does not yet send interactive file commands or prove persistence across reboot.
- There is no on-disk filesystem integration test, syscall/userspace test, fuzz target, or physical-hardware test.

## Validation policy

For changes to the kernel entry, linker script, boot requests, architecture code, shell, or VFS, run `just verify`. For memory-management and ABI code, add negative tests for overflow, malformed ranges, permission failures, and invalid user pointers before exposing those paths to userspace.

Record commands actually run and any environment limitation in change summaries; never call an unexecuted build “passing.”
