//! Kernel-side Crabshell frontend: serial input, prompts, and RAM-filesystem commands.

use crabshell::{parse, Command, ParseError, MAX_LINE_LENGTH};
use rustix_kernel::vfs::{EntryKind, FsError, RamFs, MAX_PATH_CAPACITY};

use crate::arch::x86_64::serial;
use crate::boot::BootInfo;

/// Run Crabshell forever on the bootstrap CPU.
pub fn run(filesystem: &mut RamFs, mut cwd: usize, boot_info: &BootInfo) -> ! {
    crate::kprintln!("crabshell: ready (volatile RAM filesystem)");
    print_motd(filesystem, cwd);

    let mut input = [0u8; MAX_LINE_LENGTH];
    loop {
        print_prompt(filesystem, cwd);
        let length = read_line(&mut input);
        if length == 0 {
            continue;
        }

        let line = match core::str::from_utf8(&input[..length]) {
            Ok(line) => line,
            Err(_) => {
                crate::kprintln!("crabshell: input must be valid UTF-8");
                continue;
            }
        };

        match parse(line) {
            Ok(Some(command)) => execute(command, filesystem, &mut cwd, boot_info),
            Ok(None) => {}
            Err(error) => print_parse_error(error),
        }
    }
}

fn print_prompt(filesystem: &RamFs, cwd: usize) {
    let mut path = [0u8; MAX_PATH_CAPACITY];
    match filesystem.write_path(cwd, &mut path) {
        Ok(length) => match core::str::from_utf8(&path[..length]) {
            Ok(path) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:{}# ", path)),
            Err(_) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:/?# ")),
        },
        Err(_) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:/?# ")),
    }
}

fn read_line(input: &mut [u8; MAX_LINE_LENGTH]) -> usize {
    let mut length = 0;
    loop {
        let Some(byte) = serial::try_read_byte() else {
            core::hint::spin_loop();
            continue;
        };

        match byte {
            b'\r' | b'\n' => {
                crate::kprintln!();
                return length;
            }
            0x03 => {
                crate::kprintln!("^C");
                return 0;
            }
            0x08 | 0x7f if length > 0 => {
                length -= 1;
                serial::print(format_args!("\x08 \x08"));
            }
            0x20..=0x7e if length < input.len() => {
                input[length] = byte;
                length += 1;
                serial::print(format_args!("{}", byte as char));
            }
            0x20..=0x7e => serial::print(format_args!("\x07")),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

fn execute(
    command: Command<'_>,
    filesystem: &mut RamFs,
    cwd: &mut usize,
    boot_info: &BootInfo,
) {
    match command {
        Command::Help => print_help(),
        Command::Clear => serial::print(format_args!("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")),
        Command::Pwd => {
            let mut path = [0u8; MAX_PATH_CAPACITY];
            match filesystem.write_path(*cwd, &mut path) {
                Ok(length) => match core::str::from_utf8(&path[..length]) {
                    Ok(path) => crate::kprintln!("{}", path),
                    Err(_) => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: could not display current path"),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            }
        }
        Command::Meminfo => {
            let managed = boot_info.frame_allocator.managed_frames();
            let free = boot_info.frame_allocator.free_frames();
            crate::kprintln!("usable RAM: {} bytes", boot_info.memory_map.usable_bytes());
            crate::kprintln!(
                "physical frames: {} managed, {} free, {} allocated",
                managed,
                free,
                managed - free
            );
        }
        Command::Ls(path) => {
            let directory = match path {
                Some(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
                    Ok(node) => node,
                    Err(error) => {
                        report_fs_error(error);
                        return;
                    }
                },
                None => *cwd,
            };
            list_directory(filesystem, directory);
        }
        Command::Cd(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.kind(node) {
                Ok(EntryKind::Directory) => *cwd = node,
                Ok(EntryKind::File) => report_fs_error(FsError::NotDirectory),
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Mkdir(path) => match filesystem.create_dir_path(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Touch(path) => match filesystem.open_or_create_file(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Write { path, contents } => {
            match filesystem.open_or_create_file(*cwd, path) {
                Ok(node) => match filesystem.write_file(node, contents.as_bytes()) {
                    Ok(()) => {}
                    Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            }
        }
        Command::Append { path, contents } => {
            match filesystem.open_or_create_file(*cwd, path) {
                Ok(node) => match filesystem.append_file(node, contents.as_bytes()) {
                    Ok(()) => {}
                    Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            }
        }
        Command::Cp {
            source,
            destination,
        } => match filesystem.copy_file_path(*cwd, source, destination) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Mv {
            source,
            destination,
        } => match filesystem.move_file_path(*cwd, source, destination) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Cat(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.read_file(node) {
                Ok(bytes) => match core::str::from_utf8(bytes) {
                    Ok(text) => print_file_contents(text),
                    Err(_) => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: binary file display is not supported"),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Rm(path) => match filesystem.remove_file_path(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Rmdir(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) if node == *cwd => {
                crate::kprintln!("crabshell: cannot remove the current directory");
            }
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.remove_dir(node) {
                Ok(()) => {}
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
    }
}

fn list_directory(filesystem: &RamFs, directory: usize) {
    match filesystem.kind(directory) {
        Ok(EntryKind::File) => match filesystem.entry(directory) {
            Ok(entry) => crate::kprintln!("{} ({} bytes)", entry.name, entry.size),
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        Ok(EntryKind::Directory) => match filesystem.child_count(directory) {
            Ok(0) => crate::kprintln!("(empty)"),
            Ok(count) => {
                for index in 0..count {
                    let Some(entry) = filesystem.child_at(directory, index) else {
                        crate::kprintln!("crabshell: directory changed while listing");
                        return;
                    };
                    match entry.kind {
                        EntryKind::Directory => crate::kprintln!("{}/", entry.name),
                        EntryKind::File => {
                            crate::kprintln!("{}  {} bytes", entry.name, entry.size)
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
    }
}

fn print_file_contents(text: &str) {
    for (index, line) in text.split('\n').enumerate() {
        if index != 0 {
            serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
        }
        serial::print(format_args!("{}", line.strip_suffix('\r').unwrap_or(line)));
    }
    if !text.ends_with('\n') {
        crate::kprintln!();
    }
}

fn print_motd(filesystem: &RamFs, cwd: usize) {
    if let Ok(node) = filesystem.resolve(cwd, "/etc/motd") {
        if let Ok(bytes) = filesystem.read_file(node) {
            if let Ok(text) = core::str::from_utf8(bytes) {
                print_file_contents(text);
            }
        }
    }
}

fn print_help() {
    crate::kprintln!("Crabshell commands:");
    crate::kprintln!("  help                 show this help");
    crate::kprintln!("  clear                clear an ANSI-compatible terminal");
    crate::kprintln!("  pwd                  print the current directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  meminfo              show validated memory and frame counts");
    crate::kprintln!("  ls [PATH]            list a directory or file");
    crate::kprintln!("  cd PATH              change the current directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  mkdir PATH            create a directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  touch PATH            create an empty file");
    crate::kprintln!("  write PATH TEXT       replace a file's contents");
    crate::kprintln!("  append PATH TEXT      append text to a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  cp SOURCE DEST        copy a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  mv SOURCE DEST        move/rename a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  cat PATH              print a text file");
    crate::kprintln!("  rm PATH               remove a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  rmdir PATH            remove an empty directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  write/append accept a quoted or unquoted text remainder.");
    crate::kprintln!("  RAM filesystem: 31 entries plus root; files up to 1024 bytes.");
}

fn print_parse_error(error: ParseError) {
    match error {
        ParseError::UnknownCommand => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: unknown command (try 'help')"),
        ParseError::MissingArgument => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: missing path argument"),
        ParseError::MissingText => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: missing text (usage: write PATH TEXT)"),
        ParseError::TooManyArguments => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: too many arguments"),
        ParseError::UnterminatedQuote => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: unterminated text quote"),
    }
}

fn report_fs_error(error: FsError) {
    let message = match error {
        FsError::InvalidPath => "invalid path",
        FsError::InvalidName => "invalid file name",
        FsError::NameTooLong => "file name is too long (maximum 31 UTF-8 bytes)",
        FsError::AlreadyExists => "an entry with that name already exists",
        FsError::NotFound => "path not found",
        FsError::NotDirectory => "a path component is not a directory",
        FsError::IsDirectory => "operation requires a file, not a directory",
        FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty => "directory is not empty",
        FsError::NoSpace => "RAM filesystem is full",
        FsError::FileTooLarge => "file exceeds the 1024-byte limit",
        FsError::RootOperation => "operation is not permitted on the root directory",
        FsError::BufferTooSmall => "path exceeds the display buffer",
    };
    crate::kprintln!("crabshell: {}", message);
}

#![no_std]
#![no_main]

mod arch;
mod boot;
mod shell;

use core::panic::PanicInfo;
use rustix_kernel::vfs::RamFs;

static mut RAM_FILESYSTEM: RamFs = RamFs::new();

macro_rules! kprintln {
    () => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
    ($($argument:tt)*) => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!($($argument)*));
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
}

pub(crate) use kprintln;

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn _start() -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    let boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information() {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    // SAFETY: Crabshell is the only owner of this filesystem. The bootstrap is
    // single-core and has no scheduler or filesystem-touching interrupt handlers.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
        Ok(home) => shell::run(filesystem, home, &boot_info),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever()
        }
    }
}

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

# Crabshell and the early RAM filesystem

Crabshell is Rustix's first command-line interface. The current implementation is a **kernel-mode bootstrap shell** attached to COM1, not a separate user process. Its command parser is isolated in a separate crate so the same grammar can later be reused by a graphical terminal frontend or by a userspace terminal application.

## Crate boundary

- `crates/crabshell` is an allocation-free `no_std` Rust library. It parses a borrowed command line into a `Command` value and performs no I/O, filesystem access, scheduling, or privilege changes.
- `src/shell.rs` adapts the parser to the kernel serial driver, provides a small line editor, implements commands, and owns the current working-directory node.
- `src/vfs.rs` is a fixed-capacity in-memory filesystem used by the early shell. It is not a disk filesystem and is not persistent.

This is a useful separation now: future terminal frontends can reuse parsing without importing kernel hardware or filesystem code. A future user-mode Crabshell should keep its frontend/parser layer but execute operations through a documented syscall/VFS interface; it must not link the kernel's internal filesystem as a privilege shortcut.

## Build and run

```sh
just test
just image
just smoke
just run
```

`just run` starts a headless QEMU machine and connects the guest serial port to the current terminal. Use `Ctrl+C` in the host terminal to stop QEMU. The BIOS/UEFI boot image is `target/rustix.iso`.

The kernel welcomes the user in `/home/rustix`. The initial namespace contains `/bin`, `/dev`, `/etc`, `/home/rustix`, `/tmp`, and `/var`; `/etc/motd` explains that storage is volatile.

## Commands

| Command | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `help` | List available commands and limits. |
| `clear` | Send the ANSI clear-screen/home sequence. |
| `pwd` | Print the absolute working directory. |
| `meminfo` | Show validated usable RAM and frame allocator counts. |
| `ls [PATH]` | List a directory; a file path prints that file's name and size. Defaults to the current directory. |
| `cd PATH` | Change to an existing directory. Supports absolute and relative paths, `.`, and `..`. |
| `mkdir PATH` | Create one directory; its parent must already exist. |
| `touch PATH` | Create an empty file, or leave an existing file unchanged. |
| `write PATH TEXT` | Create a file if needed and replace its contents with the remaining line. Matching outer single or double quotes around the text are removed. |
| `append PATH TEXT` | Create a file if needed and append the remaining line. |
| `cp SOURCE DEST` | Copy a file; an existing destination file is replaced. |
| `mv SOURCE DEST` | Move/rename a file; directories and existing destinations are rejected. |
| `cat PATH` | Print a UTF-8 text file. Binary data is not displayed. |
| `rm PATH` | Remove a file. Directories are rejected. |
| `rmdir PATH` | Remove an empty directory other than the current directory. |

Example:

```text
root@rustix:/home/rustix# mkdir notes
root@rustix:/home/rustix# write notes/hello.txt "hello from Rustix"
root@rustix:/home/rustix# cat notes/hello.txt
hello from Rustix
root@rustix:/home/rustix# cd ..
root@rustix:/home# pwd
/home
```

The grammar intentionally does not yet support quoted paths, escaped quotes, variables, pipes, redirection, globbing, command substitution, history, or a process launcher. Input is a single ASCII line (up to 256 bytes) from the serial port.

## RAM filesystem contract

- The root plus at most 31 live entries fit in the fixed 32-node table.
- Path components are limited to 31 UTF-8 bytes; file contents are limited to 1024 bytes each.
- Paths may be absolute or relative and support repeated `/`, `.`, and `..`.
- `write` replaces a file; `append` adds bytes; `touch` never truncates.
- `cp` copies files; `mv` moves files only and never overwrites an existing destination. `rm` handles files only. `rmdir` refuses non-empty directories and the current directory.
- Filesystem allocation is fixed-capacity; errors are reported rather than allocating a heap.
- Every file and directory disappears when the machine resets. There is no block device, journaling, metadata persistence, permission model, links, or concurrent access yet.

## Tests and limitations

Host-side tests cover path traversal, file create/write/append/copy/move/remove, entry kinds, path rendering, directory emptiness, and the parser's syntax/arity. The QEMU smoke test checks that the serial shell reaches its prompt; it does not emulate reboot persistence or prove isolation. Since the shell runs in ring 0, a parser or filesystem bug can panic the entire kernel. This implementation must not be presented as a secure or POSIX-compliant shell.

# Memory-management direction

## What exists now

`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation and classification. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.

`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and rejects invalid/double frees while merging adjacent ranges. Its bounded range metadata can report fragmentation exhaustion. The kernel initializes it from the validated map, retains it in `BootInfo`, and exposes counts through Crabshell's `meminfo` command. It does not yet allocate frames for kernel services or map/dereference any allocated frame. Rustix does not reclaim bootloader memory, manage page tables, or provide a heap. The HHDM offset is checked and logged, not used for memory access.

## Planned memory layers

1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
2. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; add real allocation callers only after the page-mapping policy and ownership rules are implemented.
3. **Kernel virtual memory:** establish explicit mapping permissions and cache attributes; prevent writable-executable mappings by default; reserve kernel, direct-map, MMIO, and guard regions.
4. **Heap:** add a global allocator only after frame allocation and page mapping are initialized. Define allocation failure behavior for kernel and interrupt contexts.
5. **Process address spaces:** isolate userspace; define copy-in/copy-out helpers and never treat user pointers as kernel references.

## Invariants to preserve

- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
- Reserved regions are never returned as free frames.
- A failed allocation leaves allocator state unchanged.
- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables.
- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, and exhaustion.

These are design requirements for future milestones, not functionality delivered by the current boot summary.

# Rustix roadmap

This roadmap is staged to keep each milestone reviewable and bootable. **Milestone 0's end-to-end image and boot validation remains pending. Milestone 1's snapshot and CPU-reporting source, plus Milestone 2's frame-allocator core, have not yet been compiled or boot-tested in the current environment.** Items below are planned unless checked off; checked implementation work is not the same as a passing end-to-end validation.

## Milestone 0 — Rust kernel bootstrap (current)

- [x] `no_std` Rust kernel binary for `x86_64-unknown-none`.
- [x] Own ELF linker layout and Limine boot-protocol requests.
- [x] COM1 serial diagnostics, memory-map/HHDM summary, and panic halt path.
- [x] Narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers and a non-blocking PS/2 raw-scancode polling driver.
- [x] `just` commands and architecture/development/security/driver documentation.
- [x] Hash-pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary distribution and checked extraction.
- [x] Reproducible BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO recipe and documented boot configuration.
- [x] Bounded QEMU serial smoke-test runner and CI workflow.
- [x] Separate no-std Crabshell command-parser crate and kernel serial shell frontend.
- [x] Fixed-capacity RAM filesystem with basic directory and text-file operations.
- [ ] Execute the end-to-end image build and QEMU Crabshell prompt smoke test successfully in CI or a local environment.

**Exit criteria:** a clean checkout builds the pinned image, boots it in the documented emulator, and captures the expected serial banner in automated validation. The workflow is implemented; the criterion remains pending until an end-to-end run passes.

## Milestone 1 — validated boot state and machine diagnostics (implementation underway)

- [x] Copy HHDM and memory-map responses into an owned `BootInfo` snapshot before shell startup.
- [x] Validate response presence/alignment, bounded entry count, nonzero ranges, checked range ends, and non-overlap; reject a malformed snapshot before entering Crabshell.
- [x] Preserve reserved, ACPI, bad-memory, loader-reclaimable, executable/module, framebuffer, and unknown region classifications without reclaiming any memory.
- [x] Report baseline CPUID vendor and kernel-relevant feature bits; document the current serial-only console.
- [x] Document that loader- and ACPI-reclaimable ranges remain reserved until their respective data is no longer needed.
- [ ] Add serial-formatting tests and validate the snapshot and diagnostics in a successful target build and emulator boot.

**Exit criteria:** malformed maps fail closed; an emulator test validates reported regions and boot metadata. The source implementation is not yet build- or boot-verified.

## Milestone 2 — memory ownership and CPU exceptions (in progress)

- [x] Fixed-capacity frame allocator over validated usable ranges, with alignment, low-memory reservation, deallocation/coalescing, fragmentation limits, and host-side tests (`src/frame.rs`); initialized in `BootInfo` and reported by Crabshell `meminfo`. It does not yet allocate frames for kernel services.
- [ ] Kernel-owned page-table management and a direct-map policy; allocated frames must not be dereferenced until mappings are explicitly established.
- [ ] Global heap with deterministic out-of-memory behavior, built only after frame allocation and page mapping work.
- [ ] GDT/TSS and IDT setup; exception handlers with register/error-code diagnostics and fault-injection tests.
- [ ] Target build, host tests, and emulator validation for the milestone.

**Exit criteria:** allocator and mapping invariants are tested, page faults are diagnosable, and the kernel remains bootable under emulator tests.

## Milestone 3 — interrupts, time, and scheduling

- Timer and interrupt-controller setup with explicit interrupt-safe locking rules.
- Kernel threads and context switching; per-CPU data before SMP work.
- Preemptive scheduling only after interrupt, stack, and lock invariants are validated.
- Application processor startup as a separate milestone, not an implicit extension of single-core code.

**Exit criteria:** deterministic thread lifecycle tests and bounded timer/preemption integration tests.

## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI

- User-mode entry/exit and isolated address spaces.
- Versioned syscall ABI, validated copy-in/copy-out, and documented error semantics.
- Initial process lifecycle, descriptor table, and executable-loading path.
- Adversarial tests for invalid pointers, bad lengths, overflow, and process teardown.

**Exit criteria:** a controlled userspace init process can execute and use a small documented syscall subset without corrupting the kernel on invalid input.

## Milestone 5 — Unix-like services and storage

- VFS and mount model, file descriptors, and a first on-disk filesystem.
- Process creation/exec/wait semantics, pipes or IPC, and signal-like delivery as designed.
- Device discovery/driver model and networking only after ownership and isolation policies exist.
- Compatibility tests for any claimed Unix/POSIX behavior; keep unsupported operations explicit.

**Exit criteria:** documented userland tools can run from a reproducible image and integration tests cover process and file semantics.

## Working rule

Each milestone should add code, tests, and updated documentation together. Do not advance the stated project status merely because an interface or design note exists. Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable subsystem stubs.

# Rustix documentation

Rustix is a 64-bit, Rust-first, Unix-like operating-system project. This index separates current implementation facts from planned interfaces: roadmap items are proposals until the corresponding code and tests exist.

## Start here

- [Project and implementation overview](architecture/overview.md)
- [Boot protocol and current entry path](architecture/boot.md)
- [Memory-management direction](architecture/memory.md)
- [x86_64 drivers and hardware boundary](architecture/drivers.md)
- [Crabshell and the volatile RAM filesystem](architecture/crabshell.md)
- [Unix-like process and syscall direction](architecture/syscall-abi.md)
- [Build and toolchain guide](development/building.md)
- [Testing and verification](development/testing.md)
- [Security and unsafe-code policy](security.md)
- [Milestones and acceptance criteria](roadmap/README.md)

## Current status

The repository contains a bare-metal `no_std` Rust kernel for `x86_64-unknown-none`. After Limine handoff it validates and copies memory-map metadata into an owned snapshot, reports baseline CPUID features, seeds a volatile RAM filesystem, and runs Crabshell over the COM1 serial console. Crabshell's allocation-free parser is a separate crate; the kernel handles command execution. The image builder and bounded QEMU prompt smoke test are wired into CI, but the latest source changes have not yet been built or boot-tested and Milestone 0's end-to-end run remains pending. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process. A bounded physical-frame allocator core is initialized from the validated map and reported by `meminfo`, but no kernel service allocates or maps frames yet; there is not yet page-table management, a heap, an interrupt subsystem, a scheduler, process isolation, a persistent filesystem, or a Unix compatibility layer.

## Documentation conventions

- **Implemented** means present in the repository and checked by current code or tests.
- **Planned** means an architectural direction, not a stable ABI or delivered capability.
- Any future ABI proposal must state versioning, error behavior, memory ownership, and compatibility expectations before it is treated as stable.

# Rustix

Rustix (Rust-unix) is an experimental, 64-bit, Unix-like operating system whose kernel is written in Rust. This repository builds the kernel itself; Limine is used only as the external boot protocol/loader, not as a substitute for a Rustix kernel.

Rustix now boots into **Crabshell**, a small kernel-mode shell on the COM1 serial terminal. It includes basic navigation and file commands backed by a fixed-capacity RAM filesystem. The filesystem is volatile and reset at every boot; this is an early kernel shell, not a userspace process or POSIX shell. The command parser lives in a separate, allocation-free `crabshell` crate so a future GUI terminal can reuse it. Scheduling, process isolation, persistent storage, a syscall ABI, networking, and userspace are still future work. See [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) for the staged plan.

## Quick start

Prerequisites: a Rust stable toolchain, `just`, Python 3, `xorriso`, QEMU (`qemu-system-x86_64`), and the target installed by `rust-toolchain.toml` (or `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`). The first image build downloads a pinned Limine binary release and verifies its SHA-256.

```sh
just help
just fmt
just test
just check
just build
just image
just smoke
just run       # interactive serial shell in QEMU; exit with Ctrl+C
just verify
```

`just build` produces `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `just image` creates `target/rustix.iso`, a hybrid BIOS/UEFI image; `just smoke` checks that Crabshell reaches its prompt; and `just run` starts an interactive QEMU session attached to the current terminal.

Try `pwd`, `ls /`, `mkdir notes`, `write notes/hello.txt "hello from Rustix"`, `cat notes/hello.txt`, and `cd ..` in Crabshell. Commands include `help`, `clear`, `pwd`, `meminfo`, `ls`, `cd`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `write`, `append`, `cp`, `mv`, `cat`, `rm`, and `rmdir`. The RAM filesystem holds at most 31 entries plus its root, with files capped at 1024 bytes. See [`docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](docs/architecture/crabshell.md) for the shell and filesystem contract, [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) for build/emulator details, and [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) for the documentation map.

## Project principles

- The kernel and operating-system implementation are Rust-first and `no_std`; architecture-specific privileged operations are isolated under `src/arch/`.
- The kernel is the product. A bootloader may initialize the machine and transfer control, but policy, memory management, scheduling, and Unix-like services belong to Rustix.
- Keep unsafe code small, documented, and adjacent to its hardware/protocol boundary.
- Build incrementally: every roadmap milestone should have build checks, tests where practical, and updated design documentation.
- Unix-like behavior is an explicit compatibility goal, not a claim of POSIX compliance today.

## Repository map

- `src/main.rs` — freestanding kernel entry point and Crabshell handoff.
- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel command executor.
- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem, with host-side tests.
- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` command parser crate; no I/O or filesystem coupling.
- `src/boot.rs` — mutable Limine response requests, validated owned boot snapshot, and diagnostics.
- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — COM1 polling driver used for shell output and input.
- `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` — baseline CPUID vendor and feature reporting.
- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling.
- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers.
- `src/memory.rs` — fixed-capacity validated physical-memory-map snapshot and host tests.
- `src/frame.rs` — bounded physical frame allocator core and host tests; not yet wired into the live kernel.
- `.cargo/config.toml`, `linker.ld` — x86_64-none code generation and ELF layout.
- `justfile` — formatting, tests, target checks, image creation, emulator smoke test, and aggregate verification.
- `limine.conf` — pinned boot configuration for the Rustix kernel.
- `scripts/boot.py` — checksum-verified Limine download, hybrid ISO assembly, and bounded QEMU validation.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — runs `just verify` on pushes and pull requests.
- `docs/` — architecture, drivers, development, security, and roadmap documentation.

//! Bootstrap GDT, TSS, and fatal exception diagnostics for x86_64.
//!
//! Hardware interrupts remain disabled. This installs exception gates only; it
//! does not initialize a PIC/APIC, enable IRQs, or provide recoverable faults.

use core::arch::{asm, global_asm};
use core::mem::{size_of, MaybeUninit};

const EXCEPTION_COUNT: usize = 32;
const KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x08;
const KERNEL_DATA_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x10;
const TSS_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x18;
const STACK_SIZE: usize = 16 * 1024;
const TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE: u64 = 0x89;

#[repr(C, packed)]
struct DescriptorTablePointer {
    limit: u16,
    base: u64,
}

#[repr(C, align(16))]
struct IdtTable([IdtEntry; 256]);

#[repr(C, packed)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct IdtEntry {
    offset_low: u16,
    selector: u16,
    ist: u8,
    attributes: u8,
    offset_middle: u16,
    offset_high: u32,
    reserved: u32,
}

impl IdtEntry {
    const MISSING: Self = Self {
        offset_low: 0,
        selector: 0,
        ist: 0,
        attributes: 0,
        offset_middle: 0,
        offset_high: 0,
        reserved: 0,
    };

    fn interrupt_gate(handler: u64, ist: u8) -> Self {
        Self {
            offset_low: handler as u16,
            selector: KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR,
            ist: ist & 0x07,
            attributes: 0x8e,
            offset_middle: (handler >> 16) as u16,
            offset_high: (handler >> 32) as u32,
            reserved: 0,
        }
    }
}

#[repr(C, packed)]
struct TaskStateSegment {
    reserved0: u32,
    rsp0: u64,
    rsp1: u64,
    rsp2: u64,
    reserved1: u64,
    ist1: u64,
    ist2: u64,
    ist3: u64,
    ist4: u64,
    ist5: u64,
    ist6: u64,
    ist7: u64,
    reserved2: u64,
    reserved3: u16,
    iomap_base: u16,
}

impl TaskStateSegment {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        reserved0: 0,
        rsp0: 0,
        rsp1: 0,
        rsp2: 0,
        reserved1: 0,
        ist1: 0,
        ist2: 0,
        ist3: 0,
        ist4: 0,
        ist5: 0,
        ist6: 0,
        ist7: 0,
        reserved2: 0,
        reserved3: 0,
        iomap_base: size_of::<Self>() as u16,
    };
}

#[repr(C, align(16))]
struct Stack([u8; STACK_SIZE]);

static mut GDT: [u64; 5] = [0; 5];
static mut IDT: IdtTable = IdtTable([IdtEntry::MISSING; 256]);
static mut TSS: TaskStateSegment = TaskStateSegment::EMPTY;
static mut RING0_STACK: Stack = Stack([0; STACK_SIZE]);
static mut DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK: Stack = Stack([0; STACK_SIZE]);

#[repr(C)]
struct ExceptionContext {
    r15: u64,
    r14: u64,
    r13: u64,
    r12: u64,
    r11: u64,
    r10: u64,
    r9: u64,
    r8: u64,
    rbp: u64,
    rdi: u64,
    rsi: u64,
    rdx: u64,
    rcx: u64,
    rbx: u64,
    rax: u64,
    vector: u64,
    error_code: u64,
    rip: u64,
    cs: u64,
    rflags: u64,
}

extern "C" {
    static exception_stub_table: [usize; EXCEPTION_COUNT];
    fn rustix_load_gdt(descriptor_table_pointer: *const DescriptorTablePointer);
}

/// Install a private kernel GDT/TSS and exception gates for vectors 0–31.
///
/// The bootstrap runs with maskable interrupts disabled. This routine leaves
/// them disabled and does not modify CR3 or the inherited page-table hierarchy.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: Single-core bootstrap ownership; the descriptor tables are private
    // static storage and are initialized before any gate is loaded.
    unsafe {
        initialize_tss();
        initialize_gdt();
        initialize_idt();
        asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags));
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_tss() {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    let double_fault_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);

    // The architectural TSS fields are packed; use unaligned raw writes rather
    // than creating references to their potentially unaligned storage.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(ring0_top);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).ist1).write_unaligned(double_fault_top);
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_gdt() {
    let tss_base = core::ptr::addr_of!(TSS) as u64;
    let tss_limit = (size_of::<TaskStateSegment>() - 1) as u64;
    let low = (tss_limit & 0xffff)
        | ((tss_base & 0x00ff_ffff) << 16)
        | (TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE << 40)
        | ((tss_limit & 0x000f_0000) << 32)
        | ((tss_base & 0xff00_0000) << 32);
    let high = tss_base >> 32;

    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[0]).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[1]).write(0x00af_9a00_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[2]).write(0x00cf_9200_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[3]).write(low);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[4]).write(high);
    }

    let gdtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<[u64; 5]>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(GDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: `GDT` and its TSS descriptor are initialized and remain live.
    unsafe { rustix_load_gdt(&gdtr) };
}

unsafe fn initialize_idt() {
    let idt_entries = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IDT.0).cast::<IdtEntry>();
    let stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(exception_stub_table).cast::<usize>();

    for vector in 0..EXCEPTION_COUNT {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains exactly 32 stub addresses.
        let handler = unsafe { stubs.add(vector).read() } as u64;
        let ist = if vector == 8 { 1 } else { 0 };
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, ist));
        }
    }

    let idtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<IdtTable>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(IDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: Every architectural exception gate is initialized in static storage.
    unsafe { asm!("lidt [{}]", in(reg) &idtr, options(readonly, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
}

/// Fatal exception target called by the assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_exception_dispatch(context: *const ExceptionContext) -> ! {
    // SAFETY: The common assembly stub passes a pointer to its normalized stack
    // frame, which remains live for the duration of this non-returning handler.
    let context = unsafe { &*context };
    crate::kprintln!(
        "KERNEL EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x} RIP={:#018x}",
        context.vector,
        exception_name(context.vector),
        context.error_code,
        context.rip
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CS={:#06x} RFLAGS={:#018x} RAX={:#018x} RBX={:#018x} RCX={:#018x}",
        context.cs,
        context.rflags,
        context.rax,
        context.rbx,
        context.rcx
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RDX={:#018x} RSI={:#018x} RDI={:#018x} RBP={:#018x}",
        context.rdx,
        context.rsi,
        context.rdi,
        context.rbp
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R8={:#018x} R9={:#018x} R10={:#018x} R11={:#018x}",
        context.r8,
        context.r9,
        context.r10,
        context.r11
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R12={:#018x} R13={:#018x} R14={:#018x} R15={:#018x}",
        context.r12,
        context.r13,
        context.r14,
        context.r15
    );

    if context.vector == 14 {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "page fault: present={} write={} user={} reserved={} instruction-fetch={}",
            context.error_code & 1 != 0,
            context.error_code & 2 != 0,
            context.error_code & 4 != 0,
            context.error_code & 8 != 0,
            context.error_code & 16 != 0
        );
        let fault_address: u64;
        // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is a privileged x86_64 operation in this handler.
        unsafe { asm!("mov {}, cr2", out(reg) fault_address, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
        crate::kprintln!("page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
    }

    loop {
        // SAFETY: Fatal exceptions are not recoverable in the current kernel.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

fn exception_name(vector: u64) -> &'static str {
    match vector {
        0 => "divide error",
        1 => "debug",
        2 => "non-maskable interrupt",
        3 => "breakpoint",
        4 => "overflow",
        5 => "bound range",
        6 => "invalid opcode",
        7 => "device not available",
        8 => "double fault",
        9 => "coprocessor segment overrun",
        10 => "invalid TSS",
        11 => "segment not present",
        12 => "stack-segment fault",
        13 => "general protection fault",
        14 => "page fault",
        16 => "x87 floating-point",
        17 => "alignment check",
        18 => "machine check",
        19 => "SIMD floating-point",
        20 => "virtualization",
        21 => "control protection",
        28 => "hypervisor injection",
        29 => "VMM communication",
        30 => "security exception",
        _ => "reserved or architecture-specific exception",
    }
}

//! Bootstrap GDT, TSS, and fatal exception diagnostics for x86_64.
//!
//! Hardware interrupts remain disabled. This installs exception gates only; it
//! does not initialize a PIC/APIC, enable IRQs, or provide recoverable faults.

use core::arch::{asm, global_asm};
use core::mem::size_of;

const EXCEPTION_COUNT: usize = 32;
const KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x08;
const KERNEL_DATA_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x10;
const TSS_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x18;
const STACK_SIZE: usize = 16 * 1024;
const TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE: u64 = 0x89;

#[repr(C, packed)]
struct DescriptorTablePointer {
    limit: u16,
    base: u64,
}

#[repr(C, align(16))]
struct IdtTable([IdtEntry; 256]);

#[repr(C, packed)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct IdtEntry {
    offset_low: u16,
    selector: u16,
    ist: u8,
    attributes: u8,
    offset_middle: u16,
    offset_high: u32,
    reserved: u32,
}

impl IdtEntry {
    const MISSING: Self = Self {
        offset_low: 0,
        selector: 0,
        ist: 0,
        attributes: 0,
        offset_middle: 0,
        offset_high: 0,
        reserved: 0,
    };

    fn interrupt_gate(handler: u64, ist: u8) -> Self {
        Self {
            offset_low: handler as u16,
            selector: KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR,
            ist: ist & 0x07,
            attributes: 0x8e,
            offset_middle: (handler >> 16) as u16,
            offset_high: (handler >> 32) as u32,
            reserved: 0,
        }
    }
}

#[repr(C, packed)]
struct TaskStateSegment {
    reserved0: u32,
    rsp0: u64,
    rsp1: u64,
    rsp2: u64,
    reserved1: u64,
    ist1: u64,
    ist2: u64,
    ist3: u64,
    ist4: u64,
    ist5: u64,
    ist6: u64,
    ist7: u64,
    reserved2: u64,
    reserved3: u16,
    iomap_base: u16,
}

impl TaskStateSegment {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        reserved0: 0,
        rsp0: 0,
        rsp1: 0,
        rsp2: 0,
        reserved1: 0,
        ist1: 0,
        ist2: 0,
        ist3: 0,
        ist4: 0,
        ist5: 0,
        ist6: 0,
        ist7: 0,
        reserved2: 0,
        reserved3: 0,
        iomap_base: size_of::<Self>() as u16,
    };
}

#[repr(C, align(16))]
struct Stack([u8; STACK_SIZE]);

static mut GDT: [u64; 5] = [0; 5];
static mut IDT: IdtTable = IdtTable([IdtEntry::MISSING; 256]);
static mut TSS: TaskStateSegment = TaskStateSegment::EMPTY;
static mut RING0_STACK: Stack = Stack([0; STACK_SIZE]);
static mut DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK: Stack = Stack([0; STACK_SIZE]);

#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct ExceptionContext {
    r15: u64,
    r14: u64,
    r13: u64,
    r12: u64,
    r11: u64,
    r10: u64,
    r9: u64,
    r8: u64,
    rbp: u64,
    rdi: u64,
    rsi: u64,
    rdx: u64,
    rcx: u64,
    rbx: u64,
    rax: u64,
    vector: u64,
    error_code: u64,
    rip: u64,
    cs: u64,
    rflags: u64,
}

extern "C" {
    static exception_stub_table: [usize; EXCEPTION_COUNT];
    fn rustix_load_gdt(descriptor_table_pointer: *const DescriptorTablePointer);
}

/// Install a private kernel GDT/TSS and exception gates for vectors 0–31.
///
/// The bootstrap runs with maskable interrupts disabled. This routine leaves
/// them disabled and does not modify CR3 or the inherited page-table hierarchy.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: Single-core bootstrap ownership; the descriptor tables are private
    // static storage and are initialized before any gate is loaded.
    unsafe {
        initialize_tss();
        initialize_gdt();
        initialize_idt();
        asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack));
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_tss() {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    let double_fault_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);

    // The architectural TSS fields are packed; use unaligned raw writes rather
    // than creating references to their potentially unaligned storage.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(ring0_top);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).ist1).write_unaligned(double_fault_top);
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_gdt() {
    let tss_base = core::ptr::addr_of!(TSS) as u64;
    let tss_limit = (size_of::<TaskStateSegment>() - 1) as u64;
    let low = (tss_limit & 0xffff)
        | ((tss_base & 0x00ff_ffff) << 16)
        | (TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE << 40)
        | ((tss_limit & 0x000f_0000) << 32)
        | ((tss_base & 0xff00_0000) << 32);
    let high = tss_base >> 32;

    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[0]).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[1]).write(0x00af_9a00_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[2]).write(0x00cf_9200_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[3]).write(low);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[4]).write(high);
    }

    let gdtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<[u64; 5]>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(GDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: `GDT` and its TSS descriptor are initialized and remain live.
    unsafe { rustix_load_gdt(&gdtr) };
}

unsafe fn initialize_idt() {
    let idt_entries = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IDT.0).cast::<IdtEntry>();
    let stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(exception_stub_table).cast::<usize>();

    for vector in 0..EXCEPTION_COUNT {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains exactly 32 stub addresses.
        let handler = unsafe { stubs.add(vector).read() } as u64;
        let ist = if vector == 8 { 1 } else { 0 };
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, ist));
        }
    }

    let idtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<IdtTable>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(IDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: Every architectural exception gate is initialized in static storage.
    unsafe { asm!("lidt [{}]", in(reg) &idtr, options(readonly, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
}

/// Fatal exception target called by the assembly stubs.

//! Bootstrap GDT, TSS, and fatal exception diagnostics for x86_64.
//!
//! Hardware interrupts remain disabled. This installs exception gates only; it
//! does not initialize a PIC/APIC, enable IRQs, or provide recoverable faults.

use core::arch::{asm, global_asm};
use core::mem::size_of;

const EXCEPTION_COUNT: usize = 32;
const KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x08;
const KERNEL_DATA_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x10;
const TSS_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x18;
const STACK_SIZE: usize = 16 * 1024;
const TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE: u64 = 0x89;

#[repr(C, packed)]
struct DescriptorTablePointer {
    limit: u16,
    base: u64,
}

#[repr(C, align(16))]
struct IdtTable([IdtEntry; 256]);

#[repr(C, packed)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct IdtEntry {
    offset_low: u16,
    selector: u16,
    ist: u8,
    attributes: u8,
    offset_middle: u16,
    offset_high: u32,
    reserved: u32,
}

impl IdtEntry {
    const MISSING: Self = Self {
        offset_low: 0,
        selector: 0,
        ist: 0,
        attributes: 0,
        offset_middle: 0,
        offset_high: 0,
        reserved: 0,
    };

    fn interrupt_gate(handler: u64, ist: u8) -> Self {
        Self {
            offset_low: handler as u16,
            selector: KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR,
            ist: ist & 0x07,
            attributes: 0x8e,
            offset_middle: (handler >> 16) as u16,
            offset_high: (handler >> 32) as u32,
            reserved: 0,
        }
    }
}

#[repr(C, packed)]
struct TaskStateSegment {
    reserved0: u32,
    rsp0: u64,
    rsp1: u64,
    rsp2: u64,
    reserved1: u64,
    ist1: u64,
    ist2: u64,
    ist3: u64,
    ist4: u64,
    ist5: u64,
    ist6: u64,
    ist7: u64,
    reserved2: u64,
    reserved3: u16,
    iomap_base: u16,
}

impl TaskStateSegment {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        reserved0: 0,
        rsp0: 0,
        rsp1: 0,
        rsp2: 0,
        reserved1: 0,
        ist1: 0,
        ist2: 0,
        ist3: 0,
        ist4: 0,
        ist5: 0,
        ist6: 0,
        ist7: 0,
        reserved2: 0,
        reserved3: 0,
        iomap_base: size_of::<Self>() as u16,
    };
}

#[repr(C, align(16))]
struct Stack([u8; STACK_SIZE]);

static mut GDT: [u64; 5] = [0; 5];
static mut IDT: IdtTable = IdtTable([IdtEntry::MISSING; 256]);
static mut TSS: TaskStateSegment = TaskStateSegment::EMPTY;
static mut RING0_STACK: Stack = Stack([0; STACK_SIZE]);
static mut DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK: Stack = Stack([0; STACK_SIZE]);

#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct ExceptionContext {
    r15: u64,
    r14: u64,
    r13: u64,
    r12: u64,
    r11: u64,
    r10: u64,
    r9: u64,
    r8: u64,
    rbp: u64,
    rdi: u64,
    rsi: u64,
    rdx: u64,
    rcx: u64,
    rbx: u64,
    rax: u64,
    vector: u64,
    error_code: u64,
    rip: u64,
    cs: u64,
    rflags: u64,
}

extern "C" {
    static exception_stub_table: [usize; EXCEPTION_COUNT];
    fn rustix_load_gdt(descriptor_table_pointer: *const DescriptorTablePointer);
}

/// Install a private kernel GDT/TSS and exception gates for vectors 0–31.
///
/// The bootstrap runs with maskable interrupts disabled. This routine leaves
/// them disabled and does not modify CR3 or the inherited page-table hierarchy.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: Single-core bootstrap ownership; the descriptor tables are private
    // static storage and are initialized before any gate is loaded.
    unsafe {
        asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack));
        initialize_tss();
        initialize_gdt();
        initialize_idt();
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_tss() {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    let double_fault_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);

    // The architectural TSS fields are packed; use unaligned raw writes rather
    // than creating references to their potentially unaligned storage.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(ring0_top);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).ist1).write_unaligned(double_fault_top);
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_gdt() {
    let tss_base = core::ptr::addr_of!(TSS) as u64;
    let tss_limit = (size_of::<TaskStateSegment>() - 1) as u64;
    let low = (tss_limit & 0xffff)
        | ((tss_base & 0x00ff_ffff) << 16)
        | (TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE << 40)
        | ((tss_limit & 0x000f_0000) << 32)
        | ((tss_base & 0xff00_0000) << 32);
    let high = tss_base >> 32;

    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[0]).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[1]).write(0x00af_9a00_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[2]).write(0x00cf_9200_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[3]).write(low);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[4]).write(high);
    }

    let gdtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<[u64; 5]>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(GDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: `GDT` and its TSS descriptor are initialized and remain live.
    unsafe { rustix_load_gdt(&gdtr) };
}

unsafe fn initialize_idt() {
    let idt_entries = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IDT.0).cast::<IdtEntry>();
    let stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(exception_stub_table).cast::<usize>();

    for vector in 0..EXCEPTION_COUNT {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains exactly 32 stub addresses.
        let handler = unsafe { stubs.add(vector).read() } as u64;
        let ist = if vector == 8 { 1 } else { 0 };
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, ist));
        }
    }

    let idtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<IdtTable>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(IDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: Every architectural exception gate is initialized in static storage.
    unsafe { asm!("lidt [{}]", in(reg) &idtr, options(readonly, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
}

/// Fatal exception target called by the assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_exception_dispatch(context: *const ExceptionContext) -> ! {
    // SAFETY: The common assembly stub passes a pointer to its normalized stack
    // frame, which remains live for the duration of this non-returning handler.
    let context = unsafe { &*context };
    crate::kprintln!(
        "KERNEL EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x} RIP={:#018x}",
        context.vector,
        exception_name(context.vector),
        context.error_code,
        context.rip
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CS={:#06x} RFLAGS={:#018x} RAX={:#018x} RBX={:#018x} RCX={:#018x}",
        context.cs,
        context.rflags,
        context.rax,
        context.rbx,
        context.rcx
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RDX={:#018x} RSI={:#018x} RDI={:#018x} RBP={:#018x}",
        context.rdx,
        context.rsi,
        context.rdi,
        context.rbp
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R8={:#018x} R9={:#018x} R10={:#018x} R11={:#018x}",
        context.r8,
        context.r9,
        context.r10,
        context.r11
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R12={:#018x} R13={:#018x} R14={:#018x} R15={:#018x}",
        context.r12,
        context.r13,
        context.r14,
        context.r15
    );

    if context.vector == 14 {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "page fault: present={} write={} user={} reserved={} instruction-fetch={}",
            context.error_code & 1 != 0,
            context.error_code & 2 != 0,
            context.error_code & 4 != 0,
            context.error_code & 8 != 0,
            context.error_code & 16 != 0
        );
        let fault_address: u64;
        // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is a privileged x86_64 operation in this handler.
        unsafe { asm!("mov {}, cr2", out(reg) fault_address, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
        crate::kprintln!("page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
    }

    loop {
        // SAFETY: Fatal exceptions are not recoverable in the current kernel.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

fn exception_name(vector: u64) -> &'static str {
    match vector {
        0 => "divide error",
        1 => "debug",
        2 => "non-maskable interrupt",
        3 => "breakpoint",
        4 => "overflow",
        5 => "bound range",
        6 => "invalid opcode",
        7 => "device not available",
        8 => "double fault",
        9 => "coprocessor segment overrun",
        10 => "invalid TSS",
        11 => "segment not present",
        12 => "stack-segment fault",
        13 => "general protection fault",
        14 => "page fault",
        16 => "x87 floating-point",
        17 => "alignment check",
        18 => "machine check",
        19 => "SIMD floating-point",
        20 => "virtualization",
        21 => "control protection",
        28 => "hypervisor injection",
        29 => "VMM communication",
        30 => "security exception",
        _ => "reserved or architecture-specific exception",
    }
}

#![no_std]
#![no_main]

mod arch;
mod boot;
mod shell;

use core::panic::PanicInfo;
use rustix_kernel::vfs::RamFs;

static mut RAM_FILESYSTEM: RamFs = RamFs::new();

macro_rules! kprintln {
    () => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
    ($($argument:tt)*) => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!($($argument)*));
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
}

pub(crate) use kprintln;

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn _start() -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    let boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information() {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    // SAFETY: Crabshell is the only owner of this filesystem. The bootstrap is
    // single-core and has no scheduler or filesystem-touching interrupt handlers.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
        Ok(home) => shell::run(filesystem, home, &boot_info),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever()
        }
    }
}

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

# Rustix roadmap

This roadmap is staged to keep each milestone reviewable and bootable. **Milestone 0's end-to-end image and boot validation remains pending. Milestone 1's snapshot and CPU-reporting source, plus Milestone 2's frame-allocator core, have not yet been compiled or boot-tested in the current environment.** Items below are planned unless checked off; checked implementation work is not the same as a passing end-to-end validation.

## Milestone 0 — Rust kernel bootstrap (current)

- [x] `no_std` Rust kernel binary for `x86_64-unknown-none`.
- [x] Own ELF linker layout and Limine boot-protocol requests.
- [x] COM1 serial diagnostics, memory-map/HHDM summary, and panic halt path.
- [x] Narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers and a non-blocking PS/2 raw-scancode polling driver.
- [x] `just` commands and architecture/development/security/driver documentation.
- [x] Hash-pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary distribution and checked extraction.
- [x] Reproducible BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO recipe and documented boot configuration.
- [x] Bounded QEMU serial smoke-test runner and CI workflow.
- [x] Separate no-std Crabshell command-parser crate and kernel serial shell frontend.
- [x] Fixed-capacity RAM filesystem with basic directory and text-file operations.
- [ ] Execute the end-to-end image build and QEMU Crabshell prompt smoke test successfully in CI or a local environment.

**Exit criteria:** a clean checkout builds the pinned image, boots it in the documented emulator, and captures the expected serial banner in automated validation. The workflow is implemented; the criterion remains pending until an end-to-end run passes.

## Milestone 1 — validated boot state and machine diagnostics (implementation underway)

- [x] Copy HHDM and memory-map responses into an owned `BootInfo` snapshot before shell startup.
- [x] Validate response presence/alignment, bounded entry count, nonzero ranges, checked range ends, and non-overlap; reject a malformed snapshot before entering Crabshell.
- [x] Preserve reserved, ACPI, bad-memory, loader-reclaimable, executable/module, framebuffer, and unknown region classifications without reclaiming any memory.
- [x] Report baseline CPUID vendor and kernel-relevant feature bits; document the current serial-only console.
- [x] Document that loader- and ACPI-reclaimable ranges remain reserved until their respective data is no longer needed.
- [ ] Add serial-formatting tests and validate the snapshot and diagnostics in a successful target build and emulator boot.

**Exit criteria:** malformed maps fail closed; an emulator test validates reported regions and boot metadata. The source implementation is not yet build- or boot-verified.

## Milestone 2 — memory ownership and CPU exceptions (in progress)

- [x] Fixed-capacity frame allocator over validated usable ranges, with alignment, low-memory reservation, deallocation/coalescing, fragmentation limits, and host-side tests (`src/frame.rs`); initialized in `BootInfo` and reported by Crabshell `meminfo`. It does not yet allocate frames for kernel services.
- [ ] Kernel-owned page-table management and a direct-map policy; the current kernel still inherits Limine mappings, and allocated frames must not be dereferenced until mappings are explicitly established.
- [ ] Global heap with deterministic out-of-memory behavior, built only after frame allocation and page mapping work.
- [x] Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT and fatal handlers for vectors 0–31; double faults use an IST stack, and page faults report CR2 plus decoded error bits. Maskable IRQs remain disabled.
- [ ] Fault-injection tests and successful target/emulator validation for the exception entry path.
- [ ] Target build, host tests, and emulator validation for the milestone.

**Exit criteria:** allocator and mapping invariants are tested, page faults are diagnosable, and the kernel remains bootable under emulator tests.

## Milestone 3 — interrupts, time, and scheduling

- Timer and interrupt-controller setup with explicit interrupt-safe locking rules.
- Kernel threads and context switching; per-CPU data before SMP work.
- Preemptive scheduling only after interrupt, stack, and lock invariants are validated.
- Application processor startup as a separate milestone, not an implicit extension of single-core code.

**Exit criteria:** deterministic thread lifecycle tests and bounded timer/preemption integration tests.

## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI

- User-mode entry/exit and isolated address spaces.
- Versioned syscall ABI, validated copy-in/copy-out, and documented error semantics.
- Initial process lifecycle, descriptor table, and executable-loading path.
- Adversarial tests for invalid pointers, bad lengths, overflow, and process teardown.

**Exit criteria:** a controlled userspace init process can execute and use a small documented syscall subset without corrupting the kernel on invalid input.

## Milestone 5 — Unix-like services and storage

- VFS and mount model, file descriptors, and a first on-disk filesystem.
- Process creation/exec/wait semantics, pipes or IPC, and signal-like delivery as designed.
- Device discovery/driver model and networking only after ownership and isolation policies exist.
- Compatibility tests for any claimed Unix/POSIX behavior; keep unsupported operations explicit.

**Exit criteria:** documented userland tools can run from a reproducible image and integration tests cover process and file semantics.

## Working rule

Each milestone should add code, tests, and updated documentation together. Do not advance the stated project status merely because an interface or design note exists. Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable subsystem stubs.

# Memory-management direction

## What exists now

`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation and classification. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.

`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and rejects invalid/double frees while merging adjacent ranges. Its bounded range metadata can report fragmentation exhaustion. The kernel initializes it from the validated map, retains it in `BootInfo`, and exposes counts through Crabshell's `meminfo` command. It does not yet allocate frames for kernel services or map/dereference any allocated frame. Rustix does not reclaim bootloader memory, manage page tables, or provide a heap. The HHDM offset is checked and logged, not used for memory access.

## Planned memory layers

1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
2. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; add real allocation callers only after the page-mapping policy and ownership rules are implemented.
3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix still runs on inherited Limine page tables. Before replacing them, preserve the executing kernel, bootstrap/Ring-0 stacks, request/response data, and exception stacks; define the HHDM extent and explicit mapping permissions/cache attributes. Keep writable-executable mappings disallowed by default and reserve MMIO and guard regions.
4. **Heap:** add a global allocator only after frame allocation and page mapping are initialized. Define allocation failure behavior for kernel and interrupt contexts.
5. **Process address spaces:** isolate userspace; define copy-in/copy-out helpers and never treat user pointers as kernel references.

## Invariants to preserve

- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
- Reserved regions are never returned as free frames.
- A failed allocation leaves allocator state unchanged.
- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables.
- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, and exhaustion.

These are design requirements for future milestones, not functionality delivered by the current boot summary.

# Security and unsafe-code policy

Rustix is an early kernel prototype, not a security-reviewed operating system. It has no user/kernel separation implementation, process isolation, security boundary, or supported deployment profile today.

## Current unsafe boundaries

- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` issues privileged x86 port-I/O instructions behind narrow driver wrappers.
- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` configures and writes to the legacy COM1 UART. It is intended for early kernel context only.
- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` reads raw bytes from a legacy PS/2-compatible controller; callers must poll without blocking.
- `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` executes CPUID for boot-time feature reporting; x86_64 requires CPUID support.
- `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` loads the GDT/TSS/IDT and exception-entry assembly, reads CR2 on page faults, and halts after printing the saved context. The exception gates are kernel-only and maskable interrupts remain disabled.
- `src/boot.rs` reads Limine response pointers and entries, then validates and copies range metadata into an owned boot snapshot. Nullness, alignment, count bounds, arithmetic, and range overlap are checked; the kernel still trusts Limine to make non-null response objects readable for the handoff lifetime.
- `src/main.rs` uses `cli` and `hlt` to stop the bootstrap CPU after a fatal startup error.
- `src/vfs.rs` and `src/shell.rs` provide a kernel-mode RAM filesystem and shell. They have no user/kernel isolation, permissions, persistence, or protection from kernel bugs; shell commands are trusted kernel code, not sandboxed applications.

Unsafe blocks should remain as small as practical and state the assumptions that make each operation valid. Avoid widening `unsafe impl` or introducing raw-pointer-based public APIs without a documented safety argument. The PS/2 routine consumes bytes from the controller, including discarding auxiliary/error bytes, so it must only be used by a single owner of that controller until input serialization is designed. External boot inputs, user pointers, MMIO, and DMA must not be treated as trusted merely because current boot data is trusted.

## Security requirements for future subsystems

- Validate every physical range and checked address calculation before mapping or allocating it.
- Enforce least privilege in page mappings; avoid writable-executable pages by default.
- Keep user memory untrusted and use explicit copy-in/copy-out routines at syscall boundaries.
- Define ownership and lifetime rules for descriptors, processes, shared memory, and device buffers.
- Test malformed input and error paths as well as successful operation.
- Do not claim isolation or security guarantees until those properties have end-to-end tests and review.

# Rustix

Rustix (Rust-unix) is an experimental, 64-bit, Unix-like operating system whose kernel is written in Rust. This repository builds the kernel itself; Limine is used only as the external boot protocol/loader, not as a substitute for a Rustix kernel.

Rustix now boots into **Crabshell**, a small kernel-mode shell on the COM1 serial terminal. It includes basic navigation and file commands backed by a fixed-capacity RAM filesystem. The filesystem is volatile and reset at every boot; this is an early kernel shell, not a userspace process or POSIX shell. The command parser lives in a separate, allocation-free `crabshell` crate so a future GUI terminal can reuse it. Scheduling, process isolation, persistent storage, a syscall ABI, networking, and userspace are still future work. See [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) for the staged plan.

## Quick start

Prerequisites: a Rust stable toolchain, `just`, Python 3, `xorriso`, QEMU (`qemu-system-x86_64`), and the target installed by `rust-toolchain.toml` (or `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`). The first image build downloads a pinned Limine binary release and verifies its SHA-256.

```sh
just help
just fmt
just test
just check
just build
just image
just smoke
just run       # interactive serial shell in QEMU; exit with Ctrl+C
just verify
```

`just build` produces `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `just image` creates `target/rustix.iso`, a hybrid BIOS/UEFI image; `just smoke` checks that Crabshell reaches its prompt; and `just run` starts an interactive QEMU session attached to the current terminal.

Try `pwd`, `ls /`, `mkdir notes`, `write notes/hello.txt "hello from Rustix"`, `cat notes/hello.txt`, and `cd ..` in Crabshell. Commands include `help`, `clear`, `pwd`, `meminfo`, `ls`, `cd`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `write`, `append`, `cp`, `mv`, `cat`, `rm`, and `rmdir`. The RAM filesystem holds at most 31 entries plus its root, with files capped at 1024 bytes. See [`docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](docs/architecture/crabshell.md) for the shell and filesystem contract, [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) for build/emulator details, and [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) for the documentation map.

## Project principles

- The kernel and operating-system implementation are Rust-first and `no_std`; architecture-specific privileged operations are isolated under `src/arch/`.
- The kernel is the product. A bootloader may initialize the machine and transfer control, but policy, memory management, scheduling, and Unix-like services belong to Rustix.
- Keep unsafe code small, documented, and adjacent to its hardware/protocol boundary.
- Build incrementally: every roadmap milestone should have build checks, tests where practical, and updated design documentation.
- Unix-like behavior is an explicit compatibility goal, not a claim of POSIX compliance today.

## Repository map

- `src/main.rs` — freestanding kernel entry point and Crabshell handoff.
- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel command executor.
- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem, with host-side tests.
- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` command parser crate; no I/O or filesystem coupling.
- `src/boot.rs` — mutable Limine response requests, validated owned boot snapshot, and diagnostics.
- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — COM1 polling driver used for shell output and input.
- `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` — baseline CPUID vendor and feature reporting.
- `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` — bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT and fatal exception diagnostics.
- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling.
- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers.
- `src/memory.rs` — fixed-capacity validated physical-memory-map snapshot and host tests.
- `src/frame.rs` — bounded physical frame allocator core and host tests; not yet wired into the live kernel.
- `.cargo/config.toml`, `linker.ld` — x86_64-none code generation and ELF layout.
- `justfile` — formatting, tests, target checks, image creation, emulator smoke test, and aggregate verification.
- `limine.conf` — pinned boot configuration for the Rustix kernel.
- `scripts/boot.py` — checksum-verified Limine download, hybrid ISO assembly, and bounded QEMU validation.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — runs `just verify` on pushes and pull requests.
- `docs/` — architecture, drivers, development, security, and roadmap documentation.

# Memory-management direction

## What exists now

`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation and classification. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.

`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and rejects invalid/double frees while merging adjacent ranges. Its bounded range metadata can report fragmentation exhaustion. The kernel initializes it from the validated map, retains it in `BootInfo`, and exposes counts through Crabshell's `meminfo` command. It does not yet allocate frames for kernel services or map/dereference any allocated frame. Rustix does not reclaim bootloader memory, own or replace the inherited Limine page tables, or provide a heap. The HHDM offset is checked and logged, not used for memory access. Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception diagnostics live in `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs`; they do not enable maskable IRQs.

## Planned memory layers

1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
2. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; add real allocation callers only after the page-mapping policy and ownership rules are implemented.
3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix still runs on inherited Limine page tables. Before replacing them, preserve the executing kernel, bootstrap/Ring-0 stacks, request/response data, and exception stacks; define the HHDM extent and explicit mapping permissions/cache attributes. Keep writable-executable mappings disallowed by default and reserve MMIO and guard regions.
4. **Heap:** add a global allocator only after frame allocation and page mapping are initialized. Define allocation failure behavior for kernel and interrupt contexts.
5. **Process address spaces:** isolate userspace; define copy-in/copy-out helpers and never treat user pointers as kernel references.

## Invariants to preserve

- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
- Reserved regions are never returned as free frames.
- A failed allocation leaves allocator state unchanged.
- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables.
- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, and exhaustion.

These are design requirements for future milestones, not functionality delivered by the current boot summary.
