```
//! Kernel-side Crabshell frontend: serial input, prompts, and RAM-filesystem commands.

use crabshell::{parse, Command, ParseError, MAX_LINE_LENGTH};
use rustix_kernel::vfs::{EntryKind, FsError, RamFs, MAX_PATH_CAPACITY};

use crate::arch::x86_64::serial;
use crate::boot::BootInfo;

/// Run Crabshell forever on the bootstrap CPU.
pub fn run(filesystem: &mut RamFs, mut cwd: usize, boot_info: &BootInfo) -> ! {
    crate::kprintln!("crabshell: ready (volatile RAM filesystem)");
    print_motd(filesystem, cwd);

    let mut input = [0u8; MAX_LINE_LENGTH];
    loop {
        print_prompt(filesystem, cwd);
        let length = read_line(&mut input);
        if length == 0 {
            continue;
        }

        let line = match core::str::from_utf8(&input[..length]) {
            Ok(line) => line,
            Err(_) => {
                crate::kprintln!("crabshell: input must be valid UTF-8");
                continue;
            }
        };

        match parse(line) {
            Ok(Some(command)) => execute(command, filesystem, &mut cwd, boot_info),
            Ok(None) => {}
            Err(error) => print_parse_error(error),
        }
    }
}

fn print_prompt(filesystem: &RamFs, cwd: usize) {
    let mut path = [0u8; MAX_PATH_CAPACITY];
    match filesystem.write_path(cwd, &mut path) {
        Ok(length) => match core::str::from_utf8(&path[..length]) {
            Ok(path) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:{}# ", path)),
            Err(_) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:/?# ")),
        },
        Err(_) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:/?# ")),
    }
}

fn read_line(input: &mut [u8; MAX_LINE_LENGTH]) -> usize {
    let mut length = 0;
    loop {
        let Some(byte) = serial::try_read_byte() else {
            core::hint::spin_loop();
            continue;
        };

        match byte {
            b'\r' | b'\n' => {
                crate::kprintln!();
                return length;
            }
            0x03 => {
                crate::kprintln!("^C");
                return 0;
            }
            0x08 | 0x7f if length > 0 => {
                length -= 1;
                serial::print(format_args!("\x08 \x08"));
            }
            0x20..=0x7e if length < input.len() => {
                input[length] = byte;
                length += 1;
                serial::print(format_args!("{}", byte as char));
            }
            0x20..=0x7e => serial::print(format_args!("\x07")),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

fn execute(
    command: Command<'_>,
    filesystem: &mut RamFs,
    cwd: &mut usize,
    boot_info: &BootInfo,
) {
    match command {
        Command::Help => print_help(),
        Command::Clear => serial::print(format_args!("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")),
        Command::Pwd => {
            let mut path = [0u8; MAX_PATH_CAPACITY];
            match filesystem.write_path(*cwd, &mut path) {
                Ok(length) => match core::str::from_utf8(&path[..length]) {
                    Ok(path) => crate::kprintln!("{}", path),
                    Err(_) => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: could not display current path"),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            }
        }
        Command::Meminfo => {
            let managed = boot_info.frame_allocator.managed_frames();
            let free = boot_info.frame_allocator.free_frames();
            crate::kprintln!("usable RAM: {} bytes", boot_info.memory_map.usable_bytes());
            crate::kprintln!(
                "physical frames: {} managed, {} free, {} allocated",
                managed,
                free,
                managed - free
            );
        }
        Command::Ls(path) => {
            let directory = match path {
                Some(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
                    Ok(node) => node,
                    Err(error) => {
                        report_fs_error(error);
                        return;
                    }
                },
                None => *cwd,
            };
            list_directory(filesystem, directory);
        }
        Command::Cd(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.kind(node) {
                Ok(EntryKind::Directory) => *cwd = node,
                Ok(EntryKind::File) => report_fs_error(FsError::NotDirectory),
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Mkdir(path) => match filesystem.create_dir_path(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Touch(path) => match filesystem.open_or_create_file(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Write { path, contents } => {
            match filesystem.open_or_create_file(*cwd, path) {
                Ok(node) => match filesystem.write_file(node, contents.as_bytes()) {
                    Ok(()) => {}
                    Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            }
        }
        Command::Append { path, contents } => {
            match filesystem.open_or_create_file(*cwd, path) {
                Ok(node) => match filesystem.append_file(node, contents.as_bytes()) {
                    Ok(()) => {}
                    Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            }
        }
        Command::Cp {
            source,
            destination,
        } => match filesystem.copy_file_path(*cwd, source, destination) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Mv {
            source,
            destination,
        } => match filesystem.move_file_path(*cwd, source, destination) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Cat(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.read_file(node) {
                Ok(bytes) => match core::str::from_utf8(bytes) {
                    Ok(text) => print_file_contents(text),
                    Err(_) => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: binary file display is not supported"),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Rm(path) => match filesystem.remove_file_path(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Rmdir(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) if node == *cwd => {
                crate::kprintln!("crabshell: cannot remove the current directory");
            }
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.remove_dir(node) {
                Ok(()) => {}
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
    }
}

fn list_directory(filesystem: &RamFs, directory: usize) {
    match filesystem.kind(directory) {
        Ok(EntryKind::File) => match filesystem.entry(directory) {
            Ok(entry) => crate::kprintln!("{} ({} bytes)", entry.name, entry.size),
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        Ok(EntryKind::Directory) => match filesystem.child_count(directory) {
            Ok(0) => crate::kprintln!("(empty)"),
            Ok(count) => {
                for index in 0..count {
                    let Some(entry) = filesystem.child_at(directory, index) else {
                        crate::kprintln!("crabshell: directory changed while listing");
                        return;
                    };
                    match entry.kind {
                        EntryKind::Directory => crate::kprintln!("{}/", entry.name),
                        EntryKind::File => {
                            crate::kprintln!("{}  {} bytes", entry.name, entry.size)
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
    }
}

fn print_file_contents(text: &str) {
    for (index, line) in text.split('\n').enumerate() {
        if index != 0 {
            serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
        }
        serial::print(format_args!("{}", line.strip_suffix('\r').unwrap_or(line)));
    }
    if !text.ends_with('\n') {
        crate::kprintln!();
    }
}

fn print_motd(filesystem: &RamFs, cwd: usize) {
    if let Ok(node) = filesystem.resolve(cwd, "/etc/motd") {
        if let Ok(bytes) = filesystem.read_file(node) {
            if let Ok(text) = core::str::from_utf8(bytes) {
                print_file_contents(text);
            }
        }
    }
}

fn print_help() {
    crate::kprintln!("Crabshell commands:");
    crate::kprintln!("  help                 show this help");
    crate::kprintln!("  clear                clear an ANSI-compatible terminal");
    crate::kprintln!("  pwd                  print the current directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  meminfo              show validated memory and frame counts");
    crate::kprintln!("  ls [PATH]            list a directory or file");
    crate::kprintln!("  cd PATH              change the current directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  mkdir PATH            create a directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  touch PATH            create an empty file");
    crate::kprintln!("  write PATH TEXT       replace a file's contents");
    crate::kprintln!("  append PATH TEXT      append text to a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  cp SOURCE DEST        copy a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  mv SOURCE DEST        move/rename a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  cat PATH              print a text file");
    crate::kprintln!("  rm PATH               remove a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  rmdir PATH            remove an empty directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  write/append accept a quoted or unquoted text remainder.");
    crate::kprintln!("  RAM filesystem: 31 entries plus root; files up to 1024 bytes.");
}

fn print_parse_error(error: ParseError) {
    match error {
        ParseError::UnknownCommand => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: unknown command (try 'help')"),
        ParseError::MissingArgument => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: missing path argument"),
        ParseError::MissingText => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: missing text (usage: write PATH TEXT)"),
        ParseError::TooManyArguments => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: too many arguments"),
        ParseError::UnterminatedQuote => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: unterminated text quote"),
    }
}

fn report_fs_error(error: FsError) {
    let message = match error {
        FsError::InvalidPath => "invalid path",
        FsError::InvalidName => "invalid file name",
        FsError::NameTooLong => "file name is too long (maximum 31 UTF-8 bytes)",
        FsError::AlreadyExists => "an entry with that name already exists",
        FsError::NotFound => "path not found",
        FsError::NotDirectory => "a path component is not a directory",
        FsError::IsDirectory => "operation requires a file, not a directory",
        FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty => "directory is not empty",
        FsError::NoSpace => "RAM filesystem is full",
        FsError::FileTooLarge => "file exceeds the 1024-byte limit",
        FsError::RootOperation => "operation is not permitted on the root directory",
        FsError::BufferTooSmall => "path exceeds the display buffer",
    };
    crate::kprintln!("crabshell: {}", message);
}

/// Owned kernel snapshot of the handoff values Rustix currently consumes.
pub struct BootInfo {
    pub hhdm_revision: u64,
    pub hhdm_offset: u64,
    pub memory_map_revision: u64,
    pub memory_map: MemoryMap,
    pub frame_allocator: FrameAllocator,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BootInfoError {
    MissingHhdmResponse,
    InvalidHhdmResponsePointer,
    InvalidHhdmOffset,
    MissingMemoryMapResponse,
    InvalidMemoryMapResponsePointer,
    MemoryMapCountDoesNotFit,
    TooManyMemoryRegions,
    EmptyMemoryMap,
    InvalidEntriesPointer,
    EntriesAddressOverflow,
    InvalidEntryPointer { index: usize },
    InvalidMemoryMap(MemoryMapError),
    FrameAllocator(FrameError),
}

/// Copy and validate the boot data needed by the current kernel.
///
/// Structural checks can reject malformed pointers and ranges, but cannot prove
/// that a loader-provided pointer is mapped and readable. That remains part of
/// the documented Limine handoff trust boundary until the kernel owns its maps.
pub fn capture_boot_information() -> Result<BootInfo, BootInfoError> {
    let hhdm_request = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(HHDM_REQUEST) };
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let hhdm_pointer = unsafe {
        core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*hhdm_request).response))
    };
    if hhdm_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingHhdmResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(hhdm_pointer) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let hhdm = unsafe { hhdm_pointer.read_volatile() };
    if hhdm.offset & 0xfff != 0 || !is_canonical_virtual_address(hhdm.offset) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmOffset);
    }

    let memory_map_request = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(MEMORY_MAP_REQUEST) };
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let memory_map_pointer = unsafe {
        core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*memory_map_request).response))
    };
    if memory_map_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingMemoryMapResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(memory_map_pointer) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMapResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let response = unsafe { memory_map_pointer.read_volatile() };
    let entry_count = usize::try_from(response.entry_count)
        .map_err(|_| BootInfoError::MemoryMapCountDoesNotFit)?;
    if entry_count > MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
        return Err(BootInfoError::TooManyMemoryRegions);
    }
    if entry_count == 0 {
        return Err(BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap);
    }
    if response.entries.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(response.entries) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    let entry_bytes = entry_count
        .checked_mul(size_of::<*const MemoryMapEntry>())
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    let entries_start = response.entries as usize;
    let entries_end = entries_start
        .checked_add(entry_bytes)
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(entries_start as u64)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address((entries_end - 1) as u64)
    {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }

    let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
    for index in 0..entry_count {
        // SAFETY: Limine promises an array of `entry_count` pointers. The count
        // is capped and pointer alignment/address arithmetic are checked above.
        let entry_pointer = unsafe { response.entries.add(index).read_volatile() };
        if !is_valid_pointer(entry_pointer) {
            return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntryPointer { index });
        }
        // SAFETY: Limine promises each non-null entry pointer is readable.
        let entry = unsafe { entry_pointer.read_volatile() };
        builder
            .push(entry.base, entry.length, entry.kind)
            .map_err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap)?;
    }

    let memory_map = builder.finish().map_err(|error| match error {
        MemoryMapError::EmptyMap => BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap,
        other => BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap(other),
    })?;
    let frame_allocator =
        FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&memory_map).map_err(BootInfoError::FrameAllocator)?;

    Ok(BootInfo {
        hhdm_revision: hhdm.revision,
        hhdm_offset: hhdm.offset,
        memory_map_revision: response.revision,
        memory_map,
        frame_allocator,
    })
}

/// Print a report from the copied snapshot; no loader pointers are used here.
pub fn report_boot_information(boot_info: &BootInfo) {
    crate::kprintln!(
        "HHDM: offset {:#018x}, response revision {}",
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.hhdm_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "memory map: {} validated regions, {} MiB usable RAM, response revision {}",
        boot_info.memory_map.regions().len(),
        boot_info.memory_map.usable_bytes() / (1024 * 1024),
        boot_info.memory_map_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "physical frames: {} managed, {} free (4 KiB each)",
        boot_info.frame_allocator.managed_frames(),
        boot_info.frame_allocator.free_frames()
    );
    for region in boot_info.memory_map.regions() {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "  [{:#018x}, {:#018x}) {:?}",
            region.start(),
            region.end(),
            region.kind()
        );
    }
    crate::kprintln!("console: COM1 serial (polling)");

    let cpu = crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::identify();
    let vendor = core::str::from_utf8(&cpu.vendor).unwrap_or("unknown");
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU: {} (basic leaf {}, extended leaf {:#x})",
        vendor,
        cpu.max_basic_leaf,
        cpu.max_extended_leaf
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU feature support: SSE2={}, NX={}, 1GiB-pages={}, long-mode={}, LA57-supported={}",
        cpu.has_sse2,
        cpu.has_nx,
        cpu.has_1g_pages,
        cpu.has_long_mode,
        cpu.has_la57
    );
}

fn is_valid_pointer<T>(pointer: *const T) -> bool {
    let start = pointer as usize;
    let Some(end) = start.checked_add(size_of::<T>()) else {
        return false;
    };
    !pointer.is_null()
        && start & (align_of::<T>() - 1) == 0
        && is_canonical_virtual_address(start as u64)
        && is_canonical_virtual_address((end - 1) as u64)
}

fn is_canonical_virtual_address(address: u64) -> bool {
    let upper_48 = address >> 48;
    let upper_57 = address >> 57;
    upper_48 == 0 || upper_48 == 0xffff || upper_57 == 0 || upper_57 == 0x7f
}

//! Bootstrap GDT, TSS, and fatal exception diagnostics for x86_64.
//!
//! Hardware interrupts remain disabled. This installs exception gates only; it
//! does not initialize a PIC/APIC, enable IRQs, or provide recoverable faults.

use core::arch::{asm, global_asm};
use core::mem::size_of;

const EXCEPTION_COUNT: usize = 32;
const KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x08;
const STACK_SIZE: usize = 16 * 1024;
const TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE: u64 = 0x89;

    limit: u16,
    base: u64,
}

struct IdtTable([IdtEntry; 256]);

    offset_low: u16,
    selector: u16,
    ist: u8,
    attributes: u8,
    offset_middle: u16,
    offset_high: u32,
    reserved: u32,

    };

    fn interrupt_gate(handler: u64, ist: u8) -> Self {
        Self {
            offset_low: handler as u16,
            selector: KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR,
            ist: ist & 0x07,
            attributes: 0x8e,
            offset_middle: (handler >> 16) as u16,
            offset_high: (handler >> 32) as u32,
            reserved: 0,
        }
    }
}

#[repr(C, packed)]
struct TaskStateSegment {
    reserved0: u32,
    rsp0: u64,
    rsp1: u64,
    rsp2: u64,
    reserved1: u64,
    ist1: u64,
    ist2: u64,
    ist3: u64,
    ist4: u64,
    ist5: u64,
    ist6: u64,
    ist7: u64,
    reserved2: u64,
    reserved3: u16,
    iomap_base: u16,
}

impl TaskStateSegment {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        reserved0: 0,
        rsp0: 0,
        rsp1: 0,
        rsp2: 0,
        reserved1: 0,
        ist1: 0,
        ist2: 0,
        ist3: 0,
        ist4: 0,
        ist5: 0,
        ist6: 0,
        ist7: 0,
        reserved2: 0,
        reserved3: 0,
        iomap_base: size_of::<Self>() as u16,
    };
}

#[repr(C, align(16))]
struct Stack([u8; STACK_SIZE]);

static mut GDT: [u64; 5] = [0; 5];
static mut IDT: IdtTable = IdtTable([IdtEntry::MISSING; 256]);
static mut TSS: TaskStateSegment = TaskStateSegment::EMPTY;
static mut RING0_STACK: Stack = Stack([0; STACK_SIZE]);
static mut DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK: Stack = Stack([0; STACK_SIZE]);

#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct ExceptionContext {
    r15: u64,
    r14: u64,
    r13: u64,
    r12: u64,
    r11: u64,
    r10: u64,
    r9: u64,
    r8: u64,
    rbp: u64,
    rdi: u64,
    rsi: u64,
    rdx: u64,
    rcx: u64,
    rbx: u64,
    rax: u64,
    vector: u64,
    error_code: u64,
    rip: u64,
    cs: u64,
    rflags: u64,
}

extern "C" {
    static exception_stub_table: [usize; EXCEPTION_COUNT];
    fn rustix_load_gdt(descriptor_table_pointer: *const DescriptorTablePointer);
}

/// Install a private kernel GDT/TSS and exception gates for vectors 0–31.
///
/// The bootstrap runs with maskable interrupts disabled. This routine leaves
/// them disabled and does not modify CR3 or the inherited page-table hierarchy.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: Single-core bootstrap ownership; the descriptor tables are private
    // static storage and are initialized before any gate is loaded.
    unsafe {
        asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack));
        initialize_tss();
        initialize_gdt();
        initialize_idt();
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_tss() {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    let double_fault_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);

    // The architectural TSS fields are packed; use unaligned raw writes rather
    // than creating references to their potentially unaligned storage.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(ring0_top);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).ist1).write_unaligned(double_fault_top);
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_gdt() {
    let tss_base = core::ptr::addr_of!(TSS) as u64;
    let tss_limit = (size_of::<TaskStateSegment>() - 1) as u64;
    let low = (tss_limit & 0xffff)
        | ((tss_base & 0x00ff_ffff) << 16)
        | (TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE << 40)
        | ((tss_limit & 0x000f_0000) << 32)
        | ((tss_base & 0xff00_0000) << 32);
    let high = tss_base >> 32;

    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[0]).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[1]).write(0x00af_9a00_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[2]).write(0x00cf_9200_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[3]).write(low);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[4]).write(high);
    }

    let gdtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<[u64; 5]>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(GDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: `GDT` and its TSS descriptor are initialized and remain live.
    unsafe { rustix_load_gdt(&gdtr) };
}

unsafe fn initialize_idt() {
    let idt_entries = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IDT.0).cast::<IdtEntry>();
    let stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(exception_stub_table).cast::<usize>();

    for vector in 0..EXCEPTION_COUNT {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains exactly 32 stub addresses.
        let handler = unsafe { stubs.add(vector).read() } as u64;
        let ist = if vector == 8 { 1 } else { 0 };
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, ist));
        }
    }

    let idtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<IdtTable>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(IDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: Every architectural exception gate is initialized in static storage.
    unsafe { asm!("lidt [{}]", in(reg) &idtr, options(readonly, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
}

/// Fatal exception target called by the assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_exception_dispatch(context: *const ExceptionContext) -> ! {
    // SAFETY: The common assembly stub passes a pointer to its normalized stack
    // frame, which remains live for the duration of this non-returning handler.
    let context = unsafe { &*context };
    crate::kprintln!(
        "KERNEL EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x} RIP={:#018x}",
        context.vector,
        exception_name(context.vector),
        context.error_code,
        context.rip
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CS={:#06x} RFLAGS={:#018x} RAX={:#018x} RBX={:#018x} RCX={:#018x}",
        context.cs,
        context.rflags,
        context.rax,
        context.rbx,
        context.rcx
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RDX={:#018x} RSI={:#018x} RDI={:#018x} RBP={:#018x}",
        context.rdx,
        context.rsi,
        context.rdi,
        context.rbp
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R8={:#018x} R9={:#018x} R10={:#018x} R11={:#018x}",
        context.r8,
        context.r9,
        context.r10,
        context.r11
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R12={:#018x} R13={:#018x} R14={:#018x} R15={:#018x}",
        context.r12,
        context.r13,
        context.r14,
        context.r15
    );

    if context.vector == 14 {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "page fault: present={} write={} user={} reserved={} instruction-fetch={}",
            context.error_code & 1 != 0,
            context.error_code & 2 != 0,
            context.error_code & 4 != 0,
            context.error_code & 8 != 0,
            context.error_code & 16 != 0
        );
        let fault_address: u64;
        // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is a privileged x86_64 operation in this handler.
        unsafe { asm!("mov {}, cr2", out(reg) fault_address, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
        crate::kprintln!("page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
    }

    loop {
        // SAFETY: Fatal exceptions are not recoverable in the current kernel.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

fn exception_name(vector: u64) -> &'static str {
    match vector {
        0 => "divide error",
        1 => "debug",
        2 => "non-maskable interrupt",
        3 => "breakpoint",
        4 => "overflow",
        5 => "bound range",
        6 => "invalid opcode",
        7 => "device not available",
        8 => "double fault",
        9 => "coprocessor segment overrun",
        10 => "invalid TSS",
        11 => "segment not present",
        12 => "stack-segment fault",
        13 => "general protection fault",
        14 => "page fault",
        16 => "x87 floating-point",
        17 => "alignment check",
        18 => "machine check",
        19 => "SIMD floating-point",
        20 => "virtualization",
        21 => "control protection",
        28 => "hypervisor injection",
        29 => "VMM communication",
        30 => "security exception",
        _ => "reserved or architecture-specific exception",
    }
}

# Boot protocol and kernel entry

## Current boot contract

Rustix currently expects a Limine-compatible x86_64 handoff. Limine is an external loader; it does not implement Rustix's kernel services. The kernel requests protocol base revision 3, the higher-half direct-map (HHDM) offset, and the memory map.

Requests are kept in `.limine_requests_start`, `.limine_requests`, and `.limine_requests_end` by `linker.ld`. The response-bearing request records are mutable and the output `.limine_requests` section is placed in a writable load segment because Limine fills their response pointers before entering Rustix. The ELF entry symbol is `_start`.

### Entry sequence

1. Limine loads the ELF and transfers control to `_start` under the x86_64 Limine protocol.
2. `_start` configures the legacy COM1 UART for polling output and input.
3. The kernel disables maskable interrupts and installs its bootstrap GDT, TSS, and fatal-exception IDT. This does not initialize IRQ delivery.
4. The kernel copies the HHDM and memory-map responses into an owned `BootInfo` snapshot, including a frame allocator built only from validated usable ranges. It rejects malformed metadata before starting the shell.
5. The kernel reports validated ranges, frame counts, and baseline CPUID features, then seeds a volatile RAM filesystem and enters Crabshell on the serial console.
6. The shell busy-polls COM1 because no scheduler or UART interrupt handler exists yet. The kernel does not return to the loader.

The memory-map snapshot stores physical regions as checked half-open ranges `[start, end)` and retains Limine's known classifications plus unknown type values. It is diagnostic metadata only: it does not authorize Rustix to access every region, reclaim loader memory, or mutate the current page tables. The HHDM offset is validated and reported but is not yet used to translate or dereference physical addresses.

## Link and target configuration

- Rust target: `x86_64-unknown-none`
- Linker script: `linker.ld`
- Kernel virtual base: `0xffffffff80000000`
- Required code-generation constraints: kernel code model, static relocation, and disabled red zone
- Rust panic strategy: abort; the panic handler logs and halts

See [`../development/building.md`](../development/building.md) for commands and toolchain setup.

## Failure behavior and limitations

Missing responses, bad pointers/alignment, invalid HHDM values, excessive counts, null entries, address arithmetic overflow, and invalid or overlapping physical ranges reject the complete boot snapshot. `_start` halts before starting Crabshell rather than continuing with partial memory metadata. Structural checks cannot establish that a non-null loader pointer is mapped and readable; that remains an explicit trust assumption of the Limine handoff. The installed exception handlers print fatal context and halt; no fault recovery or maskable IRQ delivery is provided. COM1 writes use a bounded polling loop so a non-responsive UART does not block forever.

The repository now includes a Limine v12.9.3 binary archive pin with SHA-256 verification, a hybrid ISO recipe, and a bounded QEMU serial smoke test that checks Crabshell's prompt. These workflows are automated in CI, but the boot milestone is not considered complete until that end-to-end job passes. There is still no framebuffer console, reboot/shutdown interface, or broader boot-protocol compatibility test. The available serial and keyboard drivers do not imply a general device model.

## Future boot work

The kernel now snapshots and validates the Limine map and preserves firmware and loader-reclaimable classifications without reclaiming them. No region is considered Rustix-owned or free for allocation yet. Loader-reclaimable memory must remain unavailable until Rustix has copied any needed boot data and explicitly reaches a documented reclaim point; ACPI reclaimable memory needs the ACPI tables to be copied or parsed first. Frame allocation, page-table replacement, and ownership transfer remain future work.

# Architecture overview

## Goals

Rustix is a from-scratch operating system project with its own kernel, written in Rust. The intended initial platform is 64-bit x86 (`x86_64`), with a Unix-like process and file-descriptor model. The kernel should eventually own machine initialization, physical and virtual memory management, interrupt handling, scheduling, system calls, and device policy. A bootloader is a transport into the kernel, not a replacement for those facilities.

Unix-like is a compatibility direction. It does **not** mean the current kernel is POSIX-compliant, nor does it commit the project to a particular existing kernel's internals. Compatibility profiles and a userland should be defined only after the underlying process, descriptor, and syscall semantics are implemented and tested.

## Current implementation

1. Cargo builds a `no_std`, `no_main` ELF for `x86_64-unknown-none` and uses Limine for the boot handoff.
2. `_start` initializes COM1 and exception diagnostics, captures a validated boot snapshot and frame-allocator state, reports memory/CPU information, initializes a fixed-capacity RAM filesystem, and enters Crabshell.
3. Crabshell reads an ASCII command line from the serial UART and supports basic navigation, directory creation/listing, and text-file operations.
4. The separately packaged `crabshell` `no_std` crate parses commands without allocation or dependence on kernel I/O, making that layer reusable by a future graphical frontend.
5. The kernel library contains checked memory accounting and the bounded VFS implementation, both covered by host-side unit tests.

The current shell and filesystem run in kernel mode. Files exist only in RAM and disappear at reboot. There is no heap, Rustix-owned page-table manager, interrupt descriptor table, scheduler, user/kernel isolation, syscall ABI, on-disk filesystem, network stack, or userspace process.

## Intended layers (planned)

```text
User programs and system utilities
        | versioned syscall ABI
Kernel services: processes, descriptors, VFS, IPC, signals
        | explicit ownership and authorization checks
Core kernel: scheduler, virtual memory, physical frames, interrupts
        | narrow architecture abstractions
x86_64 platform: paging, exceptions, timers, AP startup, drivers
        | Limine boot handoff only
Firmware and hardware
```

The diagram is a target decomposition, not a claim that those layers are implemented. Architecture-independent policy should live in safe Rust where possible; privileged instructions and raw device access should stay in small, reviewed architecture modules.

## Design constraints

- **Freestanding:** kernel code does not link `std`; allocation must be introduced deliberately after a physical-frame and heap strategy exists.
- **Explicit unsafe boundaries:** raw pointers from boot protocol responses and x86 port I/O are unsafe. Each use must document its preconditions and remain short-lived.
- **Fail visibly:** early boot failures should produce serial diagnostics where possible and then halt, rather than continue with invalid machine state.
- **Checked arithmetic:** physical ranges, sizes, and address translations must reject overflow.
- **No premature ABI:** userspace interfaces stay unstable until process lifetime, error conventions, copy-in/copy-out, and versioning are designed together.
- **Hardware-independent tests:** parsing, range arithmetic, and policy should be testable as ordinary host-side Rust wherever possible.

## Boot and CPU assumptions

The current target is x86_64, with a 4 KiB page-oriented linker layout and no red zone. Limine performs the initial platform setup required by its protocol. Rustix must not assume that receiving a memory-map response means it owns the loader's page tables or can overwrite reserved regions. The current bootstrap does not enable interrupts or start application processors.

See [Boot protocol](boot.md), [Memory management](memory.md), [x86_64 drivers](drivers.md), [Crabshell](crabshell.md), and [the roadmap](../roadmap/README.md) for subsystem boundaries and planned acceptance criteria.

```

# Testing and verification

## Current checks

`just verify` runs the standard development verification sequence:

1. `just fmt` — fail on formatting differences across the workspace.
2. `just test` — run host-side memory-map, frame-allocator, RAM-filesystem, and Crabshell parser tests.
3. `just check` — check the `x86_64-unknown-none` kernel target.
4. `just smoke` — build the pinned hybrid ISO, boot it in QEMU, and check that Crabshell reaches its prompt within a deadline.

Keep the Crabshell parser, VFS, memory-map validator, and frame allocator independent of hardware so syntax, path handling, storage semantics, and frame ownership can be tested without booting. The GDT/TSS/IDT entry path is privileged kernel code and currently has no host fault-injection harness; it still requires target build and QEMU validation. Add tests for boundaries and failure behavior when introducing new pure kernel helpers. The kernel binary is not a host test target.

## What current checks do not prove

- `cargo check` does not perform a final target link.
- A successful ELF link does not prove the boot protocol is recognized or `_start` is reached.
- Host unit tests do not validate privileged instructions, UART behavior, memory-map pointer validity, page tables, interrupts, or actual hardware.
- The QEMU smoke test proves the kernel reaches the shell prompt; it does not yet send interactive file commands or prove persistence across reboot.
- There is no on-disk filesystem integration test, syscall/userspace test, fuzz target, or physical-hardware test.

## Validation policy

For changes to the kernel entry, linker script, boot requests, architecture code, shell, or VFS, run `just verify`. For memory-management and ABI code, add negative tests for overflow, malformed ranges, permission failures, and invalid user pointers before exposing those paths to userspace.

Record commands actually run and any environment limitation in change summaries; never call an unexecuted build “passing.”

# Rustix roadmap

This roadmap is staged to keep each milestone reviewable and bootable. **Milestone 0's end-to-end image and boot validation remains pending. Milestone 1's snapshot/CPU reporting and Milestone 2's frame allocator and GDT/TSS/IDT source have not yet been compiled or boot-tested in the current environment.** Items below are planned unless checked off; checked implementation work is not the same as a passing end-to-end validation.

## Milestone 0 — Rust kernel bootstrap (current)

- [x] `no_std` Rust kernel binary for `x86_64-unknown-none`.
- [x] Own ELF linker layout and Limine boot-protocol requests.
- [x] COM1 serial diagnostics, memory-map/HHDM summary, and panic halt path.
- [x] Narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers and a non-blocking PS/2 raw-scancode polling driver.
- [x] `just` commands and architecture/development/security/driver documentation.
- [x] Hash-pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary distribution and checked extraction.
- [x] Reproducible BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO recipe and documented boot configuration.
- [x] Bounded QEMU serial smoke-test runner and CI workflow.
- [x] Separate no-std Crabshell command-parser crate and kernel serial shell frontend.
- [x] Fixed-capacity RAM filesystem with basic directory and text-file operations.
- [ ] Execute the end-to-end image build and QEMU Crabshell prompt smoke test successfully in CI or a local environment.

**Exit criteria:** a clean checkout builds the pinned image, boots it in the documented emulator, and captures the expected serial banner in automated validation. The workflow is implemented; the criterion remains pending until an end-to-end run passes.

## Milestone 1 — validated boot state and machine diagnostics (implementation underway)

- [x] Copy HHDM and memory-map responses into an owned `BootInfo` snapshot before shell startup.
- [x] Validate response presence/alignment, bounded entry count, nonzero ranges, checked range ends, and non-overlap; reject a malformed snapshot before entering Crabshell.
- [x] Preserve reserved, ACPI, bad-memory, loader-reclaimable, executable/module, framebuffer, and unknown region classifications without reclaiming any memory.
- [x] Report baseline CPUID vendor and kernel-relevant feature bits; document the current serial-only console.
- [x] Document that loader- and ACPI-reclaimable ranges remain reserved until their respective data is no longer needed.
- [ ] Add serial-formatting tests and validate the snapshot and diagnostics in a successful target build and emulator boot.

**Exit criteria:** malformed maps fail closed; an emulator test validates reported regions and boot metadata. The source implementation is not yet build- or boot-verified.

## Milestone 2 — memory ownership and CPU exceptions (in progress)

- [x] Fixed-capacity frame allocator over validated usable ranges, with alignment, low-memory reservation, deallocation/coalescing, fragmentation limits, and host-side tests (`src/frame.rs`); initialized in `BootInfo` and reported by Crabshell `meminfo`. It does not yet allocate frames for kernel services.
- [ ] Kernel-owned page-table management and a direct-map policy; the current kernel still inherits Limine mappings, and allocated frames must not be dereferenced until mappings are explicitly established.
- [ ] Global heap with deterministic out-of-memory behavior, built only after frame allocation and page mapping work.
- [x] Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT and fatal handlers for vectors 0–31; double faults use an IST stack, and page faults report CR2 plus decoded error bits. Maskable IRQs remain disabled.
- [ ] Fault-injection tests and successful target/emulator validation for the exception entry path.
- [ ] Target build, host tests, and emulator validation for the milestone.

**Exit criteria:** allocator and mapping invariants are tested, page faults are diagnosable, and the kernel remains bootable under emulator tests.

## Milestone 3 — interrupts, time, and scheduling

- Timer and interrupt-controller setup with explicit interrupt-safe locking rules.
- Kernel threads and context switching; per-CPU data before SMP work.
- Preemptive scheduling only after interrupt, stack, and lock invariants are validated.
- Application processor startup as a separate milestone, not an implicit extension of single-core code.

**Exit criteria:** deterministic thread lifecycle tests and bounded timer/preemption integration tests.

## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI

- User-mode entry/exit and isolated address spaces.
- Versioned syscall ABI, validated copy-in/copy-out, and documented error semantics.
- Initial process lifecycle, descriptor table, and executable-loading path.
- Adversarial tests for invalid pointers, bad lengths, overflow, and process teardown.

**Exit criteria:** a controlled userspace init process can execute and use a small documented syscall subset without corrupting the kernel on invalid input.

## Milestone 5 — Unix-like services and storage

- VFS and mount model, file descriptors, and a first on-disk filesystem.
- Process creation/exec/wait semantics, pipes or IPC, and signal-like delivery as designed.
- Device discovery/driver model and networking only after ownership and isolation policies exist.
- Compatibility tests for any claimed Unix/POSIX behavior; keep unsupported operations explicit.

**Exit criteria:** documented userland tools can run from a reproducible image and integration tests cover process and file semantics.

## Working rule

Each milestone should add code, tests, and updated documentation together. Do not advance the stated project status merely because an interface or design note exists. Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable subsystem stubs.

# Rustix documentation

Rustix is a 64-bit, Rust-first, Unix-like operating-system project. This index separates current implementation facts from planned interfaces: roadmap items are proposals until the corresponding code and tests exist.

## Start here

- [Project and implementation overview](architecture/overview.md)
- [Boot protocol and current entry path](architecture/boot.md)
- [Memory-management direction](architecture/memory.md)
- [x86_64 drivers and hardware boundary](architecture/drivers.md)
- [Crabshell and the volatile RAM filesystem](architecture/crabshell.md)
- [Unix-like process and syscall direction](architecture/syscall-abi.md)
- [Build and toolchain guide](development/building.md)
- [Testing and verification](development/testing.md)
- [Security and unsafe-code policy](security.md)
- [Milestones and acceptance criteria](roadmap/README.md)

## Current status

The repository contains a bare-metal `no_std` Rust kernel for `x86_64-unknown-none`. After Limine handoff it validates and copies memory-map metadata into an owned snapshot, reports baseline CPUID features, seeds a volatile RAM filesystem, and runs Crabshell over the COM1 serial console. Crabshell's allocation-free parser is a separate crate; the kernel handles command execution. The image builder and bounded QEMU prompt smoke test are wired into CI, but the latest source changes have not yet been built or boot-tested and Milestone 0's end-to-end run remains pending. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process. A bounded physical-frame allocator core is initialized from the validated map and reported by `meminfo`, but no kernel service allocates or maps frames yet; there is not yet page-table management, a heap, a general IRQ subsystem, a scheduler, process isolation, a persistent filesystem, or a Unix compatibility layer. Fatal CPU exceptions have basic GDT/TSS/IDT diagnostics but no recovery or fault-injection tests yet.

## Documentation conventions

- **Implemented** means present in the repository and checked by current code or tests.
- **Planned** means an architectural direction, not a stable ABI or delivered capability.
- Any future ABI proposal must state versioning, error behavior, memory ownership, and compatibility expectations before it is treated as stable.

````rustix/README.md
     1	# Rustix
     2	
     3	Rustix (Rust-unix) is an experimental, 64-bit, Unix-like operating system whose kernel is written in Rust. This repository builds the kernel itself; Limine is used only as the external boot protocol/loader, not as a substitute for a Rustix kernel.
     4	
     5	Rustix now boots into **Crabshell**, a small kernel-mode shell on the COM1 serial terminal. It includes basic navigation and file commands backed by a fixed-capacity RAM filesystem. The filesystem is volatile and reset at every boot; this is an early kernel shell, not a userspace process or POSIX shell. The command parser lives in a separate, allocation-free `crabshell` crate so a future GUI terminal can reuse it. Scheduling, process isolation, persistent storage, a syscall ABI, networking, and userspace are still future work. See [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) for the staged plan.
     6	
     7	## Quick start
     8	
     9	Prerequisites: a Rust stable toolchain, `just`, Python 3, `xorriso`, QEMU (`qemu-system-x86_64`), and the target installed by `rust-toolchain.toml` (or `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`). The first image build downloads a pinned Limine binary release and verifies its SHA-256.
    10	
    11	```sh
    12	just help
    13	just fmt
    14	just test
    15	just check
    16	just build
    17	just image
    18	just smoke
    19	just run       # interactive serial shell in QEMU; exit with Ctrl+C
    20	just verify
    21	```
    22	
    23	`just build` produces `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `just image` creates `target/rustix.iso`, a hybrid BIOS/UEFI image; `just smoke` checks that Crabshell reaches its prompt; and `just run` starts an interactive QEMU session attached to the current terminal.
    24	
    25	Try `pwd`, `ls /`, `mkdir notes`, `write notes/hello.txt "hello from Rustix"`, `cat notes/hello.txt`, and `cd ..` in Crabshell. Commands include `help`, `clear`, `pwd`, `meminfo`, `ls`, `cd`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `write`, `append`, `cp`, `mv`, `cat`, `rm`, and `rmdir`. The RAM filesystem holds at most 31 entries plus its root, with files capped at 1024 bytes. See [`docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](docs/architecture/crabshell.md) for the shell and filesystem contract, [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) for build/emulator details, and [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) for the documentation map.
    26	
    27	## Project principles
    28	
    29	- The kernel and operating-system implementation are Rust-first and `no_std`; architecture-specific privileged operations are isolated under `src/arch/`.
    30	- The kernel is the product. A bootloader may initialize the machine and transfer control, but policy, memory management, scheduling, and Unix-like services belong to Rustix.
    31	- Keep unsafe code small, documented, and adjacent to its hardware/protocol boundary.
    32	- Build incrementally: every roadmap milestone should have build checks, tests where practical, and updated design documentation.
    33	- Unix-like behavior is an explicit compatibility goal, not a claim of POSIX compliance today.
    34	
    35	## Repository map
    36	
    37	- `src/main.rs` — freestanding kernel entry point and Crabshell handoff.
    38	- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel command executor.
    39	- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem, with host-side tests.
    40	- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` command parser crate; no I/O or filesystem coupling.
    41	- `src/boot.rs` — mutable Limine response requests, validated owned boot snapshot, and diagnostics.
    42	- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — COM1 polling driver used for shell output and input.
    43	- `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` — baseline CPUID vendor and feature reporting.
    44	- `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` — bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT and fatal exception diagnostics.
    45	- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling.
    46	- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers.
    47	- `src/memory.rs` — fixed-capacity validated physical-memory-map snapshot and host tests.
    48	- `src/frame.rs` — bounded physical frame allocator core and host tests; not yet wired into the live kernel.
    49	- `.cargo/config.toml`, `linker.ld` — x86_64-none code generation and ELF layout.
    50	- `justfile` — formatting, tests, target checks, image creation, emulator smoke test, and aggregate verification.
    51	- `limine.conf` — pinned boot configuration for the Rustix kernel.
    52	- `scripts/boot.py` — checksum-verified Limine download, hybrid ISO assembly, and bounded QEMU validation.
    53	- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — runs `just verify` on pushes and pull requests.
    54	- `docs/` — architecture, drivers, development, security, and roadmap documentation.

````

````rustix/docs/development/building.md
     1	# Building Rustix
     2	
     3	## Prerequisites
     4	
     5	- Rust stable with `rustfmt`; the repository pins these in `rust-toolchain.toml`.
     6	- The `x86_64-unknown-none` target. The toolchain file requests it automatically; if needed, install it with `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`.
     7	- [`just`](https://just.systems/) to run the repository's named tasks.
     8	- Python 3.8 or newer (standard library only), with `python` on `PATH`; `xorriso`; and QEMU with `qemu-system-x86_64` for image creation and boot smoke tests.
     9	
    10	An ELF inspection tool such as `llvm-readelf` or `readelf` is useful when diagnosing linker output. The first image build downloads the pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary archive into `target/tools/` and verifies its published SHA-256 before extraction.
    11	
    12	## Common commands
    13	
    14	Run from the repository root:
    15	
    16	```sh
    17	just help
    18	just fmt       # check Rust formatting
    19	just test      # parser, RAM-filesystem, and memory tests
    20	just check     # type-check the freestanding kernel target
    21	just build     # optimized kernel ELF
    22	just image     # hybrid BIOS/UEFI ISO at target/rustix.iso
    23	just smoke     # bounded QEMU boot to the Crabshell prompt
    24	just run       # interactive serial shell in QEMU (Ctrl+C to stop)
    25	just verify    # fmt, workspace tests, target check, image, and QEMU smoke test
    26	```
    27	
    28	Equivalent Rust checks are `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --lib`, `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-none`, and `cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-none`. Image creation and QEMU validation are provided by `scripts/boot.py` and are intentionally part of `just verify`.
    29	
    30	The optimized ELF is written to `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `cargo check` checks the target without producing a boot image. The library tests run on the host and exercise code that does not require privileged instructions.
    31	
    32	## Target-specific linker setup
    33	
    34	`.cargo/config.toml` applies the Rustix linker script and x86_64 kernel constraints only to `x86_64-unknown-none`. `linker.ld` emits an ELF64 x86_64 image at the higher-half base, retains Limine request sections in a writable load segment for bootloader response pointers, and defines `_start` as the entry symbol. The build uses no third-party Rust crates; the boot protocol is represented by small in-tree Rust structures and constants.
    35	
    36	Changing the target, virtual base, relocation model, or request ABI requires updating the linker script, protocol documentation, and validation plan together. Do not use host builds of the kernel binary as evidence that the freestanding target links correctly.
    37	
    38	## Building and smoke-testing a boot image
    39	
    40	`limine.conf` boots the kernel immediately and enables 38,400-baud serial output. `just image` builds the ELF, fetches Limine v12.9.3's binary ZIP from its immutable GitHub release, checks the pinned SHA-256, prepares a BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO, and installs the BIOS boot code. The Limine archive and extracted tools remain under ignored `target/`; no third-party binaries are checked into the source tree.
    41	
    42	`just smoke` launches `target/rustix.iso` in `qemu-system-x86_64` with a 256 MiB q35 machine, headless display, captured COM1 output, and a 20-second deadline. QEMU is expected to remain running at the interactive shell; the runner terminates it at the deadline and requires the startup banner, Crabshell-ready message, and initial prompt. On a failure it prints the serial log. The log remains at `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` for inspection.
    43	
    44	`just run` launches the same image with the serial port attached to the host terminal, allowing interactive shell use. Stop the emulator with `Ctrl+C`.
    45	
    46	`just verify` includes the emulator smoke test and therefore needs Python 3, xorriso, QEMU, network access for the first Limine download, and the Rust target. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs the system tools on Ubuntu 24.04 and runs the same command. This verifies the boot path in CI; it is still not a substitute for testing physical hardware.
    47	
    48	## Troubleshooting
    49	
    50	- **Target not installed:** install `x86_64-unknown-none` as shown above.
    51	- **`just` not found:** install `just`; Rust-only checks can still be run with the Cargo commands above.

     2	
     3	Rustix is an early kernel prototype, not a security-reviewed operating system. It has no user/kernel separation implementation, process isolation, security boundary, or supported deployment profile today.

     8	- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` configures and writes to the legacy COM1 UART. It is intended for early kernel context only.
     9	- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` reads raw bytes from a legacy PS/2-compatible controller; callers must poll without blocking.
    10	- `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` executes CPUID for boot-time feature reporting; x86_64 requires CPUID support.
    11	- `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` loads the GDT/TSS/IDT and exception-entry assembly, reads CR2 on page faults, and halts after printing the saved context. The exception gates are kernel-only and maskable interrupts remain disabled.
    12	- `src/boot.rs` reads Limine response pointers and entries, then validates and copies range metadata into an owned boot snapshot. Nullness, alignment, count bounds, arithmetic, and range overlap are checked; the kernel still trusts Limine to make non-null response objects readable for the handoff lifetime.
    13	- `src/main.rs` uses `cli` and `hlt` to stop the bootstrap CPU after a fatal startup error.
    14	- `src/vfs.rs` and `src/shell.rs` provide a kernel-mode RAM filesystem and shell. They have no user/kernel isolation, permissions, persistence, or protection from kernel bugs; shell commands are trusted kernel code, not sandboxed applications.

The PS/2 routine consumes bytes from the controller, including discarding auxiliary/error bytes, so it must only be used by a single owner of that controller until input serialization is designed. External boot inputs, user pointers, MMIO, and DMA must not be treated as trusted merely because current boot data is trusted.
    17

    19	
    20	- Validate every physical range and checked address calculation before mapping or allocating it.
    21	- Enforce least privilege in page mappings; avoid writable-executable pages by default.
    22	- Keep user memory untrusted and use explicit copy-in/copy-out routines at syscall boundaries.
    23	- Define ownership and lifetime rules for descriptors, processes, shared memory, and device buffers.
    24	- Test malformed input and error paths as well as successful operation.

# Rustix agent instructions

These instructions apply to every coding agent working in this repository. Read this file before changing code. For the architecture and detailed subsystem contracts, use the linked documents under `docs/`; this file summarizes the rules agents must preserve.

## Project mission

Rustix is an experimental 64-bit, Unix-like operating system with its own Rust kernel. Limine is the external boot protocol/loader only. Do not describe Limine, a host shell, or a userspace project as the Rustix kernel.

The kernel is `no_std` and targets `x86_64-unknown-none`. Rust is the implementation language for kernel and OS components. The repository currently uses a Python standard-library script only to assemble and smoke-test the boot image; it does not replace kernel or OS functionality.

Unix-like behavior is a long-term design goal, not a claim of POSIX compatibility. Make unsupported behavior explicit rather than approximating it silently.

## Current project status — read before planning

The source contains:

- A Limine-based x86_64 kernel entry, linker layout, serial diagnostics, and boot-memory reporting.
- A separate allocation-free `no_std` `crabshell` parser crate and a kernel-mode COM1 shell frontend.
- A volatile, fixed-capacity RAM filesystem used by the shell.
- A validated, fixed-capacity boot memory-map snapshot and baseline CPUID reporting.
- A fixed-capacity physical frame allocator retained in `BootInfo`; Crabshell's `meminfo` command reports counts. No kernel service currently allocates frames for mappings or other services.
- Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception handlers for vectors 0–31. Double faults use an IST stack and page faults report CR2. Maskable IRQs remain disabled; exception recovery and fault-injection tests are not implemented.

Important incomplete work:

- The roadmap still has Milestone 0's end-to-end image build and QEMU boot validation pending. The latest source has not been established as successfully built or booted.
- Milestone 1 source exists but is not build-/boot-verified. Structural pointer checks do not prove that a Limine-provided non-null pointer is mapped or readable; that remains a loader trust boundary.
- Milestone 2 is **in progress**, not complete. Rustix still inherits Limine's page tables; it has no kernel-owned page-table manager, no heap, and no live frame allocation callers. GDT/TSS/IDT assembly and exception paths have not had fault-injection or emulator validation.
- There is no scheduler, userspace, syscall ABI, persistent filesystem, user/kernel isolation, or general IRQ subsystem.

Never advance status or check off a roadmap item merely because source code or an interface exists. Update `docs/roadmap/README.md` only to reflect implementation and validation actually achieved.

## Source-of-truth documents

Consult the relevant documentation before modifying a subsystem:

- [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) — documentation entry point and current status.
- [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) — milestone sequencing and exit criteria.
- [`docs/architecture/overview.md`](docs/architecture/overview.md) — current architecture and intended layers.
- [`docs/architecture/boot.md`](docs/architecture/boot.md) — Limine requests, boot snapshot, and trust boundary.
- [`docs/architecture/memory.md`](docs/architecture/memory.md) — memory ownership, frame allocator, and paging direction.
- [`docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](docs/architecture/crabshell.md) — parser/kernel boundary and shell/VFS contract.
- [`docs/architecture/drivers.md`](docs/architecture/drivers.md) — current driver scope and limitations.
- [`docs/security.md`](docs/security.md) — unsafe boundaries and security policy.
- [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) and [`docs/development/testing.md`](docs/development/testing.md) — supported commands and validation expectations.

When code and documentation disagree, inspect the implementation, resolve the discrepancy deliberately, and update the relevant documentation in the same change.

## Repository map

- `src/main.rs` — freestanding entry, boot snapshot acquisition, panic path, and shell handoff.
- `src/boot.rs` — mutable Limine requests, structural response/range validation, owned `BootInfo`, and boot diagnostics.
- `src/memory.rs` — allocation-free memory-map validation and known/unknown region classification.
- `src/frame.rs` — bounded physical-frame allocator core; it only uses validated `Usable` ranges, reserves the first MiB, and has fixed range metadata.
- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel-side Crabshell executor.
- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem and host-side tests.
- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` parser crate. It has no terminal, filesystem, or kernel dependencies.
- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — polling COM1 driver for shell input/output.
- `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` — bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT, assembly stubs, and fatal exception diagnostics.
- `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` — CPUID identification and selected feature reporting.
- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling; not an input subsystem.
- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow port-I/O wrappers.
- `linker.ld`, `.cargo/config.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml` — target, linker, and toolchain configuration.
- `limine.conf`, `scripts/boot.py` — boot configuration and pinned image/emulator workflow.
- `justfile` — supported development commands.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — CI validation workflow.

## Engineering rules

### Keep changes incremental and coherent

1. Inspect the relevant source, tests, docs, and call sites before editing.
2. State assumptions, invariants, and failure behavior for new kernel interfaces.
3. Prefer small vertical slices that compile and can be tested over broad scaffolding or placeholder APIs.
4. Update tests and documentation alongside behavior changes.
5. Do not change unrelated code, rename files gratuitously, add speculative features, or rewrite project history.
6. Do not commit or create branches unless the user explicitly asks.

### Rust and dependency policy

- Preserve the kernel's `no_std`/freestanding constraints. Do not introduce `std` into kernel code.
- Prefer `core` and existing in-tree abstractions. Do not add third-party Rust dependencies without a concrete need and compatibility/security review.
- Keep the Crabshell parser independent of kernel I/O and VFS implementation. Kernel execution belongs in `src/shell.rs` or an appropriate kernel service.
- Do not add allocation-dependent APIs before a real heap exists. Fixed-capacity structures must document their limits and exhaustion behavior.
- Respect the workspace structure and the host-testable `rustix-kernel` library versus freestanding `rustix` binary boundary.

### Unsafe and hardware code

Unsafe code is expected only at explicit hardware, boot-protocol, assembly, or raw-memory boundaries. Keep each unsafe block narrow and document the invariant that makes it sound. Do not add broad `unsafe impl`, mutable global references, unchecked pointer arithmetic, or unreviewed inline/global assembly.

Before changing boot or memory code, account for these facts:

- Limine fills response pointers before `_start`; the request records must remain writable in the ELF image.
- Rustix validates nullness, alignment, counts, arithmetic, and physical ranges, but cannot prove that a non-null bootloader pointer is readable.
- Physical ranges are half-open `[start, end)` and must use checked arithmetic.
- Only regions classified `Usable` may enter the frame allocator. ACPI, bootloader-reclaimable, framebuffer, reserved, unknown, and other types are not free frames.
- A `Frame` is a physical address, not a dereferenceable pointer. Do not access it through the HHDM or change CR3 until an explicit, reviewed mapping policy and ownership proof exist.
- The kernel currently inherits Limine's page tables. Do not casually replace or mutate them: preserve the executing kernel, boot stack, `BootInfo`, request/response data, exception stacks, and mappings needed to continue execution.
- The exception setup is fatal-only. It does not enable maskable interrupts, configure a PIC/APIC, or provide recovery. Do not call `sti` or claim interrupt support without an IRQ design and tests.
- The shell and VFS run in ring 0 and are not isolated or secure.

For hardware changes, document assumptions about CPU mode, selectors, stacks, page permissions, interrupt state, and failure handling. Avoid new architecture mechanisms that cannot be statically reviewed or validated.

### Shell and filesystem contract

- Crabshell is presently a kernel-mode serial shell, not a userspace program or a POSIX shell.
- Its parser is a separate `no_std`, allocation-free crate; retain that boundary.
- The RAM filesystem is volatile and bounded. Preserve explicit errors and test capacity, path, and mutation edge cases.
- Do not imply persistence, permissions, links, process launching, or shell features that do not exist.
- Update the parser tests and `docs/architecture/crabshell.md` when adding or changing commands.

## Validation workflow

Run the narrowest relevant checks first, then broaden them. From the repository root, the supported commands are:

```sh
just fmt
just test
just check
just build
just image
just smoke
just verify
```

`just test` runs host-side library tests (memory-map validation, frame allocator, VFS, and Crabshell parser). `just check` checks `x86_64-unknown-none`; `just build` links the optimized ELF. `just verify` includes formatting, host tests, target check, pinned Limine image creation, and QEMU prompt smoke test. Image/boot checks need Python, `xorriso`, QEMU, the Rust target, and network access for the first pinned Limine download.

For changes to `src/main.rs`, `src/boot.rs`, linker/request configuration, `src/arch/x86_64/`, `src/frame.rs`, or paging/heap code, the intended full validation is `just verify`. If the environment does not permit a check, report the exact blocker and leave the corresponding roadmap criterion pending.

Do not claim a check passed unless it was run and its successful result was observed. Editor diagnostics are useful but are not a substitute for `cargo test`, a target build, or QEMU. A target check is not a final link; a linked ELF is not proof of boot; a prompt smoke test is not proof of interactive shell behavior or physical-hardware correctness.

## Completion criteria for agent changes

Before reporting work complete:

- Ensure source, tests, docs, and call sites agree.
- Review unsafe and hardware assumptions, including error paths and capacity limits.
- Run appropriate formatting/tests/build/boot checks, or clearly state why they could not run.
- Report files changed, behavior delivered, validation actually observed, and remaining risks.
- Keep milestone status accurate. A subsystem is not complete just because it has code.

# Claude Code instructions for Rustix

These are project-specific instructions for Claude Code and Claude-based agents working in this repository. `AGENTS.md` is the canonical shared engineering contract; read and follow it together with this file. If advice conflicts, preserve the stricter Rustix safety and validation rule, and do not infer that an unfinished subsystem is complete.

## What this repository is

Rustix is an experimental 64-bit Unix-like operating system with its own Rust kernel. The kernel is `no_std` and targets `x86_64-unknown-none`. Limine is only the external boot protocol/loader. Do not conflate the loader with Rustix or describe a host tool as the kernel.

The project is deliberately staged. Rustix currently boots to a kernel-mode Crabshell over polling COM1, with a bounded volatile RAM filesystem. This is not a userspace terminal, persistent filesystem, secure shell, or POSIX implementation. The `crabshell` workspace crate parses commands only; kernel I/O and filesystem operations remain in the kernel.

## Status must stay honest

Before planning a task, read `docs/roadmap/README.md` and the relevant architecture document. Current source includes:

- A Limine handoff and a fixed-capacity owned boot snapshot with structural validation.
- Baseline CPUID reporting and a typed, classified memory map.
- A fixed-capacity physical frame allocator retained in `BootInfo`; Crabshell `meminfo` reports counts. No kernel service currently allocates frames.
- Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT and fatal exception stubs for vectors 0–31; the double-fault path has an IST stack, and page faults report CR2/error bits. IRQs remain disabled.
- A separate allocation-free Crabshell parser and a bounded volatile RAM filesystem.

Important limitations:

- Milestone 0's successful image build and QEMU boot smoke test remain pending for the current source.
- Milestone 1 source has not been established as build- or boot-verified. A non-null Limine pointer can still be unreadable; structural checks do not prove mapping/accessibility.
- Milestone 2 is incomplete: page tables are inherited from Limine, there is no kernel-owned page-table manager, no global heap, no live frame-allocation caller, and no fault-injection/emulator verification of the exception path.
- There is no scheduler, userspace, syscall ABI, persistent storage, user/kernel isolation, or general IRQ subsystem.

Do not check off roadmap criteria merely because code or an interface exists. Only report builds, tests, and emulator checks that you actually ran and observed passing.

## Required workflow

1. Read `AGENTS.md`, the relevant `docs/architecture/*.md` document, and the actual implementation/call sites before changing code.
2. Identify the subsystem boundary and failure behavior. For hardware work, state assumptions about privilege level, selectors, page mappings, stack state, and IF/interrupt state before coding.
3. Make the smallest coherent vertical change. Prefer tested architecture-independent helpers in `src/lib.rs` modules over untestable freestanding-only logic when that preserves the design.
4. Add or update tests for normal, boundary, malformed, and exhaustion cases. Keep parser tests in `crates/crabshell`; do not make that crate depend on kernel facilities.
5. Update the relevant architecture, testing, security, and roadmap docs in the same change.
6. Run the narrow validation first, then the broader check appropriate to the touched paths.
7. In the final summary, distinguish implementation from verification and list any environmental blocker or remaining risk.

Do not commit, create branches, run broad formatting rewrites, or modify unrelated files unless explicitly requested.

## Rustix implementation rules

### `no_std` and fixed capacity

- Kernel code must remain freestanding and `no_std`; use `core`, not `std`.
- Avoid new Rust dependencies unless there is a concrete need and compatibility/security review.
- There is no general heap. Do not add `Vec`, `String`, `Box`, or allocation-dependent interfaces to kernel paths.
- Fixed-capacity tables must document capacity, exhaustion behavior, and whether an error leaves state unchanged.
- The kernel binary is not the host test target. Keep pure logic in the `rustix-kernel` library where practical.

### Boot, memory, and physical frames

- Limine writes response pointers before `_start`; response-bearing request records and their linker section must remain writable to the loader.
- Validate pointer nullness/alignment/counts and checked arithmetic, but preserve the documented trust boundary: Rustix cannot prove a loader pointer is mapped and readable.
- All physical ranges are half-open `[start, end)`. Use checked arithmetic and reject overlaps rather than silently normalizing malformed maps.
- Only `RegionKind::Usable` ranges feed the frame allocator. Reserved, ACPI, loader-reclaimable, framebuffer, bad, executable/module, and unknown ranges are never ordinary free frames.
- A frame handle represents a physical address; it is not a pointer. Do not dereference it, add the HHDM offset and assume success, or change CR3 until a reviewed mapping policy proves the access and ownership.
- The active page tables are currently inherited from Limine. Any future replacement must preserve the executing kernel, boot stack, `BootInfo`, request/response objects, GDT/TSS/IDT data, exception stacks, and all mappings needed for continued execution.
- The current allocator is bounded and single-owner/single-core. It is not a page-table manager, heap, or concurrent allocator.

### x86_64 and exceptions

- Keep privileged instructions, port I/O, assembly, and raw pointer operations in narrow architecture modules with nearby safety comments.
- The current GDT/TSS/IDT path is fatal-only. It does not initialize a PIC/APIC, enable maskable interrupts, recover from faults, or provide a general IRQ subsystem.
- Do not add `sti`, exception recovery, preemption, or claims of interrupt support without an explicit design, ownership/locking rules, fault injection, and emulator validation.
- When editing `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs`, review normalized CPU-error-code stack layout, register-save ordering, stack alignment before calling Rust, the double-fault IST, descriptor selectors, and fatal behavior. Assembly diagnostics are not a substitute for assembling/linking the target.
- `CPUID` support bits do not prove a feature is enabled in control registers or active page tables. Label reports as supported/capable unless activation is verified.

### Crabshell and VFS

- The parser crate may contain syntax/model types, but no terminal, VFS, kernel, or hardware I/O.
- Kernel command execution belongs in `src/shell.rs`; the fixed-capacity VFS contract belongs in `src/vfs.rs`.
- RAM filesystem contents disappear on reset. Preserve explicit errors, root protection, directory rules, path limits, node limits, and file-size limits.
- When adding/changing a command, update parser behavior/tests, shell execution/help, `docs/architecture/crabshell.md`, and user-facing examples as appropriate.

## Supported validation

Run these from the repository root using `just`:

```sh
just fmt
just test
just check
just build
just image
just smoke
just verify
```

`just test` runs host tests for memory-map validation, frame allocator behavior, VFS, and Crabshell parsing. `just check` type-checks `x86_64-unknown-none`; `just build` links the release ELF. `just verify` covers formatting, host tests, target check, pinned Limine image creation, and bounded QEMU prompt smoke. Image/boot steps need Python 3, `xorriso`, QEMU, the target, and network access for the first pinned download.

Changes to boot requests/entry, `linker.ld`, `src/arch/x86_64/`, memory allocation, paging, or heap code should receive `just verify` when the environment permits. If it does not, report the exact command failure and leave the corresponding roadmap criterion unchecked.

Editor diagnostics are useful but are not proof that Rust compiled, assembly assembled, the target linked, the image booted, or the hardware path works. Never say “tests pass” when they were not run.

## Relevant documentation

- `docs/index.md` — documentation entry point and current status.
- `docs/roadmap/README.md` — sequencing and milestone exit criteria.
- `docs/architecture/overview.md` — architecture and subsystem layering.
- `docs/architecture/boot.md` — Limine request/response contract and trust boundary.
- `docs/architecture/memory.md` — ranges, frame allocator, inherited mappings, and future paging.
- `docs/architecture/crabshell.md` — parser, commands, and RAM filesystem contract.
- `docs/architecture/drivers.md` — driver status and scope.
- `docs/security.md` — unsafe boundaries and security requirements.
- `docs/development/building.md`, `docs/development/testing.md` — commands and evidence expectations.
